cards.title: A Unified Framework for Batch Correction and Imputation in Modern Mass Spectrometry Proteomics
cards.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics, including single-cell applications, are often confounded by batch effects, inter-laboratory variation, and signal drift that can obscure biological interpretation. NMFBatch addresses these sources of unwanted variation through a unified framework that combines non-negative matrix factorization with generalized additive modelling to jointly capture discrete and continuous technical effects from protein expression data. It handles missing values directly through masking and on-the-fly imputation. Benchmarking across reference datasets, plasma proteomics cohorts, simulations, and single-cell data demonstrated that NMFBatch reduced technical variation while preserving biological structure. These results establish NMFBatch as a robust framework for batch correction, harmonization, and integrative proteomics analysis from protein expression data.

cards.title: Epigenetic clocks and accelerated biological aging in people living with HIV: Emerging mechanisms and clinical implications.
cards.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has significantly improved survival among people living with HIV. However, many people living with HIV develop cardiovascular, metabolic, neurocognitive, musculoskeletal, and frailty-related conditions earlier or more frequently than HIV-negative individuals of a similar chronological age. DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks provide a method for estimating biological age and may help explain this increased burden of age-related disease. This short review aims to summarize current evidence on epigenetic age acceleration in people living with HIV, describe the biological mechanisms that may contribute to accelerated aging, examine the effects of antiretroviral therapy and sex-related factors, and discuss the possible clinical applications of epigenetic clocks. First-generation epigenetic clocks, including the Horvath and Hannum clocks, generally indicate that people living with HIV are approximately 5 to 7 years biologically older than HIV-negative individuals of a similar chronological age. However, these clocks may be affected by HIV-related changes in immune-cell composition. Newer measures, including PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, Retro-Age, and immune-composition-resistant clocks, assess different aspects of biological aging, such as physiological decline, mortality risk, the pace of aging, and retroelement-associated methylation. HIV-associated epigenetic aging appears to involve persistent viral activity, chronic immune activation, inflammation, immunosenescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, altered one‑carbon metabolism, glutathione deficiency, cellular senescence, and treatment-related metabolic or mitochondrial effects. Antiretroviral therapy may reduce epigenetic age acceleration, but it does not consistently restore biological age to the level observed in HIV-negative individuals. Sex, menopause, metabolic dysfunction, and body composition may also influence the relationship between epigenetic aging, frailty, and mortality. Epigenetic clocks may improve the assessment of biological aging in people living with HIV and could support risk stratification, early identification of frailty, and evaluation of interventions. However, longitudinal validation, standardized methods, adjustment for immune-cell composition, and evidence linking clock changes with meaningful clinical outcomes are required before these biomarkers can be used routinely in HIV care.

cards.title: A microbiota-driven neuroepithelial feed-forward circuit drives gastroesophageal junction tumorigenesis
cards.abstract: The gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) is continuously exposed to refluxed bile acids and microbial perturbations, yet how these environmental cues are converted into persistent oncogenic signaling is unknown. Here we show that bile acid remodeling enriches the oral commensal Prevotella melaninogenica at the GEJ, where bacterial succinate activates both vagal sensory neurons and SUCNR1-expressing tuft cells. Activated tuft cells release 15-deoxy-12,14-prostaglandin J2 (15-d-PGJ2), which sensitizes sensory neurons and sustains nerve remodeling, while neuronal CGRP drives expansion and tuft-cell differentiation of neuro-responsive epithelial progenitors through RAMP1. This self-reinforcing microbiota-neuron-epithelium circuit promotes dysplastic progression, and its genetic or pharmacological disruption, including with the approved CGRP antagonist rimegepant, suppresses tumor development, revealing an interceptable mechanism linking environmental dysbiosis to cancer initiation through neural circuits.

cards.title: Early dopamine elevation modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male juvenile mice
cards.abstract: Alterations in dopaminergic signaling and exposure to early-life stress are both implicated in the developmental origins of psychiatric disorders, yet little is known about how these factors interact during sensitive periods of brain maturation. We investigated whether increased dopamine availability during early postnatal development modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male C57BL/6 mice. From postnatal day (PD) 1 to PD14, mice received L-Dopa plus benserazide, maternal separation (3 h/day), their combination, or the corresponding control conditions. We assessed mice behavior between PD28 and PD32 using novel object recognition, open-field, elevated plus-maze, marble-burying, and forced-swim tests, followed by hippocampal volumetric analysis. Early L-Dopa exposure produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. In females, L-Dopa increased rearing without altering horizontal locomotion and modified open-arm exploration and stress-coping behavior, whereas in males it increased open-arm exploration and reduced climbing frequency. Maternal separation produced distinct effects in females and males and reduced repetitive digging/burying behavior in both sexes. Importantly, maternal separation frequently modified rather than potentiated the effects of L-Dopa. In both sexes, combined maternal separation and L-Dopa opposed several L-Dopa-associated alterations in open-field, elevated plus-maze, and forced-swim behaviors. Recognition memory was largely preserved across experimental conditions. L-Dopa also reduced hippocampal volume selectively in females, whereas hippocampal volume was higher in females exposed to maternal separation plus L-Dopa than in those receiving L-Dopa alone. Multivariate analyses revealed overlapping rather than treatment-specific behavioral clusters, indicating substantial individual heterogeneity and sex-dependent shifts in multidimensional behavioral profiles. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient alterations in dopamine availability and maternal separation interact non-additively during early postnatal development. Their consequences depend on sex, behavioral domain, and developmental timing, supporting a model in which neurochemical and environmental perturbations dynamically shape behavioral trajectories rather than simply producing cumulative developmental damage.

cards.title: Neuronal FICD shapes motivated behavior through modulation of dopamine receptor dynamics
cards.abstract: Motivated behaviors rely on dopaminergic signaling, which in turn depends on the correct folding and trafficking of receptors through the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Within the ER, the AMPylase enzyme FICD acts as a molecular rheostat through its modification of the chaperone BiP, dynamically tuning the organelle's responsiveness to folding perturbations and cellular stress. While the biochemistry of FICD is well-established, its role in complex animal behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FICD as a conserved contributor to the generation of motivated behavior. In Drosophila, pan-neuronal knockdown of dFic significantly reduces feeding, spontaneous locomotion, and reward-seeking behavior. These alterations occur without disrupting circadian architecture, motor capacity, or homeostatic hunger, indicating a specific loss of motivational drive. Depleting dFic within subsets of dopamine receptor-expressing (Dop1R1) neurons recapitulates these behavioral alterations. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that dFic depletion does not induce a canonical unfolded protein response, pointing to a specific post-transcriptional alteration rather than global ER stress. At the molecular level, dysregulated dFic alters the localization and abundance of Dop1R1. Finally, we demonstrate that this regulatory axis is evolutionarily conserved, as loss of FICD similarly diminishes motivated behaviors in C. elegans and mice. Together, these findings implicate FICD in the generation of motivated behavior and link dynamic control of ER proteostasis to dopamine-receptor maturation.

cards.title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
cards.abstract: Background: Machine Learning (ML) has shown promise in histopathological diagnosis, but rare tumours, like duodenal epithelial neoplasms, are challenging because large, labelled datasets are difficult to assemble. We propose a data-efficient ML pipeline for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia in whole-slide images. Methods: We assembled a five-hospital dataset of haematoxylin and eosin-stained duodenal biopsy whole slide images (WSIs) at 10x magnification, comprising 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic biopsies, including adenomas, carcinomas and neuroendocrine tumours. WSIs were divided into patches and encoded using the Hibou-B foundation model. We compared global standardisation with unsupervised site-specific standardisation of patch embeddings. Our pipeline combined principal component analysis, a Gaussian mixture model and a Random Forest classifier. We assessed generalisability using leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation across four hospitals and on an independent test set from a fifth hospital. Results: In leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation, the pipeline achieved a mean accuracy of 90%, sensitivity of 96%, specificity of 83% and an AUC of 0.96. On the external test hospital, it achieved 94% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, 95% specificity, and AUC of 0.97. Site-specific standardisation improved mean cross-validation accuracy by 20 percentage points compared with global standardisation, while the Gaussian mixture pipeline improved accuracy by 12 percentage points compared with mean pooling of patch embeddings. Conclusions: We present a data-efficient ML approach for detecting duodenal epithelial neoplasia from WSIs. Strong performance was maintained across hospitals and on an independent external test cohort despite the limited number of neoplastic training cases, supporting the feasibility of foundation-model-based approaches for rare histopathological diagnoses.

cards.title: A low-adhesion mechanism enables axon growth in the developing brain
cards.abstract: During development, axons grow through complex tissue environments to wire the brain. Axon growth speeds measured in cell culture are incompatible with the distances axons must cover in vivo. Yet how axons achieve the growth speeds required to establish long-range connectivity within a narrow embryonic developmental window, and by what mechanism, remains unknown. Here, using long-term live imaging in brain sections, mouse genetics, molecular and pharmacological perturbations, together with AxoVivo, a newly developed intravital imaging platform that resolves subcellular structures, including growth cones and cytoskeletal dynamics, in living mouse embryos, we show that axons of cortical projection neurons (CPNs) employ a low-adhesion mechanism to grow. Even as growth cones change shape and turn, axons grow an order of magnitude faster than in vitro. The actin motor myosin II controls the growth cone actin cytoskeleton and its morphology but not axon growth itself, which is instead promoted by microtubule stabilisation. Finally, super-resolution shadow imaging (SUSHI) revealed that growth cones do not pull on the surrounding extracellular matrix. Taken together, this low-adhesion mechanism driven by protruding microtubules ensures the rapid growth necessary for long-distance wiring of the developing nervous system.

cards.title: Inferotemporal cortex stimulation is perceived before its onset
cards.abstract: Neural response latency measures when stimulus-evoked activity becomes detectable, but it does not reveal when the brain assigns the causal contribution of that activity to events in the external world. We define this temporal adjustment as projected delay and measure it in the macaque inferotemporal cortex using optogenetic stimulation and behavior. Two rhesus macaques performed a cortical perturbation detection task in which a visual masker appeared at different times relative to stimulation. Detection was selectively impaired when the masker began 200 ms before stimulation. We then tested this timing using Perceptography, a method that optimizes image perturbations to mimic stimulation-evoked visual events. Image perturbations presented 200 ms before stimulation elicited higher false-alarm rates than perturbations presented at stimulation onset. Here, we show that stimulation-evoked visual events in inferotemporal cortex depend preferentially on visual information originating approximately 200 ms before the cortical perturbation. This projected delay exceeds typical inferotemporal response latencies and suggests temporally extended readout mechanisms relevant to causal models of visual perception and the timing of cortical visual prostheses.

cards.title: Cell-Cell Communication Patterns in Alzheimer's Disease Differ by Cortical Layer
cards.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Existing cell-cell communication (CCC) studies of Alzheimer's disease dementia (ADD) using cortical snRNAseq data do not account for the distinct cell-type and gene-expression profiles within cortical layers. Cortical-layer-aware CCC analysis may clarify biological mechanisms associated with ADD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). METHODS: We applied our recent analytical tool STACCato to identify CCC events associated with ADD and MCI within cortical layers, using a large-scale prefrontal cortex snRNAseq dataset (~1.4M nuclei, n=395) with cortical layers annotated from reference spatial transcriptomics data. RESULTS: We identified ADD/MCI-related CCC events with distinct patterns within cortical layers, including ADD-related interactions involving the known AD risk genes APOE and APP that were detected only in microglia in layer 5, and those with opposite effects of ADD and MCI in layers 5 and 6. DISCUSSION: Our findings on cortical-layer-aware ADD/MCI-related CCC events underscore the importance of spatially-aware genomics studies of AD.

cards.title: Multi-omic spatial mapping of the human habenula defines the molecular and anatomical organization of medial and lateral subregions
cards.abstract: The habenula (Hb) is a small epithalamic midline structure critical for reward processing and mood regulation that is implicated in many complex brain disorders, including depression and addiction. The molecular anatomy of the Hb has been well-characterized in model organisms, but little is known about its organization in the human brain, including the transcriptomic and epigenetic signatures of spatially-organized lateral (LHb) and medial (MHb) cell types. Here, we generated a high resolution spatiomolecular map of the human Hb using both multiomic single nucleus sequencing (snMultiome) and spatially-resolved transcriptomics. We measured gene expression and chromatin accessibility across 4 MHb and 5 LHb neuronal cell types as defined by transcriptomic conservation with rodents and zebrafish. We identified cell type-specific molecular specializations related to GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling as well as regulatory relationships between open chromatin regions, transcription factors, and target genes associated with depression and addiction. High resolution spatial transcriptomics identified the anatomical location of heterogeneous LHb subpopulations, including two putative inhibitory populations in the LHb. We further characterized cell-type relationships between Hb neurons and glial subtypes and predicted ligand-receptor interactions between LHb and MHb neurons. Finally, we delineated Hb cell types and spatial domains enriched in genes associated with genetic risk for psychiatric disorders, identifying the strongest enrichment in the MHb. Collectively, the generated data and analyses resolve the spatiomolecular organization of the human Hb and identify molecular-genetic associations with neuropsychiatric disease.

cards.title: Inferring organ aging, hallmark of aging and senescence scores from blood and facial photographs
cards.abstract: Aging progresses asynchronously across organs, motivating the development of organ-resolved aging clocks. Direct assessment of organ aging in living humans, however, is largely impractical. Here, we construct tissue-specific transcriptomic aging clocks and infer organ biological age from paired whole-blood (blood-organ age) and tissue RNA sequencing data in the GTEx project. We observe high variability both in the strength of aging signatures across organs and in the ability to predict organ age and organ scores from blood. Pathway analysis shows that organ aging clocks are dominated by biological processes that differ across tissues. Age-associated multi-organ modules identified in an aging multi-organ network correlation analysis and organ age features causally mediated through organ-blood-organ transcriptomic interactions support a role for systemic signaling in coupling organ aging processes. Given the established role of cellular senescence as a driver of tissue dysfunction and its tissue-specific accumulation during aging, we extend this framework to estimate burden of organ-level senescence and hallmarks of aging. Using senescence- and hallmark-associated gene sets, we derive tissue-specific senescence and hallmark scores (organ scores) and demonstrate that these burdens across multiple organs can be inferred from blood transcriptomes (blood-organ scores). Finally, in pursuit of extending these models to other blood omics and alternative non-invasive assessments, we evaluate whether blood methylation (methylation-blood-organ age and scores) and facial photographs (facial-blood-organ age and scores) can serve as proxies for blood-organ age and blood-organ scores in independent cohorts (Edifice Health and Health and Retirement Study). The methylation- and facial-blood-organ age and scores were associated with mortality in additional testing cohorts (Framingham Heart Study and IMDB-WIKI dataset). These results establish a cross-modal framework for inferring organ-specific aging and senescence from minimally invasive data.

cards.title: Alzheimer's Disease-Associated Proteomic Changes in Olfactory Stem Cells Show Pathway-Level Transcriptomic Overlap
cards.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive, neurodegenerative disorder and the leading cause of dementia worldwide. Although recent therapeutic advances have provided some disease-modifying potential, there is currently no curative treatment for AD, highlighting the need for improved disease models and early biomarkers. Olfactory mucosal stem cells, which can be expanded in vitro as olfactory neurosphere-derived (ONS) cells, represent a promising source for biomarker discovery because olfactory tissue is more accessible than central nervous system tissue and has been reported to exhibit AD-related pathological changes. In this study, we used subcellular fractionation-based proteomics, reconstructed bulk proteomics and integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analyses to characterise alterations in ONS cells derived from healthy control, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD individuals. Fraction-specific proteomics identified cytoplasmic and nuclear-enriched protein abundance changes, including alterations in proteins and pathways associated with cytoskeletal organisation, RNA processing, intracellular trafficking, autophagy and mitochondrial/metabolic processes. Reduced LC3B abundance in cytoplasmic AD ONS cells was supported by western blot analysis, although LC3B abundance alone does not indicate altered autophagic flux. Reconstructed bulk proteomics identified 40 FDR-significant proteins in AD compared with HC, defining an AD-associated protein signature enriched for extracellular matrix, cytoskeletal, organelle-associated and RNA-processing pathways. Despite proteomic enrichment of mitochondrial and metabolic pathways, Seahorse Mito Stress Test analysis did not identify significant group-level differences in mitochondrial respiration. Integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analysis revealed partial RNA-protein concordance and pathway-level overlap across disease-associated processes. Together, these findings support the use of patient-derived ONS cells as a model for investigating AD- and MCI-associated molecular changes and highlight protein signatures for further validation.

cards.title: SNX13 and SNX14 interorganelle tethers suppress lysosome membrane damage and neurodegeneration
cards.abstract: Lysosome membrane permeabilization (LMP) is an emerging signature of neurodegenerative diseases, yet the mechanisms that enable an effective repair are largely undefined, particularly in neurons. Here, we reveal sorting nexin (SNX) proteins SNX13 and SNX14 maintain lysosome membrane lipid composition to support efficient LMP repair and neuronal survival. We identify loss of function mutations in SNX13 in children manifesting a previously unrecognized cerebellar neurodegenerative disorder. Consistently, Snx13 ablation in mice causes cerebellar Purkinje cell death and signatures of ataxia-like motor deficits. We show loss of SNX13 or its ataxia-linked paralog SNX14 perturbs lysosome morphology, positioning, and acidity and causes increased susceptibility to lysosome damage. Using lysosome immunoprecipitation and proteomics, we comprehensively map lysosome proteome remodeling during membrane damage and repair, finding that SNX13 or SNX14 deficiency blunts recruitment of repair machinery, including ESCRTs and PITT pathway proteins, to damaged lysosomes. Mechanistically, we determine SNX13 and SNX14 support lysosome integrity through interorganelle lipid crosstalk. We define SNX13 and SNX14 as lipid binding proteins that localize to ER-lysosome junctions, where they support lysosomal phosphoinositide levels in response to membrane damage. In line with this, loss of SNX13 or SNX14 impairs lysosome PtdIns4P signaling. Altogether, our work reveals a conserved mechanism of interorganelle lipid crosstalk by SNX13/14 family proteins that safeguards lysosome membranes, maintaining them competent for repair, and is defective in cerebellar neurodegeneration.

cards.title: Foundation Models Improve Perturbation Response Prediction
cards.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to genetic or chemical perturbations is a long-standing goal in biology. Recent applications of foundation models to this task have yielded contradictory results regarding their superiority over simple baselines. We conducted an extensive analysis of the utility of pretrained embeddings (including but not limited to biological foundation models) for perturbation response prediction, covering over 600 embedding-task pairs. While some foundation models fail to outperform simple baselines, others yield consistent improvements. However, the strongest pretrained embeddings are those derived from prior knowledge. We also developed methods for integrating multiple pretrained embeddings to make better predictions. Our results confirm that pretrained embeddings can enable more accurate simulations of cellular behavior.

cards.title: The limbic navigation system as a hierarchical RNN
cards.abstract: Path-integration-trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can reproduce grid-like and head-direction-like representations, but most existing models rely on low-dimensional velocity inputs and do not capture the hierarchical organisation of the brain's self-localisation circuit. We introduce a hierarchical recurrent neural network (HRNN) that separately processes angular velocity and linear speed to perform simultaneous angular and positional path integration. Trained on these tasks, the HRNN generalises to longer timescales than seen during training and develops neural response properties resembling all the key cell types: angular velocity cells, head direction cells, speed cells, conjunctive and pure grid cells. The learned circuit also recovers key motifs of the navigation system, including attractor dynamics and asymmetric connectivity patterns. Perturbation analyses reveal functional information flow across the hierarchy, consistent with experimental observations. Finally, introducing theta-paced mutual inhibition between two learned angular-velocity subpopulations enables the HRNN to reproduce the bidirectional theta sweeps observed in empirical data. These results establish hierarchical task-driven RNNs as a biologically interpretable framework for linking neural representations, circuit motifs, and population dynamics in spatial navigation, while enabling targeted in silico perturbations and the generation of experimentally testable predictions.

cards.title: DCAF: Unifying Data Validity, Evaluation Validity and Predictive Modeling for Single-cell Perturbation Simulation
cards.abstract: Single-cell perturbation profiling is limited by cost and throughput, while computational methods remain constrained by inconsistent evaluation and underperformance relative to simple baselines. Here we present DCAF, a unified framework for single-cell perturbation simulation that that jointly addresses data validity, evaluation validity and predictive modeling. Among its three components, DCAF-data addresses the single-measurement limitation by reconstructing pre- and post-perturbation status using entropy-regularized optimal transport, and is demonstrated on both cell line and multi-cell type datasets. DCAF-criterion evaluates log fold changes in non-silenced genes to improve sensitivity to model error and robustness to zero inflation noise, validated on synthetic datasets. DCAF-model combines JEPA with explicit modeling for regulatory-dynamics modeling for interpretable prediction. Across benchmarks, DCAF outperforms state-of-the-art deep-learning methods, as well as mean and linear baselines in cross-gene, cross-cell-type and cross-region generalization. In adult Mouse brain, DCAF recapitulates known cell-type-specific regulatory heterogeneity of Dgcr8 knockdown at both cell type and gene levels. DCAF thus provides a rigorous and biologically grounded foundation for reliable perturbation simulation across development, disease and therapeutic discovery.

cards.title: Enabling Spatially Resolved Gene Expression Analysis in a Multilayer Paper-Based In Vitro Tumor Model
cards.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity is a defining feature of solid tumors, yet molecular analysis of three-dimensional (3D) in vitro tumor models is often performed as a bulk measurement, potentially obscuring position-dependent cellular responses. Here, we establish an analytical workflow for spatially resolved gene-expression analysis in a multilayer paper-based 3D tumor model by addressing the challenge of RNA recovery from cell-laden paper-Matrigel scaffolds. Using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, multiple RNA extraction strategies were systematically evaluated across conventional culture, Matrigel, paper, and composite paper-Matrigel environments. Conventional silica-column extraction yielded only 3.39 {+/-} 0.93 ng/L RNA from the composite scaffold, whereas TRIzol-chloroform extraction increased recovery to 201.13 {+/-} 38.32 ng/L. The optimized workflow subsequently enabled independent RNA recovery from all eight layers of a multi-layer paper-based in vitro tumor, with concentrations ranging from 113.06 {+/-} 5.00 to 245.26 {+/-} 15.76 ng/L and purity suitable for downstream qRT-PCR analysis. Layer-resolved profiling of untreated cultures revealed distinct spatial patterns in HIF1A, HIF2A, VEGFA, and GLUT4 expression across the multilayer construct. To evaluate the workflow under pharmacological perturbation, cultures were exposed to 5 M doxorubicin (DOX) for 48 h. Relative cell viability exhibited a non-monotonic spatial profile, whereas DOX-induced HIF1A and VEGFA expression generally became more pronounced toward the deeper layers when each treated layer was compared with its corresponding untreated control. Collectively, these results establish a workflow for converting individually addressable regions of a multilayer 3D tumor model into spatially resolved transcriptional measurements, enabling analysis of both baseline spatial heterogeneity and position-dependent molecular responses to pharmacological perturbation.

cards.title: The Alzheimer's disease risk gene ABCA7 regulates microglial lysosomal and lipid homeostasis and promotes phagocytosis to maintain neuronal health
cards.abstract: Background: Loss of function mutations in the lipid transporter ABCA7 have been linked to increased risk for late onset Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although rare and common variants in ABCA7 associated with AD alter the coding sequence and are predicted to impair protein function, the precise cell-type consequences of ABCA7 deficiency remain incompletely defined. Methods: We used CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) that were deficient for ABCA7 (ABCA7-KO) and their wild-type (ABCA7-WT) isogenic counterparts and subsequently performed unbiased proteomics on differentiated astrocytes (iAs), neurons (iNs) and microglia (iMGs). ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs produced the largest proteomic changes, so we therefore conducted additional functional analyses to define its effects on microglial lysosomal activity, phagocytosis, and lipid metabolism. In addition, we leveraged CRISPR/Cas9 to correct the ABCA7 rs3752246 AD risk variant in patient-derived iPSCs and compared proteomic and functional phenotypes between corrected iMGs and isogenic mutant carriers. Finally, we examined the functional consequence of ABCA7-deficient microglia on neurons. Results: ABCA7-KO iMGs were deficient for proteins involved in lysosome function, measured by down-regulated lysosomal proteomic signatures, as well as reduced DQ-BSA activity and reduced LAMP1+ area. Additionally, ABCA7-KO iMGs displayed impaired phagocytic capacity and increased inflammatory markers, including MHC proteins CD1A and CD1E, and IL-18. Multi-omic integration of lipidomic and proteomic profiles nominated a dysregulated metabolic network characterized by altered phospholipid steady-state metabolism and increased lipid peroxidation in ABCA7-KO iMGs. This was complemented by an accumulation of polyunsaturated triacylglycerols and lipid droplets, suggesting that ABCA7 deficiency disrupts intracellular lipid dynamics. This was supported by the alleviation of lysosomal and lipid droplet phenotypes through the inhibiting the synthesis of triacylglycerols. Concordantly, proteomic and functional analyses revealed lysosomal dysfunction in rs3752246-mutant iMGs, suggesting a shared ABCA7-dependent mechanism underlying AD risk. Tri-cultures of iNs, iAs and iMGs revealed that ABCA7 deficiency in iMGs worsened AD-relevant neuronal measures such as tau phosphorylation and synapse number. Conclusions: This work supplies evidence for the important role of ABCA7 in microglia and provides unique insights into the molecular and functional consequences of reduced ABCA7 function in lysosomal and lipid regulation, paving a path forward to a more comprehensive understanding of AD molecular subtypes and personalized therapeutics.

cards.title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease
cards.abstract: Background: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood. Methods: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis. Results: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI. Conclusions: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

cards.title: Subcellular spatial proteomics of the close animal relative, Capsaspora owczarzaki
cards.abstract: Capsaspora owczarzaki is one of the closest relatives of animals and an increasingly tractable model for investigating the evolution of multicellularity. However, very little cell biological work has been done on the sister linages to animals. Subcellular spatial proteomics (SSP) is a technique that can localize thousands of proteins to subcellular compartments in a single experiment by combining cell fractionation with sensitive mass spectrometry. To provide broad insight into the localization of the Capsaspora proteome, we performed SSP based on a label-free version of LOPIT-DC (Localisation of Organelle Proteins by Isotope Tagging after Differential ultraCentrifugation). We detected 6,466 proteins, corresponding to 68.4% of the predicted Capsaspora proteome, and assigned high-confidence localizations to 3,106 of them across 13 subcellular compartments. This study serves as a proteomic dataset to resolve cellular compartmentalization in a close relative of animals, enabling downstream evolutionary, biological, and functional analyses. Investigators interested in using these data prior to publication are encouraged to contact us to avoid overlap and to facilitate coordinated and collaborative use of this resource.

cards.title: Subcellular spatial proteomics of the heterotrophic nanoflagellate, Cafeteria roenbergensis
cards.abstract: Cafeteria roenbergensis is the best-studied free-living heterotrophic nanoflagellate, an abundant marine bacterivore and the host of the giant virus CroV, yet almost nothing is known about how its cell is organized. To provide broad insight into the localization of its proteome, we used subcellular spatial proteomics (SSP), based on a label-free version of LOPIT-DC (Localisation of Organelle Proteins by Isotope Tagging after Differential ultraCentrifugation), in which organelles are separated by differential centrifugation and each protein is assigned to a compartment from its abundance profile across fractions. We detected 5,948 proteins (5,889 protein groups), corresponding to 69.7% of the predicted C. roenbergensis proteome, and assigned high-confidence localizations to 2,945 proteins across 14 subcellular compartments, including basal body/cilia, cytosol, ER, Golgi, lysosome, membrane-trafficking, mitochondria, nucleoplasm, nucleus, peroxisome, plasma membrane, proteasome, ribosome, and spliceosome. This study serves as a proteomic dataset to resolve protein compartmentalization in a free-living heterotrophic stramenopile, enabling evolutionary, biological and functional insight and analysis. Investigators interested in using these data prior to publication are encouraged to contact us to avoid overlap and to facilitate coordinated and collaborative use of this resource.

cards.title: El Niño, capture success, and wing fluctuating asymmetry in Drosophila sturtevanti Duda, 1927
cards.abstract: Fluctuating asymmetry (FA) is widely used as a proxy for developmental instability, although reduced rather than increased FA, has occasionally been reported under particularly challenging conditions, possibly because environmental filtering removes less developmentally stable individuals. Here, we investigated temporal variation in wing shape asymmetry in males of Drosophila sturtevanti collected in 2022, 2024, and 2026 at the same sampling site, an urban Atlantic Forest fragment. Sampling in 2022 and 2026 were completed during single field expeditions in early April, whereas in 2024 repeated collections were required until mid-May because of markedly low capture success. We therefore examined whether this difference was associated with unusual environmental conditions and whether FA was higher in 2024, as expected under greater developmental perturbation. Daily temperature and relative humidity were examined from early March onward, encompassing approximately one month before adult emergence. The 2024 sampling period was warmer and drier than the corresponding periods in 2022 and 2026 and coincided with the final phase of the strong 2023-2024 El Niño event. Contrary to our prediction, FA was significantly lower in 2024. The magnitude of directional asymmetry remained similar among years, although the spatial pattern of the DA vector differed between 2024 and 2026. The coincidence of reduced capture success and reduced FA is consistent with the hypothesis that adverse conditions may impose demographic filtering, such that individuals expressing greater developmental instability are less likely to contribute to the sampled adult population.

cards.title: Human Th17 state classification reveals a selective vulnerability in acylcarnitine metabolism in type 2 diabetes
cards.abstract: Th17 cells are categorized as non-pathogenic (Th17np) and pathogenic (Th17p), states defined primarily in murine autoimmune models. In contrast, studying these states in humans remains difficult because these subsets lack validated identifiers. We developed a nanovial-based single-cell ELISA to isolate cytokine-secreting human Th17 cells and define Th17np vs Th17p cell transcriptional states. These signatures enabled predictive classification and flow-cytometric identification across tissues and diseases. Application of these strategies with single-cell metabolic modeling and functional profiling revealed that Th17np cells predominate in type 2 diabetes yet exhibit impaired fatty acid oxidation capacity despite elevated carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A). CRISPR perturbation and pharmacologic inhibition identified acylcarnitine metabolism as a regulator of Th17 state balance and exposed a selective metabolic vulnerability in type 2 diabetes. This framework links human Th17 cell pathogenicity to lipid metabolism.

cards.title: Plasma proteomic signatures of biological aging and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease risk: a prospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Biological aging is associated with incident metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but the underlying proteomic mechanisms remain largely unknown. This study aimed to systematically characterize the plasma proteomic landscape and identify specific biomarkers that mediate the aging-MASLD axis. We analyzed the associations between four multi-dimensional biological aging indicators (telomere length, frailty index, Klemera-Doubal method biological age, and phenotypic age), 2911 plasma proteins, and incident MASLD among 52,131 UK Biobank participants. A rigorous two-stage analytical pipeline, integrating multivariable linear and elastic net regression, was applied to screen robust aging-related proteins. Cox proportional hazard regression models and mediation analyses were employed to assess their roles in MASLD risk, followed by comprehensive tissue and functional enrichment analyses to elucidate underlying biological mechanisms. During a median follow-up of 13.60 years, 762 participants developed MASLD. All biological aging indicators were significantly linked to MASLD incidence. We identified distinct proteomic signatures for these biological aging indicators. Furthermore, multiple proteins significantly mediated the corresponding association, explaining 0.5 to 50.7% of the risk. Notably, 769 unique mediators were identified, anchored by a core signature of five shared proteins (AXL, CCL19, CPM, REN, and TNFRSF11B) across all four indicators. Enrichment analyses revealed a multi-organ origin (predominantly lung, adipose tissue, and arteries), highlighting the dominance of immune-inflammatory pathways. Plasma proteins partially mediate the increased MASLD risk driven by biological aging. These findings underscore the roles of systemic immune-inflammatory signaling, providing biomarkers for early risk stratification and potential novel therapeutic targets for aging-associated hepatic pathology.

cards.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction of renal tubular epithelial cells in chronic kidney disease-associated fibrosis: from organelle homeostasis to multicellular remodeling.
cards.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, and renal fibrosis is a common pathological correlate of progressive loss of kidney function. Renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs), particularly proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTECs), contain abundant mitochondria and depend on oxidative metabolism to support solute transport. This metabolic specialization renders them vulnerable to hypoxia, lipotoxicity, uremic toxins, aging, inflammation, and hemodynamic stress. Persistent mitochondrial injury can suppress fatty acid oxidation and oxidative phosphorylation, deplete nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, increase mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, destabilize mitochondrial DNA, and disrupt biogenesis, dynamics, mitochondria-associated membrane signaling, and mitophagy. These abnormalities promote maladaptive repair, senescence, inflammatory cell death, and paracrine signaling to fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelial cells, and pericytes. Evidence is organized within a tubule-to-niche framework that distinguishes causal perturbation from temporal or transcriptomic association, model-specific findings from cross-model convergence, and experimental efficacy from clinical translation. Single-cell, spatial, and organoid studies are considered alongside evidence from human biopsy specimens and biomarkers. Mitochondrial dysfunction is thus treated as a context-dependent contributor to, and amplifier of, CKD-associated fibrotic remodeling rather than a universal initiating event. Although strategies targeting bioenergetics, redox balance, mitochondrial quality control, and tubular delivery are promising, translation is constrained by disease heterogeneity, intervention timing, target specificity, pharmacokinetics, and the scarcity of validated human antifibrotic endpoints.

cards.title: Phosphorylation-dependent Remodeling of the CLOCK/BMAL1/nucleosome Complex
cards.abstract: Phosphorylation of the CLOCK/BMAL1 complex is a reversible posttranslational modification that plays a central role in regulating circadian oscillations; however, its underlying mechanistic basis remains poorly understood. Although biochemical studies have shown that phosphorylation modulates CLOCK/BMAL1 binding to DNA, yet it remains unclear whether these effects are confined to local perturbation or also propagate through allosteric effects. Moreover, the influence of phosphorylation on histone dynamics and transcription factor nucleosome interactions has not been systematically investigated. Here, we address these questions using atomistic trajectories obtained through backmapping of coarse grained molecular dynamics simulations based on the recently resolved cryo EM structure of the CLOCK/BMAL1 and nucleosome complex. We investigated three experimentally identified phosphorylation states: CLOCK bHLHS38/42, BMAL1 bHLHS78, and simultaneous phosphorylation of both proteins. Our results demonstrate that phosphorylation regulates CLOCK and BMAL1 asymmetrically. Whereas phosphorylation weakens the interaction of the modified bHLH domain with the Ebox, BMAL1 phosphorylation simultaneously enhances DNA engagement by the CLOCK bHLH domain, an effect that persists in the doubly phosphorylated complex. Steered pulling simulations showed that phosphorylation of the CLOCK bHLH domain results in mechanical stability comparable to that of the unphosphorylated system. In contrast, BMAL1 phosphorylation appears to reduce the mechanical stability of the bHLH DNA interaction. Beyond modulating DNA binding, phosphorylation remodels protein histone interactions by altering contacts between the CLOCK PASB domain and histone H3 and between the BMAL1 PASA domain and the H2A/H2B acidic patch, while simultaneously rewiring residue-correlation and allosteric communication networks throughout the heterodimer. Importantly, phosphorylation increases the separation between the CLOCK HI loop and the H3 1L1 elbow, supporting a structural model in which phosphorylation provides a more permissive environment for CRY1 recruitment to the chromatin-bound CLOCK BMAL1 complex, thereby facilitating displacement-type transcriptional repression. Collectively, our findings reveal that phosphorylation regulates the CLOCK/BMAL1 complex through coordinated remodeling of DNA binding, nucleosome interactions, and long-range allosteric communication, providing a mechanistic framework for circadian transcriptional repression and a foundation for the rational design of therapeutics targeting the molecular circadian clock.

cards.title: Biotin-operated ligand trapping enables dynamic spatial redistribution of protein and organelle in living cells
cards.abstract: Controlling protein localization through chemical biology tools is essential for mechanistic interrogations, functional perturbations, and therapeutic development. While existing tools cover a wide range of applications, no single approach simultaneously enables inducible trapping, controlled release, and visualization of a protein of interest (POI). To address this gap, we developed Biotin-Operated Ligand Trapping (BOLT), which combines a HaloTag-fused POI with a streptavidin trap. Desthiobiotin-conjugated Janelia Fluor HaloTag ligands enable POI visualization, trapping, and biotin-operated release. We demonstrate BOLT's capacity in synchronized secretory cargo release, microtubule-directed organelle movement and hitchhiking, and ectopically localizing nuclear transcription factor. Importantly, pulse-chase BOLT further reveals bidirectional endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi trafficking of an endogenous Golgi enzyme and distinguishes recycled from newly synthesized enzyme populations using distinct HTLs. Altogether, BOLT provides an all-in-one platform to interrogate how subcellular localization regulates protein function across HaloTag-compatible systems.

cards.title: Discovering Latent Scientific Concepts through Discrete Representation Learning
cards.abstract: Scientific imaging is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Advances in multiplex immunofluorescence, computational pathology, and electron microscopy now enable observation of biological and physical systems at unprecedented spatial resolution. Rather than simply classifying known objects, these data offer the opportunity to discover previously unknown organizational principles. However, scientific image datasets are typically highly curated, information-rich, and limited in size, making reliable representation learning particularly challenging. We show that standard continuous self-supervised adaptation can become unstable in this regime, allowing teacher representations to drift and degrading downstream transfer. We introduce Kodiak, a discrete representation learning architecture that discovers latent scientific concepts through Sinkhorn-balanced codebook assignments. Instead of learning unconstrained continuous embeddings, Kodiak constructs a reusable vocabulary of discrete concepts that provides stable supervision for both masked-patch prediction and cross-view representation learning within a single-stage framework. Across five scientific imaging domains, including multiplex immunofluorescence for pancreatic cancer pathology and scanning electron microscopy, Kodiak consistently improves representation quality under both continued foundation-model adaptation and training from scratch. Beyond improved classification and transfer,the learned concepts are interpretable, reusable, and produce spatially coherent concept maps that support applications such as cell phenotyping, segmentation-free patch phenotyping, spatial niche discovery, tissue organization, and materials characterization. We view Kodiak as the representation-learning engine of our foundation model for spatial biology. More broadly, our results suggest that discrete representation learning provides a principled foundation for discovering reusable latent scientific concepts that can accelerate scientific interpretation across imaging domains.

cards.title: Embodied mechanical sensing through self-generated motion in climbing plants
cards.abstract: Embodied mechanical intelligence and morphological computation enable adaptive behavior by shifting computation from centralized control to body mechanics. Yet how dynamical material structures encode environmental information remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question using climbing plants as a minimal decentralized system. Combining force measurements with physical modeling, we show that circumnutating shoots generate predictable forces against candidate supports, and that the interaction is equivalent to a rotating cantilever governed by torque balance. Force amplitude is determined by stem stiffness and geometry, while the timescale is set by circumnutation rate. Twining occurs only after reaching a critical torque threshold, corresponding to a deformation that reflects support stability and geometric reach. Motorized perturbations further show that twining time scales inversely with effective circumnutation rate. Together, these results show how self-generated motion extracts actionable information about the environment, while the tapered geometry and spatially varying mechanics of the shoot encode the decision-making threshold for attachment.

cards.title: Cellular Density Homeostasis Is Governed by an Anisotropic Attractor and Predictive Feedback Control
cards.abstract: Cell density is a fundamental biophysical property of living cells, yet the dynamical architecture underlying density homeostasis remains unknown. Here, we reconstruct the geometry, dynamics, and control structure governing cellular density regulation from single-cell mass-volume measurements acquired during recovery from osmotic perturbation. We identify a persistent anisotropic attractor in mass-volume state space that permits coordinated density-preserving fluctuations while strongly suppressing density-changing deviations. Optimal transport analysis reveals directed recovery trajectories confined to this attractor, enabling inference of an effective density-restoring control law. Density deviations are associated with coordinated changes in biomass accumulation and volume expansion that together generate an effective density-restoring control law. Moreover, density error contains significant predictive information regarding future corrective behavior, revealing an information-rich component of cellular regulation. Together, these findings establish cellular density homeostasis as an emergent dynamical control process and demonstrate how attractor reconstruction, optimal transport, and information theory can be combined to uncover the organizing principles of biological homeostasis.

cards.title: Defining transcriptomic niches in human fibrotic lung with multi-sample spatial transcriptomics analysis using the MAPLE algorithm
cards.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an age-related lung disease marked by patchy parenchymal fibrosis that disrupts gas exchange and leads to respiratory failure. Single-cell RNA-seq studies have revealed cellular heterogeneity in IPF, but the spatial contexts underlying alveolar epithelial cell loss, honeycomb cyst formation, and fibroblastic foci remain unclear, motivating comparisons based on multi-sample spatial transcriptomics (ST) across clinical and anatomical conditions. Here, we present a comprehensive pipeline for analyzing multi-sample lung ST data that accounts for experimental design, featuring the MAPLE algorithm to jointly identify cell-spot subpopulations and discover spatial biomarkers, with validation using 10X Xenium ST data. Our analysis reveals that IPF progression involves epithelial-to-mesenchymal state transitions and region-specific fibrotic programs, characterized by extracellular matrix remodeling in the upper lobes and B-cell-enriched immune niches in the lower lobes. We identify fibrotic regions with senescent cell (SnC) enrichment and demonstrate their spatial colocalization with aberrant basaloid niches.

cards.title: Generative modeling reveals the connection between nuclear morphology and gene expression
cards.abstract: How transcriptional programs shape nuclear morphology, and how morphological features in turn reflect and influence cell identity and function, remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce COSMIC, a bidirectional generative framework that enables quantitative decomposition of transcriptional variance reflected in nuclear morphology and morphological variance explained by gene expression. Pretrained on over 21 million segmented nuclei, COSMIC models cross-modal relationships by using a multimodal dataset acquired with IRIS, a technology that captures high-resolution images and transcriptomes from the same single cells. COSMIC learns relationships between gene expression and nuclear morphology, enabling the identification of genes whose expression covaries with nuclear morphological variation. In prostate cancer cells, COSMIC distinguishes chemotherapy-responsive and -resistant cell states through coordinated morphological and transcriptional changes, revealing morphology-associated genes linked to tumour state. Applied to spatial transcriptomics of zebrafish embryogenesis, COSMIC reveals how local cellular neighborhoods influence morphology-expression relationships. These results demonstrate that generative modeling powered by paired single-cell measurements can quantify the information shared between nuclear morphology and gene expression, opening new avenues for mechanistic discovery in both basic and translational cell biology.

cards.title: Fine-tuned Medical Vision-Language Model (MedGemma 1.5 4B) with and without Structured Radiologist Descriptors versus EU-TIRADS for Malignancy Risk Stratification of Thyroid Nodules at Ultrasound: A Tunisian Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
cards.abstract: Purpose. To evaluate a medical vision-language foundation model fine-tuned on thyroid ultrasound images, with or without the radiologist's structured descriptors, against expert-rated EU-TIRADS for the classification of thyroid nodules as benign or malignant. Materials and Methods. This retrospective study included nodules that underwent ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA) between January 2019 and August 2025 in two Tunisian centers, with consecutive recruitment, together with a selection of images from an international public dataset. Of 1,580 nodules, 1,456 (272 malignant; 1,280 patients) with an interpretable cytological or histological reference standard were allocated at patient level to training (n = 942), validation (n = 258) and a test set sealed before training (n = 256; 51 malignant). MedGemma 1.5 4B was fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation under four input configurations: the image with nodule biometry, with or without age and sex (A, B); A with chain-of-thought supervision (C); and A plus the eleven qualitative descriptors of the radiologist's structured report (D). The EU-TIRADS category was never a model input. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were compared with DeLong's test and a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 0.05; EU-TIRADS >= 4 was the prespecified comparator, with >= 5 as a sensitivity analysis. Results. Config D reached an AUROC of 0.953 (95% CI 0.909-0.976), versus 0.948 (0.894-0.972) for EU-TIRADS (difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.016 to +0.025), which met the non-inferiority criterion; Configs A-C, without the qualitative descriptors, reached 0.883-0.892 (Holm-adjusted p = 0.045 versus EU-TIRADS). At >= 4, EU-TIRADS had a sensitivity of 98.0% and produced 94 false positives among 205 benign nodules; at a threshold fixed on validation data, Config D reclassified 72 of them as negative while missing two additional cancers. Against EU-TIRADS >= 5 (sensitivity 92.2%, specificity 95.1%), Config D at its native threshold (88.2%, 94.1%) did not classify more nodules correctly (McNemar p = 0.22), and at its two other thresholds it classified fewer nodules correctly (p = 0.004 and 0.007). Raw probabilities were miscalibrated (expected calibration error 0.117 for Config D), and Platt scaling within the test set reduced this error to 0.019-0.040. Conclusion. Given the ultrasound image together with the radiologist's structured descriptors, the fine-tuned model matched expert EU-TIRADS discrimination and, against the >= 4 threshold, reclassified most false positives as negative, a gain concentrated in category 4 and based on only three cancers in category 4. It is best positioned as a report-standardizing second reader in the EU-TIRADS 4 gray zone, pending prospective external validation.

cards.title: Probabilistic uncertainty in virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology is largely redundant with the predicted mean
cards.abstract: Deep learning has enabled virtual spatial transcriptomics from histology, offering a scalable approach to molecular profiling of routinely archived tissue without molecular assays. However, reliable uncertainty estimates are essential for identifying potentially inaccurate predictions, and it remains unclear whether existing methods provide useful information about prediction reliability. Here, we present a systematic benchmark of uncertainty estimation for virtual spatial transcriptomics across three cancer cohorts spanning melanoma, lung, and kidney tumors. We evaluate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using probabilistic likelihoods and approximate Bayesian methods alongside histology-free and training-free baselines, assessing both calibration and error informativeness. Across cohorts and methods, uncertainty is associated with prediction error, but the predicted mean largely explains this association. After accounting for the mean, uncertainty provides only weak information about larger errors. Moreover, good calibration does not imply informative uncertainty, with simple distributions fitted without histology achieving comparable calibration. We therefore distinguish calibrated from informative uncertainty and argue that uncertainty should provide information about prediction error beyond the predicted mean. This benchmark provides a framework for systematic uncertainty evaluation in virtual spatial transcriptomics. Code availability: https://github.com/ratschlab/uncertainty-vst-2026

cards.title: Cost-utility analysis of deep learning-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening using chest radiographs: implications of diagnostic thresholds and confirmatory testing.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis often goes undetected until a fracture occurs. Using a deep learning model to analyze routine chest radiographs may cost-effectively identify at-risk individuals. Economic benefit depends on how common the disease is, how the model is calibrated, and whether patients follow through with confirmatory bone density testing and pharmacological treatment initiation. Osteoporosis is common among postmenopausal women and often unrecognized until fragility fractures occur, despite its clinical and economic burden. Deep learning (DL)-based opportunistic screening using existing chest radiographs is a potential approach, but its economic value may vary with disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and care pathway completion. To assess the economic value of a DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening approach among Taiwanese postmenopausal women. A cost-utility analysis was conducted from the Taiwan healthcare perspective using a hybrid decision tree and Markov model. The model simulated a cohort of 50-year-old postmenopausal women over a 50-year horizon. Model inputs, including diagnostic performance, long-term outcomes, costs, and utilities, were derived from published literature, preferably local sources. Additional analyses examined alternative prevalence settings, sensitivity and specificity combinations, and confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation rates. In the base case, assuming full care-pathway completion, DL-based screening was cost-effective versus no screening, with an ICER of 21,827 per QALY, below the willingness-to-pay threshold of one GDP per capita in Taiwan. The approach became cost-effective when osteoporosis prevalence exceeded 14.3%. Across the diagnostic continuum, a sensitivity of 86.6% and specificity of 76.3% generated the greatest economic benefit. DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening was cost-effective under full care-pathway implementation. Its value depended on disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and completion of confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation, and was not maintained under real-world examination estimates observed in Taiwan. Strengthening the post-screening care pathway is therefore central to realizing this value.

cards.title: Multiple non-redundant functions underlie the essentiality of lipopolysaccharide in Gram-negative bacteria
cards.abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is well known for its immunostimulatory activity and its contribution to the permeability barrier of the Gram-negative outer membrane. Yet LPS is essential for growth in nearly all Gram-negative bacteria, even under laboratory conditions where its barrier function should be less critical. LPS contributes to envelope mechanics, membrane biogenesis, and cell division, but whether any of these functions accounts for its essentiality remains unclear. Here, we systematically tested these possibilities by depleting LPS in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Osmoprotection largely preserved cell-envelope integrity but not viability, demonstrating that the mechanical contribution of LPS alone cannot explain its essentiality. Genetic perturbations that increase peptidoglycan rigidity or alter phospholipid homeostasis partially improved growth, supporting independent roles for LPS in envelope mechanics and membrane biogenesis. An unbiased suppressor screen further identified activation of the MarA regulon as a potent mechanism for surviving LPS depletion. Protection required transport by the AcrAB-TolC multidrug efflux pump, revealing an unexpected connection between efflux and cell-envelope homeostasis. Thus, LPS essentiality emerges from multiple non-redundant contributions to Gram-negative cell-envelope physiology.

cards.title: Normative Temperature, Demographic Categories, and the Limits of Infrared Thermometry
cards.abstract: Objective. Temperature readings are routinely stratified by race and ethnicity, though significant group differences may reflect physiology, instrument noise, or categorization rather than biology. This study tests whether these categories partition facial infrared thermography measurements beyond individual variation and baseline device noise. Approach. A secondary analysis of thermography data (n = 951 adults) compares inner-canthus maximum (TCEmax) and full-face maximum (Tmax) temperatures across five administrative categories via one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), mixed-effects modeling, Bland-Altman analysis against oral reference, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis. Main results. ANOVA returns significant group differences (p < 0.001; eta-squared = 0.04 for TCEmax, 0.03 for Tmax), but the total spread (0.2 to 0.3 degrees Celsius) is comparable to device accuracy and within-subject variability. Individual variation accounts for 95% of TCEmax variance, and adding simulated Gaussian noise to participant-level temperatures (sigma = 0.10 to 0.30 degrees Celsius) preserves the complete group-mean rank order in as few as 37.5% of iterations. Significance. Testing whether a group difference survives perturbation at the scale of instrument accuracy offers a check against treating significance alone as evidence of physiology. Here, observed group differences are small relative to measurement variability, and their physiological interpretation remains uncertain, with implications for clinical tools that treat administrative categories as biologically meaningful.

cards.title: Carbendazim Disrupts Cellular Homeostasis and Proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans: A Global Proteomic Approach
cards.abstract: The extensive use of the broad-spectrum fungicide carbendazim (CBZ) has raised increasing environmental concerns due to its persistence and toxicity, leading to regulatory restrictions in several countries. Despite its widespread occurrence, the molecular mechanisms underlying CBZ toxicity in non-target organisms remain poorly understood. Here, we employed quantitative proteomics to characterize the systemic molecular response of Caenorhabditis elegans following exposure to a sublethal concentration of CBZ (0.01 mg.mL-1) from the L1 larval stage to day 1 of adulthood. A total of 273 differentially abundant proteins were identified in the N2 strain. Functional enrichment analysis revealed coordinated alterations in biological processes associated with protein synthesis, proteostasis, mitochondrial function, energy and lipid metabolism, intracellular trafficking, chromatin organization, and redox homeostasis, indicating extensive cellular reprogramming in response to CBZ exposure. Protein-protein interaction network analysis further identified ribosomal proteins and translation-associated factors as the principal hub proteins, suggesting that disruption of the translational machinery represents a central molecular event underlying CBZ toxicity. Collectively, these findings show that CBZ's biological effects extend beyond its established role as a microtubule-disrupting fungicide, affecting multiple interconnected cellular pathways involved in maintaining homeostasis. This study provides the first comprehensive proteomic characterization of CBZ toxicity in C. elegans, offering new mechanistic insights into its mode of action and highlighting the utility of integrative proteomics for assessing the impact of environmental contaminants on non-target organisms.

cards.title: Rigidity-Aware Geometric Pretraining for Protein Design and Conformational Ensembles
cards.abstract: Generative models have recently advanced de novo protein design by learning the statistical regularities of natural structures. However, current approaches face three key limitations: (1) Existing methods cannot jointly learn protein geometry and design tasks, where pretraining can be a solution; (2) Current pretraining methods mostly rely on local, non-rigid atomic representations for property prediction downstream tasks, limiting global geometric understanding for protein generation tasks; and (3) Existing approaches have yet to effectively model the rich dynamic and conformational information of protein structures. To overcome these issues, we introduce RigidSSL (Rigidity-Aware Self-Supervised Learning}, a geometric pretraining framework that front-loads geometry learning prior to generative finetuning. Phase I (RigidSSL-Perturb) learns geometric priors from 432K structures from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with simulated perturbations. Phase II (RigidSSL-MD) refines these representations on 1.3K molecular dynamics trajectories to capture physically realistic transitions. Underpinning both phases is a bi-directional, rigidity-aware flow matching objective that jointly optimizes translational and rotational dynamics to maximize mutual information between conformations. Empirically, RigidSSL variants improve designability by up to 43% while enhancing novelty and diversity in unconditional generation. Furthermore, RigidSSL-Perturb improves the success rate by 5.8% in zero-shot motif scaffolding and RigidSSL-MD captures more biophysically realistic conformational ensembles in G protein-coupled receptor modeling. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZhanghanNi/RigidSSL.git.

cards.title: Homeostatic feedback model of energy metabolism with adaptive enzyme levels exhibits problem solving behavior
cards.abstract: Metabolic networks are typically viewed as homeostatic systems that stabilize flux, energy charge, redox balance, and metabolite availability under perturbation. However, it remains unclear whether the same feedback architectures that support metabolic robustness can also generate learning-like, experience-dependent adaptation. Here, we develop a coarse-grained dynamical model of mammalian energy metabolism to test whether prior perturbation can improve future metabolic responses. The model represents core glucose, glutamine, fatty acid, and oxidative phosphorylation pathways as coupled ordinary differential equations with Michaelis-Menten-type fluxes, product-inhibition feedback, adaptive enzyme-capacity regulation, and explicit ATP costs for enzyme adjustment. Rather than aiming to reproduce quantitative fluxes for a specific cell type, the framework is designed to expose how metabolic feedback, regulatory cost, repeated perturbation, and environmental variability interact. We use this model to ask whether adaptive enzyme regulation enables improved recovery after repeated challenges, whether such effects depend on energetic control costs, and whether environmental variability broadens or constrains the set of reachable adaptive states. This approach provides a tractable way to investigate how homeostatic metabolic regulation may give rise to experience-dependent metabolic plasticity.

cards.title: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
cards.abstract: Background: Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods: Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MTRNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive MTRNR1 assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed in an international EQA programme. Results: Materials were homogeneous, workflow-compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates between 87.5 and 100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions: Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme deployment demonstrated feasibility in decentralised settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.

cards.title: Staphylococcus aureus GpsB, Stk, and VraSR form a cell wall surveillance network to maintain cell envelope integrity and mediate antibiotic resistance
cards.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is an alarming threat to public health worldwide. Specifically, drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus remains a major contributor to global mortality. Therefore, in-depth understanding of antibiotic resistance mechanisms is urgently needed to inform alternative therapeutic strategies. We previously showed that GpsB is a critical regulator of cell wall synthesis in S. aureus. GpsB executes its regulatory role via protein-protein interactions. Yet, how GpsB function is modulated in this organism has remained unclear. Intriguingly, a prior proteomics report indicated that GpsB is phosphorylated at six different residues by the sole serine/threonine kinase Stk. Hence, we explored the physiological significance of GpsB phosphorylation. We identify three phosphosites that are each independently sufficient to drive GpsB phosphoregulation, which likely alters its partner preference. We find that cells lacking gpsB exhibit heightened fosfomycin sensitivity, and that this is exacerbated by stk deletion. Our findings reveal that GpsB collaborates with Stk and the VraSR cell wall stress response system to coordinate the demand-driven availability of cell wall precursors. Collectively, this report establishes GpsB as a pivotal peptidoglycan supply chain sentinel that together with Stk and VraSR forms an integrated cell wall stress monitoring network that maintains cell envelope homeostasis and aids in antibiotic resistance.

cards.title: PIK-75 suppresses an SREBP-centred sterol programme in PIK3CA-altered small-cell lung cancer cells, but attribution to p110α remains unresolved
cards.abstract: Abstract: Background. Class IA PI3K isoforms are candidate therapeutic targets in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). The transcriptional consequences of isoform-directed inhibitors in SCLC cells have not been compared genome-wide. Methods. We re-analysed GEO series GSE40564: PIK3CA-altered NCI-H69 cells treated for 24 h with vehicle, PIK-75 (p110-directed) or TGX-221 (p110{beta}-directed), three arrays per group (Affymetrix HG-U133 Plus 2.0). Differential expression used limma, with re-processing from raw files and spike-in-anchored normalisation as sensitivity analyses. Gene sets were assessed by effect size, competitive and rotation tests, and size-matched random-set nulls. Isoform dependency was examined in DepMap CRISPR screens. A PIK-75 response score was tested in 81 primary SCLCs against random-signature nulls. Results. PIK-75 reduced SREBP-controlled sterol- and lipid-synthesis genes (SQLE, HMGCS1, HMGCR, LDLR, SCD; log2 fold-change -1.1 to -1.6). Cholesterol, mTORC1, hypoxia and glycolysis gene sets fell far more than size-matched random sets. E2F-target and homologous-repair genes fell more modestly, including BRCA1 (-0.91). The response was broad: 11,645 of 17,458 genes changed at FDR < 0.05, but only 316 decreased and 20 increased significantly beyond two-fold, an asymmetry that persisted under spike-in-anchored normalisation. TGX-221 changed 358 genes, none two-fold. Its set-level effects were four- to nine-fold smaller and depended on two of three replicates. PIK-75 did not induce canonical FOXO targets, and it inhibits kinases other than p110, so the response cannot be attributed to p110 alone. In DepMap, SCLC lines depended more on PIK3CA than on PIK3CB (median Chronos -0.38 vs -0.15), as did other lineages. In patients, the response score was not associated with survival or subtype beyond what random gene signatures achieve (empirical p = 0.14 and 0.11). Conclusion. PIK-75, but not TGX-221, suppresses an SREBP-centred anabolic transcriptional programme in NCI-H69 cells. Attributing this to p110 requires confirmation with selective inhibitors or genetic perturbation.

cards.title: Task demands shift motor learning from adaptation to feedback control in an unconstrained bimanual task
cards.abstract: Bimanual actions are common in daily life, yet how task demands shape reliance on learning and control mechanisms remains largely unknown. We examined this in 73 participants who lifted a plate in virtual reality while we distorted visual motion of their right hand. During right-hand-only lifting, aftereffects were present but incomplete. Bimanual lifting with the same right-hand perturbation shifted learning further from adaptation toward feedback control: participants developed compensatory hand adjustments and showed smaller aftereffects. Relaxing precision demands improved success but neither restored aftereffects nor reduced compensation. Removing interlimb conflict by perturbing both hands did not improve success but eased compensatory adjustments and restored plate aftereffects to unimanual levels. Success rate during learning did not correlate with aftereffects, but faster movement speed did. This demonstrates that precision demands and interlimb conflict independently shift learning strategy in bimanual contexts.
