cards.title: Cross-Tissue Inflammatory Convergence Supports a Putative Muscle-Brain Axis in Alzheimer's Disease
cards.abstract: Background Reduced muscle strength is associated with cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD), suggesting that skeletal-muscle aging and AD-related neurodegeneration may share biological mechanisms. Vascular dysfunction, immune activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling have been implicated in both tissues, but the extent of shared cellular and molecular programs remains unclear. We investigated cross-tissue transcriptional programs in aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue and evaluated whether related signals are detectable in peripheral blood. Methods We analyzed independent, unpaired human transcriptomic datasets from skeletal muscle (23 donors), the SEA-AD middle temporal gyrus atlas (84 donors), and peripheral blood. Donor-aware models identified age-associated changes in muscle and transcriptomic changes across continuous pseudoprogression score (CPS) in brain. Cross-tissue comparisons focused on 30 brain donors within an early CPS window. Shared tissue-derived programs were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and independently tested in frailty bulk-blood and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) whole-blood datasets. CellOracle simulations were used to prioritize candidate transcriptional regulators. Results Aging muscle showed increased inflammatory, extracellular-matrix, and stromal communication programs. During early AD-related brain progression, vascular and immune populations showed increasing inflammatory and matrix-associated activity together with shifts in intercellular communication. Cross-tissue analysis identified six concordantly enriched pathways comprising 109 leading-edge genes in endothelial populations and four pathways comprising 51 genes in myeloid populations. Related peripheral-blood signatures varied across cohorts and cell types. However, in independent frailty and ADNI mild cognitive impairment and AD datasets, 23 of 30 predefined tissue-derived pathway-subset tests showed significant positive enrichment after false-discovery-rate correction, whereas individual gene-level bulk-blood associations did not survive correction. CellOracle analyses prioritized ETS2 and BHLHE40 as exploratory endothelial regulators whose simulated perturbation consistently reduced selected shared program scores across tissues. Conclusions Aging skeletal muscle and AD-related brain tissue exhibit convergent endothelial and myeloid inflammatory programs, with related pathway-level signals detectable in peripheral blood. These cross-tissue programs and candidate endothelial regulators provide testable hypotheses for mechanisms linking systemic aging, muscle dysfunction, and AD-related neurodegeneration.

cards.title: Larger Pre-Speech Auditory Modulation Is Associated With Smaller Corrective Responses To Auditory Errors
cards.abstract: PurposeDuring speech planning, the brain predicts the auditory consequences of its movements and modulates the auditory system--a process called pre-speech auditory modulation (PSAM). We investigated the link between PSAM and behavioral error correction and determined how aging influences these mechanisms. MethodsSeventeen young adults (18-32 years) and 13 older adults (50-85 years) performed a speaking task involving auditory feedback perturbations and a silent reading control. We measured electrophysiological responses (N1/P2) to auditory probes during speech planning and correlated these modulations with the magnitude of participants subsequent behavioral corrective responses. ResultsBoth groups showed significant modulation of N1 and P2. However, N1 modulation correlated with corrective responses only in young adults. Older adults showed reduced behavioral corrections and smaller, delayed P2 components. Despite these age-related behavioral differences and the loss of the modulation-correction correlation, older adults maintained modulation magnitudes comparable to those of younger adults. ConclusionsN1 modulation serves as a neural index of the brains predictive processes during speech planning. Aging appears to selectively disrupt the integration of these signals into motor output rather than the internal generation of the predictions themselves.

cards.title: HyperCom: a hypergraph-based method to infer cell-resolved cell-cell communication
cards.abstract: Cell-cell communication underpins intercellular responses allowing cells to dynamically change states across conditions; however current methods typically aggregate signals by cell type annotations which may introduce biases. We developed HyperCom, a hypergraph-based method to infer cell-resolved cell-cell communication from single cell transcriptomics data. HyperCom constructs a hypergraph from known ligand-receptor interactions and the expression of those ligands and receptors in individual cells and performs graph diffusion on the hypergraph to score cells on a continuous spectrum from sender to receiver for each LR pair. HyperCom then generates a cell-type agnostic ranking of LR pairs by communication either over the whole dataset or in a condition-aware manner. Validation of HyperCom on physical cell-to-cell contact, spatial, and multicondition datasets highlight its flexibility to capture subtle per cell communication information. HyperCom is available as a species-agnostic, scalable, and open source R package: https://github.com/pawelab/HyperCom.

cards.title: 3D MERFISH reveals cell-type diversity generated by mRNA partitioning in spiralian embryogenesis
cards.abstract: Cell type diversification during development is often attributed to differential gene transcription. Here, we show that, during Crepidula atrasolea embryogenesis, transcriptomically distinct cell types arise through differential distribution of pre-existing mRNAs. Combining immunofluorescence, live imaging, and whole-mount 3D spatial transcriptomics (MERFISH) of over 40 embryos, we show that many mRNAs form subcellular aggregates during mitosis, which segregate asymmetrically between daughter cells through microtubule associations. Cell divisions thus simultaneously increase cell number and diversity, producing six transcriptomically distinct cell quartets in the 24-cell stage embryo. We modeled aggregate compositions across cell divisions using transcript abundance and quantified transcript-specific affinity. These results establish mRNA sorting and inheritance as a scalable cell type patterning mechanism and provide a framework for investigating how mRNA segregation shapes animal development.

cards.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Editing of Myeloid Lectins Reveals Target-Dependent Transcriptional Remodeling in Tumor-Associated Macrophages
cards.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) integrate multiple microenvironmental signals, including lectin-mediated recognition of tumor-associated glycans. Although several myeloid lectins have been implicated in tumor-macrophage interactions, their contributions to immunosuppressive TAM phenotypes remain poorly defined. We implemented a CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein (RNP) workflow in primary human monocytes to enable comparative loss-of-function interrogation of five potentially immunosuppressive lectins we previously reported. CRISPR-Cas9 RNP delivery conditions were benchmarked in freshly isolated monocytes using CD14 as a technical target, followed by sgRNA editing efficiency screening for CLEC4E, CLEC6A, CD209, SELL, and SIGLEC9 in HeLa S3 cells. Selected guides were applied to primary monocytes before co-culture in a 3D model with BT474 breast cancer cells. Editing was quantified by Sanger-sequencing deconvolution, while co-culture-derived CD45+ macrophages were isolated by fluorescence-activated cell sorting and characterized by bulk RNA sequencing. All five lectins were successfully perturbed, although gene editing efficiency remained target- and donor-dependent. Transcriptomic analysis revealed target-specific reprogramming and recurrent immunometabolic responses. mTORC1 signaling was consistently enriched, together with the remodeling of cholesterol homeostasis, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation. CLEC6A deletion achieved attenuation of hypoxia-, angiogenesis-, and TNF/NF-kB-associated programs. CD209 and SIGLEC9 deletion similarly reduced hypoxia- and angiogenesis-associated signatures while promoting lipid and oxidative metabolism. CLEC4E perturbation induced broad remodeling of lipid and oxidative metabolism and stress-response, despite comparatively limited editing efficiency. Comparative lectin perturbation thus identified CLEC6A as the strongest candidate for further mechanistic investigation, while CLEC4E showed broad transcriptional remodeling despite lower editing efficiency, supporting its prioritization for improved genetic interrogation. Responses to CD209 and SIGLEC9 targeting further support tumor glycan-myeloid signaling as a regulator of TAM state. Overall, lectin perturbation redirected TAM transcriptional states through distinct immunometabolic programs rather than a uniform pro-inflammatory polarization, highlighting lectin-dependent immunometabolic regulation as a promising axis for further investigation.

cards.title: PIE: Generalizing perturbation effects across unseen perturbations, contexts and datasets
cards.abstract: Predicting cellular response to perturbations is key to understanding biological mechanisms and selecting therapeutic targets. However, generalizing across cellular contexts, perturbations, and experimental datasets remains challenging due to incomplete representations of the system being perturbed and the difficulty of measuring true perturbation effects within that system. We introduce PIE, a model that addresses these limitations by reformulating the learning task around population level perturbation effects and incorporating auxiliary inputs that better characterize the biological system. PIE directly predicts differentially expressed genes and changes in gene expression for each (context, perturbation) pair, using external biological knowledge, baseline gene expression, and observed perturbation responses. Its architecture accommodates input sources with variable feature sets and predicts effects on genes seen and unseen during training. On the Replogle Nadig dataset, PIE achieves state of the art performance on most metrics across all tested generalization settings, including the most challenging setting where both the context and perturbation are unseen during training. For predicting differentially expressed genes, PIE achieves 1.2 to 3.2 times the AUPRC of the strongest baseline in each setting: across unseen contexts, perturbations, experimental datasets, and jointly unseen contexts and perturbations. Overall, PIE provides a framework for generalizing perturbation effects across diverse experimental conditions.

cards.title: Rank Normalization Enables Cross Pathway Comparison in Degradation Resolved Proteome Turnover Analysis
cards.abstract: Protein homeostasis, or proteostasis, is essential for cellular health, and its disruption contributes to cancer, aging, and neurodegenerative disease. Proteostasis is maintained largely by two intracellular degradation systems: the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) and the autophagy lysosomal pathway (ALP). Here, we combine pulse stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture (pSILAC) with selective inhibition of the UPS or ALP to quantify pathway-dependent protein turnover and identify substrates that are preferentially cleared through each route. Direct comparison of these perturbations is complicated by their markedly different response distributions. To address the mismatch in dynamic range, we developed a normalization strategy based on within-condition ranks. Protein stabilization values are converted to percentile scores before comparison across pathways, placing both perturbations on a common relative response scale. Across two independent pSILAC experiments, 5,518 proteins were quantified in at least one condition, and 3,814 yielded high confidence half-life measurements in control, proteasome-inhibited, and lysosome-inhibited conditions. Rank normalization resolved pathway sensitivities that were obscured by direct comparison of absolute half-life changes. Importantly, the method reports relative pathway preference rather than absolute pathway contribution, exchanging effect size magnitude for comparability across perturbations with unequal response distributions. Integration with a curated proteostasis network annotation revealed coherent pathway preferences, including coordinated stabilization of proteasome core and regulatory subunits following lysosomal inhibition. This finding provides proteome-wide quantitative evidence for proteaphagy that complements previous targeted observations. Together, these results establish rank normalization as a practical strategy for comparing degradation resolved proteome turnover across perturbations with different dynamic ranges.

cards.title: Engineering robust cardiomyocyte differentiation from iPSCs through WNT-mediated process window expansion
cards.abstract: Lack of robustness and high variability in cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) remain critical challenges for cardiac regenerative medicine and biological research. Guided by developmental principles of lineage specification, we investigated whether early WNT inhibition could expand the process window of CM differentiation and thereby improve robustness. To test this, we compared early WNT inhibition from days 1--5 with standard inhibition from days 3--5 following a 1-day CHIR99021 (CHIR) treatment for WNT activation. Focusing on CHIR concentration as a critical parameter, we found that early WNT inhibition substantially broadened the concentration window yielding [≥]80% differentiation efficiency across distinct hiPSC lines. Extending the analysis to a two-dimensional parameter space incorporating cell density revealed a markedly expanded [≥]80% process window. Temporal analysis of lineage-specific transcription factor expression showed that early WNT inhibition suppressed paraxial mesoderm (PM) specification, likely through MSGN1 suppression, in the range of high initial WNT activation that otherwise favored PM fate, thereby extending the process window. It also suppressed definitive endoderm (DE) specification within the expanded window, promoting a more favorable lateral plate mesoderm/cardiac fate. We further demonstrated substantially reduced variability under parameter perturbations and across wells and batches, accompanied by higher differentiation efficiency, without compromising CM phenotypes. These findings demonstrate early WNT inhibition as an effective strategy for expanding the process window of CM differentiation and improving robustness, while exemplifying the process engineering principle that a broader window can support more robust differentiation, with potential relevance to stem cell--based bioprocesses.

cards.title: Ghrelin Alleviates Aging‐Related Cognitive Impairment by Regulating Autophagy‐Related Signaling via the <scp>SHBG</scp> / <scp>JNK1</scp> /Beclin1 Axis in Microglia
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Cognitive impairment (CI) associated with aging and immunosenescence is linked to metabolic alterations. Microglial senescence and dysregulated autophagy have been implicated as major contributors to this process, but the underlying metabolic regulators remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key metabolic regulators of CI and elucidate their underlying mechanisms. Human cohort analyses, older and D‐galactose (D‐gal)‐induced mouse models, and microglial cell models were integrated to investigate the metabolic regulation of CI. Clinical analyses identified ghrelin as the factor most strongly associated with CI. Older and D‐gal mice exhibited CI, microglial senescence, enhanced inflammation, and elevated ghrelin. Ghrelin treatment improved cognitive function, attenuated microglial senescence, and suppressed inflammation, whereas high‐dose ghrelin induced growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) desensitization. Sex hormone‐binding globulin (SHBG) showed mainly cytoplasmic localization, was identified as a potential mediator of ghrelin signaling in microglia, and its expression was downregulated following ghrelin treatment. Transcriptomic profiling revealed significant enrichment of autophagy‐related pathways in ghrelin‐treated microglia. Ghrelin altered autophagy‐related markers, as indicated by increased Beclin1 and LC3 and decreased p62. SHBG overexpression or JNK1 inhibition attenuated the ghrelin‐induced alterations in autophagy‐related markers and anti‐senescent effects, whereas Beclin1 overexpression partially rescued these inhibitory effects caused by SHBG overexpression. In conclusion, ghrelin alleviated aging‐related CI, with mechanistic evidence indicating that the modulation of microglial autophagy‐related mechanisms through the SHBG/JNK1/Beclin1 axis may contribute to its protective effects, thereby providing a potential therapeutic strategy for aging‐related CI.

cards.title: From Regenerative to Degenerative Niche: Multicellular Crosstalk and Population Dynamics in Skeletal Muscle Aging
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Skeletal muscle aging is increasingly recognized as a failure of tissue‐level coordination rather than a consequence of isolated defects in individual cell types. Recent advances in single‐cell, spatial, and multimodal omics have revealed that aging remodels the abundance, functional states, and interactions of muscle‐resident populations, shifting the tissue from a regenerative niche toward a degenerative niche. In this Review, we summarize current evidence supporting this conceptual transition by focusing on multicellular crosstalk and population dynamics within the aging muscle microenvironment. We discuss how age‐dependent remodeling of muscle stem cells, fibro‐adipogenic progenitors, immune cells, vascular cells, and neuromuscular components collectively disrupts the temporal coordination required for effective regeneration. Rather than acting independently, these populations become locked in maladaptive signaling circuits that promote persistent inflammation, fibrosis, senescence, impaired vascular support, and neuromuscular dysfunction, ultimately compromising tissue repair and muscle function. We further distinguish ligand‐receptor interactions inferred from single‐cell atlases from signaling pathways that have been functionally validated in vivo, highlighting the importance of establishing causal mechanisms underlying intercellular communication. Finally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring multicellular coordination—including modulation of stromal, immune, vascular, and neuromuscular interactions—rather than targeting single cell populations in isolation. We propose that rebuilding regenerative communication networks, instead of simply eliminating dysfunctional cells, represents a promising framework for developing interventions against sarcopenia and age‐related muscle decline.

cards.title: Combined negative effects of simultaneous perturbations on grassland functionality
cards.abstract: 1. Grassland ecosystems are pivotal for global biodiversity, carbon (C) storage and food security. This biome, however, together with the ecosystem services it provides, is threatened by global change perturbations. These perturbations rarely occur in isolation and most often affect environments simultaneously, which is a pressing issue in ecology. Nevertheless, most of the research conducted so far has focussed on single simultaneous perturbations or pairs thereof. The few examples considering the effect of more than two simultaneous perturbations focussed only on plants or soil separately, which ignores the potential buffering or feedback effects on ecosystem functioning induced by plant-soils interactions. 2. To tackle this knowledge gap, we used an experimental setup involving mesocosms (soil and plants intact) collected in an extensively managed permanent grassland. Mesocosms were arranged in a greenhouse experiment where we applied individual and combined global change perturbations (up to ten in total) including application of fertilisers, pesticides and antibiotics, simulated trampling and grazing, heat stress and drought. Measured ecosystem functions and properties included a large set of biological, physical and chemical soil and plant associated variables. 3. Results showed that multiple perturbations in most cases had negative effects irrespective of the direction found for individual perturbations. However, in contrast to previous bare soil experiments, we only found scarce evidence for substantial synergistic effects of simultaneous perturbations in our experiment conducted with mesocosms that contained vegetation. This suggests a mitigating impact of plants on soil responses to global change. Moreover, we found a strong dominative effect of drought on ecosystem functioning, driving most of the effects observed. 4. Synthesis: Our results highlight the importance of evaluating global change impacts under more realistic settings, i.e., applying multiple perturbations simultaneously and including plant-soil interactions. Mitigation of global change in terrestrial ecosystems will only be possible once we holistically understand how ecosystems respond to altered conditions.

cards.title: Interpretable machine learning coupled to gene regulatory networks uncovers subcircuits underlying cell fate decisions
cards.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) model causal linkages that control cell fate decisions and differentiation transitions. Prioritizing regulatory subnetworks underlying cell state differences is of critical importance, but current methods including those reliant on topological metrics introduce circularity as the metrics prioritizing TFs are computed from the same networks whose assumptions they inherit. Separately, interpretable machine learning methods can identify latent factors (LFs) that discriminate cellular states with formal statistical guarantees but do not model regulatory linkages. Here, we present FOCAL (Factor-Outcome Coupling for Assessment of Linkages), a paradigm to prioritize regulatory subnetworks by coupling state-specific and dynamic GRNs with outcome-supervised LFs learned using interpretable machine learning without reference to network topology. This shifts GRN focus from macroscopic TF nodes to state-specific and dynamic TF-gene linkages. In B and T cells, FOCAL identified GIFs (GRNs coupled to Interpretable latent Factors), prioritized regulatory subnetworks underlying established states as well as transient regulatory episodes preceding them. By coupling LFs learnt from perturbation experiments of lineage-defining TFs, FOCAL identified transcriptional predisposition to alternative fates within progenitor cell populations before overt differentiation. This uncovered a novel NFATC2-IRF8 interplay in activated B cells, that was validated by in-vitro and in-vivo genetic perturbations. The two transcription factors act cooperatively to restrain extrafollicular plasmablast differentiation and promote germinal center B cell fate.

cards.title: Association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of long-bone fractures: a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: To assess the association between the metabolic score for insulin resistance and nonunion after surgical treatment of extremity long-bone fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 601 adults who underwent internal fixation for extremity long-bone fractures and completed at least 12 months of follow-up. METS-IR was calculated using pre-operative body mass index, fasting blood glucose, triglycerides and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Potential confounders were selected by LASSO logistic regression with ten-fold cross-validation. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the independent and nonlinear associations between METS-IR and fracture nonunion. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed to examine whether the association was consistent across different clinical subgroups. Of the 601 patients, 139 developed nonunion. METS-IR was higher in patients with nonunion than in those who achieved union (45 ± 5 vs. 36 ± 5, P < 0.001). After adjustment for LASSO-selected covariates, each one-unit increase in METS-IR was associated with higher odds of nonunion (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.24-1.38; P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant overall association and evidence of nonlinearity (P for overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.037). The association was generally consistent across sex, diabetes status, injury mechanism, and reduction method, while an interaction was observed for age (P for interaction = 0.029). Higher METS-IR was independently associated with fracture nonunion and showed a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. METS-IR may provide additional metabolic information for identifying patients at increased risk of impaired fracture healing.

cards.title: Benchmarking LLM-based Information Extraction Tools for Medical Documents
cards.abstract: Background: Medical documents are a crucial resource for medical research around the world. While troves of valuable health data exist, they are largely computationally inaccessible as hard copies of unstructured text. Moreover, the persistent prevalence of fax machines in medical settings contributes to further degradation of document quality. Manual data extraction from these documents is time-consuming and resource intensive. However, large language models (LLMs) have recently shown great promise for automated digitization and information extraction (IE), greatly improving upon previous technologies in terms of accuracy. Objective: Here we aim to survey the landscape of LLM-based IE tools with respect to their applicability to biomedical documents and to systematically benchmark them on synthetic documents with paired reference extractions. We put special focus on locally executable tools and models that suit privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Methods: We reviewed LLM-based IE tools from the literature and assessed them with respect to their suitability for use in biomedical research. We found only one of these tools (NuExtract2) to satisfy our selection criteria and compared it to LLM foundation models prompted to perform extractions. We created 200 mock molecular test reports with paired reference data using a bespoke procedural generation approach and evaluated the tools' performance across different prompting strategies, input modalities, and document qualities. Results: We found model performance to be very sensitive to input modalities and quality. The best overall performance was observed for the proprietary GPT 4.1-mini, with an F1 score of 79.2% averaged across quality levels and modalities. The best performing open-weights model was Mistral-small 3.1 with an average F1 score of 76.2%. The NuExtract2 model was the only one able to run on regular laptop computers, but did not perform well. Surprisingly, we found the choice of one-shot over zero-shot prompts to only have a small effect size on extraction performance in most cases. Conclusions: LLMs place the automatic processing of highly complex medical documents in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings within reach, but still require human oversight. cards.title: CBAM-enhanced MaxViT-Tiny for gastrointestinal endoscopy image classification: Robustness, explainability, and external validation
cards.abstract: Automated classification of the huge number of images generated during gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is required for reliable and interpretable diagnosis, but there is concern about the vulnerability of deep models to adversarial perturbations. In the current study, a MaxViT-Tiny backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) head is used for 8-class classification of the Kvasir endoscopic images. After deleting duplicate images, 3,996 images remained, which were split into a training set (70%), a validation set (15%) and a test set (15%); the model was compared with five backbones using the same CBAM head under three random seeds. The proposed model obtained the highest test accuracy of 94.33%, a macro F1 score of 0.9431, and a macro area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9975, with a mean accuracy of 93.72 {+/-} 1.06% across all seeds. White-box FGSM, PGD, CW-L2, and MI-FGSM attacks greatly reduced the accuracy: after adversarial fine-tuning, the accuracy under FGSM was 74.17%, while the accuracy under PGD and MI-FGSM was below 4%, showing poor cross-attack generalization. A preliminary attack detector obtained an AUC of 0.857. Grad-CAM++, Score-CAM, and GradientSHAP sometimes identified clinically relevant regions, but also sometimes focused on non-anatomical artefacts. High accuracy on clean images, even with attention augmentation, therefore does not imply high accuracy on adversarial images or reliable explanations, and the model needs further verification on independent datasets and multi-centre validation before clinical use.

cards.title: GOLDEN: Gene expression and allele-informed decomposition for genetic heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomic data
cards.abstract: Motivation Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables exploration of cellular interactions, including immune responses. However, current methods rely on pathologists, with limitations in addressing genetic heterogeneity, where niches harboring nonclonal cells, including placental or allograft tissues, are present. Deciphering these interindividual mixtures remains challenging. Results For deciphering interindividual heterogeneity in ST, we developed GOLDEN (Gene expressiOn and aLlele-informed DEcomposition for geNetic heterogeneity), which involves an allele-aware multitask network that encodes spot-level expressions into shared latent representations. Incorporating allele features, dual heads classify spot identity (target, nontarget, or mixed) and estimate target fractions. We utilized synthetic ST data with spot-level ground truth using semiallogeneic single-cell profiles. For these synthetic benchmarks, GOLDEN achieved reliable deconvolution, with high correlation (Pearson's r = 0.977) and low error (mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.045) in fraction estimation and consistent predictions across real-world STs. These predictions were genetically validated. Using GOLDEN, resolving spot-level genetic heterogeneity is feasible. Availability and implementation GOLDEN and the simulation code for ST are available at https://github.com/othertics/GOLDEN.

cards.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement
cards.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics platforms such as Xenium require a predefined gene panel, and the genes in that panel are detected less efficiently, and to gene-specific degrees, in the spatial assay than in the single-cell reference used to choose them. We present X-SPEAR, a framework that couples DART marker selection with probe-level off-target assessment. DART learns short, interpretable Boolean gene rules and assembles several gene-disjoint rules per cell type. Its detection-aware training thins the reference to per-gene detection rates measured in a different, already completed experiment, so no Xenium data from the target tissue are needed before the panel is ordered. On held-out Xenium data from ovarian cancer, mouse brain and cervical cancer, DART substantially outperformed existing marker-selection methods at matched panel size, by 0.04-0.11 macro-F1 over Wilcoxon rank-sum, 0.04-0.08 over COSG and 0.10-0.18 over NS-Forest, and it reached Wilcoxon's best accuracy with 42-69% fewer genes. Ablations show that most of this gain comes from detection-aware training, which also improves other rank-based selectors and requires a detection profile measured with the same assay chemistry. At similar accuracy, DART's rule structure adds rules that faithfully summarise the downstream classifier, robustness to single-probe loss across 45 retinal ganglion cell subtypes, and better resolution of closely related cell states. We are applying X-SPEAR to design a Xenium panel for mouse retinal ganglion cell subtypes, and its in situ evaluation is in progress. X-SPEAR is available as an open-source Python package.

cards.title: Real-Time Neurotransmitter Sensing in Midbrain Organoids Using 3D Carbon Cup Electrodes
cards.abstract: Real time, chemically selective detection of neurotransmitter release in brain organoids remains a challenge due to their complex three dimensional architecture and limited optical accessibility. We introduce 3D printed carbon cup electrodes (CCEs) -pyrolyzed, multi level pillar structures - designed to confine a single organoid, increase electroactive surface area, and enable amperometric recordings of oxidizable neurotransmitters. The CCEs exhibit excellent electrochemical performance and reproducibility, supporting diffusion controlled dopamine redox behavior without interference from culture medium. Using ventral midbrain (vMB) organoids at two maturation stages (Day 30 and Day 90), we demonstrate real time detection of potassium evoked dopamine release directly from organoids. Mature organoids exhibit higher peak currents, correlating with increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression confirmed by immunocytochemistry. Embedding organoids in Matrigel significantly attenuates dopamine signals, indicating a diffusion barrier that limits stimulant access and/or dopamine transport to the electrode. Repetitive stimulations reveal progressive depletion of dopamine stores, consistent with diminished vesicular release. Chemical perturbations using 6 hydroxydopamine and verapamil further validate the platform by producing substantial reductions in dopamine release accompanied by loss of TH neurons. These results establish CCEs as a powerful tool for label free, real-time monitoring of neurotransmission in human organoids, with potential for multiplexed sensing and integration of enzymatic detection strategies for non electroactive neurotransmitters.

cards.title: Glucose-Lowering Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes-Associated Sarcopenia: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence and a Muscle-Centred Framework.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognised as a clinically important comorbidity in diabetes mellitus, particularly in older adults and individuals with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Because skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, declines in muscle mass, quality, strength and physical performance may exacerbate insulin resistance and glycaemic instability and increase the risks of frailty, disability, falls, fractures, cardiovascular events and mortality. Contemporary glucose-lowering therapies have transformed diabetes care through established cardiorenal benefits and weight reduction, yet skeletal muscle outcomes are rarely prespecified or systematically assessed in pivotal trials. This evidence gap is especially relevant for weight-reducing agents such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, which are often associated with reductions in dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived or bioelectrical impedance analysis-derived lean-mass estimates. However, these changes should be interpreted cautiously, as they often occur in the context of overall weight loss and may be influenced by alterations in body water. In addition, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry- or dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived lean-mass estimates do not directly quantify contractile skeletal muscle. Accordingly, reductions in lean-mass estimates alone are insufficient to infer clinically meaningful muscle loss without concurrent assessment of muscle strength or physical performance. This narrative review summarises the bidirectional mechanisms linking diabetes and sarcopenia and appraises major glucose-lowering drug classes from a muscle-centred perspective. It integrates mechanistic insights with human evidence on muscle-relevant outcomes, including body composition, strength and physical performance, and addresses practical safety and monitoring considerations in sarcopenia-prone phenotypes, including sarcopenic obesity. We also propose a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating Cardiorenal-Muscle Quadrant Framework that considers glycaemic efficacy and cardiorenal benefit alongside muscle reserve, functional status and treatment-related risks, with emphasis on functional monitoring, resistance exercise, nutritional optimisation and individualised glycaemic targets in older or frail adults.

cards.title: Rational Design of a Photoactivated Fluorescent Probe for Thiol-ene Mediated Protein Labelling
cards.abstract: Fluorescent labelling of biomolecules enables the visualization and tracking of molecular processes in cells, providing insights into cellular function and disease mechanisms. Despite recent advances in bioorthogonal labelling, efficient and site-selective strategies for targeting alkene functionalities remain limited. Here, we report AbzSH, a compact aminobenzamide-based fluorescent thiol probe for selective alkene labelling through thiol-ene ligation. Photoinduced ligation proceeds under mild, radical-mediated conditions in aqueous media and exhibits broad substrate compatibility, including carbohydrate, amino acid, and steroid scaffolds. The method is readily extended to protein labelling, enabling selective modification of both chemically functionalized proteins and engineered proteins containing genetically encoded alkene motifs. Efficient and chemoselective labelling was further demonstrated in complex cell lysates, highlighting the robustness of the approach in biologically relevant environments. Collectively, these results establish AbzSH as a versatile fluorescent probe for alkene-directed biomolecular labelling and provide a broadly applicable platform for chemical biology, molecular imaging, proteomics, and drug discovery.

cards.title: A hippocampal digital Twin reveals latent structure in freely flying bats
cards.abstract: Concurrent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), large-scale neuronal recording, and behavioral tracking have enabled increasingly powerful predictive models of brain-behavior relationships. Yet predictive accuracy does not automatically yield interpretable principles of neural organization, particularly during natural behavior, where the relevant variables computed are often unknown in advance. Here, we developed a functional digital twin of the hippocampus, trained jointly on large-scale neural activity and self-directed three-dimensional flight in freely flying bats. A multimodal, multitask transformer accurately predicted both neural activity and behavior, outperformed standard approaches, and generalized across recording sessions. Interrogating the model's representations suggested a form of hippocampal generalization across self-selected trajectories that was not apparent in physical coordinates, but was plainly visible in the model's low-dimensional latent space. We confirmed this organization directly in the recorded neural activity: neurons fired at corresponding stages of spatially distinct paths connecting the same origin and destination, preserving their relative firing order even as their firing fields shifted with the path. Analysis of neuron-specific readouts further identified functional relationships among neurons that generalized from flight to waking rest and sleep, brain states never used for training, and differed systematically between the hippocampal subregions CA1 and CA3. Together, these results show how AI-based functional digital twins can complement conventional analysis by generating testable hypotheses about neural organization during natural behavior.

cards.title: Discoidins are cytosolic lectins that recognize methylated L-rhamnose epitopes on mycobacterial glycolipids and glycopeptidolipids upon vacuole damage
cards.abstract: Mycobacteria are surrounded by a dynamic, glycolipid-rich envelope that governs virulence and immune recognition, yet how cytosolic lectins sense its organization during intracellular infection remains unclear. Here, we show that Dictyostelium discoideum discoidins act as cytosolic sensors of mycobacterial envelope exposure. During infection, Mycobacterium marinum damages the limiting vacuolar membrane, triggering recruitment of all canonical isoforms (DscA, DscC, DscD, and DscE) to distinct foci around bacilli. Discoidins are not recruited after sterile endolysosomal damage, indicating that, unlike galectins, they recognize non-self surface-associated bacterial glycans rather than exposed host glycans. DscA and DscE display distinct glycan specificities. Combining transposon mutagenesis, synthetic glycan arrays, biochemical fractionation, and envelope mutants, we identify a restricted set of lipid-associated determinants enriched in methylated L-rhamnose motifs within LOS-, PGL-, and GPL-related structures. Recognition requires the conserved beta-galactoside-binding pocket of the H-type lectin domain, and isoform-specific synthetic disaccharides inhibit binding to intact bacteria. Analyses exclude AG-PG, AM/LAM, alpha-glucan, and TDM as major ligands and identify LOS and GPL-like glycolipids as dominant targets. PDIM/PGL or LOS disruption reduces discoidin binding to intact bacteria, although some ligands remain detectable in envelope extracts, underscoring the importance of accessibility. LOS deficiency also reduces DscA recruitment to intracellular bacilli. Therefore, binding of discoidins to glycan epitopes depends on ligand presence and accessibility, as well as on envelope perturbations and unmasking of specific glycolipids and glycopeptidolipids. These findings reveal pathogen envelope glycans as direct targets of cytosolic lectin surveillance and establish discoidins as probes of mycobacterial envelope remodeling during infection.

cards.title: STRUCTURAL AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS ANALYSIS OF HUMAN β-DEFENSIN 1 VARIANTS REVEALS DISTINCT PERTURBATION SIGNATURES
cards.abstract: Human {beta}-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to investigate the molecular consequences of 93 human-observed hBD-1 missense variants. Evaluation of hBD-1 missense variants across sequence-, structure-, and dynamics-based dimensions reveals variant-specific molecular perturbation signatures that complement conventional and static biophysical predictions. By treating naturally occurring substitutions as a perturbation series across a compact defensin scaffold, this study identifies multiple molecular routes through which sequence variation can remodel an endogenous antimicrobial peptide and prioritizes variants for direct structure-function testing. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for investigating how naturally occurring hBD-1 variation may influence peptide behavior and, ultimately, antimicrobial function.

cards.title: Physical Basis Of pKa Shift For Ionizable Lipids In An LNP-like Environment
cards.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading drug delivery platform for mRNA or other nucleic acid-based therapeutics. LNP platforms are typically composed of ionizable aminolipids, phospholipids, sterols, and lipids tagged with polyethylene glycol. The ionizable aminolipids are typically cationic at low pH, allowing them to encapsulate negatively charged mRNA. The pH at which the ionizable head groups change charge states, the apparent pKa, is crucial to understand the characteristics and formulation of LNP. However, this is difficult to measure as the apparent pKa differs from the pKa of the aminolipids in bulk solution due to the complex chemical and charge environment. In this study, we use molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with alchemical free energy perturbation to calculate the pKa shift as a function of lipid composition, treating LNP-like and vesicle-like environments. Our results show that the pH-dependent structure of the systems affects the trends in pKa shifts in complex ways, driven by factors including surface electrostatics and lipid internalization. Our all-atom simulation protocol allows us to efficiently estimate the apparent pKa of LNP-like models formed with novel ionizable aminolipids and estimate how it will change with composition.

cards.title: Biophysical modeling of excitation/inhibition imbalance in Alzheimer's disease
cards.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves early sensory and perceptual changes that can precede memory decline. We developed a two-layer rate-based neural model of early and higher visual areas with feedforward, feedback, and recurrent connections to examine how excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance shapes visual motion perception in AD. METHODS: Using Motion-Induced Position Shift and Altered Motion Repulsion stimuli, we factorially manipulated excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) subfield power and connectivity to examine their effects on illusion representation across visual layers. RESULTS: Increased E, decreased I, and increased E/I reduced illusion representation, consistent with reduced illusion susceptibility in AD, whereas the converse increased illusion representation, reflecting neurotypical processing. Higher-level layer 2 representations were more resistant to E/I perturbations than lower-level layer 1. Illusion representation was less affected by E/I increases in intra-areal (recurrent) connectivity than in inter-areal (feedforward/feedback) connectivity. DISCUSSION: This mechanistic framework links E/I balance and connectivity to altered visual motion illusion representations in AD and suggests that E/I and connectivity measures may provide probes of early AD neurobiology. The framework may also generalize beyond vision.

cards.title: Electroacupuncture Targeting the NLRP3 Inflammasome in Senescence‑associated Cognitive Impairment: Mechanistic Synthesis and Meta‑analysis of Clinical Randomized Controlled Trials.
cards.abstract: Global population aging leads to a growing clinical demand for interventions against age-related cognitive decline (ARCD), including mild cognitive impairment (MCI, termed senescence-associated cognitive impairment [SACI] in this review)-a prodromal pathological stage preceding Alzheimer's disease (AD) and vascular dementia. Chronic microglia-mediated neuroinflammation, predominantly triggered by excessive NLRP3 inflammasome activation, acts as a key upstream mediator of hippocampal neuronal injury and gradual cognitive decline in preclinical aging models.Manual acupuncture and electroacupuncture (EA) exert reproducible neuroprotective effects against cognitive deficits, yet a comprehensive, multi-layered regulatory framework unifying NLRP3-centered molecular mechanisms of acupuncture remains absent from current literature. This review systematically summarizes NLRP3‑dependent pathological cascades in SACI and outlines four synergistic signaling axes through which acupuncture may modulate excessive NLRP3‑dependent inflammatory responses to potentially alleviate neurotoxic inflammatory injury.Persistent overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome triggers self-amplifying inflammatory feedback cycles in hippocampal tissue through four interrelated pathological processes: impaired autophagic clearance, disrupted mitochondrial homeostasis, persistent endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis.Acupuncture counteracts NLRP3-dependent neural injury through synergistic multi-target modulation: (1) activation of AMPK/mTOR signaling to restore defective autophagy; (2) suppression of the ROS-TXNIP cascade to block NLRP3 transcriptional priming and protein oligomerization; (3) phenotypic reprogramming of microglia from pro-inflammatory M1 toward anti-inflammatory M2 states; (4) inhibition of pyroptotic execution by blunting caspase-1 maturation and GSDMD proteolytic cleavage. Collectively, available pre‑clinical evidence suggests these signaling axes constitute a bidirectionally‑interconnected hypothetical protective network that may mitigate chronic neuroinflammation.A meta analysis integrating nine eligible randomized controlled trials (published 2015-2025) involving 614 participants was performed. After subject dropout, 599 participants completed the studies. Pooled analyses of heterogeneous acupuncture/electroacupuncture RCTs revealed that intervention was associated with short‑term improvements in MoCA and MMSE scores and reduction in peripheral pro‑inflammatory cytokine IL‑6. Pooled effect sizes were moderately larger in MCI subgroups compared with patients with early AD. Nevertheless, substantial methodological heterogeneity existed across included trials, and these short term observational findings cannot confirm durable disease modifying benefits.Severe methodological heterogeneity across existing trials-including inconsistent acupoint prescriptions, divergent EA stimulation parameters, and variable treatment cycles-impairs cross-study comparability and translational reproducibility. Herein, we synthesize high‑quality preclinical and clinical evidence to propose a provisional consensus‑oriented translational reference protocol for electroacupuncture, intended for standardized mechanistic research rather than routine clinical intervention.Collectively, the NLRP3 inflammasome constitutes a tractable therapeutic target for acupuncture-mediated SACI intervention. Acupuncture exerts pleiotropic neuroprotection by dampening NLRP3-dependent neuroinflammation, alongside complementary NLRP3-independent regulatory pathways. This review‑meta‑analysis provides preliminary translational theoretical evidence for a provisional electroacupuncture intervention framework targeting NLRP3‑mediated neuroinflammation in MCI and early‑AD. Future high‑quality, multi‑center RCTs are warranted to validate these preliminary findings.

cards.title: CONSTITUTIVE STIM1L DELETION ALTERS STORE-OPERATED CALCIUM ENTRY KINETICS BUT DOES NOT PERTURB THE DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION OF MOUSE SKELETAL MUSCLE
cards.abstract: Store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) is a ubiquitous calcium (Ca2+) signalling mechanism that replenishes endoplasmic and sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ stores. We previously identified STIM1L, a skeletal muscle-enriched STIM1 splice variant that enables rapid SOCE activation in human myotubes. To determine its physiological role in vivo, we generated a constitutive knockout mouse model that selectively abolishes STIM1L expression while preserving the canonical STIM1 isoform. Stim1l-KO mice developed normally and exhibited no overt abnormalities, but both sexes showed reduced voluntary wheel-running activity, suggesting neuromuscular perturbation. Skeletal muscle deprived of STIM1L did not show any histological alterations or changes in fibre- type and size. Likewise, force-frequency relationships and fatigue resistance measured ex vivo in isolated extensor digitorum longus and soleus muscles were indistinguishable from control muscles. This lack of difference may be explained by the increased expression of STIM1 in several skeletal muscles and suggests that changes in the voluntary running activity of Stim1l-KO mice may arise from STIM1L loss in non-muscular tissues, including the central nervous system. Notwithstanding, primary myotubes derived from Stim1l-KO mice displayed a marked delay in SOCE activation kinetics, whereas SOCE amplitude remained comparable to controls. This was consistent with a compensatory STIM1 upregulation maintaining overall Ca2+ entry capacity. Interestingly, electrically evoked Ca2+ transients in intact Stim1l-KO flexor digitorum brevis fibres exhibited significantly faster decay kinetics than controls. This revealed another role of STIM1L in Ca2+ handling in skeletal muscle that appears independent of its contribution to SOCE activation. Together, these findings establish STIM1L as a regulator of SOCE activation kinetics and indicate an additional role in myofibre Ca2+ clearance, while suggesting that compensatory upregulation of canonical STIM1 may preserve muscle structure and contractile function in its absence in mice.

cards.title: Time-resolved proteomic analysis of hepatitis B virus infection
cards.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its impact on host proteome dynamics during early infection remains poorly defined. Here, we performed time-resolved label-free quantitative (LFQ) proteomics to characterise the host response to HBV infection in human HepG2 hepatoma cells. Across five time points spanning the first three weeks of infection, we quantified 5,365 unique proteins, including two HBV proteins (C/preC-derived and S), revealing subtle yet coordinated changes in the hepatocellular proteome. Early infection was characterised by selective alterations in cytoskeletal organisation, extracellular matrix components, and focal adhesion pathways, alongside enrichment of complement-associated proteins. Notably, we identified a transient, specific increase in the abundance of complement component C5 without a corresponding change in C3, indicating differential regulation of complement pathway members during infection. These findings define a temporally resolved proteomic landscape of HBV host interactions and uncover previously underappreciated complement dynamics consistent with a selective and restrained host response. Together, this provides a framework for mechanistic studies of early viral infection and host adaptation.

cards.title: Impact of bisphosphonate drug holidays on bone mineral density and osteoporotic fracture risk: real-world evidence from a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Bisphosphonate drug holidays can reduce rare adverse effects, but their skeletal impact is unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, ALN holiday caused modest BMD loss and BTMs rise without increased fracture risk; effects of ZOL holiday were minimal. This study suggests bisphosphonate drug holidays are safe for selected patients with regular monitoring. Bisphosphonate (BP) drug holiday prevents rare adverse effects of BPs in osteoporotic patients, but its effect on bone mineral density (BMD), bone turnover markers (BTMs), and fracture risk is still unclear. This study aimed to investigate BMD/BTM variations and clinical fracture risk for patients undergoing BP drug holidays. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, patients who received ≥4.5 years of alendronate (ALN) or ≥3 doses of zoledronate (ZOL) were included. BMD at the lumbar spine (LS), femoral neck (FN), and total hip (TH), BTMs, and 3-year fracture incidence were assessed between drug holiday (ALN: n = 71; ZOL: n = 20) and ongoing treatment groups (ALN: n = 59; ZOL: n = 47). Compared with ongoing ALN therapy, initiating drug holiday resulted in moderate declines in BMD at LS (-2.23%, 95% CI: -3.70% to -0.76%), TH (-1.62%, 95% CI: -2.68% to -0.56%), and FN (-1.89%, 95% CI: -3.49% to -0.28%) within 1 year. BTMs all rose significantly over 1 year, yet remained below pretreatment levels for at least 3 years. In contrast, there were no significant differences in BMD (1-year LS: -0.47%, 95% CI: -2.38% to 1.43%, TH: -1.07%, 95% CI: -2.77% to 0.64%) and BTM changes between ZOL groups at 1- and 2-year follow-up. No significant differences in clinical fragility fractures were observed between ALN groups (9.9% vs. 6.8%; HR 1.45) and ZOL groups (5% vs. 6.4%). Our findings support that BP drug holidays are feasible for selected patients with adequate BMD. ZOL conferred more sustained skeletal protection than ALN, particularly at the LS, whereas ALN discontinuation was associated with earlier and more pronounced BMD decline and BTM elevation; annual monitoring of BMD and BTMs appears particularly important during the ALN drug holiday period.

cards.title: Early-onset spontaneous murine mammary tumors show increased lymphocyte representation and reduced MHC antigen presentation
cards.abstract: Simple Summary Not all breast tumors behave the same way, and part of the reason may be inherited rather than caused by the tumor itself. Using mice that carry the same cancer-causing HER2/neu gene but differ in genetic background, we found that introduction of the PWK/PhJ genetic background was associated with tumors that appeared about a month earlier. These early tumors contained a larger proportion of immune cells, including T and B cells, but the T-cell population showed reduced expression of genes associated with cytotoxic activity. At the same time, the tumors had lower levels of proteins and genes that let the immune system recognize tumor cells, alongside higher levels of structural proteins that can make tissue stiffer and easier for cancer to invade. These findings suggest that genetic background shapes not only how quickly breast tumors arise but also how well the immune system can recognize them, a distinction that may matter for future immune-based treatments. Background/Objectives: Genetic background modifies cancer risk and phenotype in humans, but its influence on the tumor immune microenvironment and antigen-presentation machinery in ErbB2 (HER2/neu)-driven breast cancer is not well defined. We used a genetically diverse mouse cross to test whether the wild-derived PWK/PhJ background alters immune representation and antigen presentation in a NeuT model of HER2/neu-positive breast cancer. Methods: Previously, quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping using Diversity Outbred mice and r/qtl2 identified candidate loci driving tumor onset and growth. The wild-derived PWK/PhJ genetic background was predicted to harbor genes that regulated early onset of HER2/neu-driven tumors. BALB NeuT and (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT female mice were monitored twice weekly for spontaneous mammary tumor onset and growth. Tumor immune composition was profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Protein abundance was measured by data-independent acquisition proteomics in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumor tissue (n=5 per genotype). Single-nucleus multiome (RNA + ATAC), bulk RNA-seq, and H3K27ac datasets from the same strain comparison were analyzed for focused MHC II cross-layer analyses. Results: As predicted, (BALBxPWK) F1 NeuT mice developed tumors significantly earlier than the parental BALB NeuT mice (10 vs. 15 weeks of age; p < 0.0001). In the scRNA-seq dataset, F1 tumors showed greater representation of Cd3e-expressing T cells and a Cd79a-expressing B-cell population not detected in BALB NeuT tumors, and a distinct neutrophil cluster; F1 T cells also showed lower expression of the cytotoxicity-associated genes Tox, Ltk, Nkg7, and Gzmb relative to BALB NeuT tumor-infiltrating T cells. Proteomics identified 46 differentially abundant proteins (25 higher, 21 lower in F1), with coordinate down-regulation of Stat1, Tapbp, Parp9, and Dtx3l alongside MHC class I and II proteins and up-regulation of extracellular-matrix and elastic-fiber proteins. Focused cross-layer analysis showed lower whole-tumor expression of a Stat1/MHC II-associated gene set together with reduced epithelial chromatin accessibility at selected regions near Cd74 and H2-Aa. Conclusions: The PWK/PhJ genetic background is associated with earlier HER2-driven tumor onset, greater lymphocyte proportion, and reduced activity of a STAT1-associated antigen-presentation program despite similar post-onset tumor growth kinetics.

cards.title: Informing risk stratification and vaccine policy via a predictive mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection
cards.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 human challenge studies enabled unprecedented high frequency temporal measurements of immune determinants of viral control. We integrated prior knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 replication, innate, cytotoxic T cell and antibody responses into a dynamic model which captured viral-load kinetics in seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype virus. The model predicted measured innate and adaptive immune dynamics. Perturbation analyses indicated that innate immunity limits peak viral load, whereas antibodies principally mediate clearance while cytotoxic T cells become critical in antibody deficiency. Pre-existing antibodies suppressed both viral replication and subsequent immune activation- a prediction validated in a second challenge study of seropositive participants infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The model explains how specific immunodeficiencies may increase susceptibility to severe or persistent infection, supporting clinical risk stratification. It suggests that T cell-targeted vaccination strategies may provide limited protection without effective neutralising antibodies, and that attenuated boosting after low-dose exposure requires repeated vaccination to reduce breakthrough infections, informing public health policy.

cards.title: The essential role of connective-tissue cells during axolotl limb regeneration
cards.abstract: Axolotls (Ambystoma mexicanum) are known for their remarkable limb-regeneration abilities, which involve the formation of the blastema, a specialized structure consisting of progenitor cells contributed by all major tissues of the limb. Lateral plate mesoderm (LPM)-derived connective tissue (CT) cells dedifferentiate and play a critical role in blastema formation and subsequent limb regeneration. However, the complexity of the blastema cellular composition and the extent of CT participation and necessity have not been rigorously explored. To address this gap, we conducted spatial transcriptomics using a select array of probes, revealing that CT cells constitute up to 75% of the blastema cells. Genetic ablation of CT cells significantly delays or truncates limb regeneration, underscoring their necessity during this process. Analysis of the molecular profile during blastema formation identifies a temporally ordered gene expression pattern reflecting sequential phases of CT cell dedifferentiation, proliferation, and redifferentiation. Finally, a cell-cell communication inference identifies a CT-cell-autonomous FGFR1/AKT1 signaling axis as a cell-intrinsic molecular requirement for limb regeneration. Together, our work reaffirms the central role of CT cells in axolotl limb regeneration and lays the foundation for identifying molecular mechanisms that govern blastema formation during the initial phases of limb regeneration.

cards.title: Histology-aware Inference of Cell-cell Communication in Spatial Transcriptomics
cards.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is fundamental to tissue organization and function, yet inferring communication from spatial transcriptomics (ST) remains challenging because molecular and spatial information does not fully capture the anatomical context of signaling. Paired hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained images provide complementary insights into tissue architecture and cellular morphology, which remain underutilized as the explicit contextual constraint of CCC inference. Here we present HARMONIC, a histology-aware graph learning framework for anatomically contextualized CCC inference from ST and H&E images. HARMONIC uses conditional mutual information to model dependencies among tissue architecture, ligand-receptor-mediated signaling, gene expression and morphology, and integrates these representations through self-supervised graph learning. Across synthetic and biological datasets spanning platforms, species and tissues, HARMONIC suppresses less anatomically plausible interactions while recovering context-supported signaling across tumor-immune interfaces, necrotic transitions, anatomical compartments and microvascular structures. These findings establish tissue architecture as the explicit contextual constraint of spatial CCC inference.

cards.title: Single Cell Proteomics reveals partial uncoupling of the Glycerol-3-Phosphate shuttle to compensate for Electron Transport Chain dysfunction in Alexander Disease GFAP mutations
cards.abstract: Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare genetic leukodystrophy caused by dominant mutations in the gene coding for the astrocytic intermediate filament protein Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP). Understanding disease mechanisms is complicated by the fact that mutant GFAP promotes further GFAP accumulation, making it difficult to distinguish mutation-specific effects from those caused by elevated GFAP levels. Here, we performed mass spectrometry-based single cell proteomics to investigate proteomic alterations associated with increasing levels of wildtype GFAP and a common AxD-causing mutant GFAP R239C. By analyzing individual cells spanning a broad range of GFAP expression levels, we separated dosage-dependent effects from mutation-specific responses. Cells expressing high levels of wildtype GFAP increasingly resembled R239C-expressing cells at the proteomic level, supporting a role for GFAP accumulation in disease pathogenesis. In contrast, mutant GFAP specifically correlated with increased mitochondrial antioxidant enzymes and remodeling of the proteasome tailored toward ATP- and ubiquitin-independent degradation of oxidized proteins. Integration with proteomics data from patient-derived cortical organoids revealed increased abundance of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins and respiratory chain assembly factors without corresponding changes in mitochondrially encoded proteins, suggesting impaired electron transport chain (ETC) assembly. Consistent with this, AxD cells displayed reduced oxygen consumption, increased glycolytic activity, enhanced utilization of the cytosolic part of the glycerol-3-phosphate (G3P) shuttle, and accumulation of triacylglycerides and lipid droplets. We propose that ETC dysfunction promotes partial uncoupling of the G3P shuttle, allowing sustained regeneration of cytosolic NAD to support glycolysis while diverting G3P toward lipid synthesis and storage. By regenerating NAD through the G3P shuttle rather than lactate fermentation, AxD astrocytes may sustain glycolytic flux while preserving lactate production, an important metabolic substrate for neighboring neurons. Together, our findings identify ETC dysfunction as a central feature of AxD and suggest that metabolic adaptation through the G3P shuttle links mitochondrial dysfunction to glycolytic reprogramming and lipid accumulation. More broadly, these results provide new insight into how astrocyte dysfunction drives molecular pathways implicated in neurodegeneration.

cards.title: A latent space thermodynamic model of cell differentiation
cards.abstract: Inferring the governing dynamics of differentiation that capture cell state evolution remains a central challenge in single-cell biology. We present Single-Cell Latent Space Dynamics (scLSD), a thermodynamics-inspired framework that models cell differentiation as evolution on a learned Waddington landscape in latent space. scLSD jointly infers a low-dimensional cell state, a differentiable potential function governing developmental flow, and a local entropy term that associates with cellular plasticity. Using a neural ordinary differential equation, scLSD reconstructs continuous differentiation trajectories from time-ordered single-cell data. Across diverse developmental systems, scLSD accurately recovers lineage hierarchies, predicts fate commitment for unseen cell types, and outperforms existing trajectory inference approaches in directional and cell fate prediction accuracy. In silico gene perturbations reveal how individual regulators reshape the landscape, and the proposed entropy measure is informative of plasticity in development and cancer.

cards.title: The Sensitivity of 13C-Metabolic Flux Analysis to Biomass Composition Underscores the Need for Accurate Biomass Formulation in Escherichia coli
cards.abstract: Quantifying intracellular fluxes through 13C-metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA) provides a detailed view of cellular metabolism. While model formulation, including biomass synthesis reactions, is known to influence flux estimations, the degree to which biomass composition affects 13C-MFA outcomes in Escherichia coli remains debated. Here, we reconstructed a genome-scale 13C-MFA model of E. coli incorporating explicit nucleotide biosynthesis and a modular biomass formulation that separates protein, RNA, and other components. Using isotopic labeling experiments and systematic perturbations of biomass composition, we demonstrate that 13C-MFA can robustly differentiate subtle shifts in the protein/RNA ratio, with deviations as small as 2-3% producing statistically significant but biologically interpretable changes in model fit. Reaction-level analyses revealed consistent flux adjustments across amino acid and nucleotide biosynthesis, while pathways in one-carbon metabolism, particularly serine, glycine, and threonine interconversions, exhibited the strongest responses. Collectively, these results highlight the robustness and discriminative power of 13C-MFA and also demonstrate the importance of accurate biomass composition measurement in E. coli 13C-MFA, given the intrinsic sensitivity of the method to macromolecular stoichiometry.

cards.title: Inferring structural complexity from dynamical measures
cards.abstract: Complexity, commonly defined as the coexistence of integration and differentiation, is a fundamental property of thalamocortical networks and is regarded as a prerequisite for adaptive brain function and consciousness. A variety of metrics have been developed to estimate neural complexity from recorded activity and are increasingly employed in both research and clinical settings. Yet, the extent to which these measures reflect specific architectural features of the underlying circuits remains poorly understood. Here, we used Wilson-Cowan mean-field equations to simulate neural dynamics across networks spanning a broad range of architectures. By systematically rewiring connectivity, we generated graded variations in the structural integration-differentiation balance and assessed a panel of complexity measures derived either from spontaneous activity (observational metrics) or from responses to external perturbations (perturbational metrics). Observational measures exhibited markedly heterogeneous behavior: some were primarily sensitive to network integration, others to differentiation, whereas some showed limited sensitivity to architectural manipulations. In contrast, perturbational measures robustly peaked at intermediate rewiring steps and scaled with small-worldness, consistent with architectures that combine local recurrence and distributed communication. Moreover, perturbational metrics proved robust to common-driver confounds and were highest in a wake-like regime near critical instability, declining as sleep-like dynamics became more widespread across the network. Taken together, these findings map widely used empirical complexity measures onto specific network architectures, reveal dynamical factors that can bias observational estimates, and provide guidance for inferring complexity in systems whose internal organization is inaccessible, unconventional, or only partially known, including brain organoids, non-human nervous systems, and synthetic neural networks.

cards.title: muDM: A Queryable Multi-Resolution Data Model for Vector Geometry in Spatial Bioimaging
cards.abstract: Spatial bioimaging combines raster imagery with vector geometries that encode molecular measurements, connectivity, and anatomical labels. A major challenge is to connect and jointly query these resources at scale, because the vector structures that locate them cannot be searched across resolutions. muDM is a spatial data model for associating vector geometry with its annotated records. Under a single schema, it arranges 2D and 3D geometries, together with their identities and measurements, as a precomputed multi-resolution pyramid, a columnar store that can be queried in place from object storage and equivalent render-ready tiles from the same index. Deployed in a public catalog containing more than 100 datasets, this single model supports connectome meshes, multiplexed tissue imaging, and spatial transcriptomics. For neuron meshes, classifiers which use geometry together with linked synapse counts exceed the performance of geometry-only models, while coarser levels preserved most balanced accuracy and using up to two orders of magnitude less stored geometry.

cards.title: Quantitative fluorescence lifetime imaging of protein microenvironments by genetically encoded compact benzodiazole probes
cards.abstract: Quantitative fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) is limited by a lack of probes that combine single-residue specificity, minimal steric perturbation, visible-light excitation, and strong environment-dependent lifetime contrast. We introduce benzodiazole-based non-canonical amino acids (BD-ncAAs) as compact, genetically encoded sensors for site-specific FLIM. Using an engineered pyrrolysyl-tRNA synthetase pair, we incorporate three different BD-ncAAs into proteins in living cells. Site-specific incorporation of BD-ncAAs into a nanobody at different positions preserved native structure and antigen binding. The lead probe, cyano-substituted CBDS, exhibits visible-light excitation, large Stokes shifts, and pronounced environment-dependent fluorescence lifetimes spanning 1 to 24 ns. Under wash-free, live-cell FLIM conditions, CBDS quantitatively resolves localized structural microenvironments and transmembrane hydration gradients, while also distinguishing distinct states during protein secretion in eukaryotes. BD-ncAAs present genetically encoded, minimally perturbing reporters for tracking target proteins, detecting interactions with binding partners, and quantifying site-specific solvent accessibility in living cells by quantitative FLIM.

cards.title: Genetic circuit rewiring underlies a lineage-specific patterning machinery on butterfly wings
cards.abstract: Phenotypes evolve through changes in gene regulatory networks (GRNs), but how changes in network topology contribute to phenotypic evolution is still poorly understood. Butterfly wing color patterns provide a tractable system to answer this question. Here, we compared the expression of four color pattern genes, WntA, pdm3, ivory, and Optix, in five nymphalid butterflies, and tested their regulatory connections through genetic perturbations in three species spanning 80 million years of divergence. We found broadly conserved 1) regulatory hierarchy linking early pattern instruction via WntA signaling to subsequent color readout via ivory and Optix, 2) positive autoregulation in WntA signaling, and 3) positive regulation from WntA signaling to pdm3. Notably, we discovered lineage-specific negative feedback from pdm3 to WntA signaling in Vanessa cardui, which closes a reciprocal WntA-pdm3 feedback loop that refines complex pattern elements. We show that developmental programs can evolve by rewiring internal interactions among pre-existing GRN nodes, emphasizing the importance of network topology in phenotypic evolution.

cards.title: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
cards.abstract: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. Methods: An ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. Results: Internal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. Conclusions: FM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

cards.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Fusion Models to Predict Response to Venetoclax and Azacitidine in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukemia
cards.abstract: Venetoclax and azacitidine (ven-aza) is a standard of care therapy for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients unfit to receive intensive therapy, and may also be appropriate for certain fit patients. Models predicting response to ven-aza currently focus predominantly on genetics. Here, we present two multimodal fusion models: a custom ResNet-34-based model and a pathology foundation model fine-tuned for bone marrow smear (BMS) images that combine clinical and genetic variables with whole slide images. Training on 193 newly diagnosed AML patients who received ven-aza, we obtained an area-under-the-receiver-operating-characteristic (AUROC) of 0.79 and 0.82 for the ResNet-based and fine-tuned foundation models in a heldout test set, and 0.76 and 0.73 in an external validation set, predicting best response to this therapy. Sensitivity analysis showed that fusing image data with clinical and genetic variables outperformed training on either modality alone. In univariable and multivariable analyses, image-based classification was an independent predictive marker, second only in effect size to IDH1/2 mutation status, outperforming other genetic alterations. Image-based explainability showed high model attention on myeloblasts, suggesting previously unrecognized cell-specific patterns associated with response. Our findings suggest BMS images complement genetic biomarkers to refine outcome prediction in ven-aza treatment and incentivize AI-supported outcome prediction, including bone marrow morphology.
