cards.title: Identifiability of metabolic resilience from sparse longitudinal metabolomics
cards.abstract: Sparse and irregular longitudinal metabolomic measurements can make dynamical quantities numerically estimable without making them scientifically identifiable. We formulate effective-landscape inference as an observation-timescale inverse problem and evaluate its operating characteristics using stochastic systems with known ground truth and longitudinal stool metabolomics from the Integrative Human Microbiome Project. Across simulation ensembles, recovery of a known double-well topology declined sharply as observations became sparse, whereas the tested monostable controls did not generate spurious secondary minima. Findings establish an identifiability hierarchy: global topology requires sufficient within-subject state-space coverage, whereas local return descriptors remain vulnerable to bias from the observation process. The framework therefore shifts the emphasis from assigning stability labels to determining what a sampling design can support. It provides a basis for designing denser longitudinal experiments and for validating clinical and machine-learning studies in which sparse observations might otherwise be overinterpreted as evidence about underlying dynamics.

cards.title: Mesodermal-niche interactions direct specification and differentiation of pancreatic endocrine cells in human multilineage organoids
cards.abstract: Tissues develop and function within complex microenvironments, where diverse cell types interact through tightly regulated spatial and temporal cues. These interactions shape cell identity, differentiation, and spatial organisation, ultimately establishing functional tissue architecture. Understanding and modelling these processes in humans therefore require multicellular systems that capture the cellular diversity and interactions of developing tissues. Here, we combine spatial transcriptomics of the human foetal pancreas with an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-based multilineage model that recapitulates key features of human endocrine pancreatic development and incorporates a mesoderm-derived cellular niche. We comprehensively characterise the multilineage organoid transcriptomes across differentiation stages and benchmark their fidelity against single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles of human foetal pancreas. We demonstrate that iPSC-derived pancreatic mesenchymal cells promote endocrine commitment by restricting off-target cell fates and enhancing {beta}-cell differentiation. Together, these findings establish a framework for investigating the cellular mechanisms underlying human endocrine development and disease.

cards.title: Cause-excluded Effect Evaluation: a framework for the faithful assessment of genetic perturbation target identification
cards.abstract: Identifying which gene drives a desired cell-state transition is a foundational inverse problem in target discovery and cell-state engineering, yet far less developed than forward prediction. We show that prevailing benchmarks inflate performance through two artefacts: training leakage, where test-perturbation cells are seen during fitting, and evaluation leakage, where the perturbed gene's own expression change exposes the answer. Here, we introduce Cause-excluded Effect Evaluation (CEE), a framework that separates train and test perturbation targets, removes target-gene self-effects from expression profiles and scores candidates in downstream response space. With CEE, we find that simple structure-based methods consistently outperform complex deep learning models across 16 single-cell perturbation datasets, revealing that the recoverable signal is governed by low-rank and additive structure in perturbation responses rather than by model complexity. Our work disentangles evaluation artefacts from genuine predictive capacity and offers a design principle for developing perturbation target identification methods.

cards.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics of inherited retinal degeneration reveals broad and focal organization of disease responses
cards.abstract: Inherited retinal degenerations are largely monogenic disorders characterized by progressive photoreceptor dysfunction and death. Although the transcriptomic responses to inherited degeneration are well-characterized, how these responses are spatially organized across the retinal axis has not been mapped. Here, we used seqFISH to spatially profile 173 cell identity and degeneration-associated genes with single-cell, single-transcript resolution in male wild-type and LCA5gt/gtmouse retinas at early, intermediate, and advanced disease stages. In early disease, rod injury and stress response markers were enriched in the superior retina, while rod function and identity markers were enriched in the inferior retina. Nested within the broader superior-inferior organization, a coordinated rod injury response comprising Edn2, Fgf2, Socs3, and Stat3 was organized into focal regions on the order of 100 m in width, with high-response regions directly adjacent to low-response regions. These focal regions were locally enriched for markers of Muller reactive gliosis and rod stress responses. Our single-cell spatiotemporal map reveals that transcriptional responses to degeneration vary at both the broad and focal scales, and offers a framework for investigating how local tissue properties and interactions among neighboring cells may contribute to disease progression.

cards.title: Matched primary-metastasis single-nucleus and spatial profiling of leiomyosarcoma identifies antigen-presenting fibroblasts at the tumor-organ interface
cards.abstract: Leiomyosarcoma is an aggressive soft tissue sarcoma that metastasizes preferentially to lung and liver. Because matched primary and metastatic specimens are rarely available, the cellular changes that accompany metastatic progression remain poorly defined. Here we combined single-nucleus RNA sequencing of archival FFPE tissue from four matched primary-metastasis pairs (two lung, two liver metastases; 48,941 nuclei) with imaging-based spatial transcriptomics of an extended tissue microarray cohort of 21 patients (69 cores, 313,218 cells). Malignant cells, not assignable from transcriptomic references alone, were defined by inferred copy number profiles that were concordant with matched DNA methylation arrays and confirmed the clonal origin of each metastasis. Malignant metaprograms were organ-associated, with a stress- and hypoxia-associated program enriched in lung metastases and a proliferative, matrix-remodeling program enriched in liver metastases. Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs) were enriched in metastases relative to matched primaries. This shift was reproduced in the spatial cohort (p = 0.001), where apCAFs formed a discrete band at the tumor-organ interface between malignant cells and adjacent parenchyma, whereas they were sparse and randomly distributed in primary tumors. Spatial transcriptomics further resolved the malignant compartment into three histomolecular phenotypes: (i) smooth-muscle-like with myxoid features, (ii) GPNMB with anaplastic features, and (iii) PDGFRB with vessel-rich stroma, each with a concordant immunohistochemical (-SMA, GPNMB, PDGFRB) and morphological correlate. Together, our data provide a matched primary-metastasis reference for leiomyosarcoma, identify apCAFs as a spatially organized, metastasis-associated stromal population, and delineate histomolecular phenotypes recognizable by routine immunohistochemistry, including a GPNMB phenotype potentially amenable to GPNMB-directed therapies.

cards.title: Fluorescent proteins misreport ribosome abundance under translation inhibition
cards.abstract: Fluorescent proteins are widely used as quantitative reporters of protein abundance in living cells. Here we show that this relationship can break down under translation inhibition: the cellular ribosomal abundance can increase while fluorescence intensity remains unchanged or even decreases. Using fluorescent reporters of ribosome abundance in Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis, we find that cellular fluorescence intensity quantitatively tracks ribosome abundance, inferred by RNA-to-protein ratio, under nutrient-limited growth but that is no longer true during chloramphenicol treatment. In E. coli, the discrepancy occurs with transcriptional and translational reporters and with both ribosomal protein and ribosomal RNA promoters. To distinguish changes in fluorescence output per reporter from changes in reporter abundance, we constructed a fluorescent protein-LacZ dual reporter in which fluorescence and an independent enzymatic estimate of reporter abundance are obtained from the same protein. Under translation inhibition, LacZ-derived reporter abundance increases whereas fluorescence intensity remains approximately constant, showing that fluorescence output per unit reporter abundance decreases. In a companion study, Bakshi and colleagues demonstrate that the effect extends to other fluorescent proteins and other translation inhibitors, indicating that it is not specific to a particular fluorescent protein or translation inhibitor. Our results show that fluorescent-protein calibration can be condition-dependent and cannot be assumed to transfer across physiological perturbations.

cards.title: Benchmarking niche identification via domain segmentation for spatial transcriptomics data
cards.abstract: Tissue niches are spatially organized microenvironments in which coordinated multicellular interactions shape cellular states and biological functions. Currently, niche identification is routinely performed using domain segmentation frameworks. While interrelated, spatial domains and niches are not fundamentally equivalent. The former emphasizes intra-domain compositional consistency and transcriptomic homogeneity, whereas the latter is defined by the emergent properties of localized signaling gradients and the functional reciprocity between key cell lineages. Here, we present a high-resolution reference by thoroughly annotating single-cell resolution CosMx ST data of a human follicular lymphoid hyperplasia lymph node, a dynamic, non-compartmentalized tissue containing several critical immune niches defined by specific lineage architectures. We systematically benchmarked 16 contemporary domain segmentation algorithms, demonstrating that most methods in their default configurations fail to recapitulate biologically defined niche boundaries. Our analysis reveals that the definitive, disjoint spatial distributions of key functional lineages are frequently obscured by the stochastic infiltration of peripheral cell types. Such reduction in the spatial signal-to-noise ratio represents a primary bottleneck for existing algorithms, which prioritize local transcriptomic variance over global architectural logic. Following this observation, we demonstrate that strategic weighting of core functional lineages can restore the resolution of spatial niches in select domain segmentation frameworks. Cross-comparison against compartmentalized tissues further underscores the unique challenges of niche identification in non-mechanically separated environments and clarifies the fundamental divergence between structural domain segmentation and functional niche discovery. Our work delineates the limitations of current paradigms and advocates for the development of specialized computational approaches tailored specifically to the complexity of functional microenvironments.

cards.title: Safety-Relevant Biomedical Machine Learning Should Adopt Stability-First Reporting
cards.abstract: Biomedical Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly evaluated through Independent and Identically Distributed (IID) benchmarks, even when deployment involves irregular observation, missingness, distribution shift, and high failure costs. This position paper argues for a stability-oriented reporting standard for safety-relevant biomedical ML. The central requirement is not a specific model class or optimizer, but auditable evidence: performance should be reported under clinically plausible perturbations such as thinning, timestamp jitter, bursty missingness, channel dropout, and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) shift. When authors invoke training-stability diagnostics, those diagnostics should be hazard-linked: their assumptions, operational meaning, and relationship to stress-test degradation should be stated explicitly. We use controlled mechanism probes to illustrate two hazards that IID scores can hide: observation-process dependence under irregular sampling, and perturbation sensitivity associated with high-curvature training regimes such as Edge of Stability (EoS). We do not propose Neural ODEs, continuous-time models, Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), or EoS metrics as default prescriptions. Instead, we propose a minimum reporting standard that makes robustness claims testable and supports escalation to more complex modelling or optimization only when stress tests justify the cost.

cards.title: Distinct Multimodal Brain Profiles Bridging Age of First Alcohol Use and Subsequent Substance Use in Young Adults
cards.abstract: Age of first alcohol use is associated with alterations in brain development and an increased risk of problematic substance use later in life. However, it remains unclear if neurobiological alterations associated with first-use age are present in young adulthood and how these alterations may be associated with different patterns of adult substance use. In this study, we employed SuperBigFLICA, a semi-supervised multimodal imaging data fusion approach, to identify joint structural morphometric and functional MRI (fMRI) brain profiles present in adulthood that are most predictive of age of alcohol first-use in the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult cohort (n=622). Our model achieved moderate performance (r=0.22 in external validation), identifying multimodal structure-function profiles predictive of first-use largely involving frontal regions. We then utilized Canonical Correlation Analysis to determine whether these multimodal brain profiles were differentially linked to patterns of adult substance use behaviors. We identified three significant brain modes (Mode 1: r = 0.2750, p = 0.014; Mode 2: r = 0.2249, p = 0.005; Mode 3: r = 0.1568, p = 0.029) associated with distinct profiles of alcohol and cannabis use. Together, we identified multimodal brain patterns in young adults that predict age of first use of alcohol and demonstrated that resulting multimodal structure-function brain profiles capture distinct multivariate patterns of adult substance use, providing a more integrated view of substance use neurobiology.

cards.title: Ghrelin Alleviates Aging-Related Cognitive Impairment by Regulating Autophagy-Related Signaling via the SHBG/JNK1/Beclin1 Axis in Microglia.
cards.abstract: Cognitive impairment (CI) associated with aging and immunosenescence is linked to metabolic alterations. Microglial senescence and dysregulated autophagy have been implicated as major contributors to this process, but the underlying metabolic regulators remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key metabolic regulators of CI and elucidate their underlying mechanisms. Human cohort analyses, older and D-galactose (D-gal)-induced mouse models, and microglial cell models were integrated to investigate the metabolic regulation of CI. Clinical analyses identified ghrelin as the factor most strongly associated with CI. Older and D-gal mice exhibited CI, microglial senescence, enhanced inflammation, and elevated ghrelin. Ghrelin treatment improved cognitive function, attenuated microglial senescence, and suppressed inflammation, whereas high-dose ghrelin induced growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) desensitization. Sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) showed mainly cytoplasmic localization, was identified as a potential mediator of ghrelin signaling in microglia, and its expression was downregulated following ghrelin treatment. Transcriptomic profiling revealed significant enrichment of autophagy-related pathways in ghrelin-treated microglia. Ghrelin altered autophagy-related markers, as indicated by increased Beclin1 and LC3 and decreased p62. SHBG overexpression or JNK1 inhibition attenuated the ghrelin-induced alterations in autophagy-related markers and anti-senescent effects, whereas Beclin1 overexpression partially rescued these inhibitory effects caused by SHBG overexpression. In conclusion, ghrelin alleviated aging-related CI, with mechanistic evidence indicating that the modulation of microglial autophagy-related mechanisms through the SHBG/JNK1/Beclin1 axis may contribute to its protective effects, thereby providing a potential therapeutic strategy for aging-related CI.

cards.title: Surgical delay is not associated with increased mortality in Greenlandic hip fracture patients: a 5-year retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Hip fractures are associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Guidelines recommend surgery within 24 h, but Greenland's vast geography and Arctic weather often delay surgical treatment. Our aims were (1) to describe the time until surgery among hip fracture patients in Greenland and (2) to evaluate its association with 30-day and 1-year mortality. All patients with hip fracture ICD-10 codes DS720, DS721 and DS722 from 2018 through 2022 were included. Data on time of diagnosis, time to operation, reason for delay, ASA score, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and time of death were collected from patient records. Crude and adjusted analyses were performed. Among 262 patients, the mean time to surgery was 91.4 h, and more than 24 h delay occurred in 90% of them. Mortality did not increase with surgical delay (30 days, OR = 1.0, 95% CI 0.8-1.1; 1 year, OR = 0.9, 0.8-1.1). Mortality rates were comparable to a parallel Danish cohort (30-day mortality of 9.9% vs 10.8% and 1-year mortality of 29.4% vs 28%), with distinctly shorter delays. Mortality was raised with a worse ASA score 3 (OR = 3.8, 1.9-7.4; p < 0.001) and CCI (OR = 3.1, 1.6-5.9; p = 0.001), and with age >70 years (OR = 2.5, 95% CI 1.1-5.9; p = 0.032). The constraint of vast distances and harsh weather in the Arctic causes long surgical delays in hip fracture patients, yet the inability to meet the surgical timeline recommended did not adversely affect mortality in hip fracture patients in Greenland. This questions a general need for fast-track surgery in resource-limited areas.

cards.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Individual Angiotensin Receptor Blockers on Osteoporosis and Osteoporotic Fracture Risk: A Nationwide Active-Comparator New-User Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a major cause of morbidity and fragility fractures in older adults, and increasing evidence suggests that antihypertensive therapies may influence skeletal health beyond blood pressure control. Although angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have been associated with favorable skeletal outcomes, whether clinically relevant heterogeneity exists among individual ARBs remains unclear. Telmisartan possesses distinctive pharmacological properties, including partial peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) agonistic activity, which may confer additional effects on bone metabolism. This study evaluated whether skeletal outcomes differ between telmisartan and other ARBs using an active-comparator new-user design. To evaluate whether clinically relevant differences in osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture risk exist between telmisartan and other ARBs using Taiwan's Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC) Database. Using Longitudinal Generation Tracking Database (LGTD) housed within the Health and Welfare Data Science Center (HWDC), we conducted a nationwide active-comparator new-user cohort study. Hypertensive patients aged 51-80 years who newly initiated telmisartan or another ARB between 2002 and 2021 were identified. Propensity score matching (1:4) was performed to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was a composite of incident osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture and time to first osteoporotic fracture was additionally evaluated as a secondary outcome. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. During a mean follow-up of 4.35 ± 4.12 years, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis or osteoporotic fracture compared with other ARBs (adjusted HR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.53-0.79). In analyses of individual outcomes, telmisartan use was associated with lower risks of osteoporosis (adjusted HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.84) and hip fracture (adjusted HR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.70). In the secondary fracture-only analysis, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of first osteoporotic fracture (adjusted HR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90). Compared with other ARBs, telmisartan use was associated with a lower risk of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fractures in this nationwide cohort. These findings suggest that clinically relevant heterogeneity may exist within the ARB class and that antihypertensive drug selection may influence skeletal outcomes beyond blood pressure control. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

cards.title: Deep learning-enabled monitoring of postoperative fracture healing on serial radiographs: a 150-patient study using an enhanced YOLOv11 framework.
cards.abstract: To develop and validate a deep learning framework for classifying postoperative time-points as a proxy task for monitoring longitudinal fracture healing progression from serial radiographs. This retrospective study included 150 patients with paired pre-treatment and follow-up X-ray images. We built a detection-guided pipeline comprising (1) fracture-region localization using an enhanced YOLOv11 detector integrating attention mechanism, Focal-SIoU loss, and data augmentation, and (2) healing-status prediction from detected regions of interest by quantifying callus formation and fracture-line changes over time. Data were split at the patient level into training/validation/test cohorts. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, F1 score, ROC/AUC, and calibration, and compared with clinician readings. The YOLOv11-guided framework achieved reliable fracture localization and consistent healing assessment on serial radiographs. On the independent test set, it showed stable discriminative ability across follow-up stages and improved robustness over manual interpretation, particularly at early postoperative time points when radiographic changes are subtle. This single-center study demonstrates a technical framework for objective and scalable radiograph-based longitudinal fracture-healing monitoring. External, multi-center validation is required before broader clinical deployment. The proposed detection-enhanced YOLOv11 framework may support clinical follow-up and decision-making after fracture surgery.

cards.title: Re-Evaluating Predictive Performance in the Clinical Risk Analysis Index of Frailty.
cards.abstract: To examine whether the Risk Analysis Index (RAI), last calibrated in 2010-2014, requires scoring system changes to remain an effective measure of surgical frailty. The RAI is among the most validated and widely used measures of surgical frailty. However, like any clinical prediction model, the RAI's scoring system might be prone to algorithmic drift that could invalidate continued use. Retrospective cohort study of patients evaluated in outpatient surgery clinics at Veterans Health Administration (VHA) or University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC). All-cause mortality was measured 180 days after frailty assessment using the RAI-clinical questionnaire (RAI-C). In 410,715 patients from UPMC and 190,044 patients from VHA, the existing RAI-C scoring system demonstrated strong discrimination (c = 0.868 95% CI [0.864-0.872] for UPMC, 0.827 [0.822-0.832] for VHA) which improved modestly after recalibrating parameter weights (c = 0.872 95% CI [0.868-0.876], for UPMC, 0.839 [0.834-0.845] for VHA). Calibration improved slightly, especially at the extremes where the model tends to underpredict mortality, but little change was observed in the range around the threshold of frailty. Of note, the scoring weights associated with a cancer diagnosis demonstrated some multicollinearity-driven instability, but cancer remained the largest contributor to total score. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that reclassification of just a single additional patient as frail would require screening 1400-6000 patients with the recalibrated system, depending on the threshold score defining frailty, and after accounting for the harms of false-positive classification, weighted proportional to the odds at each threshold probability. The RAI scoring system remains robust after a decade of widespread use without evidence of meaningful algorithmic drift. The minimal incremental improvement associated with recalibration does not justify the resources required to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system.

cards.title: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. Not applicable.

cards.title: TiSAM: fusing spatial and histopathology foundation models for whole-slide image segmentation
cards.abstract: Semantic segmentation of whole-slide images (WSIs) quantifies tissue composition and architecture, but existing models require extensive annotation and lose accuracy as the number of tissue classes increases or on heterogeneous, cross-scanner datasets. Here, we present the Tissue Segment Anything Model (TiSAM), which fuses SAM3 spatial features with UNI2-h pathology features within a multi-scale decoder. Because public benchmarks contain few tissue classes, we release MegaMouse, comprising 36,833 annotations of 52 tissue classes from 12 mouse organs, and an 11-class human pancreas dataset. TiSAM achieved the highest overall performance across four public datasets compared to existing convolutional neural network and vision transformer models, maintained high accuracy on MegaMouse, and maintained high accuracy in the human pancreas dataset when trained on as few as 5 annotated WSIs where previous integrations of SAM with pathology foundation models did not. TiSAM segmentations were also more consistent across eight slide scanners compared to other models. These results establish TiSAM as a general and highly adaptable framework for tissue segmentation, enabling studies containing many tissue classes, limited annotations, or images from multiple scanners.

cards.title: Wide-angled proteomics in giant cell arteritis reveals complement pathway activation
cards.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is an immune-mediated vasculitis that can cause serious morbidity including sight loss, stroke and aortic aneurysm. There is an unmet need for blood-based biomarkers and novel therapeutics. We measured plasma protein levels using the SomaScan v4.1 platform, comprising 7,273 protein measurements (SOMAmers) reflecting 6,596 unique protein targets. We profiled the proteome in 113 patients who presented acutely with possible GCA. 56 had biopsy-proven GCA and 57 did not have GCA (non-GCA). We found 144 SOMAmers increased and 151 reduced in GCA. Dysregulated biological pathways included IL6-JAK-STAT3 signalling, chemokines for both myeloid (e.g. CXCL2, CXCL3, CCL18, CCL23) and lymphoid cells (e.g. CXCL9, CXCL13), and the complement system (e.g. C9, CFHR5, C5a, Factor B). Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assays (ELISAs) confirmed elevated plasma levels of C5a, the terminal complement complex, Factor B and CFHR5 in GCA. We developed a 26-protein signature that distinguished GCA from non-GCA (area-under-the curve, AUC, 0.93) and validated the diagnostic signature in external datasets. Our data implicate terminal complement pathway activation in GCA, raising the possibility of complement-directed therapies. We show proof-of-principle that a multiplex protein biomarker could be used as a diagnostic adjunct in suspected GCA.

cards.title: Integrating dorsolateral prefrontal cortex multi-omics and GWAS summary data enhances gene-mapping of Parkinson's disease
cards.abstract: Although dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) is not the main site of the Parkinson disease's (PD) defining pathology, DLPFC is still functionally and structurally relevant as PD progresses - particularly for the cognitive/executive dimension of PD in later stages. To enhance the gene-mapping of PD, we integrated xQTL weights derived from bulk RNA-seq (n=931), single-nucleus RNA-seq (n=415), and bulk proteomics (n=716) data of DLPFC with the largest available GWAS summary data of PD in European population. Through integrative Omnibus TWAS and PWAS analyses, we detected risk genes associated with PD through genetically predicted bulk or cell-type-aware gene expression, or bulk protein abundances in DLPFC. We detected 39 significant risk genes by bulk TWAS, 66 unique genes by cell-type-aware TWAS across six brain cell types, and 17 by bulk PWAS. Importantly, 57.9% (11/19) bulk and 62.5% (20/32) cell-type-aware independent TWAS risk genes had PWAS locus support. Comparing these TWAS/PWAS findings in DLPFC to significant PD TWAS risk genes detected using the bulk RNA-seq data of substantia nigra from the GTEx V10 (n=183) and the same GWAS summary data of PD, 53.8% (21/39) bulk TWAS risk genes, 36.4% (24/66) unique cell-type-aware TWAS genes, and 17.6% (3/17) PWAS genes in DLPFC were also found significant in substantia nigra. Protein-protein interaction analyses indicated connectivity of our detected risk genes in DLPFC with established PD-associated genes such as MAPT, SNCA, and LRRC37A. Cell-type-aware TWAS risk genes were enriched in apoptosis signaling, and T-cell activation was enriched across the bulk TWAS, cell-type-aware TWAS, and PWAS results.

cards.title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a metabolic and energetic signature associated with neuronal dENL/AF9 suppression in aged flies
cards.abstract: Maintenance of neuronal function during aging requires metabolic adaptation, yet how metabolite-sensitive chromatin regulators contribute to this process remains unclear. YEATS-domain proteins, including ENL and AF9, recognize histone acylation marks and are positioned at the interface between cellular metabolism and transcriptional regulation. We previously showed that pan-neuronal suppression of dENL/AF9, the single Drosophila orthologue of mammalian ENL and AF9, extends lifespan, preserves healthspan, and enhances oxidative-stress resistance. Here, we used multi-omics and biochemical analyses to define the molecular state associated with neuronal dENL/AF9 suppression. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a markedly stronger response in aged than young male fly heads, with prominent enrichment of fatty-acid degradation and several intermediary metabolic pathways in the aged dataset. Guided by this age-related transcriptional response, we focused subsequent profiling on aged heads, where independent molecular layers converged on a distinct metabolic and energetic signature. Lipidomics identified reduced abundance of multiple triglyceride-related and fatty acid derivatives, while metabolomics revealed changes in central-carbon/TCA-, nicotinamide-, and purine-associated features. Proteomics implicated mitochondrial and ATP-associated processes, accompanied by increased ATP abundance and a higher NAD/NADH ratio. Matched lipidome-metabolome integration further identified citrate as a cross-omics feature inversely associated with altered triglyceride and ceramide species, linking central-carbon and lipid-associated components of the molecular signature. Together, these findings identify a stronger transcriptional response to neuronal dENL/AF9 suppression in aged flies and a distinct metabolic and energetic molecular signature in aged fly heads, providing candidate molecular correlates of the previously established longevity phenotype and a framework for studies of neuronal aging biology.

cards.title: Deep-learning-based design of an orthogonal self-labeling protein from K-Ras(G12C)
cards.abstract: Self-labeling protein (SLP) tags enable versatile labeling of proteins in live cells, yet only two SLPs are commonly used, limiting multiplexing. Here, we repurposed the oncoprotein K-Ras(G12C) and its covalent inhibitors to create a third, orthogonal SLP system. We used a deep-learning-based approach to radically redesign the sequence of K-Ras(G12C) while preserving its covalent-inhibitor binding pocket. Our top design, LUCI-tag, is a 19 kDa, monomeric, thermostable SLP that rapidly and covalently reacts with commercially available K-Ras(G12C) inhibitors bearing diverse payloads. Unlike existing SLPs, LUCI-tag exhibited payload-agnostic labeling kinetics, outperforming HaloTag7 and SNAP-tag for a negatively charged payload. X-ray crystal structures of drug-bound and drug-free LUCI-tag showed the design was structurally accurate and contained a preorganized inhibitor-binding pocket that could explain its rapid labeling kinetics. Proteomics and cell-signaling experiments confirmed LUCI-tag is biologically inert. LUCI-tag enabled rapid, wash-free, live-cell imaging and simultaneous three-color multiplexed experiments with HaloTag7 and SNAP-tag. This work establishes LUCI-tag as an immediately useful orthogonal SLP and demonstrates that covalent drug-target pairs can be repurposed into a broadly applicable platform for protein labeling.

cards.title: Centered cross-context perturbation transfer on the public 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge benchmark
cards.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses across cellular contexts requires transferring both expression direction and differential-expression priority. We developed a compact numerical method that combines public perturbation summaries with a differential-expression kernel fitted to H1 CRISPRi training targets. The method centers an independent KOLF2.1J source on known training targets, transfers its response signs and magnitude ranks, and uses isotonic regression to render predicted expression means. We evaluated the frozen model retrospectively on the released public TEST100 of the 2025 Virtual Cell Challenge, using an external KOLF source released in 2026. The model achieved DES 0.371834, PDS 0.8614, and MAE 0.302206. With reconstructed historical anchors, its composite score was 0.341344, compared with the archived champion score of 0.340052, a difference of +0.001292. The comparison showed higher DES and lower PDS, with zero normalized MAE contributions for both methods. Source centering also improved development PDS across all three TRAIN folds and official VALIDATION. These results demonstrate a practical numerical approach to cross-context perturbation transfer and differential-expression ranking.

cards.title: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review.
cards.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain unclear. This systematic review of eight randomized controlled trials (n = 493) evaluating dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived bone mineral density reports findings separately for each agent, without pooling, because the trials evaluated four pharmacologically distinct agents differing markedly in weight-lowering potency. The evidence is sparse for every agent and is insufficient to establish the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in this population. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for weight management, yet their skeletal effects remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the randomized evidence on bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers in adults with overweight or obesity, reporting findings separately for each individual agent. This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review (INPLASY202630076) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (January 2015 to July 2026). Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with mean baseline body mass index (BMI) > 25 kg/m², compared a GLP-1 RA with placebo or another antidiabetic therapy for ≥12 weeks, and reported BMD assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Because the included trials evaluated pharmacologically distinct agents that differ substantially in weight-lowering potency, results were synthesized narratively and reported separately by agent; no meta-analysis was performed. Eight RCTs (n = 493) were included. Three trials were at low risk of bias (Eriksson 2019; Hygum 2020; Hansen 2024) and five raised some concerns, principally regarding the randomization process and selective reporting; no agent is supported by more than one trial at low risk of bias. (Cai 2021 contributes two treatment arms assessed separately, giving nine comparisons in the risk-of-bias assessment.) Evidence was unevenly distributed across agents: semaglutide and dulaglutide were each evaluated in one trial, liraglutide in two, and exenatide in five. Five of the eight trials enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes, including all four that randomized an insulin comparator arm; three enrolled adults without diabetes, of which one was defined by obesity alone. By study-level mean baseline BMI, five trials lay in the obese range ( ≥ 30 kg/m²) and three in the overweight range (25 to <30 kg/m²). The single semaglutide trial (Hansen 2024; n = 64; low risk of bias), which produced the largest weight loss of any trial (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -6.8 kg vs placebo), reported reduced lumbar spine BMD (ETD - 0.018 g/cm², p = 0.007), reduced whole-body BMD (mean difference [MD] -0.02 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.03 to -0.01), and increased C-terminal telopeptide (CTX; MD 166.50 pg/mL; 95% CI 66.60 to 266.40). Liraglutide was evaluated at two doses with divergent results. At the weight-management dose of 3.0 mg daily, in the only trial conducted in adults with obesity and without diabetes (Jensen 2024; ETD - 6.7 kg vs placebo), lumbar spine BMD (MD - 0.019 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.034 to -0.004) and total hip BMD (MD - 0.013 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.024 to -0.002) were reduced. At the diabetes dose of 1.8 mg daily (Hygum 2020; -3.8 kg), no site changed materially (lumbar spine MD 0.00 g/cm²; 95% CI - 0.01 to 0.01). Exenatide trials were inconsistent, ranging from 0.03 g/cm² (95% CI 0.02 to 0.03) at the lumbar spine (Renyuan 2015) to -0.04 g/cm² (95% CI - 0.15 to 0.07; Akyay 2023). Certainty of evidence was very low for every agent. The randomized evidence is too sparse and too clinically heterogeneous to determine the skeletal effects of GLP-1 RA therapy in adults with overweight or obesity. Each agent has been evaluated in at most five small trials, most conducted in adults with type 2 diabetes rather than in adults with obesity alone. The two trials producing the largest weight loss, one of semaglutide and one of liraglutide 3.0 mg, both reported reduced lumbar spine and total hip BMD at closely similar magnitudes of weight loss, and the semaglutide trial additionally reported increased bone resorption. This convergence warrants dedicated evaluation rather than extrapolation across the drug class. Adequately powered, agent-specific trials with fracture endpoints are required. INPLASY202630076.

cards.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics.
cards.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

cards.title: Rapid experience-dependent tuning of spinal and transcortical stretch reflexes supports goal-directed movement
cards.abstract: The short-latency stretch reflex (SLR) is the fastest sensorimotor response in human limbs. The spinal SLR scales with background muscle activity and is affected by recent movement history. But adaptive plasticity of spinal reflexes has classically been studied through operant conditioning, which induces an arbitrary change in reflex size over days to weeks. In contrast, rapid, experience-dependent feedback adaptation is often attributed to transcortical mechanisms underlying the long-latency reflex (LLR). Whether task constraints can progressively shape the SLR within a single session remains unclear. Here, naive human adults (n = 16; 9 females, 7 males) performed an instructed-delay reaching task while holding a robotic manipulandum which delivered brief haptic perturbations during action preparation. We recorded high-density surface electromyography (64-channel arrays) from the pectoralis major and posterior deltoid to investigate reflex gains. Pre-perturbation muscle activity showed no systematic goal-directed change. With a long-enough preparatory delay (750 ms), SLR gains decreased progressively with experience when the planned movement was expected to stretch the homonymous muscle, rather than shorten it. This tuning occurred in both muscles, was evident within individual participants, and was accompanied by a corresponding decrease in reflexively generated force opposing perturbations toward the cued target. No such tuning was detected with a short preparatory delay (250 ms). LLR responses were goal-directed from the first trial blocks and progressed in a comparable manner across the session, at both preparatory delays. Our study shows that spinal feedback circuits can progressively adapt within a single session to support the performance of goal-directed movements.

cards.title: Age-driven miR-29 trades youthful plasticity for epigenetic fidelity
cards.abstract: Throughout life, somatic cells must preserve their identity while retaining the capacity to adapt. How this balance shifts with ageing and rejuvenation remains unclear. Here we identify miR-29 as a central point of convergence between the transcriptional programmes of physiological ageing and two routes to rejuvenation: induced reprogramming and the natural reset of early development. miR-29 rises with ageing, falls in both rejuvenation settings and shows the most conserved age-associated increase across vertebrates. miR-29 inhibition opposes transcriptional ageing, whereas mimics promote an older transcriptional state. Methylome analysis reveals a broader function: inhibition releases the miR-29 brake on remodelling, and mimic treatment reinforces it. This release increases methylation at repeat-associated CpGs and lowers epigenetic-clock estimates through unequal contributions in opposite directions. Inhibition also amplifies stimulus-induced methylation changes but reduces fidelity to lineage-specific methylation patterns. We extend this relationship to cancer, where low miR-29 expression marks tumours with younger epigenetic-age estimates yet greater methylation divergence from their tissue of origin. These findings identify miR-29 as a control point linking ageing, rejuvenation and cancer, and support a maladaptive trade-off model in which epigenetic fidelity is preserved at the expense of the plasticity needed for methylome maintenance and adaptation.

cards.title: TFAM Dependent Mitochondrial Fitness Limits CD8⁺ T Cell Immunopathology and Sustains Protective Immunity during Viral Pneumonia
cards.abstract: During respiratory virus infections, CD8 T cells kill virus-infected cells and establish antigen-specific immune memory, but excessive or dysregulated responses can also contribute to lung immunopathology. The development and maintenance of optimal CD8 T cell effector and memory responses depend on mitochondrial fitness, which can be compromised across multiple physiologic and pathologic conditions. However, how impaired mitochondrial fitness affect antiviral CD8 T cell responses remains poorly understood. Here, we used a CD8 T cell-specific TFAM-haploinsufficient mouse model to induce moderate mitochondrial stress without the severe mitochondrial dysfunction associated with complete TFAM loss, providing a genetically controlled model of mitochondrial perturbations relevant to physiologic conditions. TFAM insufficiency disrupted mitochondrial integrity and cellular bioenergetics and increased mitochondrial DNA and oxidative stress in CD8 T cells. During primary influenza A virus (IAV) infection, TFAM-insufficient CD8 T cells exhibited heightened cytotoxic activity and inflammatory responses associated with lung immunopathology, followed by progressive functional exhaustion, diminished antigen-specific responses, and impaired protective immunity. Consistent with the physiologic relevance of these findings, CD8 T cells from older individuals exhibited reduced TFAM expression and mitochondrial function. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that moderate mitochondrial stress can alter the trajectory of antiviral CD8 T cell responses, promoting pathogenic effector activity during acute infection while compromising subsequent protective immunity.

cards.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
cards.abstract: Existing supervised and self-supervised EEG models mainly learn within-segment discriminative or reconstructive representations, leaving transitions between adjacent EEG segments underexplored. We propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model for EEG seizure detection that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment from the current EEG state, conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals. A learnable query-based fusion module aggregates the multimodal synchronized signals into a compact physiological condition. Pretraining uses no seizure labels; downstream detection retains only the frozen EEG encoder and a linear probe. On the SeizeIT2 dataset with a strict patient-wise split, the model achieved an AUPRC of 0.3748, ROC-AUC of 0.8025, and balanced accuracy of 0.7308, outperforming official database baselines (SVM with hand-crafted features and ChronoNet), an external baseline (DSAINet), and a foundation model (NeuroLM). Ablations show a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder, supporting multimodal-conditioned latent transition learning for wearable EEG representation learning.

cards.title: Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer
cards.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables region-resolved investigation of tumor metabolism, yet translating gene expression into reliable metabolic flux predictions remains challenging because genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs). Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomic data from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor, spanning normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3 and 3+4 tissues, with Human-GEM using an E-Flux framework incorporating defined nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. An initial naive implementation produced TICs in all twelve flux solutions, with total internal fluxes 190-890-fold higher than those obtained using the revised workflow. All flux solutions were certified free of TICs, and 94.7% of 17,592 loopless flux bounds were determined exactly. Within the analyzed tissue, predicted metabolic similarity was associated with spatial region (permutation p = 0.023) but not histological state (p = 0.52), revealing model-predicted heterogeneity even between regions sharing the same Gleason grade. Flux-based target prioritization identified fatty acid uptake-associated genes (CD36, FABPs, and SLC27A1/4), although the dominant uptake signal was confined to one malignant region, suggesting a localized metabolic hypothesis rather than an established therapeutic vulnerability. Analysis of the zinc-citrate-aconitase axis further demonstrated that zinc-dependent citrate redistribution was absent under baseline conditions and emerged only when oxidative demand, elimination of a cytosolic aconitase bypass, and strong mitochondrial aconitase inhibition coincided. These findings establish the importance of thermodynamic quality control and physiologically informed constraints in spatial metabolic modeling, while distinguishing computationally feasible flux predictions from experimentally validated metabolic mechanisms. The resulting framework provides a reproducible foundation for investigating spatial metabolic heterogeneity and prioritizing testable hypotheses for future experimental validation.

cards.title: Distinct spatial organization of human hippocampal perfusion and microvascular pulsatility across age
cards.abstract: Arterial pulsation can modulate neuronal activity through mechanosensitive pathways in mice, but whether vascular pulsatility is similarly related to neural organization in humans remains unclear. Here, using 7T MRI in 35 young and older adults, we mapped cerebral perfusion and microvascular volumetric pulsatility index (mvPI) across the unfolded hippocampus and integrated these measures with histological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic reference maps. Perfusion and mvPI exhibited distinct spatial organization and age-related differences. In young adults, perfusion preferentially corresponded to parvalbumin-interneuron density and beta/gamma distribution, whereas mvPI was associated with theta-band distribution. A number of associations detected in young adults were not detected in the older adults maps. Spectral simulations showed qualitative similarity to heartbeat-related phase resetting as one possible explanation for the mvPI-theta relationship, while spatial transcriptomics revealed perivascular enrichment of PIEZO2, a candidate mediator of vascular mechanotransduction. Together, these findings establish perfusion and tissue-level pulsatility as distinct dimensions of human hippocampal vascular organization and provide a framework for investigating their relationships with neural dynamics across aging.

cards.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
cards.abstract: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge." Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge. The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

cards.title: Blood-based PhenoAge may reflect disease burden rather than biological aging in cancer
cards.abstract: PhenoAge, a blood-based biological aging clock, is associated with cancer outcomes, a finding taken as evidence that biological aging shapes prognosis. In 3,067 patients undergoing primary tumor resection, PhenoAge acceleration rose with tumor stage. One or two of its eight blood components, differing by cancer type, carried the prognostic signal, and replacing its general-population weights with equal weights did not weaken it. In cancer, PhenoAge may reflect disease burden rather than biological aging.

cards.title: Sustained Maternal Cortisol Elevation Links Metabolic Stress to Fetal Growth Restriction in a Guinea Pig Model of Undernutrition
cards.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) resulting from maternal undernutrition is commonly attributed to insufficient nutrient substrate delivery to the fetus. However, the contribution of maternal physiological stress responses to this outcome remains poorly characterized. Using the well-established guinea pig maternal nutrient restriction (MNR) model, we conducted a comprehensive retrospective analysis to interrogate the hypothesis that maternal stress physiology actively mediates fetal growth outcomes beyond simple substrate limitation. Maternal salivary and serum cortisol were significantly elevated in MNR dams throughout pregnancy despite no baseline differences at conception, indicating that hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation was specifically triggered by the combined physiological demands of pregnancy and nutritional constraint. The sustained cortisol elevation was accompanied by acute metabolic perturbations at mid-pregnancy, including hypoglycemia and depleted circulating lipids. While most acute metabolic disturbances resolved by near-term, cortisol remained elevated, and MNR fetuses exhibited parallel cortisol elevation alongside sustained growth restriction. Maternal weight divergence emerged only in late gestation and was driven primarily by reduced conceptus weight. Maternal organ analysis revealed selective hepatic enlargement with apparent lipid accumulation in MNR dams near-term. Overall, these findings help to reframe nutrition-related FGR as a condition in which maternal adaptive stress responses, reduced nutritional components and placental insufficiency are mechanistically intertwined, with important implications for the design of effective interventions beyond simply nutrient supplementation.

cards.title: The microbiota of a wild butterfly species over three decades of climate change
cards.abstract: As microbes can support essential functions related to many aspects of host physiology, changes in microbial communities can affect host physiology and fitness. Although the effects of thermal conditions on host-associated microbiomes have been demonstrated in laboratory settings, how climate change might affect the structure and functionality of microbial communities in wild populations remains poorly understood. We took advantage of the long-term field survey of the Glanville fritillary butterfly (Melitaea cinxia) metapopulation on the [A]land Islands, in the Baltic Sea, to fill this gap. We investigated whether bacterial communities associated with larvae showed gradual temporal change in response to slow environmental warming across a 28-year period, or whether these communities responded through abrupt change following a sudden drought event that triggered bottlenecks in their butterfly host population. Using 16S rRNA metabarcoding and metagenomic sequencing, we first showed that M. cinxia harbours a set of stable resident bacteria, including Pseudomonas, Telluria, and Enterobacteriaceae bacteria. We also characterized a gradual shift in the M. cinxia associated bacterial community over three decades of increasing temperatures and decreasing precipitations. This shift was not unidirectional for all bacterial taxa, as the dominant Telluria and Pseudomonas showed opposing responses to environmental trends. Additionally, the 2018 extreme drought, which triggered acute host population bottlenecks, was associated with a severe disruption of M. cinxia microbiota, and the loss of key Enterobacteriaceae taxa. However, the M. cinxia bacterial community appeared to recover towards pre-drought structure in subsequent years, suggesting resilience to acute climatic perturbations in this system.

cards.title: Ubiquitin ligase RNF126 exerts functions in lysosomal damage response and lysosomal homeostasis maintenance
cards.abstract: The response to lysosomal membrane permeabilization involves extensive ubiquitylation at the lysosome; however, the ubiquitin ligases identified so far cannot account for the complexity of the response. Using extensive spatial proteomics, we identified RNF126 as a new ligase that is robustly recruited to lysosomes in response to a range of different damage triggers across distinct cell types. Recruitment is mediated independent of BAG6 via an arginine-rich stretch in the low-complexity region of RNF126 to mostly unacidified lysosomes in the perinuclear region. Ubiquitin remnant mass spectrometry identified several damage-induced RNF126 substrates, among them known lysosomal damage response components and potential new factors that might drive regeneration from lysosomal damage. Consistently, RNF126 deletion resulted in persistent lysosomal swelling. In addition, we uncovered a constitutive role of RNF126 in lysosomal homeostasis maintenance. Hence, our findings identified the ubiquitin ligase RNF126 as novel lysosomal health regulating factor with functions in homeostasis and stress conditions.

cards.title: Benchmarking Recording-Level Clinical Speech De-identification for Privacy-Preserving Clinical Audio
cards.abstract: Transcript-based de-identification protects textual records but leaves sensitive health information (SHI) directly audible in source recordings, limiting trustworthy reuse of clinical audio. However, standardized evaluations of recording-level SHI detection remain limited. We established the SREDH-AICUP 2025 benchmark to evaluate recording-level SHI detection systems and characterize the approaches. All 22 qualifying systems combined automatic speech recognition with downstream SHI detection, whereas we additionally evaluated end-to-end detection from audio. Pipeline baselines outperformed the end-to-end baseline in transcription (MER, 0.123 vs 0.155) and SHI detection (macro-F1, 0.507-0.653 vs 0.422). Synthetic Mandarin speech-text augmentation enabled the end-to-end model to detect Mandarin SHI that was not identified without augmentation (macro-F1, 0.171 vs 0). Foundation models showed category-specific differences in SHI recognition, and type-aware adaptive routing improved macro-F1 from 0.656 to 0.697. These findings establish standardized reference performance, characterize current system designs, and demonstrate how language-specific augmentation and category-aware model integration can improve recording-level SHI detection.

cards.title: Reprogramming bone homeostasis: The recoupling-oriented framework of bidirectional regulation strategies for osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Current osteoporosis treatments reduce fracture risk by suppressing bone resorption, stimulating bone formation, or combining both effects. Yet these clinical benefits do not show whether formation has resumed at sites where bone was previously resorbed. This Review uses a remodeling recoupling framework to examine this resorption-to-formation transition. We define recoupling as restoration of the sequence from resorption through reversal to osteoblast recruitment and bone formation. This differs from bidirectional regulation, in which osteoblast activity increases and osteoclast activity decreases without evidence that the two responses are linked. We review the cellular communication, signaling pathways, cell-survival mechanisms, and systemic conditions that influence this transition. We also assess candidate targets and treatments according to the strength of clinical, human, animal, and mechanistic evidence. The available evidence is strongest for established therapies and several human-supported pathways, whereas many proposed targets and delivery approaches remain preclinical. This framework may help guide treatment sequencing, patient selection, bone-targeted delivery, and the development of measures that determine whether formation follows resorption.

cards.title: Do LLM Proposers Improve Budgeted Search for Ionizable Lipids?
cards.abstract: Efficient lipid design under limited experimental budgets is a central challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. We introduce LEAF (Lipid Evolutionary Adaptive Framework), a matched-budget protocol for testing whether language-model proposers improve combinatorial molecular search relative to classical baselines. The study uses a 30,044-candidate ionizable-lipid space, a frozen Gaussian-process oracle fitted to experimental potency labels, and a separate active-learning surrogate. Four language models evaluated over eight seeds and three splits show no significant improvement over genetic-algorithm or random-search baselines. For Llama 8B, 79.1% of acquisition-selected queries repeat previously evaluated archive members. Removing duplicates reduces the performance gap on some splits but increases proposal cost and can prevent budget exhaustion. Larger models reduce duplication without establishing superiority or equivalence. Exploratory scored prompts and stricter novelty controls yield positive median differences against the genetic algorithm, yet wide intervals and shared-seed dependence preclude stronger conclusions. A validated single-assay reanalysis preserves the chemotype-cold deficit at a smaller numerical scale, and exploratory expected hypervolume improvement does not reverse the result. Follow-up checks address whether proposers genuinely use injected evidence. These checks include a zero-shot leakage probe, rank-only and chain-of-thought-rationale prompts, a score-shuffle perturbation, an evidence-conflict probe, and a genuine reasoning-mode proposer. They show measurable engagement with supplied information without a corresponding performance gain. LEAF isolates proposal quality as the experimental variable and documents a concrete failure mode of zero-shot LLM proposers under controlled budgets.

cards.title: Recovering Hidden Neural Oscillatory Modes from Partial Observations through Delay Embedding and Perturbation
cards.abstract: Characterising the oscillatory behaviour generated by neural interactions is central to systems neuroscience because these dynamical properties are linked to brain function. However, inferring latent neural dynamics is challenging because recordings sample only part of the system. Time-delay embedding allows dynamical modes to be estimated from partial recordings, using methods such as Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel DMD). Despite its promise, two questions remain: what dynamical information is recoverable through time-delay embedding, and how can recovery be improved? We address both questions using control theory. Our framework centres on factorising the Hankel matrix of delay-embedded observations into an observability matrix and a trajectory matrix with the form of a controllability matrix. We show that their ranks impose complementary constraints on what any delay-embedding method can recover: delay embedding can increase observability rank, while perturbation can increase trajectory rank by exciting otherwise inactive modes. We validate this framework using Hankel DMD in simulations and human electrocorticography (ECoG). In both, perturbation increased the number of fast-decaying mode estimates, whereas greater delay depth increased the number of reliably estimated modes and, in ECoG, extended their frequency range. These results clarify what partial recordings can reveal about neural dynamics and how to reveal more.

cards.title: ESX-1 remodels the Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen storage compartment in macrophages
cards.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) secretes antigenic proteins that drive protective T cell responses, yet how Mtb intracellular localization affects the trafficking and spatiotemporal distribution of mycobacterial antigens in macrophages remains elusive. Here, we developed a split fluorescent protein reporter to monitor the dynamics of the TB vaccine lead antigen Ag85B in infected human macrophages. We discovered that Mtb triggers the formation and remodeling of two distinct types of Mtb Antigen Storage Compartment (MASC) that retains Ag85 within macrophage membranes. Using subcellular spatial proteomics, we profiled the composition of the MASC, identifying both the Mtb and macrophage proteins that constitute these compartments. Unexpectedly, MASCs are defined by metabolic compartmentalization and rewiring to lipid metabolism in both the macrophage and Mtb. Thus, Mtb builds via the ESX-1 system a metabolically distinct antigen storage compartment in immune cells, with potential implications for antigen selection and delivery in TB vaccine development.

cards.title: Desflurane Increases Hippocampal RAF-MAPK-MSK1 Protein Levels and Reduces CLOCK Expression: Sorafenib Attenuates Cognitive Impairment in Aged Mice.
cards.abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is common after anesthesia and surgery in older adults, yet no targeted therapy exists, and the mechanism linking volatile anesthetic exposure to circadian dysregulation in the aged hippocampus is undefined. Here we show that RAF manipulation bidirectionally alters CLOCK protein levels in HT22 hippocampal neurons, and that RAF-MAPK-MSK1 protein abundance is inversely related to CLOCK levels in the aged hippocampus after desflurane exposure. Aged C57BL/6 mice (18 months, both sexes) were exposed to 2% desflurane for 2 h, with or without pretreatment with the multi-kinase RAF inhibitor sorafenib (50 mg/kg), and phenotypes were assessed by Western blot, immunofluorescence, in vivo electroencephalography, whole-cell patch-clamp recordings of CA1 pyramidal neurons, and behavioral testing (righting reflex, contextual fear conditioning, Morris water maze). Parallel dissection in HT22 hippocampal neurons employed RAF knockdown, overexpression, and pharmacological inhibition. Desflurane increased total c-Raf, ERK1/2 (MAPK), and MSK1 protein levels-phosphorylation status was not assessed-while reducing CLOCK in both HT22 cells and aged hippocampus, accompanied by cellular senescence, impaired S-phase entry, increased hippocampal β-galactosidase and α-synuclein immunoreactivity, synaptic excitation-inhibition imbalance, and deficits in contextual fear memory and spatial learning. In HT22 cells, RAF knockdown normalized kinase abundance and restored CLOCK, whereas overexpression exacerbated these changes. In aged mice, sorafenib restored CLOCK, attenuated hippocampal β-galactosidase and α-synuclein immunoreactivity, and improved cognitive performance. These findings support a link between RAF-MAPK-MSK1 protein abundance and hippocampal CLOCK in desflurane-induced cognitive impairment and nominate RAF inhibition as a candidate strategy warranting further preclinical study.

cards.title: Association between RANK gene polymorphism and early femoral neck bone loss in kidney transplant recipients.
cards.abstract: Rapid bone mineral density (BMD) loss and fracture risk are major complications of kidney transplantation (KTx), partly attributed to glucocorticoid-impaired bone remodeling. We investigated associations between early postoperative femoral neck BMD (BMD-FN) decline and single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in genes related to glucocorticoid sensitivity and bone metabolism. Sixty-nine adult patients who underwent living-donor KTx in 2015-2024 were investigated. The primary endpoint was annualized BMD-FN change (%) between preoperative and 12 ± 6 months postoperative DXA. Patients with significant prior glucocorticoid exposure, postoperative pulse therapy, or anti-osteoporotic treatment were excluded. Four SNPs (NR3C1 [rs41423247], TNFRSF11A [rs1805034, rs884205], and LRP5 [rs3736228]) were genotyped and analyzed using multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex. The median annualized BMD-FN change was - 3.4% (IQR - 6.6 to - 0.7). Among the four SNPs, only TNFRSF11A rs884205 was significantly associated with greater BMD loss; A risk allele carriers showed greater decline than the CC genotype (β = - 2.75; 95% CI, - 4.82 to - 0.68; P = 0.010). No significant associations were observed for NR3C1 (rs41423247), TNFRSF11A (rs1805034), and LRP5 (rs3736228). However, after adjustment for baseline BMD-FN, which was higher in risk-allele carriers, the rs884205 association was attenuated and no longer significant (β = -1.92%; 95% CI, -3.94 to 0.09; P = 0.062). In the early post-KTx period, the TNFRSF11A rs884205 risk allele may be associated with greater annualized BMD-FN decline, although this did not persist after baseline BMD-FN adjustment. These findings are preliminary and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts.

cards.title: Are we at risk of increasing sarcopenia? Implications for osteoarthritis and osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is a progressive skeletal muscle disorder characterised by reduced muscle strength, impaired muscle quantity or quality, and declining physical performance, with important consequences for falls, fractures, disability, and loss of independence. Whether sarcopenia prevalence itself is rising remains difficult to quantify because diagnostic frameworks and surveillance methods vary, yet a growing burden is plausible. Population ageing, increasing multimorbidity, obesity, hospitalisation, surgery, and incomplete recovery after musculoskeletal events are likely to increase the absolute number of people living with low musculoskeletal reserve. Osteoarthritis (OA) and osteoporosis (OP) are central to this problem because they amplify the functional consequences of weakness and reduced loading. OA may lead to strength loss through pain, inflammation, altered movement, and activity restriction, while OP increases the likelihood that falls or loading errors will result in fracture and subsequent deconditioning. Shared mechanisms for sarcopenia include mechanical unloading, adiposity-related metabolic dysfunction, inflammageing, mitochondrial stress, endocrine change, and nutritional insufficiency, although the strength of evidence differs across pathways. New weight-loss approaches using glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) may substantially affect sarcopenia risk and therefore require careful consideration. Current diagnostic frameworks increasingly prioritise muscle strength and performance over lean mass alone, supporting pragmatic case-finding in older adults with severe OA, fragility fracture, recurrent falls, poor postoperative recovery, or weight loss. Current management should focus on progressive resistance and balance training, adequate energy and protein intake, guideline-based OP care, optimised OA treatment, and protection of mobility during transitions of care. The most immediate clinical gains are likely to come from integrating existing rheumatology, orthopaedic, fracture-prevention, rehabilitation, and nutritional services rather than from any osteosarcopenia-specific drug therapy.

cards.title: Attractor dynamics underlie sequence working memory in data-constrained recurrent neural networks
cards.abstract: Sequences of stimuli can be maintained in working memory by encoding each item, together with its position, as a distinct pattern of neural population activity. Competing hypotheses about the underlying dynamics have been proposed: patterns of activity might be supported either by stable attractor states that persist over time, or by transient sequential dynamics. To investigate the dynamics underlying sequence memory, we developed a framework for fitting low-rank recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to multi-session recordings of spiking activity, and applied it to 2,488 units recorded across 30 sessions in two macaques. Our data-constrained RNNs generated population spiking activity which closely resembled neural data and recovered single-unit tuning properties across sessions. Consistent with prior work, fitted networks represented items presented at different sequence positions in separate low-dimensional subspaces in the neural activity, alongside a dominant temporal component. The RNNs enabled direct investigation of the underlying dynamics: By isolating the temporal and stimulus subspaces, we found a manifold of fixed points emerged during the memory retention period. Targeted perturbation analyses confirmed that activity within this manifold is consistent with attractor-like dynamics, and predict that brief optogenetic perturbations delivered along this attractive manifold can selectively induce persistent shifts in neural activity and decoded behavior. Together, our results indicate that sequence working memory is organized by position-specific coding subspaces, within which attractor states maintain persistent representations, while activity evolves along time-varying dimensions.

cards.title: Evaluation of Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation methods for metaproteomics using a model microbiome
cards.abstract: We present a multi-organism, ground-truth metaproteomic dataset generated using data-dependent acquisition Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation (ddaPASEF) and data-independent acquisition (diaPASEF) on a trapped ion mobility mass spectrometer. The dataset comprises 28 species (30 strains) spanning Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya, and bacteriophages, assembled into an uneven mock community with a 400-fold dynamic range of organismal abundance. Four biological replicates were processed using a standardized sample preparation workflow and analyzed using described LC-MS conditions. Raw data, search outputs, protein coverage metrics, quantitative abundance estimates, and strain-specific peptide evidence are provided. The dataset enables evaluation of proteome depth, proteome coverage, quantitative reproducibility, and strain-level resolution across acquisition strategies. diaPASEF yielded broader peptide and protein detection and deeper sequence coverage, while both methods accurately quantified high-abundance organisms. Detection evidence for low-abundance bacteriophages and single-amino-acid-variant peptides is included to support benchmarking of taxonomic and strain-resolved analyses. This dataset provides a comprehensive reference for developing and validating metaproteomic workflows, protein inference strategies, and ion mobility-aware computational tools.

cards.title: Precocious maturation and Purkinje cell dysfunction in the mouse Chd8 haploinsufficient cerebellum
cards.abstract: The cerebellum plays an emerging, but understudied, role in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Mutations in CHD8 cause a monogenic NDD (CHD8-NDD) characterized by autism and other manifestations, and prior work in Chd8 mutant mice reported cerebellar abnormalities, raising the possibility of cerebellar contribution to CHD8-NDD. To comprehensively characterize the impact of Chd8 haploinsufficiency on cerebellar development and function, we profiled the postnatal day 12 (P12) cerebellum of germline Chd8+/- mice using transcriptomic, morphological, and electrophysiological approaches. Gross cerebellar morphology was unaffected, but single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed transcriptomic signatures of pathophysiology across cell types, including accelerated maturation of molecular layer interneurons and granule cells, and altered myelination state of oligodendrocytes. Purkinje cells (PCs) showed the strongest transcriptomic burden of any cell type and, consistent with this, exhibited altered morphology and electrophysiological properties. Bulk RNA sequencing confirmed that transcriptomic pathology persists into adulthood, indicating lasting impacts on both neuronal and glial gene expression. Together, these results capture cell-type-specific cerebellar perturbations associated with Chd8 haploinsufficiency and support the cerebellum as a relevant site of pathology in CHD8-NDD.
