cards.title: Risk factors for revisions in patients following total hip arthroplasty and hemiarthroplasty due to femoral neck fractures.
cards.abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and hemiarthroplasty (HA) are established treatments for displaced femoral neck fractures (FNF), yet factors associated with revision following either procedure remain poorly defined. This study evaluated demographic, clinical, and laboratory predictors of revision after THA and HA for FNF. A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary trauma centre including 2,522 patients treated with arthroplasty for FNF (885 THA, 1,637 HA). Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and pre- and postoperative laboratory parameters were compared between patients who underwent revision and those who did not. Variables significant on univariate analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine optimal cutoff values for significant continuous predictors. Revision occurred in 93 of 885 THA patients (10.5%) and 43 of 1,637 HA patients (2.6%) (p < 0.001). In the THA cohort, patients requiring revision were younger (65.4 vs. 72.5 years, p < 0.001), had shorter hospital stays (5.4 vs. 7.5 days, p = 0.001), higher postoperative haemoglobin (10.5 vs. 9.6 g/dL, p < 0.001), and lower postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (10.8 vs. 15.7 mg/dL, p = 0.007). Multivariable analysis identified younger age (OR 0.94 per year, 95% CI 0.91-0.98; p = 0.003), higher postoperative haemoglobin (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01-1.66; p = 0.044), and lower postoperative CRP (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.90-0.99; p = 0.029) as independent predictors of revision. ROC analysis identified age < 60 years (AUC 0.66) and postoperative haemoglobin ≥ 10.55 g/dL (AUC 0.63) as optimal thresholds. In the HA cohort, only postoperative lymphocyte count differed significantly between revision and non-revision groups, precluding multivariable analysis. Revision following arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture was substantially more common after THA than HA. Among THA patients, revision was associated with younger age and markers of better postoperative physiological recovery rather than medical frailty. These findings suggest that revision risk after fracture-related THA may largely reflect the greater activity level and longer survivorship of healthier patients, information that may assist preoperative counseling and individualized procedure selection.

cards.title: BioCluster: Clustering and Zero-Shot Labeling of Ecological Images Using Foundation Models
cards.abstract: The increasing automation of biodiversity monitoring is generating large volumes of ecological images requiring taxonomic identification, creating a substantial annotation bottleneck. Assigning species-level labels requires considerable time and expert knowledge, limiting scalability. We propose BioCluster, a framework for unsupervised clustering and zero-shot labeling of ecological images using foundation models. The framework extracts image embeddings from pretrained models and groups images into taxonomic clusters without task-specific training. Species labels are assigned through zero-shot text matching against the taxa expected in the dataset. We investigate dimensionality reduction and six clustering algorithms for organizing fine-grained imagery. A per-image uncertainty score combines clustering and labeling information to sort images into three confidence tiers, so experts can focus on uncertain and unlabeled cases. We evaluate it on two moth and two bird datasets, with one annotated camera-trap collection per taxonomic group. For these camera-trap datasets, per-image species-level accuracy reached 84% on DK-Moth and 83% on HUGO-Bench Aves. An interactive report presents clusters and zero-shot labels by confidence tier and prioritizes cases requiring expert review. The framework provides a training-free approach for organizing and labeling ecological image collections, reducing manual annotation while retaining expert oversight and demonstrating the potential of foundation models for scalable, semi-automated annotation.

cards.title: Research Progress on the Precise Classification and Individualized Diagnosis and Treatment of Nocturia.
cards.abstract: Nocturia is a common urological symptom whose prevalence increases progressively with age. It not only impairs sleep and quality of life but also increases the risk of adverse events, including falls and fractures. Clinical management remains limited by inadequate evaluation of underlying etiologies, imprecise phenotyping, and suboptimal therapeutic responses. To facilitate standardized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, we reviewed and summarized relevant literature published over the past decade. Focusing on four major subtypes, nocturnal polyuria (NP), diminished bladder capacity (DBC), global polyuria (GP), and sleep disorder-predominant nocturia (SDP), we developed a clinical framework integrating precise assessment, phenotypic classification, and individualized treatment. This review compares the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying different phenotypes, identifies the voiding diary as the cornerstone of assessment, and proposes a streamlined three-step clinical phenotyping algorithm. A stepwise treatment strategy tailored to different subtypes is outlined, incorporating psychological counseling, lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, physical therapy, and surgery. This review provides a reference for the precise and individualized management of nocturia and highlights the potential future roles of digital assessment and multidisciplinary care.

cards.title: Metagenomic contextualization of proteins with state space models
cards.abstract: Genomic foundation models have emerged as powerful tools for learning representations of biological sequences, but existing approaches predominantly rely on Transformer architectures, whose quadratic attention complexity limits their ability to capture long-range genomic context. This limitation is particularly relevant for metagenomics, where sequencing data have increased more than 500-fold since 2011, generating increasingly large and diverse datasets. For example, gLM2, a Transformer-based mixed-modality genomic language model, was trained with a context window of 4,096 tokens, limiting its ability to capture extended genomic context within metagenomic contigs. Developing scalable architectures capable of processing longer sequences while integrating protein and nucleotide information is therefore essential for advancing genomic foundation models. We introduce Nammu, a 167-million-parameter, bidirectional Mamba-based genomic foundation model that integrates protein and nucleotide sequences within a 20,000-token context window. Leveraging the linear scaling of state-space models, Nammu was trained using a curriculum learning strategy on the OpenMetaGenomic (OMG) corpus, first incorporating 64 million protein sequences followed by 32 million mixed-modality metagenomic contigs. Despite using approximately 37\% fewer training tokens than gLM2, Nammu outperformed this Transformer-based model in taxonomic classification across all evaluated taxonomic ranks on a marine metagenomic dataset from the Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation (CAMI). On the exact-feature-unmatched CAMI II Strain Madness test set, Nammu achieved higher all-contig genus-classification accuracy than Kraken2 (0.9182 versus 0.8142). Nammu further outperformed gLM2 (150M) in KEGG Orthology prediction using deep-sea metagenome-assembled genomes. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of state-space architectures for scalable, multimodal genomic representation learning and highlight their ability to support accurate taxonomic and functional predictions from metagenomic sequences.

cards.title: Patient-specific management in high-risk revision total hip arthroplasty: mid-term outcomes of a next-generation constrained acetabular liner.
cards.abstract: Managing recurrent instability in revision total hip arthroplasty (rTHA) requires a personalized approach, as traditional constrained liners often yield suboptimal results due to locking-mechanism failure and limited impingement-free range of motion. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term clinical outcomes of a novel constrained acetabular liner (CAL) when utilized as a patient-specific solution for a high-risk cohort undergoing complex rTHA. By tailoring the constraint to individual biomechanical deficits, this next-generation device seeks to mitigate historic failure modes. We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients who underwent 37 rTHA procedures with a next-generation CAL at a single urban academic center between March 2017 and October 2023. Average follow-up was 4.7 years (range, 0.3 to 9.7 years). The most common indication for rTHA was instability (70.3%), followed by infection (16.2%), aseptic loosening (10.8%), and polyethylene wear (2.7%). Just over one third of patients (37.5%) had undergone a prior revision. Preoperative constructs included fixed-bearing (37.8%), dual-mobility (32.4%), CAL (24.3%), static spacer (2.7%), and hemiarthroplasty (2.7%). In most procedures (70.3%), the CAL was implanted into a pre-existing acetabular cup, whereas 29.7% involved both cup and liner revision. Following rTHA, no cases of implant wear, breakage, acetabular cup aseptic loosening, or periprosthetic fracture were observed. Six patients (18.8%) underwent a total of sixteen subsequent reoperations after CAL implantation-10 for instability and 6 for infection. Among instability-related reoperations, 4 involved revision to a new next-generation CAL. Survivorship free from all-cause reoperation was 83.8% at one year and 72.6% at latest follow-up. This study demonstrates favorable mid-term clinical outcomes and reoperation-free survivorship following complex revision THA using a novel constrained acetabular liner system. For patient cohorts suffering from severe recurrent dislocation, this next-generation CAL provides an effective, tailored tool in the surgical armamentarium by adapting to unique patient anatomy and soft-tissue compromises. Further research with larger sample sizes and extended follow-up is needed to assess long-term durability.

cards.title: Decision benchmarking reveals when protein foundation models add experimental value
cards.abstract: Protein engineering is shifting from model-based variant scoring to deciding what to measure next. This exposes a limitation of fixed-dataset benchmarks, which rank predictors without showing when their advantage survives as evidence accumulates. We therefore introduce decision benchmarking across 217 ProteinGym assays, 2.47 million variants and 95 predictors to evaluate whether models and measurements improve decisions at matched cost. Zero-shot accuracy explained less than one-fifth of the variation in discovery after calibration. Calibrated priors exceeded budget-matched additivity at 20-100 measurements, but the advantage narrowed as component measurements accumulated. Measured additivity then overtook zero-shot models after 50-100 measurements for top-variant discovery and around 500 for global ranking. The same principle showed that double-mutant measurements improved prediction in models using mutation identity, whereas prediction-guided acquisition improved discovery. Evidence-based routing improved strategy selection. Decision benchmarking thus identifies which strategy adds value given the information already available and the decision that follows.

cards.title: [Thoracic trauma in Hungary today: heritage, current challenges and future directions].
cards.abstract: Thoracic trauma is an important contributor to morbidity and mortality among severely injured patients. While the management of immediately life-threatening intrathoracic injuries is relatively well defined, the treatment of severe blunt chest wall injuries, particularly multiple rib fractures and flail chest, remains variable across institutions. This review aims to summarize the current situation of thoracic trauma care in Hungary, with special emphasis on chest wall injuries and the role of surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF). SSRF should no longer be regarded as an isolated technical procedure, but as part of the complex, multidisciplinary management of patients with rib fractures. Therapeutic decision-making should be based not only on the number of fractured ribs, but also on fracture pattern, chest wall instability, pain, respiratory mechanics, pulmonary parenchymal injury, the patient's physiological reserve, overall injury severity and timing of surgery. The development of thoracic trauma care in Hungary requires a shared indication language, protocol-based imaging, early reassessment, multimodal analgesia, physiotherapy, transparent regional referral pathways and auditable outcome measurement. The existing Hungarian expertise in trauma surgery, thoracic surgery, emergency medicine and intensive care provides a realistic basis for establishing a structured, nationally applicable model of thoracic trauma care. cards.title: Hip Structural Analysis and Multiple Fragility Fractures: Evidence from a Large Cross-Sectional Clinical Cohort.
cards.abstract: Hip structural analysis parameters (HSAP) are associated with hip fracture risk, but associations with multiple fragility fracture phenotypes remain poorly characterised. We analysed 11 DXA-derived HSAP in patients referred between June 2004 and November 2019. Five mutually exclusive fracture phenotypes were defined: no fracture, single hip fracture, single non-hip fracture, multiple non-hip fractures, and multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture. Separate multinomial logistic regression models were fitted for each HSAP reported as odds ratio (OR) per standard deviation increase, adjusted for FRAX covariates and left femoral BMD. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied across all tests. A right-hip sensitivity analysis assessed bilateral consistency. 35,647 patients were included (mean age 64.5 years, 82% female). Of 13,777 (38.6%) with a fragility fracture, 1044 (2.9%) had a single hip fracture, 9723 (27.3%) a single non-hip fracture, 2268 (6.4%) multiple non-hip fractures, and 742 (2.1%) multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture. After multiple testing correction, no meaningful associations were observed for isolated hip or non-hip fracture phenotypes. Multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture were independently associated with greater hip axis length (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.28 to 1.63), neck diameter (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.38), and centre of mass to upper neck margin distance (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.21 to 1.51). HSAP were significantly associated with multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture rather than isolated fracture phenotypes, potentially reflecting local structural vulnerability and broader biomechanical instability.

cards.title: Sex shapes capillary flows and oxygen extraction in the middle-aged mouse brain
cards.abstract: Sex differences in brain aging are well documented, but their origin within the cerebrovascular hierarchy remains unclear. Here we show that cortical blood flow is higher in female than male mice at 15 months of age, at a point when an earlier sex difference in pulsatility and resistance indices has already converged, pial vessel diameter shows no difference between sexes, and estrogen levels are similar between sexes. Using an indicator-dilution and intravascular oxygen measurements using two-photon microscopy, we found that capillary transit-time heterogeneity (CTH) scales more steeply with mean transit time in females, consistent with a passively regulated capillary network, and that this is accompanied by reduced oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) without deficit in arterial oxygen delivery. Spatial transcriptomics reveals that sex differences are organized into distinct regional programs, most prominently in white matter, where a male-associated myelin and axonogenesis signature accompanies reduced white matter volume in females. These molecular and structural differences coincide with elevated hippocampal microglial reactivity and an altered spatial search strategy in females, without any detectable differences in circulating markers of stress, blood-brain barrier integrity, or immunity. Together, these findings indicate that sex differences in the aging brain are expressed at the level of capillary flow regulation and regional tissue programs rather than through bulk cerebral blood flow alone, and that elevated blood flow in females can mask, rather than reflect, adequate tissue oxygenation.

cards.title: DeepD enables efficient genome modeling and controllable long-context sequence generation across domains of life
cards.abstract: Genome foundation models hold great potential for advancing biological research, but modeling diverse complex genomes and generating controllable genome-scale sequences remain challenging. We present DeepD, a phylogeny-informed sparse mixture-of-experts model operating at single-nucleotide resolution over a 1-million-token context while reducing active computation. Pretrained on unselected whole-genome sequences across all domains of life, DeepD learns genic and intergenic sequence features and supports broad sequence-to-function prediction across species. DeepD performs well in human protein fitness and disease variants effect prediction, such as BRCA1 and BRCA2, with particular strength in regulatory regions, such as promoter and transcription-factor binding sites. Expert routing captures exon-intron boundaries, transposable elements, and distal cis-regulatory elements. DeepD also generates experimentally validated core promoters with specified transcriptional strengths. Finally, the Context-Anchor-Body strategy enables generation of complete yeast chromosome sequences and megabase-scale Arabidopsis segments, preserving gene structure and order while introducing variations within natural ranges. Together, DeepD is an efficient genome foundation model that unifies accurate sequence-to-function prediction with controllable genome-scale generation, advancing predictive and generative design of complex genomes.

cards.title: Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics
cards.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies enable the identification of spatially variable genes that can shed light on tissue structure and function. However, spatial variability of gene expression can be due not only to biological function but also technical artifact. We develop a model for spatially variable capture that forms part of a bursty transcription model, allowing us to distinguish biological variability from spatially variable technical noise. Our approach is implemented in a program called stipple, which we demonstrate can be useful for identifying and interpreting spatial gene expression variation from spatial transcriptomics assays.

cards.title: PlantGeneAnn: a high-accuracy ab initio plant gene annotation tool fine-tuned from a genome foundation model
cards.abstract: Structural annotation remains a bottleneck for translating the growing catalog of high-quality plant genomes into biological insights, as current pipelines rely on RNA-seq and homologous protein evidence that are often unavailable for non-model species. Existing ab initio tools are constrained by model scale and perform poorly in complex plant genomic regions. We present PlantGeneAnn, a plant-optimized ab initio gene annotation tool fine-tuned from a genome foundation model. It combines a Mamba-MoE DNA encoder with a U-Net-style embedding decoder and a semi-Markov decoding pipeline. Trained on 40 angiosperm species, PlantGeneAnn establishes a new state-of-the-art (SOTA) across a stringent 20-species benchmark, significantly outperforming Helixer, Tiberius, and ANNEVO at exon-, intron-, and locus-levels, with mean F1 scores of 0.856, 0.880, and 0.707, respectively. It also enables efficient customized fine-tuning: LoRA fine-tuning increased the locus-level F1 of the out-of-distribution bryophyte Physcomitrium patens from 0.581 to 0.736, with performance plateauing at 40% of the fine-tuning data. Notably, PlantGeneAnn requires substantially lower peak memory usage than other baseline tools, allowing annotation of large plant genomes on standard personal workstations. PlantGeneAnn thus provides accurate, hardware-friendly ab initio annotation for diverse plant genomes, particularly newly assembled genomes, population-scale projects, and non-model plants.

cards.title: Impact of clinical frailty on mortality after elective surgery in patients aged ≥ 90 years admitted to critical care: a binational intensive care registry analysis.
cards.abstract: Increasing numbers of patients aged ≥ 90 years require elective surgery. Frailty is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of peri-operative risk, but high-quality evidence to understand the impact on outcomes in this age group is limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Adult Patient Database. Patients aged ≥ 90 years admitted to ICU following elective surgery were included, encompassing planned and unplanned ICU admissions. Frailty was assessed at ICU admission using the Clinical Frailty Scale and patients categorised as non-frail or frail. Propensity score matching was performed to balance age; sex; acute illness severity; and comorbidities. Primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU mortality; in-hospital mortality; return to pre-admission residence; and ICU and duration of hospital stay. The matched cohort comprised 5398 patients (2699 without frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 1-4) and 2699 living with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 5-8)), with good post-matching covariate balance. Mortality in ICU was low and not significantly different between patients who were frail and non-frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (matched hazard ratio (HR) 1.66, 95%CI 1.22-2.27, p = 0.001) and higher 1-year mortality (matched HR 1.66, 95%CI 1.47-1.87, p < 0.001). Patients without frailty had higher odds of returning to their pre-admission residence at hospital discharge than patients living with frailty (matched OR 1.45, 95%CI 1.29-1.62, p < 0.001). Patients who were frail experienced longer hospital stays and higher rates of postoperative complications, including delirium and acute renal failure. Among patients aged ≥ 90 years undergoing elective surgery with postoperative intensive care admission, frailty is strongly associated with prolonged recovery and worse short and long-term outcomes. Incorporation of frailty assessment into peri-operative pathways may improve risk stratification, shared decision-making and personalised care for patients aged ≥ 90 years.

cards.title: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes
cards.abstract: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.

cards.title: Inherent limitations of zero-shot mutation prediction in protein engineering
cards.abstract: Predicting mutation effects is critical for protein engineering. A commonly pursued strategy is zero-shot prediction with deep-learning models, whose performance is typically evaluated using aggregate benchmark scores that obscure multidimensional biological tradeoffs. Here, we evaluate sequence, structure, and hybrid foundation models across curated datasets to expose the practical limitations of zero-shot predictions. We demonstrate that model performance is highly variable and heavily influenced by experimental noise and competing phenotypic goals. Notably, predictions from competing models often correlate more strongly with one another than with experimental outcomes. While current models effectively filter deleterious mutations and enrich high-scoring variants for natural functions, they struggle to identify precise optimal mutations and consistently fail to predict mutations that drive new-to-nature functions. These models learn from evolutionary constraints that tend to oppose the extreme biophysical optimizations required in targeted engineering. Consequently, zero-shot scoring serves as a valuable initial filter but cannot substitute for task-specific prediction.

cards.title: Covariance Nonstationarity is Evident in Spatial Transcriptomics and Provides a New Categorization of Spatially Varying Genes
cards.abstract: Gaussian process models underlie many spatial transcriptomics tools but typically assume stationary covariance. To test this assumption, we use approximate Bayes factors from R-INLA to compare stationary and non-stationary Matern covariance functions across 12 Visium datasets; covariance non-stationarity is substantially evident as it appears in 3% to 50% of genes across datasets. We find that gene sets associated with effector functions are enriched among genes favoring non-stationary spatial covariance.

cards.title: Effects of gliflozins on bone health of patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
cards.abstract: Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are a crucial therapy for chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet concerns persist regarding their impact on bone metabolism. This systematic review evaluates the skeletal safety and metabolic effects of SGLT2i in patients with CKD. A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies was conducted. Data on study design, population characteristics, baseline kidney function, bone-related comorbidities, and outcomes (osteoporosis, fractures, falls, amputations, and bone mineral markers) were summarized. Risk of bias was evaluated according to the included category. The analysis revealed that while one RCT and a cohort study reported a significantly increased risk of bone fracture and amputation, this finding was not replicated in other subsequent cohort studies and other RCTs, which generally showed non-significant differences. Of note, the reporting of bone-related outcomes was inconsistent throughout the literature, and a substantial proportion of the evidence derives from studies primarily designed for patients with type 2 diabetes, largely involving early-stage CKD subgroups. One study suggests that SGLT2i may favorably modulate markers of CKD-mineral bone disease (MBD), reporting reduced risk of hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, high parathyroid hormone, and low vitamin D levels. The reviewed literature primarily included data on empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin. Mostly, SGLT2i demonstrated a possible reassuring skeletal safety profile in CKD. Initial safety concerns regarding fractures have not been consistently supported, although evidence in moderate-to-advanced CKD remains limited. Long-term, prospectively defined skeletal outcomes are needed to confirm these findings and clarify class effects.

cards.title: Bone health in diabetes mellitus.
cards.abstract: Bone health depends on a complex interplay between cellular and extracellular components that together preserve skeletal integrity, microarchitecture, and mechanical strength. Disturbance of this balance in a range of pathophysiological states, particularly in diseases such as diabetes mellitus, may substantially impair bone quality, delay fracture healing, and increase fracture risk. This review summarizes the main mechanisms linking diabetes and bone health, with emphasis on advanced glycation, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, hormonal and osteoimmune dysregulation, microvascular impairment, and altered mesenchymal stem cell fate. We also review bone turnover markers, the skeletal effects of contemporary glucose-lowering therapies, and emerging methodological approaches, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses. A more integrated understanding of these processes may improve risk stratification, treatment decisions, and prevention of skeletal complications in diabetes.

cards.title: Transitions to Comfort Measures Only Among Patients Hospitalized With Sepsis: Clinical Drivers and Implications for Mortality
cards.abstract: Background Mortality in sepsis is often considered a direct consequence of infection and organ dysfunction, although many deaths occur after withdrawal of life sustaining treatment. The clinical factors leading to these decisions and their implications for interpreting sepsis mortality are not well characterized. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of a prospective observational cohort of adults with physician adjudicated sepsis at a tertiary academic medical center. Patients who transitioned to comfort measures only (CMO) during the index hospitalization underwent structured chart review to characterize baseline health and functional status, clinical severity, care preferences, anticipated outcomes following survival, and the primary reason for CMO transition. Results Among 239 patients with adjudicated sepsis, 42 (17.6%) transitioned to CMO. These patients had substantial underlying disease, including malignancy in 76% and immunocompromised status in 62%. However, 88% lived at home before hospitalization, 52% were independent in activities of daily living, an additional 26% were partially independent, and 90% were full code on admission. Progressive multi organ failure (19%), refractory septic shock (19%), and irreversible respiratory failure (12%) accounted for half of CMO transitions, while advanced frailty (5%) and poor baseline functional status (2%) were infrequent primary reasons. Median time from admission to CMO was 16 days (IQR 7 to 33), and median time from admission to death was 18 days (IQR 11 to 35). Anticipated ventilator dependence (62%), dialysis dependence (36%), and cognitive impairment frequently influenced goals of care discussions. Overall, 38 patients died during the index hospitalization, and 35 (92%) of these deaths followed transition to CMO. Conclusions Most CMO transitions in this cohort occurred after an evolving course of severe sepsis and were driven primarily by progressive organ dysfunction and failure to recover rather than advanced frailty or poor baseline function. These findings identify failure to recover after the acute septic insult as an important clinical trajectory and highlight the need to account for treatment limitation when interpreting sepsis mortality. Understanding why some patients recover from sepsis associated organ dysfunction while others progress to irreversible organ failure may help identify patients and mechanisms for future therapeutic intervention.

cards.title: Risk stratification for unfavorable outcome after resection of selected brain metastases in patients with multiple brain metastases.
cards.abstract: Surgical removal of brain metastases (BM) may improve patients' prognosis when substantial tumor debulking is achieved. Patients with multiple lesions may be offered surgery for symptomatic lesions or to obtain histopathologic diagnosis. There is only few evidence on risk analysis for resection of selected BMs in patients with multiple BMs. In this bicentric study, patients with multiple BM (i.e. n ≥ 2) who underwent microsurgery for selected lesions between 2021 and 2024 were included. Demographic data, Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS), 5-item modified frailty index (mFI-5), clinical course and MR-imaging including volumetric assessment of tumor volumes were analyzed. The primary endpoint was 90-day mortality. Secondary endpoints were institutional discharge, length of inpatient stay, and allocation to adjuvant treatment. One-hundred-and-thirty-two patients met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 63 years (IQR 21.8) and 54 (40.9%) were female. Ninety patients (68.2%) had 2-4 BMs and 42 patients (31.8%) had ≥ 5 BMs. The median resected tumor volume was 15.4 (IQR 21.6) cm³ per patient. The 90-day mortality was 28% (37/132). Factors associated with increased 90-day mortality included advanced age (p < 0.001), lower preoperative KPS (p = 0.048), lack of adjuvant treatment (p < 0.001) and higher mFI-5 score (p = 0.008). Lower preoperative KPS (p < 0.001) and higher mFI-5 scores (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with discharge to institutional care rather than home. Length of postoperative in-hospital stay inversely correlated with KPS (rs = -0.29, p = 0.001) and positively with mFI-5 score (rs = 0.26, p = 0.003) but not with age, tumor volumes or number of lesions. In patients with multiple BM, increasing age, increased frailty and low preoperative KPS influenced 90-day mortality and short-term outcome. Resection for symptom relief or tissue diagnosis in these patients may be performed with these precautions.

cards.title: RFM: A Lightweight Retinal Foundation Model for Generalised Oculomics
cards.abstract: Foundation models for colour fundus photography (CFP) are candidate visual encoders for multimodal medical AI, but existing models are large and are assessed under fine-tuning rather than the frozen-encoder conditions such systems impose. We present RFM (Retinal Foundation Model), a 64-million-parameter Vision Transformer initialised from DINOv3-Base and domain-adapted with the LeJEPA joint-embedding predictive self-supervised objective with domain-specific pretext tasks, on 4.3 million CFPs from the North East London Diabetic Eye Screening Programme. A single linear head per task on one frozen backbone measures representation generalisability, not fine-tuning capacity. Across six external datasets spanning diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading, glaucoma detection, ten UK Biobank biomarker phenotypes and 3-year incidence of myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke and Parkinson's disease, RFM attains the lowest mean absolute error of any frozen model on all seven regression phenotypes and a higher area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) than any RETFound variant on all eight matched classification benchmarks. It also attains the highest AUROC of any model evaluated on four of the five ophthalmic benchmarks, with 4.8x fewer parameters than RETFound-MAE and RETFound-DINOv2. Applied to UK Biobank without retraining, RFM exceeds the best published retinal foundation-model AUROC for 3-year myocardial infarction and ischaemic stroke; the Parkinson's endpoint (11 cases) is inconclusive. DINOv3-Base without retinal pre-training, read the same way, stays competitive on DR grading but falls clearly behind on glaucoma, and the feature-extraction convention alone is worth up to 0.154 AUROC. One lightweight backbone yields generalised representations serving ophthalmic grading, biomarker regression and incidence prediction.

cards.title: Increased screw backout with non-inlay design retrograde femoral nails.
cards.abstract: To compare the rate of distal interlocking screw backout between inlay-design and non-inlay design retrograde intramedullary femoral nails in the treatment of distal femur fractures. Adults with AO/OTA 33 distal femur fractures treated with a retrograde ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) inlay-design nail (RFNA; DePuy Synthes) or a non-inlay design nail (T2 SCN; Stryker) between January 2015 and June 2025 at a single Level I academic trauma center with a minimum follow-up of 3 months were retrospectively reviewed. The primary outcome was distal interlocking screw backout. Secondary outcomes included time to backout diagnosis, backout distance, and rate of symptomatic screw removal. All outcomes were compared between the inlay-design and the non-inlay design cohorts. A total of 134 patients were included: 76 in the inlay cohort and 58 in the non-inlay cohort. The inlay cohort demonstrated a significantly lower rate of distal interlocking screw backout compared to the non-inlay cohort (5.3% vs. 19.0%; RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.09-0.83; p = 0.02), corresponding to a 72.2% relative risk reduction. Time to backout diagnosis and backout distance did not differ significantly between designs. The rate of symptomatic screw removal was significantly lower in the inlay cohort (1.3% vs. 10.3%; p = 0.04). The distal transverse screw was the most common screw with backout in both cohorts. The ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) inlay at the distal interlocking interface of a retrograde femoral nail was associated with significantly lower rates of distal interlocking screw backout and symptomatic screw removal. When backout did occur, polyethylene inlay did not impact time to diagnosis and backout distance.

cards.title: The phenotype of pelvic and acetabular fractures in adults aged 50 and older: a national database analysis in the Netherlands.
cards.abstract: Brief Nationwide data show rising pelvic and acetabular fracture incidence, yet patient profiles and outcomes remain underexplored. In our cohort of 7,120 patients ≥50 years, pelvic fractures were frailer overall while mortality was similar to acetabular fracture patients. Findings support distinguishing fracture types and considering pelvic fractures as major osteoporotic fractures. Pelvic and acetabular fractures are increasingly common in aging populations and carry substantial clinical and societal burdens. As these injuries are often grouped together despite potentially different patient characteristics and outcomes, this study aimed to provide a comprehensive, nationwide phenotypic description of patients aged 50 years and older with pelvic or acetabular fractures in the Netherlands. A retrospective population-based cohort study was conducted using national claims and population data from Statistics Netherlands (CBS). All individuals aged ≥50 years diagnosed with a pelvic or acetabular fracture in 2019 were included. Demographics, comorbidities, treatment modality, care utilization, 1-year readmission, and mortality were compared between fracture types and sex. 7120 patients were included (6091 pelvic, 1029 acetabular). Pelvic fracture patients were older than acetabular fracture patients (mean age 77 vs 74), often female (79% vs 36%), with higher pre-injury rates of osteoporosis, connective tissue disease, and polypharmacy (all p < 0.05). Acetabular fractures showed more hospital admissions (53% vs 35%), surgical treatment (28% vs 4.4%), and complication-related readmission (9.7% vs 1.8%), most evident in male patients. New major fracture rates (6.6% vs 8.4%) and 1-year mortality rates (15% vs 17%) were comparable. Pelvic and acetabular fractures reflect distinct phenotypes in patients aged 50 and older, with pelvic fractures more closely linked to frailty and osteoporosis, most apparent in females. These findings support differentiating between fractures in research and clinical care and call for reconsideration of pelvic fractures within major osteoporotic fracture definitions, as their clinical profile seems similar to that of hip fracture patients.

cards.title: Pervasive Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Genomic Foundation Models
cards.abstract: Genomic foundation models are revolutionizing biological research and biotechnology, yet their vulnerability to data poisoning remains poorly characterized. Here we show that backdoor attacks can be reliably implanted during fine-tuning across diverse model architectures, tasks and model scales by poisoning only a small fraction of training data with short DNA motifs, including triggers derived from transposon terminal inverted repeats (TIRs). Attack success rates are generally high across encoder-based and autoregressive models, while clean-task performance remains almost unchanged. Increasing model scale does not confer measurable resistance. To detect such threats, we develop a two-stage auditing framework that flags potentially poisoned sequences through localized single-nucleotide mutation sensitivity in model predictions, without prior knowledge of trigger sequences. These results identify downstream fine-tuning as an attack surface for genomic foundation models and motivate stronger data provenance, adversarial evaluation and post-training security auditing.

cards.title: Patterns of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Initiation Compared With Other Glucose-Lowering and Anti-Obesity Therapies Among Older Adults
cards.abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have rapidly expanded from primarily glucose-lowering agents for type 2 diabetes (T2D) to therapies used across diabetes, obesity, and cardiometabolic disease. Prescribing has risen sharply since 2018, especially with the broader uptake of semaglutide-based products. Still, real-world initiation patterns remain incompletely characterized in older adults with varying levels of cognitive vulnerability and frailty. Methods: We analyzed treatment patterns of GLP-1RA use in a retrospective cohort of adults aged >=65 years with T2D in a regional healthcare system from 2018 to 2026. We describe the demographic and clinical characteristics of new initiators of GLP-1RAs compared with initiators of alternative therapies, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i). We analyzed a sub-cohort of patients to identify the prevalence of baseline cognitive concerns using a large language model (LLM). We used a LASSO logistic regression to identify important predictors of GLP-1RA initiation compared to other therapies. Results: Of 58,754 adults aged 65 years or older with T2D, 5,095 initiated GLP-1RA, 5,483 initiated a SGLT2 inhibitor, and 1,516 initiated a DPP-4 inhibitor. GLP-1RA initiators were younger (mean 75.2 [SD 4.9] vs 77.7 [6.0] and 79.5 [7.1] years) and less often aged 80 years or older (17.7% vs 35.0% and 47.6%). The largest difference across groups was adiposity: mean BMI was 33.8 (6.2) vs 29.7 (5.7) and 28.6 (5.6) kg/m2 (SMD 0.592), with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher in 72.1% vs 41.9% and 34.0%. Glycemic control was similar (mean HbA1c 7.46% vs 7.38% and 7.70%; SMD 0.165). GLP-1RA initiators were younger; more likely to be overweight; had lower average comorbidity index; and less dementia, heart failure, and renal disease than those initiating alternative therapies. GLP-1RA initiators had fewer hospitalizations 1-year prior to drug initiation. In a LASSO model, BMI greater than 27 kg/m2 was the strongest predictor of GLP-1RA initiation (positive), followed by baseline congestive heart failure (negative) and baseline hospitalization (negative). Conclusion: In this cohort of older adults, those with T2D who initiated GLP-1RAs were younger and had less comorbidities at baseline compared to initiators of other T2D therapies. Overweight BMI was the strongest predictor of GLP-1RAs initiation, whereas baseline HbA1c was similar across groups, suggesting that the decision to start GLP1-RA is more influenced by adiposity than glycemic control. Our analysis of real-world prescribing patterns appear to be in alignment with guidelines for Type II diabetes treatment1, which recommend GLP-1RA treatment for glucose lowering and weight management and SGLT2 treatment in those with risk of cardiovascular disease or heart failure.

cards.title: Interaction between mental health conditions and hip fracture on the 30-day risk of infection among older adults: a Danish matched cohort study.
cards.abstract: Infections are a frequent complication following hip fracture (HF) surgery. Although approximately 30% of patients undergoing HF surgery have a mental health condition, its potential interaction on the risk of post-operative infection remains uncertain. Using Danish nationwide registries, we included a cohort of patients with HF aged ≥ 65 years operated during 2004-21 (n=100 335) and an age- and sex-matched comparison cohort from the general population without HF at the index date (n=498 943). Mental health conditions were identified using diagnosis codes F00-F48. Outcomes were hospital-treated infections (H-TIs) and hospital- or community-treated infections (HC-TIs) within 30 days after surgery. Cumulative incidence with 95% confidence intervals (CI) was estimated with death as competing risk. Interaction was assessed on an absolute and relative scale. The highest incidence of H-TIs was observed among patients with HF and mood disorders (18.1%, 95% CI: 17.3-19.0) and comparators with anxiety disorders (2%, 95% CI: 1.8-2.5). Among patients with HF, the highest incidence of HC-TIs was in those with dementia (43.0%, 95% CI: 42.2-43.9). Likewise, comparators with dementia had the highest incidence of HC-TIs (18.4%, 95% CI: 17.9-18.8). Across mental health condition categories, attributable fractions ranged from 1.1% to 32.3% for H-TIs and 10.8%-19.7% for HC-TIs. The strongest synergistic effect was observed in patients with psychoactive substance use for both H-TIs and HC-TIs. Patients with HF and mental health conditions are at higher risk of infection than comparators. Mental health conditions and HF interact synergistically, which increases the infection risk by more than 30%, highlighting the need for targeted treatment for patients with HF and mental health conditions.

cards.title: Regional variation in vertebral bone marrow adiposity: a population-based atlas of age- and sex-specific patterns.
cards.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is a metabolically active fat depot implicated in skeletal aging and systemic metabolism. While chemical shift-encoding MRI enables noninvasive quantification of bone marrow fat fraction (BMFF), current knowledge of vertebral BMAT is largely limited to small cohorts or restricted anatomical regions. To characterize the spatial distribution of vertebral bone marrow fat fraction across the spine and determine region-specific associations with age and sex in a population-based cohort. In this retrospective study, MRI data from 82,920 UK Biobank participants recruited between 2006 and 2010 were analyzed. The baseline case subset (n = 81,318) had a mean age of 54.8 ± 7.6 years, and 42,113/81,318 (51.8%) were female. Automated vertebral body segmentation enabled voxel-wise BMFF quantification using Dixon MRI. Vertebra- and region-level BMFF metrics were derived. Associations with age and sex were assessed using region-specific linear regression. Vertebral BMAT demonstrated a non-linear cranio-caudal pattern. Mean BMFF was ~ 39% in the cervical, ~ 55% in the thoracic, ~ 45% in the lumbar spine, and ~ 70% in the sacrum. BMAT increased with age in all regions (all p < 0.001; increase per decade: cervical 3.33%, thoracic 3.41%, lumbar 2.95%, sacral 3.83%). Females exhibited higher BMFF than males across all regions (all p < 0.001). The overall spatial pattern remained consistent across age groups and sexes. Vertebral BMAT exhibits a structured, non-linear spatial distribution with region-specific age- and sex-dependent patterns. This population-based atlas provides normative reference data supporting region-specific BMAT assessment in skeletal and metabolic disease.

cards.title: Prostaglandin E2-mediated aging microenvironment fuels pathogenic fibrosis in cesarean section scar defect.
cards.abstract: With the increasing rates of cesarean section (CS), cesarean section scar defect (CSD) has become an escalating clinical concern due to uterine dysfunction and reduced fertility. However, the biological basis of CSD remains poorly understood, particularly the mechanisms of impaired uterine repair after CS and the causes of failure in conventional repair surgeries. This study integrates metabolomics, transcriptomics, a newly developed mouse model, and functional assays to elucidate the complex interplay between senescence and fibrosis in CSD. Our findings identify upregulation of the PGES/prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) axis as a key upstream event that disrupts uterine healing. Elevated PGE2 preferentially induces early senescence of macrophages, which transmit pro-senescent signals to uterine fibroblasts through IL-1β/IL-1R signaling. This sequential senescence cascade drives excessive fibroblast activation and progressive fibrosis, ultimately impairing uterine structure and function. In mouse CS models, inhibition of the PGES/PGE2 pathway and anti-aging strategies significantly attenuate fibrosis and restore coordinated myometrial and endometrial repair. Our findings uncover a macrophage-fibroblast senescence relay to fibrotic scar formation in CSD and provide a translational rationale for targeting PGE2 signaling and senescence to improve uterine repair after CS.

cards.title: Predicting tracheostomy after operative cervical spine trauma: development and internal validation of the Tracheostomy Likelihood Score.
cards.abstract: Tracheostomy decisions after operative cervical spine trauma vary widely, and existing prediction tools were developed in heterogeneous populations that included nonoperative patients or rely on variables not consistently available early after injury. No validated score exists specifically for surgically managed cervical trauma patients. The authors sought to develop and internally validate a practical risk score to estimate tracheostomy risk after operative cervical spine trauma. The authors performed a retrospective cohort study of adults (≥ 18 years) who underwent operative management for traumatic cervical spine injury at a single level I trauma center (2017-2021). The primary outcome was postoperative tracheostomy during the index hospitalization. Candidate predictors available at or shortly after admission were selected a priori based on clinical plausibility and prior literature, then evaluated using multivariable logistic regression with a parsimonious model-building strategy. Model discrimination, calibration, and accuracy were internally validated using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation (10 repeats, 100 total fits) and bootstrap validation with optimism correction. Regression coefficients were converted into an integer Tracheostomy Likelihood Score (TLS) for bedside risk stratification. Of 515 patients (66 tracheostomies [12.8%]), 461 with assessable admission American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) examinations comprised the primary modeling cohort (47 tracheostomies [10.2%]). The final 6-variable model included admission AIS grade, clinically significant traumatic brain injury, number of cervical fracture levels, thoracic injury, nonspine injuries requiring surgery, and intubation on admission. Admission AIS grade (OR 2.27 per grade, p < 0.001) and intubation on admission (OR 6.54, p < 0.001) were the strongest independent predictors. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination (apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.903 [95% CI 0.858-0.945]) with preserved performance after repeated cross-validation (AUC 0.883 [95% CI 0.830-0.933]) and minimal overfitting (bootstrap optimism 1.5%). The TLS preserved nearly all the model's performance (AUC 0.897 [95% CI 0.849-0.943]) and stratified observed tracheostomy risk from 1.7% (TLS 0-5) to 10.7% (TLS 6-10) and 61.2% (TLS > 10), representing an approximately 36-fold gradient. On sensitivity analyses reincorporating patients with untestable AIS examinations, discrimination remained excellent (AUC 0.883-0.891). The 6-variable TLS accurately stratifies tracheostomy risk after operative cervical spine trauma using early clinical and imaging data, including in patients whose neurological status cannot be formally assessed. This simple bedside tool may support more consistent airway planning, facilitate multidisciplinary communication, and improve patient and family counseling regarding anticipated respiratory trajectories.

cards.title: Objective Physical Performance Predicts 10-Year Fracture Risk Without Densitometry in Older Men and Women: Development and Head-to-Head Comparison with FRAX in MrOS and SOF.
cards.abstract: FRAX estimates 10-year fracture probability from clinical risk factors and, for best performance, DXA-derived bone mineral density (BMD), limiting its use where densitometry is unavailable. We tested whether a five-variable, laboratory- and imaging-free model (age, body-mass index, grip strength, gait speed and chair-stand rate; M5) predicts incident fracture and how it compares with FRAX. In community-dwelling older men (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study, n = 5994; 73.7 years) and women (Study of Osteoporotic Fractures, n = 9704; 71.6 years) with baseline physical-performance measures and adjudicated incident major osteoporotic fracture (848 and 2522 events), M5 was developed by five-fold cross-validation; we assessed time-dependent AUC at 5, 10 and 15 years, calibration and decision-curve net benefit. Comparators were FRAX in men and a conservative FRAX-surrogate model (in-cohort clinical risk factors) in women, since individually linked, licensed FRAX scores were not available for SOF. In men, M5 discriminated fracture better than FRAX without BMD (10-year ΔAUC + 0.052, 95% CI + 0.023 to + 0.080) and did not differ significantly from FRAX with BMD (+ 0.029, - 0.005 to + 0.063) in this cross-validated, in-cohort comparison; adding BMD to M5 gave the highest discrimination. In women, M5 did not differ significantly from the FRAX-surrogate comparator (- 0.008, - 0.018 to + 0.002), and BMD-based models performed best. M5 was well calibrated (calibration slope 0.97-0.98) and gave higher (men) or equivalent (women) net benefit. Death was a major competing event (72.7% of men, 61.4% of women) but changed 10-year incidence by ~ 1 percentage point. A five-variable, laboratory- and imaging-free model incorporating physical performance stratifies 10-year fracture risk at least as well as FRAX without BMD in men, without requiring imaging, laboratory tests or fracture history. Because M5 was developed within these cohorts whereas FRAX is an external, fixed algorithm, part of this margin reflects development asymmetry; the findings are promising but require external validation before clinical use, and do not replace measured BMD.

cards.title: Self-reported geriatric impairments and treatment toxicity in older patients with multiple myeloma.
cards.abstract: Frailty influences treatment outcomes in older patients with multiple myeloma (MM), yet existing frailty tools capture limited geriatric domains and are incompletely studied in the context of contemporary therapies. We prospectively evaluated patient-reported comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) domains and their associations with treatment toxicity and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) in older adults with MM. Patients aged ≥60 years with newly diagnosed or relapsed/refractory MM initiating a new therapy completed electronic CGA and PRO questionnaires at baseline and 4 months. Outcomes included clinician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity, treatment adaptations, health care use, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). A cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) was derived from CGA and HRQOL domains. Among 90 patients (mean age, 72 years), geriatric impairments were common, particularly physical function domains. High-grade nonhematologic toxicities were significantly associated with older age, comorbidities, patient-reported functional limitations, and anxiety. Toxicity rates on the PRO version of the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) were higher than on CTCAE, highlighting a discordance between physician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity. Frailty was present in 22% and associated with worse baseline HRQOL and increased high-grade nonhematologic toxicity but not treatment adaptations or health care use. Average CGA and HRQOL scores remained stable over 4 months, although individual trajectories varied. Patient-reported geriatric impairments are prevalent in older adults with MM and strongly associated with nonhematologic toxicities even in the contemporary treatment era. Physician-reported CTCAE may not fully reflect patients' symptom burden. Heterogeneity in individual geriatric trajectories during treatment emphasize the need for longitudinal assessment. This study was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05918185.

cards.title: The aging secretome as a candidate driver of bone remodeling imbalance: myokines, adipokines, and senescence-associated secretory factors
cards.abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on the spatial and temporal coupling of osteoclastic resorption to osteoblastic formation. With aging, this balance shifts toward net bone loss alongside sarcopenia, marrow adipose expansion, and chronic low-grade inflammation. These parallel changes may be linked by a shared set of secreted signals, termed here the aging secretome. We distinguish functional remodeling imbalance, defined as a sustained shift between formation and resorption, from direct uncoupling, in which a resorption-to-formation coupling signal is demonstrably disrupted. The aging secretome comprises three principal arms: muscle-derived signals, including myostatin, irisin, and myogenic extracellular vesicles; fat-derived signals, including leptin, adiponectin, and marrow adipocyte lipotoxicity; and senescence-associated secretory factors, particularly those involving senescent osteocytes, TNF-α, and IL-6. Inflammaging is treated as a shared contextual amplifier rather than a separate signaling arm. These pathways converge on key regulators of skeletal remodeling, including RANKL, Wnt–sclerostin, and IGF-1. This framework also provides a common context for comparing pathway-specific interventions, such as activin type II receptor blockade and sclerostin inhibition, with broader approaches targeting senescence or inflammation. An early phase 2 senolytic trial was negative overall, with only an exploratory signal in women with high senescent-cell burden. The aging secretome should therefore be viewed as an organizing framework whose individual pathways and relative contributions require further validation in human bone.

cards.title: Prognostic associations between patient-reported outcomes and progression-free and overall survival in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%: results from the RATIONALE-305 trial.
cards.abstract: In RATIONALE-305, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival (OS) versus placebo plus chemotherapy in advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC) with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor area positivity (TAP) score ≥ 5% and in all patients. Here, we present a three-component joint model (JM) developed to evaluate associations between patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and risk of progression-free survival (PFS) and OS events. Longitudinal PRO data were analyzed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22. The JM linked: (1) a linear mixed model (LMM) for change from baseline in PRO scores; (2) a Cox model for time to recurrent symptomatic deterioration (RS-D); and (3) a Cox model to evaluate the RS-D event frailty prediction of PFS and OS. 475 patients in the PD-L1 ≥ 5% subgroup (tislelizumab + chemotherapy, n = 238; placebo + chemotherapy, n = 237) were evaluated. In PFS and OS LMMs, tislelizumab + chemotherapy versus placebo + chemotherapy was associated with improved GHS/QoL (global health status/quality of life) (p = 0.01) and reduced dietary restrictions (p = 0.05). In the OS LMM, tislelizumab + chemotherapy was associated with reduced upper GI symptoms (p = 0.01) and reductions in dietary restrictions (p = 0.02). RS-D in GHS/QoL, pain, and dietary restrictions were leading predictors of PFS risk. Across all QLQ-C30 and QLQ-STO22 domains, tislelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly reduced the risk of progression or death (PFS HRs 0.55-0.65; 35-45% reduction) and death (OS HRs 0.65-0.73; 27-35% reduction); all p ≤ 0.01. PROs have significant prognostic value for disease progression and survival in patients with PD-L1 TAP score ≥ 5%. NCT03777657 ( http://clinicaltrials.gov ).

cards.title: AltORF-encoded microprotein recruits primary-ORF-encoded dehydrogenase to cell poles upon heat shock
cards.abstract: Alternative open reading frames (altORFs) initiating from in-frame or out-of-frame start sites within annotated protein-coding genes represent a largely unexplored source of protein-coding potential and remain poorly understood in terms of regulation, function, and impact on physiology. Here we investigate Escherichia coli GndA, encoded by an out-of-frame altORF within gnd, which encodes 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase. We observe that the GndA protein is induced by heat shock, consistent with the initial identification in a quantitative membrane proteomics screen, but is unstable, while the levels of the stable Gnd dehydrogenase are unchanged. Using translational fusion assays and in vivo RNA structure probing, we show that an internal complementary sequence upstream of gndA acts as a thermo-responsive secondary RNA structure controlling GndA translation. Mutagenesis of either gnd or gndA reduce heat shock survival of E. coli indicating both gene products are important for resistance. GndA fractionates with membranes consistent with in silico predictions that the protein forms an amphipathic -helix. In contrast, Gnd is predominantly cytoplasmic but shows GndA-dependent relocalization to cell poles upon heat shock. Together, our results demonstrate that an altORF-encoded microprotein is required for stress-dependent relocalization of its primary ORF partner, revealing a functional interplay between proteins encoded by overlapping ORFs in bacterial stress adaptation.

cards.title: In-silico Tandem Mass Spectral Libraries for the Blood Exposome and Metabolomics Workbench Databases: Application of Gemini Large Language Model
cards.abstract: Human body contains endogenous metabolites, nutrients and xenobiotics chemicals. These chemicals can be detected in a biospecimen using high-resolution mass spectrometry instruments, yielding metabolomic and exposomic datasets. Mass spectral libraries are critical components of these workflows to annotate experimental data with chemical information. In this data descriptor, we report mass spectral libraries for human-relevant small molecules, that are generated using Google Gemini large-language model. Using an optimized chain-of-thought prompt and instructions, we have generated mass spectra for each compound at high/medium/low energy fragmentation level. Each spectrum was reported in the NIST MSP text format for easy to use by metabolomics software. These libraries cover 91,231 unique 2D structures from the Blood Exposome Database and the Metabolomics Workbench data repository. Technical validation was shown by comparing the Gemini-generated spectra against NIST 23 mass spectral database, which demonstrated 55% accuracy. LLMs represent a useful and accessible tool for expanding in-silico spectral libraries to annotate compounds in the HRMS data for human biospecimens and may accelerate the compound annotation in metabolomics and exposomics.

cards.title: Increased EV yield and bioactivity of matrix-bound nanovesicles compared to conditioned culture medium-derived extracellular vesicles
cards.abstract: Aim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoparticles secreted by cells for cell-cell communication functions, such as wound repair, but low yields often limit their use. Several isolation methods have been explored to increase EV yield from conditioned culture medium (liquid-EVs); however, few studies compare isolation techniques and yield between liquid-EVs and matrix-bound nanovesicles (MBVs), a novel EV subtype embedded within the extracellular matrix. Methods: We isolate liquid-EVs and MBVs from mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) using size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and ultracentrifugation (UC) across various timepoints (14, 21, 24, 30 days). EVs are characterized by their yield, size, morphology, protein concentration, surface marker expression (CD9, CD81, ALIX), zeta potential, and influence on fibroblast wound closure. Results: We find that isolation method influences yield, where both SEC isolated liquid-EVs and MBVs yield higher particle counts and protein compared to UC. Interestingly, we find that regardless of isolation method, MBVs have a significantly higher yield than liquid-EVs from the same culture (15.6-fold higher using UC and 7.49-fold higher using SEC). Culturing for 24 days yielded the greatest number of MBV particles and protein. We performed a fibroblast scratch assay to assess bioactivity and found that liquid-EVs decreased wound closure compared to a medium control, whereas MBVs did not. Conclusion: Our work suggests SEC maximizes particle and protein yields for MSC-EVs. By achieving much higher yields of MBVs compared to liquid-EVs, and their promise as a wound repair strategy, we offer an alternative EV choice when EV yields are an issue towards translation.

cards.title: Mouse Neural Organoids Model the Mature In Vivo Synaptic Proteome
cards.abstract: Neural organoids represent a promising approach for modelling neural circuits and neurological disease, yet their utility depends on whether they can recapitulate the molecular complexity of mature brain synapses. Here, we optimized a protocol to generate mature forebrain organoids from mouse embryonic stem cells and used time-resolved proteomics to define the emergence of synaptic proteins during maturation. Using fluorescence-activated synaptosome sorting coupled with mass spectrometry, we quantified the synapse-enriched proteome and found a high correlation with matched in vivo synaptic proteomes. These findings demonstrate that complex mature synaptic molecular architecture is present within an in vitro organoid environment.

cards.title: Combined Anterior-Posterior vs. Posterior-Only Fusion in Adult Spinal Deformity Radiographic, Clinical, and Mechanical Outcomes With Longitudinal Mixed-Effects Analysis.
cards.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo compare radiographic, clinical, and mechanical outcomes of posterior-only versus combined anterior-posterior fusion in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients undergoing long-segment thoracolumbar fusion with pelvic fixation.MethodsConsecutive ASD patients undergoing instrumented fusion ≥7 levels with pelvic fixation at a single center (2016-2023) were stratified by surgical approach. Longitudinal radiographic changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation. Mechanical complications were evaluated with Kaplan-Meier survival and Cox proportional hazards analysis.Results207 patients were included (posterior-only, n=115; combined, n=92). Mean age was 62.1 ± 11.1 years (77.8% female), with mean follow-up of 46.2 ± 21.2 months. The combined approach demonstrated significantly greater DiD estimates for lumbar lordosis (-7.8° to -9.2°, all p<0.001), relative pelvic version mismatch (+3.4° to +4.2°, all p<0.001), and GAP score (-1.8 to -2.1, all p<0.001) at all postoperative timepoints. DiD estimates were stable across three covariate specifications. Rod fractures occurred in 14.8% of posterior-only versus 3.3% of combined patients (p=0.008), with superior rod fracture-free survival in the combined cohort (log-rank p=0.019). In the primary Cox model, the combined approach showed a non-significant trend toward lower rod fracture hazard (HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.10-1.24, p=0.10). Patient-reported outcomes improved comparably in both groups.ConclusionsIn long-segment ASD fusion with pelvic fixation, the combined anterior-posterior approach was associated with greater sustained sagittal correction and lower rod fracture rates, while both approaches provided comparable clinical improvement.

cards.title: Chemical proteomics suggests sofosbuvir is metabolically attached to proteins through a UMPylation-like pathway.
cards.abstract: Sofosbuvir is a pronucleotide prodrug (ProTide) that releases a uridine monophosphate analogue, which could modify proteins chemically or through UMP-transferring enzymes. cards.title: ChEBI-N - Enrichment Analysis with the ChEBI Ontology
cards.abstract: Introduction: Biological and chemical ontologies are structured representations that can be used to map entities such as metabolites onto broader chemical and biological categories. Enrichment analysis applied to such ontologies identifies classes whose representation within a set deviates from an expected background distribution, helping to interpret complex metabolomics measurements. Objectives: This study aimed to develop a tool for ChEBI (Chemical Entities of Biological Interest) ontology-based enrichment analysis, named ChEBI-N (ChEBI eNrichment). It is a successor of the previous tool BiNChE, with new features that broaden its applicability. Methods: We reimplemented BiNChE and extended it to accept SMILES or InChI strings as well as ChEBI IDs. These broaden applicability to datasets with entities that are not yet present in ChEBI. We also constructed organism-specific background populations. Results: We demonstrate the tool on three published metabolomics datasets covering wine, cheese, and human plasma samples. ChEBI-N correctly highlighted relevant enriched classes in all three datasets, such as flavonoids in the wine dataset and fatty acid classes in the cheese dataset. Comparing organism-specific and full-ChEBI backgrounds shows that restricted backgrounds reduce the inflated significance of generic classes, although the most enriched classes remain largely consistent. Conclusion: ChEBI-N is an extended successor to BiNChE for ontology-based enrichment analysis of metabolomics data, offering a hypothesis-generating complement to existing metabolomics analysis pipelines. Availability: ChEBI-N is freely available at chebin.hastingslab.org or as a Python package (pypi.org/project/chebin), with source code at github.com/ontology-tools/chebin, archived at Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23264219) and Software Heritage (swh:1:rev:133a41792704eb7f1db746f36a5ae97e9247b2b7).

cards.title: Predictors of Interfacility Transfer in Head and Neck Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Study.
cards.abstract: Traumatic head and neck (H/N) injuries frequently present to level III/IV trauma centers, yet many require care available only at higher-level facilities. This study aims to characterize transfer patterns in H/N trauma patients initially treated at level III/IV centers. The National Trauma Data Bank was queried for adults with H/N trauma initially presenting to level III/IV trauma centers between 2007 and 2015. Univariate analysis compared cohort characteristics, while multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors of transfer. In total, 18,454 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 5923 (32.1%) were transferred. Cut/piercing and striking injuries were associated with greater transfer odds (aOR: 1.328, 1.653), while motor vehicle trauma was associated with decreased odds (aOR: 0.845, 95% CI: 0.763-0.937). Transfer was associated with jaw dislocation (aOR: 1.871, 95% CI: 1.228-2.852) and H/N burns (aOR: 8.832, 95% CI: 7.131-10.940). Mandibular (aOR: 2.53, 95% CI: 2.19-2.93), skull base (aOR: 1.379, 95% CI 1.229-1.547), and malar/maxillary fractures (aOR: 1.314, 95% CI: 1.163-1.486) increased transfer odds, while nasal bone fracture decreased odds (aOR: 0.817, 95% CI: 0.741-0.901). Isolated H/N injury increased transfer odds (aOR: 1.379, 95% CI: 1.247-1.526). Transferred cohorts most commonly underwent diagnostic imaging and simple bedside procedures prior to transfer. Interfacility transfer is driven primarily by injury patterns rather than physiologic instability, likely reflecting anticipated need for subspecialty surgical intervention. Understanding injury-specific transfer predictors may optimize trauma systems and resource utilization while ensuring timely specialized care.

cards.title: Cost Analysis of Maxillofacial Trauma Treatment in Three Major Ministry of Health Malaysia Hospitals.
cards.abstract: Maxillofacial trauma imposes a considerable burden on healthcare systems. The Facial Injury Severity Scale (FISS) may help to estimate treatment complexity and healthcare resource requirements. However, evidence regarding its relationship with treatment costs and resource utilization in Malaysian public hospitals remains limited. To evaluate the relationship between FISS scores, treatment costs, and healthcare resource utilization among maxillofacial trauma patients treated in Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) hospitals. A retrospective multicenter cohort study included 132 adult patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) for maxillofacial fractures between January and December 2022 in 3 MOH hospitals. FISS scores were characterized as low (1-5), moderate (6-10), and high (>10) severity groups. Healthcare resource utilization was assessed using operating theatre (OT) duration, length of stay (LOS), and treatment cost. Treatment costs were estimated from the healthcare provider's perspective using a combination of activity-based and top-down costing approaches. Unadjusted differences across FISS groups were evaluated, and multivariable-adjusted general linear models were used to examine associations between FISS severity groups and each outcome after adjustment for age, gender, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), study site, and injury-to-OT time. Increasing FISS severity was associated with significantly longer OT duration (118 versus 135 versus 162 min; P<0.001), prolonged LOS (4 d versus 4 d versus 9 d; P=0.048), and higher treatment costs (RM 6564.47 versus RM 8065.28 versus RM 9830.90; P=0.003). After adjustment for age, gender, GCS, study site, and injury-to-OT time, significant differences across FISS categories remained for OT duration (P=0.001) and treatment cost (P=0.001), whereas the association with LOS was no longer statistically significant (P=0.201). Adjusted mean OT duration increased from 145.42 minutes in the low-FISS group to 220.94 minutes in the high-FISS group, while adjusted mean treatment cost increased from RM 7158.23 to RM 9552.91. The mean treatment cost per patient was RM 7592.43 ± 2364.14 (USD 1807.72 ± 562.89). Plating and screw costs (28.97%) and personnel costs (20.44%) were the largest contributors to treatment expenditure, while the operating theatre accounted for 60.18% of the total cost. Higher FISS scores were associated with greater healthcare resource utilization and treatment costs among maxillofacial trauma patients treated in MOH hospitals. After adjustment for relevant and institutional factors, higher FISS severity remained significantly associated with longer operative duration and higher treatment cost, whereas the association with LOS was attenuated. These findings support the potential use of FISS as a practical indicator of operative resource requirements and treatment expenditure in maxillofacial trauma care.

cards.title: A Tissue Virus Microenvironment with Activated Stress Responses Underlies Durable SIV Persistence
cards.abstract: HIV persistence during suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART) remains a central barrier to cure, with the majority of reservoirs residing in gut-associated lymphoid tissues (GALT). Here, we define a spatially organized viral microenvironment (VME) that sustains reservoir durability and governs early viral rebound by comparing animals initiating ART early after infection (transient reservoirs) versus late (persistent reservoirs). Using immunoPET/CT-guided sampling of SIV-infected rhesus macaques combined with spatial transcriptomics, we interrogated tissue sites of viral production during the eclipse phase following analytical treatment interruption (ATI). Our results revealed that viral rebound from persistent reservoirs arises from discrete, transcriptionally active foci enriched in the mucosa lining the gut lumen. Eclipse phase persistent reservoirs were characterized by increased proviral burden and a distinct tissue state marked by activation of stress-response, metabolic, mitochondrial, and cell cycle programs coupled to repression of cytoplasmic translation and increased cellular senescence. These features co-occurred with immunosuppressive cellular architectures resembling tertiary lymphoid structures enriched for Treg cells, innate lymphoid cells, and mast cells, regulated by Treg-centered cell-cell interaction networks. In contrast, transient reservoirs displayed enhanced translational and metabolic activity and were embedded within immune-active environments enriched for CD8+ T cells, Th17, Tfh, and activated CD4+ T cells. Machine learning identified stress adaptation, hypoxia, metabolic rewiring, and cytoskeletal remodeling pathways as dominant predictors of viral density within persistent VMEs, with strong convergence on programs observed in tumor microenvironments (TME). Orthogonal validation confirmed activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) at sites of viral production in concurrence with results of immunofluorescent microscopy revealing SIV gag expression in two populations primarily in the mucosa, differentiated by the phosphorylation of eIF2alpha. Together, these findings establish the VME as a critical determinant of reservoir persistence, integrating immune regulation, tissue remodeling, and translational control to enable viral survival. This framework suggests that effective HIV cure strategies will require coordinated disruption of VME-supportive functions in addition to targeting infected cells.
