cards.title: WISER: spectral whitening of fixed effects for improved breeding value estimation in structured, unbalanced, and genotype-environment-confounded populations
cards.abstract: This work introduces WISER (whitening and successive least squares estimation refinement), a whitening-based method designed to improve breeding value (BV) estimation by accounting for population structure and genetic covariance within experimental designs. WISER provides a generalized framework applicable across diverse experimental designs, species, and omics datasets, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), metabolomics, and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) used as phenomic predictors. Central to WISER is whitening, a statistical transformation that decorrelates variables and standardizes their variances. From a spectral perspective, WISER reweights the fixed-effect design according to the eigenspectrum of the genetic covariance matrix, attenuating dominant directions of genetic variation rather than explicitly correcting for a predefined subset of eigenvectors. This transformation aims to reduce confounding between genetic structure and environmental effects during BV estimation. WISER was evaluated across four species and 33 traits, including rice, maize, apple, and Scots pine, using several genomic prediction models and was compared with LS-means and BLUP-based BV estimation. Genomic predictive abilities based on WISER-estimated BVs consistently exceeded those obtained with LS-means and BLUP across the predictive models evaluated. These results support WISER as a flexible framework for BV estimation and downstream omics-based prediction in structured and unbalanced experimental populations. cards.title: Ctcf deficiency in myofibers induces pathological genome reprogramming toward the spontaneous development of myopathy
cards.abstract: How perennial, postmitotic multinucleated tissues, such as skeletal myofibers, maintain their identity and transcriptional adaptation to homeostatic perturbations through adult life is an outstanding question. To address this issue, we investigated the consequences of loss of 3D-genome architecture in skeletal muscles by generating myofiber-specific Ctcf-deficient (CtcfmKO) mice. CtcfmKO mice did not exhibit muscular phenotype at birth but spontaneously developed a severe myopathy. Integrated analysis of snRNAseq, ATACseq and promoter-capture Hi-C revealed both common and fiber-type specific patterns of dysregulated gene expression associated with alterations in chromatin accessibility and promoter-based interactions in Ctcf-deficient myonuclei at distinct stages of myopathy development. Decreased chromatin accessibility at promoters and changes in their connectivity with distal elements were observed across all myonuclei as a direct consequence of Ctcf deficiency at early stages and associated with downregulation of genes implicated in myofiber contraction and anabolism, metabolism, adhesion and neuromuscular transmission. Conversely, at later stages, upregulation of genes leading to persistent activation of ER stress/UPR and catabolism resulted from global reconfiguration of chromatin structure and connectivity, partly as indirect consequence of Ctcf deficiency. Notably, type-IIB myonuclei exhibited specific alterations in gene expression that culminated in loss of fiber-type identity and ectopic expression of inflammatory genes. These results reveal a requirement of Ctcf for maintenance of fiber-type identity and transcriptional adaptation in vivo, through multilayered control of 3D genome integrity. They also indicate an unprecedented association between Ctcf deficiency in myofibers and susceptibility to develop myopathies, whereby Ctcf dispensability for developmental myogenesis confers vulnerability to develop myopathic syndromes.

cards.title: Comment on "Inpatient mortality following hip fracture in the United States: an updated analysis of over one million cases".
cards.abstract: This commentary examines the statistical and methodological limitations of a recent national analysis of inpatient hip fracture mortality using the Epic Cosmos database. Four concerns are raised. First, the reported Spearman correlation between a four-category Social Vulnerability Index and mortality lacked statistical power because it was calculated across only four aggregated data points, and collapsing a continuous index into ordinal bins discarded patient-level variation needed to detect a dose-response relationship. Second, do-not-resuscitate status, documented in over one-third of patients, was omitted from the analysis of racial mortality differences, despite its direct influence on in-hospital mortality timing and its potential to confound comparisons unrelated to surgical risk. Third, the regional analysis reported the distribution of deaths across regions rather than region-specific mortality rates, conflating hospital volume with mortality risk. These limitations should be addressed before the reported demographic and regional patterns are used to guide resource allocation or clinical practice.

cards.title: Probabilistic forecasting of prefecture-level influenza in Japan accounting for surveillance data release histories
cards.abstract: Background. Public-health use of influenza surveillance - situational awareness, planning for clinical surge, and issuing advisories or warnings - needs more than an accurate point estimate of next week's count. What matters operationally is whether a rise is caught early, whether the direction of change is right, and whether an alert threshold is about to be crossed, all with honest uncertainty. For such use a forecast must also respect reporting delay, later data revision, and the calibration of its prediction intervals. Using Japan's sentinel surveillance, we evaluated short-term probabilistic forecasts that respect the data release history, and we measured what adding other surveillance series contributes, focusing on the properties that matter for public-health decisions. Methods. The target was the number of influenza reports per sentinel site in each of the 47 prefectures. For each forecast we predicted, as quantiles, the value 1-4 weeks after the most recent observed week. We compared three models: a ridge regression trained jointly across prefectures; a gradient-boosting quantile regression (GBQR) that learns from many surveillance series; and their equal-weight combination on the log scale. Six seasons were used to develop the models. The 2025/26 season was held out as a temporal evaluation period after the specification was fixed; because its epidemic profile had already been seen, it is not a fully independent prospective test. We scored forecasts with the weighted interval score (WIS) and checked prediction-interval coverage. For the Japanese target series we used the value first published for each week; some auxiliary series were taken as retrieved and therefore include later revisions. Results. In 2025/26, the combination's WIS relative to a persistence forecast was 0.841, 0.811, 0.794 and 0.818 at horizons of 1-4 observed weeks - that is, 16-21% lower than persistence. Coverage of the 80% prediction interval was 79.7%, 77.1%, 74.5% and 75.1%, and of the 95% interval 94.3%, 93.4%, 92.6% and 91.8%. Adding auxiliary series improved the GBQR over the development period. However, on the original scale the combination's edge over ridge regression was not statistically clear, and in some low-level rising phases the combination did worse than ridge. Conclusions. Over the period studied, models that share information across regions scored better than a persistence forecast. For public-health use, however, the operative questions are the real lead time once reporting delay is accounted for, whether rises from low levels and threshold exceedances are caught in time, and whether the upper prediction intervals are wide enough; on these, the present evidence is not yet sufficient. The 2025 change to the sentinel system also means that pre-change advisory and warning thresholds cannot be read mechanically. A prospective evaluation with strictly controlled data availability is needed before such forecasts are used to support advisories or planning.

cards.title: Mutation in Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum F1C1 cytochrome p450 homologue impairs virulence through root but not through shoot of tomato plants
cards.abstract: Ralstonia pseudosolanacearum causes a lethal bacterial wilt disease in many plants. The pathogen enters through roots and systemically colonizes the xylem tissue, resulting in wilting and eventual death of the host. Using transposon mutagenesis followed by screening in tomato seedlings, we identified a mutant exhibiting virulence deficiency by root inoculation, but not by leaf inoculation. The mutation was recreated in the wild-type genome via natural transformation to prove the linkage of virulence deficiency with the transposon insertion. Whole genome sequencing revealed that the transposon insertion was in a cyp450 homologue, encoding cytochrome P450 monooxygenase. Two independent targeted mutations were generated in the cyp450 gene, and both the mutants recapitulated the root-specific virulence deficiency. The mutants rarely cause disease in mature plants following soil drenching but remained fully virulent upon petiole pricking inoculation. Complementation with the full length cyp450 gene amplified from the wild-type strain F1C1 restored virulence in the mutant. Compared to the wild-type F1C1, the cyp450 mutants exhibited greater sensitivity to tomato root extracts. HR-LCMS of tomato root extracts revealed the occurrence of several antimicrobial compounds. Cytochrome P450 enzymes are known to mediate the degradation or biosynthesis of diverse metabolites in bacteria. Considering the virulence difference due to the mode of inoculation, our findings indicate that cyp450 contributes to tissue-specific adaptation of the pathogen during infection has opened an avenue for integrating tissue metabolomics with bacterial wilt susceptibility research.

cards.title: Delayed Multi-Compartment Traumatic Hernias After Blunt Abdominal Trauma: A Case-Based Review of Diagnosis and Staged Management.
cards.abstract: BackgroundTraumatic diaphragmatic hernias (TDHs) and traumatic abdominal wall hernias (TAWHs) are uncommon sequelae of blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) and may be missed during the initial evaluation. Delayed presentation can occur months to years later, resulting in incarceration, obstruction, or respiratory compromise.Case PresentationA 61-year-old woman presented 1 year after a motor vehicle collision with abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, and dyspnea. Computed tomography demonstrated an incarcerated left diaphragmatic hernia containing colon and omentum, along with a right flank hernia containing ascending colon. Review of prior imaging revealed a flank hematoma and subtle abdominal wall disruption at the time of initial injury. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic repair of the diaphragmatic hernia followed by elective robotic transabdominal preperitoneal repair of the flank hernia 2 months later.DiscussionThis case illustrates a pattern of delayed multi-compartment traumatic herniation resulting from thoracoabdominal force transmission. Diagnostic delays may occur because of competing priorities during polytrauma management, limitations of initial imaging, and delayed development of herniation, especially when the injuries are subtle. Findings such as rib fractures, pneumothorax, abdominal wall hematoma, and persistent symptoms should prompt continued surveillance.ConclusionDelayed multi-compartment traumatic hernias represent a diagnostic challenge requiring a high index of suspicion, longitudinal surveillance, and individualized management. A staged operative approach based on symptom severity and anatomic location can effectively address differing levels of clinical urgency.

cards.title: Stent-Graft Fracture 18 Years After Hybrid Repair of Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Possible Risk of Retrograde Reconstruction.
cards.abstract: We report the case of a patient who underwent hybrid repair for a type V thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. The procedure ensured durable aneurysm exclusion and visceral perfusion for 18 years. Eighteen years after surgery, the stent-graft fractured occurred at the visceral artery segment. Fluid-structure interaction analysis revealed a progressive elevation of von Mises stress at the eventual fracture site. Compared with in situ reconstruction, retrograde reconstruction in hybrid repair may increase the risk of stent-related complications. Monitoring von Mises stress during follow-up may help predict fracture and allow early intervention.Clinical ImpactLate stent-graft fracture after hybrid repair can occur despite effective aneurysm exclusion and satisfactory visceral perfusion. This case highlights the importance of long-term surveillance of graft integrity and changes in aortic morphology. A gradual increase in tortuosity and progressive elongation of the aorta may warrant particular attention, even many years after surgery. Fluid-structure interaction analysis linked progressive elevation of von Mises stress to the eventual fracture site and suggested that retrograde reconstruction may increase localized stress compared with in situ reconstruction. Integrating longitudinal imaging with patient-specific stress analysis may help clinicians recognize graft segments that warrant closer follow-up.

cards.title: Sense and Sensibility: Sensible Quality Control and Data Decision-Making in Passive Sensing Data for Adolescent Substance Use Risk Prediction
cards.abstract: Background: Passively collected smartphone and wearable data, combined with genomic information, may enable scalable early identification of youth who are at risk for substance use disorder. However, heterogeneous data collected in naturalistic settings limit researcher control over data quality, requiring substantial preprocessing. Data cleaning and feature engineering decisions can meaningfully influence analytic outcomes yet are often minimally described or omitted in published work. Objectives: We provide rationales and recommendations for common preprocessing challenges in passive sensing research, including establishing inclusion criteria when "outliers" may reflect true behavioral variability, analyzing differences across smartphone operating systems, handling observations collected outside protocol windows, and engineering features for machine learning applications. Methods: We illustrate principled approaches to these challenges using smartphone and Fitbit data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (ABCD). The sample was drawn from the available half of the year-4 follow-up (data release 5.1; N = 4,754; ages 13-14). Results: Extreme outlying observations were concentrated among low-engagement participants with few observed days. Smartphone usage among Apple users appeared under-recorded relative to Android users when compared with self-report measures. Fitbit-derived behavior differed systematically between observations collected within versus outside protocol windows. We also identified potential errors in the study's default preprocessing pipeline. Conclusion: We recommend prioritizing person-level inclusion criteria that preserve meaningful behavioral variability, examining temporal distributions rather than assuming observations are exchangeable, and thoroughly investigating and reporting data quality issues. Although illustrated using the ABCD Study, these principles broadly apply to research using smartphones, wearables, and other digital data sources.

cards.title: Ribosome-Associated GTPase Drg1 Links Cytosolic Translation to Mitochondrial Homeostasis
cards.abstract: Coordination of the functionalities among key organelles is essential for maintaining the complexity and adaptability of the eukaryotic cell. Functionally versatile proteins, such as GTPases, often assume important roles in this process. A ribosome-binding GTPase called Developmentally-regulated GTP-binding (Drg) protein is a conserved family of GTPases that promotes protein synthesis and regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, suggesting their importance for cell growth and proliferation. Mitochondrial proteostasis requires coordination between cytosolic translation and the targeting, import, and assembly of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins. However, the ribosome-associated factors that support this coordination remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the conserved GTPase Drg1, one of the two Drg paralogues in eukaryotic cells, as a translation factor required for mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular fitness. Human Drg1 and its cofactor Dfrp1 are associated with translating ribosomes and co-sedimented with polysomes. Deletion of Drg1 in HEK293T cells caused altered mitochondrial morphology, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and impaired expression of a mitochondrially targeted reporter. Re-expression of wild-type Drg1 restored ATP production and reporter expression, demonstrating that Drg1 is required for its cellular function. Mitochondria-directed APEX2 proximity proteomics further connected Drg1-dependent translation to proteins involved in mitochondrial protein import, respiratory-chain function, and mitochondrial protein synthesis. Reporter analyses indicated that Drg1 loss preferentially compromises productive translation toward the 3' region of the coding sequence. Together, these findings establish Drg1 as a ribosome-associated translation factor that supports the synthesis and homeostasis of proteins required for mitochondrial function. At the molecular level, loss of cellular homeostasis that is caused by compromised translation of cytoplasmically synthesized proteins functionally related to mitochondria underpins the observed phenomenon. Our results reveal a previously underappreciated connection between the cytosolic translation machinery and mitochondrial maintenance and provide a framework for understanding how defects in a conserved translational GTPase impair cellular energy metabolism and physiology.

cards.title: Use of routine clinical data in adults with chronic diseases for identifying risk of frailty: results from the UK Biobank study
cards.abstract: Frailty assessment is increasingly recommended for risk stratification in chronic disease management, but systematic clinical screening for frailty remains difficult to implement because it is resource-intensive. We investigated whether routinely collected clinical measures could be repurposed to prioritize adults with chronic diseases for clinical frailty assessment. We conducted a prediction study using UK Biobank data. A stacked ensemble model was developed using 12 routinely and low cost measured clinical variables to predict frailty. Gain metrics were used to quantify the proportion of frailty cases identified when screening was restricted to individuals with the highest predicted risk of frailty. We compared health profiles (mortality, polypharmacy, self-rated health, falls) of frail and non-frail individuals across different levels of predicted risk. The robustness of this screening strategy was evaluated across 3,284 modelling settings. Among 281,729 participants (mean age 57.9; 54.7% women) with at least one chronic condition, 5.8% were frail. In the validation sample (N validation=93,910, N training=187,819), screening only the 20% of participants with the highest predicted risk of frailty identified 55.6% of all frailty cases, corresponding to a 2.78-fold improvement compared to random screening. Overall, the model recovered 53.4% of the maximum achievable improvement over random screening. Frailty remained always associated with poor outcomes. Screening performance remained consistent across alternative modelling settings. Routinely collected clinical measures can improve the efficiency of frailty screening among adults living with chronic diseases by prioritizing individuals based on their level of risk. Since these data are already gathered during routine care, this risk-prioritization strategy could support scalable screening without increasing testing burden or clinical workload.

cards.title: Osteoporosis in Pediatric Orthopaedics: Congenital Diseases, Medical Management, and Perioperative Considerations.
cards.abstract: Pediatric osteoporosis is a heterogeneous group of primary and secondary disorders that creates challenges for orthopaedic surgeons. This review summarizes evidence on conditions commonly encountered in pediatric orthopedic practice, medical management strategies, and perioperative care for children with bone fragility. Diagnostic approaches have been evolving toward integrating fracture characteristics, skeletal risk factors, and bone mineral density (BMD). A single low-trauma vertebral compression fracture is now sufficient for diagnosis of osteoporosis in children regardless of BMD. Intravenous bisphosphonates remain first-line therapy, with recent meta-analyses confirming consistent BMD gains and, observationally, a reduction in fracture risk. Bisphosphonates are generally given to children who have sustained low-trauma vertebral fractures and considered for other children with recurrent long bone fractures with low BMD. Early intervention with bisphosphonates may also be warranted for children with high-risk diseases, such as Duchenne's Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Biologic agents are emerging in clinical trials and select specialized use, but further research is needed to understand their role in pediatric osteoporosis. Denosumab carries a substantial risk for rebound hypercalcemia in children with osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), limiting its use to selected indications. Preliminary reporting from a large trial of anti-sclerostin therapy in children with osteogenesis imperfecta suggests significant BMD increases while fracture-reduction endpoints were not met, underscoring the limitations of BMD as a surrogate in pediatric bone fragility trials. Providing optimal care for this unique group of patients requires multidisciplinary coordination amongst orthopaedic surgeons, endocrinologists, geneticists, and rehabilitation specialists. Evidence-based management includes preoperative bone health evaluation, procedure-specific modifications in fragile bone, nutritional optimization, and coordinated bisphosphonate timing.

cards.title: Acute-phase reaction and fracture outcomes from zoledronic acid: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Zoledronic acid (ZOL), an intravenous bisphosphonate used to treat osteoporosis, is frequently associated with the development of an acute-phase reaction (APR). Although some studies have reported that the APR may correlate with fracture outcomes, the evidence remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to investigate the association between the occurrence of an APR and fracture outcomes following ZOL therapy. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and ClinicalTrials.gov through April 2025 for observational studies and secondary analyses of randomized controlled trials in adults with osteoporosis. The primary outcome was the incidence of osteoporotic fractures. Secondary outcomes were mortality and changes in bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover markers (BTMs). The meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models and the certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Seven studies were included in the final analysis. No significant association was observed between APR and fracture risk (all fractures: odds ratio (OR) 0.79, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.19-3.26; vertebral fractures: OR 0.76, 95%CI 0.17-3.32). Similarly, no significant association was found between developing an APR and all-cause mortality, or changes in BMD, or BTMs. The certainty of the evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Current evidence is insufficient to establish a clear association between ZOL-induced APR and fracture risk, mortality, or BMD outcomes among patients with osteoporosis. To accurately capture potential associations, future large-scale prospective studies should enroll high-risk patients, including bisphosphonate-naïve individuals, and evaluate baseline BTMs and short-term mortality.

cards.title: Disentangling maternal pregnancy and fetal-specific plasma signatures through integrated proteomics and site-specific N-glycoproteomics
cards.abstract: During pregnancy, mother and fetus co-exist albeit as two physiologically distinct individuals, connected through the placenta and the umbilical cord. This connection allows for the exchange of vital substances, while individual blood homeostasis remains intact. We hypothesized that comparing maternal and cord plasma (N-glyco)proteomes would provide insights into the biological communication and unique physiological state of each individual. As comparing only matched maternal and umbilical cord blood plasma misses a crucial identifier in determining whether observed changes are related to infancy, pregnancy or both, we designed a triad study by adding a non-pregnant women control group. This allowed us to distinguish pregnancy-specific proteins and their potentially altered N-glycosylation from those in infancy. We found that the fetus and mother have distinct proteomes, N-glycoproteoforms and alternative complement regulation. Moreover, we observed that pregnancy in women led to specific N-glycosylation changes on a select set of primarily HDL-associated and acute-phase proteins. Lastly, our data provide evidence for an early fetal development of the humoral immune system as especially fetal IgM displayed distinctive N-glycosylation signatures.

cards.title: Verification Debt in Automated Biological Research Workflows: A Proof-of-Concept
cards.abstract: Recent biological research has shown significant interest and progress towards adoption of agentic AI systems. Domain specific agentic platforms with access to large collections of biological tools with code generation and/or querying capabilities, such as Biomni (illustrative case in point), are representative of the capability to orchestrate automated research workflows. Such platforms enable collaborative AI workspace for drug discovery, genomics, bioinformatics, literature research, and experimental planning for biologists and researchers. When such platforms are used for the aforementioned workflows, individually validating every agentic decision and the research process by which it was reached becomes challenging due to the scale of decisions involved and oftentimes, insufficient disclosure of assumptions and methodological choices, limited traceability of evidence, and interpretive judgments embedded throughout the workflow, giving rise to verification debt. Verification debt in agentic environments could result in unexpected failures and consequences in downstream experiments. This study focuses on empirical qualitative characterization of verification debt in agentic (prompt to outcomes) workflows. Biomni was chosen the testing AI agentic platform in this study mainly due to the descriptive traces it provides to track every agentic step. Verification debt is examined through two complementary angles: the individual agentic decision steps that carry claims and evidence, and the underlying research process by which the agent arrives at and reports them. This study attempts to characterize verification debt with 10 test cases (covering proteomics, genomics and drug discovery) with varying degree of biological nuance across three identical and independent runs. Verification debt is represented through 9 decision-step metrics and 13 research-process metrics, and also propose the VERIFY framework for evaluating scientific verifiability and validity in agentic workflows.

cards.title: Metabolic rewiring induces a viral mimicry-mediated quiescence in glioblastoma
cards.abstract: Glioblastoma is a highly aggressive brain tumour driven by therapy-resistant glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) that switch between dormant and proliferative states through poorly defined programs. In this study, we identify SAT1, encoding the rate-limiting polyamine-catabolic enzyme SSAT1, as enriched in quiescent GSCs, linking metabolic rewiring to dormancy. Pharmacologic induction of SSAT1 with the polyamine analogue N1,N11-Diethylnorspermine (DENSpm) triggers a chemoprotective, reversible growth arrest in patient-derived GSCs, independent of stemness, differentiation or senescence. SAT1-induced dormancy coincides with reduced eIF5A hypusination and global protein translation, and a marked rise in double-stranded RNA that activates type I interferon signalling. Knocking down the mitochondrial antiviral-signalling protein, essential for antiviral innate immunity, partially reverses this growth arrest, establishing viral mimicry as functionally required for dormancy. Single-cell and cohort analyses across GSCs and neural stem cells demonstrate that susceptibility to metabolically induced quiescence is set by an intrinsic inflammatory tone and lysosomal dependency, defining a context-dependent metabolic-immune axis which can be targeted to prevent GBM progression.

cards.title: Spatially distinct molecular and immune responses to ozone exposure during mutant surfactant protein-C-induced lung injury.
cards.abstract: Environmental exposure and genetic mutations are key factors in the pathogenesis and exacerbation of fibrosis. This work maps the distribution ozone (O3) signals and examines the impact of exposure in lung remodeling. Spatial transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were performed on CD68+ macrophages and CD45- non-immune cells from histologically distinct regions of air- or O3-exposed (0.8 ppm, 3 h) SP-C mutant lungs. Fibrosis was initiated by tamoxifen-mediated induction of a disease-linked Surfactant Protein (SP)-C gene mutation. The effects of O3 exposure prior or after SP-C induction were assessed via histology, flow cytometry, and immunohistochemistry. Multi-omics analysis of O3 injury revealed spatially restricted and cell-specific responses, characterized by mitochondrial metabolism and antioxidant pathway enrichment in injured-region macrophages, while peri-injured cells displayed pro-survival and lipid metabolism signatures. O3 exposure induced senescence and cell-cycle regulatory signals in all CD45- cells, with peri-injured exhibiting additional metabolic and collagen remodeling pathways. Proteomics showed widespread phospho-signaling in CD45- cells, an effect restricted to peri-injured areas in CD68+ macrophages. O3 exposure in fibrosing SP-C mutant mice caused Ly6Chi monocyte influx at 3 days but dampened the expansion of CD4+/CD8+ T cell observed in the O3 exposed uninduced lung. Fibrotic remodeling, cell proliferation (Ki67), and immune composition were not influenced by O3 exposure at 7 days, though their combination increased mouse mortality and inflammatory cell activation (iNOS). These data identify O3 exposure as a modifier of regional inflammatory and stress-response pathways with modest effects on disease progression in the SP-C mutant lung.

cards.title: Proteomics of highly post-translationally modified proteins in kidney tubulointerstitium
cards.abstract: Kidney disease affects over 850 million people and leads to degradation of the kidney cortical compartments and kidney failure. Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA) is a universal feature of chronic kidney disease, yet the sequence of tubulointerstitial matrix protein (matrisome) changes that underlie the development and progression of IFTA are not fully understood. In particular, post-translational modifications which may stabilize key matrisome components and result in irreversible and functionally detrimental interstitial fibrosis or tubular basement membrane thickening, have yet to be characterized. Post-translational modifications (e.g., acetylation) have been shown to contribute to kidney diseases, yet they have not been investigated in chronic kidney disease progression. Herein, we established feasibility of matrisome protein quantification in the tubulointerstitium, with concurrent matrisome protein post-translational modification quantification, in archived diagnostic human kidney biopsies, using laser capture microdissection, liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and bioinformatics analysis. In this pilot study, we focused on two conditions associated with IFTA progression: diabetic nephropathy and kidney transplantation. We examined both healthy and chronically damaged tubulointerstitium in two human kidney biopsies, one representing each condition. We identified signature protein markers of tubulointerstitium (e.g., UMOD, SLC12A1) in abundance, confirming sample composition, and observed uniformity in protein abundance across replicates from the same biopsies. We found increases in certain collagen isoforms (COL1A1, COL6A3) and other ancillary proteins in areas of IFTA. We also successfully quantified post-translational modifications, confirming that hydroxylproline was the most abundant modification in healthy tubulointerstitium from the kidney transplant biopsy, and that hydroxyllysine was also highly abundant and could be confidently quantitated on two collagen isoforms (COL1A1, COL4A2). Lastly, we performed power analysis to determine the required sample size to achieve significant power and false discovery rate. Several proteins exhibited large Hedge effect sizes in the tubulointerstitium (ANPEP, PRODH2), indicating their potential usefulness as fibrosis signatures. Our study is a first step toward comprehensive characterization of tubulointerstitial matrisome changes, including post-translational modifications seen with IFTA progression. Subsequent studies will potentially reveal new molecular markers of key early events in chronic kidney disease progression, and new therapeutic targets for mitigating this process. Data are available via ProteomeXchange identifier PXD079025.

cards.title: Cell-specific isolation and functional analysis of primary cardiomyocyte-derived large extracellular vesicles from infarcted mouse hearts
cards.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles secreted by all cells and serve as critical mediators of intercellular communication in both physiological and pathological contexts. However, elucidating the precise functions of endogenous EVs remains challenged by a fundamental technical bottleneck: current isolation methodologies depend on shared physical properties or generic surface markers, preventing the selective enrichment of cell-type-specific EVs within complex tissues. Consequently, EVs recovered from biofluids or tissue extracts represent heterogeneous populations, confounding the direct attribution of biochemical signatures and biological activities to distinct cellular origins. Here, we describe a versatile genetic-labeling and affinity-based purification strategy that enables the selective isolation of cell-specific primary EV. Using cardiomyocyte-derived EV (CM-EVs) as a proof-of-concept, we crossed Myh6-Cre mice with the ROSA26-mTmG reporter line to restrict membrane-targeted GFP expression to cardiomyocytes. Following myocardial infarction, cardiac EV were recovered and GFP-positive CM-EVs were selectively purified by anti-GFP nanobody-based magnetic pulldown. This approach yields highly enriched, functional cardiomyocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (CM-EVs). To accommodate diverse analytical needs, we established two distinct elution workflows: (i) a denaturing protocol optimized for downstream proteomics and immunoblotting, and (ii) a gentle, non-denaturing protocol that preserves vesicle integrity and biological activity for downstream in vitro and in vivo functional assays. Using this method, we characterized CM-EVs size distribution and proteomic signature, and demonstrated their capacity to transfer functional cargo to target cells in vitro. Because the purification approach relies solely on targeting a genetically restricted membrane tag rather than assumed surface markers, it is immediately adaptable to virtually any cell type for which a validated Cre driver exists. This method removes a long-standing bottleneck in EV research and provides a broadly applicable platform for deciphering the biochemical composition and in-vivo functions of cell-type-specific primary EV in physiological and pathological settings.

cards.title: Structural streamlining of axonemal doublet microtubules in Plasmodium male gametes
cards.abstract: Male gametogenesis in malaria parasites produces up to eight flagellated gametes within approximately 15 min, requiring de novo construction of motile axonemes on an unusually short timescale. Here we combine cellular cryo-electron tomography, high-resolution cryo-EM, proteomics, and parasite genetics to define the molecular architecture and assembly states of the Plasmodium male gamete axoneme. The doublet microtubules retain the principal surface-associated motility modules but contain a markedly reduced luminal microtubule inner protein network. Their inner junction lacks PACRG and is instead organized by CFAP20 and CFAP52, whose combined loss disrupts doublet integrity and exflagellation. We further identify a calmodulin protein at the outer dynein arm docking region and show that outer dynein arms accumulate progressively during gametogenesis. These findings establish distinct form of axonemal remodeling in Plasmodium and reveal the ordered assembly of structural and motor modules during rapid male gamete formation.

cards.title: Clinical Outcomes of an Improved Arthroscopic Suture-Bridge Technique Assisted by a "5 O'clock" Portal for Acute Bony Bankart Lesions.
cards.abstract: Bony Bankart lesion is a primary cause of traumatic shoulder instability. Although the arthroscopic suture bridge technique has been applied clinically, its operative complexity remains a challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term clinical and radiological efficacy of a modified suture bridge technique combined with anchor insertion through a "5 o'clock" accessory portal for treating acute bony Bankart lesions. This study retrospectively analyzed 36 patients with acute bony Bankart lesions who underwent the modified surgical treatment between January 2019 and February 2023. All patients were followed up for at least 2 years. Preoperative and final follow-up assessments included VAS, Constant-Murley, ASES, UCLA, and Rowe scores, as well as shoulder range of motion (ROM). Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-tests to compare preoperative and postoperative clinical scores and ROM. Fracture reduction and healing were assessed via CT 3D reconstruction at 6 months postoperatively. The mean follow-up period was 28.8 months. At the final follow-up, all clinical functional scores and ROM showed significant improvement compared to the preoperative status (p < 0.001). CT 3D reconstruction at 6 months postoperatively showed successful reduction of the fracture fragment in all patients. The mean glenoid bone loss decreased from 18.2% ± 6.5% preoperatively to 2.5% ± 1.5% at follow-up (p < 0.001). The fracture healing rate was 97.2%. Eighty percent of patients successfully returned to a pre-injury or higher level of sport. The redislocation rate was 2.8%, and the total complication rate was 5.6%. The modified suture-bridge technique using a "5 o'clock" accessory portal is a reliable and reproducible method for treating acute bony Bankart lesions. This approach achieves anatomical fracture reduction and yields excellent mid-term clinical and radiological outcomes with a low risk of complications.

cards.title: Fracture Risk Stratification by REMS: A 5 Years Prospective Longitudinal Multicentre Study.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass and deterioration of bone microarchitecture. Current predictive tools, mainly based on DXA-BMD, do not full capture all the factors contributing to bone deterioration. By combining information on bone quantity (T-score) and skeletal fragility (Fragility Score, FS), the Radiofrequency Echographic Multi-Spectrometry provides an integrated measure of fracture susceptibility known as fracture risk stratification. We aimed To evaluate the ability of REMS fracture risk stratification through a 5 years prospective longitudinal multicentre study. A non-parametric Mann-Whitney test was used to assess differences of REMS T-score and FS between fractured and non-fractured patients. Additionally, Chi-squared tests, Cochran-Armitage trend tests, class-specific unadjusted logistic regressions and standardized residual analyses were performed to evaluate the proposed stratification model. A total of 4443 female patients was recruited and n = 4017 underwent REMS scans. The Chi-squared and the Cochran-Armitage trend tests showed that the distribution of fractured patients differed across the 7 risk classes with a strong positive monotonic trend at lumbar spine (Z = 47.83; p < 0.0001) and femoral neck (Z = 75.41; p < 0.0001). From a clinical perspective, both Class-specific binary logistic regression and standardized residuals clearly identified two opposite risk profiles: patients belonging to the low-risk classes exhibited a significantly reduced probability of fracture, whereas those in the high-risk classes showed a markedly increased fracture risk. This 5-year longitudinal study supports the clinical consistency of a REMS composite approach for fracture risk stratification based on the integration of REMS BMD T-score and Fragility Score.

cards.title: Effects of Drought, Followed by Waterlogging, on Biomass, Leaf Physiology and Chemistry of Wheat Partly Depend on Fertilisation
cards.abstract: Drought and waterlogging are prominent climate change challenges that, alone or in sequence, pronouncedly constrain agricultural crop production. A better understanding of relationships between water availability and nutrition regarding plant functioning is needed to optimise fertilisation under these challenges. We investigated impacts of drought, waterlogging and drought followed by waterlogging under two fertilisation regimes (low, normal) on various traits of wheat (Triticum aestivum). Next to biomass and photosynthesis measurements, cross-platform metabolomics was applied for in-depth metabolic analyses of flag leaves. We found detrimental effects of drought and drought-waterlogging on shoot and root biomass, especially at normal fertilisation, while photosynthetic traits were not or only slightly affected. Foliar nitrogen contents were higher in plants exposed to drought or to drought-waterlogging. Numerous primary and specialised metabolites were modulated by fertilisation and/ or watering. In particular, amino acids, benzoxazinoids and flavonoids were affected by fertilisation. Due to watering especially several amino acids changed in concentrations, with the induction pattern partly depending on fertilisation. Our study deepens the understanding of the interplay between water and nutrient availabilities as well as nutritional demands, growth and metabolism of wheat. This is highly relevant to balance sustainable agricultural nutrient management under the challenges of ongoing climate change.

cards.title: An integrated experimental-computational framework for elasto-plastic characterization and spatial mapping of canine bone properties.
cards.abstract: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental-computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load-displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

cards.title: Targeting the gut-bone axis in osteoporosis: probiotic interventions and other microbiota-based therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic bone metabolic disorder characterized by impaired bone homeostasis and increased fracture susceptibility. With the rapid aging of the global population, the number of fractures related to osteoporosis continues to increase, along with persistently high rates of disability and mortality, thereby imposing a huge and constantly growing burden on the healthcare system. Emerging evidence indicates that probiotics, as key regulators of host metabolic and immune networks, play critical roles in the pathogenesis, progression, and therapeutic modulation of OP. Through a bidirectional regulatory network known as the gut-bone axis, probiotics influence the dynamic balance between bone formation and bone resorption via multiple interconnected mechanisms, including immune modulation, microbial metabolite production, intestinal barrier integrity, and endocrine signaling. Recent animal and clinical studies further demonstrate that targeted modulation of the gut microbiota to restore gut-bone axis homeostasis can significantly improve bone mineral density and related skeletal parameters, highlighting the translational potential of probiotic-based interventions. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which probiotics regulate bone metabolism and places particular emphasis on emerging microbiota-based mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, with a specific focus on probiotics, aiming to provide a theoretical framework and future translational directions for the development of innovative microbiota-based treatments for OP.

cards.title: Osteoporosis medication initiation after proximal humerus fractures is low, but associated with decreased secondary fragility fracture risk.
cards.abstract: To 1) identify factors associated with osteoporosis medication (OPM) prescription after proximal humerus fractures and 2) evaluate rates of secondary osteoporotic fragility fracture (OFF) between patients treated with OPM vs those who were not. Retrospective cohort analysis. TriNetX Health Research Network. Patients aged 60 years or older who sustained a proximal humerus fracture (PHF) (OTA/AO 11) between 2005 and 2025 were categorized into groups based on if they were or were not prescribed OPM within 1 year after a PHF. The primary outcome was prescription of OPM after PHF. Patient demographics were assessed between patients who were or were not prescribed OPM. Pairwise comparisons of proportions were performed using two-proportion Z-tests with Bonferroni correction. A matched cohort analysis was conducted to assess rates of secondary OFF after PHF. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios (OR). A total of 180,304 patients with PHFs were identified, with 6627 (3.7%) patients prescribed OPM after a PHF. Female patients were more likely to be prescribed OPM (84.6% vs 68.0%, P < 0.001). Black patients were less likely to be prescribed OPM (2.7% vs 5.1%, P < 0.001). After matching, patients who were prescribed OPM after a PHF had a decreased 1-year mortality rate (OR = 0.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.66-0.94; P = 0.008) and lower rate of secondary fragility fractures (OR = 0.63, 95% confidence interval, 0.56-0.72; P < 0.001). Osteoporosis medications are not commonly initiated after geriatric PHFs. OPM initiation after PHF was associated with lower rates of secondary OFF and 1-year mortality. Level III, Prognostic.

cards.title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
cards.abstract: To evaluate the impact of estrogen hormone therapy on venous thrombotic events for femoral neck fractures treated with either total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA). Retrospective cohort analysis. TriNetX Health Research Network. Patients who sustained a femoral neck fracture (OTA/AO 31B) between 2005 and 2025 who were treated with either THA or HA were categorized into groups based on whether they were prescribed systemic estrogen hormone therapy (EHT) within 3 months before or after their fracture. The primary outcomes were deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 3 months after their fracture. A matched cohort was created after a 1:1 propensity match for demographics, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios. A total of 39,631 patients with femoral neck fractures treated with either a THA or HA were identified. Of these, 330 (0.8%) patients with femoral neck fractures were prescribed estrogen within 3 months before or after their fracture. After a matched cohort comparison, there were no statistically significant differences in rates of PE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-3.03; P = 0.525) or for DVT (OR = 1.67; 95% CI, 0.78-3.61; P = 0.184). Systemic EHT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of DVT or PE after operatively treated femoral neck fractures with THA or HA. Level III, Prognostic.

cards.title: The potential of psychological intervention to decrease the risk of anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis.
cards.abstract: Emotional distress in pulmonary fibrosis remains under-recognised and poorly addressed. This study assessed changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms following an individualised psychological intervention. Single-centre, single-arm before-and-after observational study of an individualised psychological intervention delivered in routine ILD care, combining acceptance and commitment therapy, humanistic-existential techniques, and psychophysiological interventions. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) before and after the intervention. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience measures (PREMs) were collected. Response was analysed across characteristics defined before any analysis of outcome data (age, sex, disease severity [ILD-GAP], frailty [CFS], time since diagnosis, and baseline HADS). Thirty patients were included (50.0% women; mean age 71.0 years). At baseline, 76.7% scored ≥8 on HADS-anxiety and 76.7% on HADS-depression, indicatingclinically relevant symptom risk. Six patients discontinued (lung transplantation, palliative care, or death; n = 2 each). Among 24 evaluable patients, mean HADS-anxiety decreased from 11.3 to 6.6 (mean difference 4.7; 97.5% CI 2.6-6.9; p < 0.001) and HADS-depression from 10.7 to 5.5 (mean difference 5.2; 97.5% CI 3.2-7.2; p < 0.001). HADS-anxiety score improved in 19 patients, was unchanged in 3 and worsened in 2; HADS-depression score improved in 20, was unchanged in 2 and worsened in 2. No patient worsened in HADS category. No differences in response were detected by age, sex, disease severity, frailtyor time since diagnosis. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience scores were high (totalscore 9.4 [SD 0.7] in patients and 9.5 [SD 0.7] in caregivers). In this uncontrolled study, an individualised psychological intervention was associated with reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms and a lower proportion of patients at risk of clinically relevant anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis. These findings suggest the potential of psychological care within routine ILD follow-up and require confirmation in randomised controlled trials.

cards.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
cards.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

cards.title: Preoperative Frailty as a Predictor of Quality of Life Outcomes Following Cytoreductive Surgery.
cards.abstract: Frailty has emerged as a critical determinant of postoperative risk in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS + HIPEC). However, its impact on postoperative quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative frailty and postoperative QoL in patients undergoing CRS + HIPEC. This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital between May 2017 and June 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), with patients classified as frail (CFS ≥ 4) or non-frail (CFS < 4). QoL outcomes were evaluated using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5 L) and Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey at five time points. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years). Of the 364 included patients, 49 (13.5%) were classified as frail. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes, particularly in mobility, self-care, usual activities, and physical component summary (PCS) scores (all p ≤ 0.003) at baseline. These impairments persisted at three and 6 months postoperatively. Pain and discomfort also emerged as significant issues for frail patients at both three- and 6-months following surgery (p = 0.018 and p = 0.005, respectively). Older frail patients (≥ 65 years) experienced significantly greater impairments in self-care and usual activities at 6 months postoperatively, along with lower mental health summary (MCS) scores at 12 months compared to the non-frail group. Preoperative frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes following CRS + HIPEC, highlighting the importance of routine frailty screening and prehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes in vulnerable patients.

cards.title: Mortality and healthcare utilization after proximal humeral fractures in patients aged 65 years and older: a register-based cohort study.
cards.abstract: Proximal humeral fractures are associated with substantial pain, impaired mobility, and reduced quality of life, yet no widely accepted guidelines for post-fracture care exist. This study investigates one-year mortality and identifies pre-fracture risk factors associated with mortality. Further, it examines changes in healthcare utilization and associated risk factors across hospitals, municipalities, and primary care before and after the fracture. Patients aged ≥65 years with proximal humeral fracture were identified from the CROSS-TRACKS cohort. One-year mortality was analysed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression, adjusting for sex, age, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), civil status, and residential status. Changes in hospital contacts, municipal services, and primary care contacts were assessed using paired t-tests, and their associations with sex, age, CCI, civil status, and residential status were examined using multiple linear regression. One-year mortality was 11.6% (95% confidence interval (CI) 10.8; 12.3). Male sex, older age, higher CCI, unmarried status, and nursing home residency were associated with increased mortality. From the year before to the year after the fracture, hospital contacts increased by a mean of 2.1 (95% CI: 2.0; 2.3), municipal services by 339.1 (95% CI: 294.6; 383.5), and primary care contacts by 4.4 (95% CI: 3.9; 4.8). Older age and higher CCI were associated with increased healthcare utilization. Patients with proximal humeral fractures had high one-year mortality and increased healthcare utilization. Older age and high CCI were associated with both outcomes. These findings highlight the need for standardized, evidence-based protocols with patient-centred principles for this frail population.

cards.title: The role of the CYP1A1 gene in long-term glucocorticoid-related adverse effects.
cards.abstract: CYP1A1 gene variants may influence the development of AE of chronic GC treatment. The rs1799814 polymorphism was associated with increased BMI and lower levels of bone turnover markers, independent of GC dose, suggesting reduced GC metabolism. No association was found with OP and/or Fx, BMD or TBS values. Long-term glucocorticoid (GC) use can produce adverse effects (AE) including obesity, diabetes, osteoporosis and fractures. The variability in AE severity suggests a genetic influence. CYP1A1, a cytochrome P450 family enzyme involved in GC metabolism, may play a role. This study aimed to genotype CYP1A1 variants in patients on chronic GC treatment and analyse their relationship with long-term AE. Seventy patients (56 ± 16.6 years; 71.4% female; 47.1% postmenopausal) receiving chronic GC treatment ( ≥5 mg/ day for >3 months) were included. Clinical data were collected at baseline and at 5 years of follow-up, including OP risk factors, previous and incidental fractures, GC dose and duration, disease activity, anthropometric data, bone metabolism parameters, bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular bone score (TBS) (by DXA), and vertebral fractures (X-ray). CYP1A1 gene sequencing was performed by NGS using Amplicon Deep Sequencing on an Ion Torrent platform. Four CYP1A1 polymorphisms were identified: rs41279188, rs1048943, rs1799814 and rs4646422. Nine patients had rs1048943, nine rs1799814, one rs4646422 and one rs41279188 polymorphisms, respectively. Patients with the rs1799814 polymorphism (13%) had higher BMI (29.3 vs. 25.5; p = 0.019) and greater BMI change over 5 years (ΔBMI: 1.7 vs. -0.32; p = 0.02; adjusted for cumulative GC dose). Additionally, they presented lower bone turnover markers (NTx: 21 vs. 40 nMol/mMol, p = 0.003, CTx: 0.16 vs. 0.29 ng/mL, p = 0.068, OC: 16.6 vs. 19.3 ng/mL, p = 0.059). No associations were found between CYP1A1 polymorphisms and the presence of osteoporosis and/or fractures, BMD or TBS values. The CYP1A1 rs1799814 polymorphism is associated with more severe GC-related AE, suggesting reduced GC metabolism.

cards.title: Homocitrulline and 3-year mortality in older hospitalised adults: an exploratory study.
cards.abstract: Reliable biomarkers may allow early risk stratification for mortality in older adults. Post-translational modification-derived products (PTMDPs), such as homocitrulline, and the tissue accumulation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), measured by skin autofluorescence, have been suggested as potential biomarkers of adverse outcomes in older and frail individuals. The aim of this study was to assess their association with 3-year mortality following hospitalisation. We followed a cohort of 250 hospitalised patients over 3 years. Serum PTMDPs (homocitrulline, carboxymethyllysine, pentosidine, and MG-H1) were measured using liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry, and AGEs were quantified by skin autofluorescence. We examined associations with mortality using bivariable analyses and a multivariable Cox regression model. An exploratory cut-off for homocitrulline was established at the third quartile of its distribution within the study population. During follow-up, 92 deaths occurred. In bivariable analyses, all biomarkers were associated with mortality. In the multivariable model, homocitrulline levels of >400 μmol/mol Lys were significantly associated with mortality (hazard ratio 1.73, 95 % confidence interval 1.06-2.82), after adjustment for age, frailty, and comorbidities. The model's predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76, was only slightly affected by the exclusion of homocitrulline (AUC=0.755). These results indicate that although elevated homocitrulline was independently associated with mortality, its incremental value for risk prediction was modest. Larger studies are needed to further evaluate the clinical utility of PTMDPs, especially homocitrulline, for risk prediction and clinical decision-making.

cards.title: "Metabolic Diets and Fasting in Oncology: Integrating Guideline-Based Nutrition, Nutrition Assessments and Biomarker-Driven Clinical Pathology".
cards.abstract: Popular narratives often promote "special diets" as strategies to cure cancer, frequently invoking autophagy and Nobel-related discoveries. In contrast, international oncology nutrition guidelines state that no diet has been proven to reproducibly cure cancer. This review integrates guideline-based oncology nutrition, experimental metabolic diets and a biomarker-driven clinical pathology perspective within a translational framework. This narrative review synthesizes international and national oncology nutrition guidelines and clinical evidence on fasting, fasting-mimicking diets, time-restricted eating, intermittent fasting, Ramadan fasting and ketogenic diets in cancer. Priority was given to randomized and prospective trials, systematic reviews and selected mechanistic studies, with attention to nutritional risk, toxicity, metabolic and inflammatory markers, body composition, cachexia staging and pathological response. Current guidelines discourage restrictive diets outside evidence-based care and recommend early nutritional screening and stepwise nutrition support. Clinical studies suggest that fasting-related regimens and ketogenic diets may improve selected metabolic, hematological, quality-of-life and pathological endpoints in carefully selected patients, but reproducible survival benefit has not been established. Cachexia-oriented models indicate that cancer-related nutritional decline is multidimensional and partly integrates biochemical, inflammatory, functional and patient-reported domains. Mechanistic studies support plausible effects on autophagy, nutrient-sensing pathways, ketone metabolism, inflammation and the tumor microenvironment. The evidence supports a clear distinction between guideline-based oncology nutrition, which is fundamental supportive care, and metabolic diets or fasting regimens, which remain experimental adjuncts rather than curative treatments. The translational opportunity lies in embedding these interventions within malnutrition-, sarcopenia- and cachexia-aware frameworks and using biomarkers to improve risk stratification, patient selection and mechanistic interpretation.

cards.title: Vitamin D Deficiency and Up to 10-Year Risk of Incident Cataract in Adults Aged ≥50: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Age-related cataracts are a leading cause of blindness, and their prevalence increases markedly after age 50. Vitamin D may help maintain lens homeostasis, but evidence linking vitamin D deficiency (VDD) to cataract risk remains limited. We examined the association between VDD and incident age-related cataract during a follow-up of up to 10 years. This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Patients with persistent VDD (two serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels ≤19.90 ng/mL) were 1:1 propensity score-matched with those with sufficient levels (≥30.00 ng/mL), with a two-year landmark period. The primary outcome was incident age-related cataract. The secondary outcomes included cataract surgery and all-cause mortality. Positive and negative control outcomes were assessed as complementary evaluations of potential bias. Each matched cohort included 233,425 patients. VDD was associated with a higher risk of incident age-related cataracts (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.65-1.78; p<0.001). Cataract surgery (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.67-1.90; p<0.001) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.45-1.52; p<0.001) were also more frequent in the VDD group. The positive control (osteoporotic fracture, HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.51-1.83) supported exposure validity, whereas the negative control (diseases of the appendix) showed no significant association (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.97-1.16; p=0.180). After additional adjustment for pre-index ophthalmological service utilization, the association remained (adjusted HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.62-1.70). In an exploratory analysis, vitamin D insufficiency was also associated with incident cataract (HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.51-1.62). Sensitivity analyses showed attenuated but persistent associations when restricting the study period to 2016-2023 (HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.39-1.53) and to patients with documented pre-index ophthalmological service utilization (HR 1.39, 95% CI 1.27-1.52). VDD was associated with an increased up to 10-year risk of incident age-related cataracts in adults aged ≥50 years. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

cards.title: Cystathionine beta-synthase alleviates intervertebral disc degeneration by inhibiting ferroptosis of nucleus pulposus cells via the PI3K-AKT Axis.
cards.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is the leading cause of low back pain, affecting 619 million people worldwide in 2020, yet no effective disease-modifying therapy is clinically available to reverse its progression. Ferroptosis has been proven to be a core driver of IVDD by inducing injury to nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs). The regulatory role of cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) in IVDD and its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the biological function of CBS in IVDD and elucidate the mechanism by which it regulates NPC ferroptosis. We found that CBS expression was significantly downregulated in degenerated human NP tissues and rat IVDD models and was negatively correlated with degeneration severity and ferroptosis activation. Functional assays showed that CBS knockdown markedly exacerbated TBHP-induced matrix metabolic imbalance, senescence, and ferroptosis in NPCs, while CBS overexpression effectively alleviated these pathological phenotypes. Transcriptomic analysis, biochemical validation, and pharmacological inhibition experiments implicated PI3K-AKT signaling in the ferroptosis-related effects associated with CBS modulation in NPCs. In vivo, S-Adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) administration attenuated needle puncture-induced IVDD in rats, restored disc height and NP water content, and suppressed intradiscal ferroptosis. Because SAM has pleiotropic biological actions, these in vivo effects cannot be attributed exclusively to CBS. Collectively, our findings support a protective role for CBS against IVDD through suppression of NPC ferroptosis and implicate PI3K-AKT signaling as a contributing pathway.

cards.title: Osteoporosis Screening Gaps Among Patients Undergoing Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is associated with elevated complication rates after lumbar fusion surgery. Despite this, osteoporosis remains both underscreened and undertreated in the United States. Currently, rates of dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DEXA) screening before lumbar fusion surgery are unknown, as is the proportion of patients who, after being diagnosed with osteoporosis, receive appropriate treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess osteoporosis screening and treatment rates among patients undergoing lumbar fusion surgery. Patients older than 50 years undergoing lumbar fusion for lumbar stenosis with degenerative spondylolisthesis were identified using the TriNetX database. Patients receiving surgery for indications of malignancy or infection, as well as those with diagnoses of osteoporosis before the screening window, were excluded. The prevalence of DEXA scans in the 2 years before fusion was calculated for the overall cohort and for high-risk cohorts defined by Endocrinology Society guidelines. A secondary analysis assessed rates of osteoporosis treatment among patients receiving preoperative DEXA scans. Of 46,104 patients who underwent lumbar fusion surgery, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a preoperative DEXA scan in the 2 years before their fusion. Women were more likely to receive DEXA scans than men (OR, 3.93; 95% CI, 3.64 to 4.23; P < 0.001). Only 5.6% of high-risk men and 17.5% of high-risk women received preoperative DEXA screening. Among patients diagnosed with osteoporosis after DEXA screening, only 11.0% received anabolic therapy and 23.1% received antiresorptive therapy. Despite most patients undergoing lumbar fusion being at risk of osteoporosis (and eligible for screening), a small minority were screened using DEXA in the 2 years before surgery. Efforts are warranted to increase the prevalence of DEXA screening so that osteoporosis is appropriately diagnosed and treated before lumbar fusion surgery.

cards.title: Comorbidities and outcomes associated with young adult hip fracture: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: The prognosis of hip fracture in younger adults (YAs) aged 18-50 years is unestablished. Large studies that rigorously assess risk factors for hip fracture in YAs, their associated functional outcomes and mortality are lacking. While international guidelines recommend comprehensive bone health assessment and consideration of pharmacotherapy in YAs with major fragility fractures, rates of implementation of these guidelines are unknown. We systematically reviewed the existing literature on YAs with hip fracture to identify (1) clinical risk factors for hip fracture, (2) functional outcomes beyond 12 months from hip fracture (including employment and mortality) and (3) referral rates for bone health assessment. Forty-four studies were included from 1875 eligible abstracts. Twenty-three studies reported data on question 1. Psychiatric disease (15% [10-23%]), glucocorticoid exposure (5% [2-14%]), psychotropic exposure (12% [3-42%]), alcohol excess (15% [6-38%]) and cigarette smoking (36% [25-49%]) were highly prevalent in YAs with hip fracture. Twenty-six studies contributed data on question 2, including four that provided mortality data. There is either good or excellent functional recovery in ≥80% of YAs by 12 months following hip fracture; however, up to 15% experience poor outcomes at two years. Mortality rates beyond one year were only reported in one study. Only eight studies were designed specifically to investigate risk factors for, or outcomes associated with, YA hip fracture. Three studies reported outcomes of interest by fracture mechanism. The Quality in Prognosis Studies tool was used to assess the risk of bias of included studies. 24/44 (54.5%) were found to have a moderate or high risk of bias. One study reported data on question 3. Psychiatric morbidity, alcohol excess and smoking were the major risk factors associated with hip fracture in YAs. Further research is required to establish the risk factors for minimal trauma hip fracture in YAs. Limited data on mortality in YAs following hip fracture are concerning and deserve further investigation.

cards.title: Cerebrospinal fluid cell-free DNA methylation captures disease-specific biology in tauopathies.
cards.abstract: BackgroundDifferentiating tau-related dementias remains challenging, particularly during early disease stages when clinical symptoms overlap. Existing biomarkers mainly reflect downstream pathology and provide limited insight into disease-specific molecular processes.ObjectiveWe examined whether cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation could distinguish Alzheimer's disease (AD), behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).MethodsPromoter methylation of 20 genes associated with AD risk, neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and glymphatic or lymphatic regulation was analyzed in CSF and matched plasma cfDNA from controls (n = 15), AD (n = 21), bvFTD (n = 14), and PSP (n = 17). cfDNA concentration and fragmentomic profiles were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Findings were validated in an independent cohort.ResultsCSF cfDNA concentrations were increased in AD, whereas fragment size distributions were similar across diagnostic groups. Disease-associated methylation signatures were prominent in CSF but weak or absent in plasma. AD demonstrated widespread hypomethylation of inflammatory and senescence-associated genes together with hypermethylation of glymphatic and lymphatic regulators. bvFTD showed intermediate glial- and stress-related methylation changes, while PSP retained relatively preserved inflammatory and clearance-associated profiles. CSF methylation panels consistently outperformed plasma-derived markers for disease classification. ROC analyses demonstrated strong discrimination for AD, with AUC values reaching 0.84-0.85, while plasma-based markers showed limited diagnostic utility.ConclusionsCSF cfDNA methylation captures disease-specific epigenetic states linked to core pathogenic pathways in tau-related dementias. This approach may provide a biologically informative and clinically useful platform for molecular classification and diagnostic stratification.

cards.title: Denosumab Biosimilars Versus Denosumab in Postmenopausal Osteoporosis: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
cards.abstract: Denosumab is one of the first-line drugs for postmenopausal osteoporosis with high risk of fracture, but the cost limits its use. Denosumab biosimilars are a more affordable solution, though it is underutilized due to hesitation among clinicians and patients due to concerns for differences in efficacy and safety. We conducted an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing efficacy and safety of denosumab biosimilars to denosumab. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane databases and Clinical Trials.gov were searched for studies comparing denosumab biosimilars to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis. We pooled mean differences (MD) for continuous outcomes and risk ratios (RR) for binary outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using REML-based I2 statistics and Cochran's Q test. Statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.6.0. Fourteen RCTs comprising 5595 participants were included, of whom 2825 participants (50.5%) received biosimilars. There was no statistical difference between percent change from baseline at 6 and 12 months respectively for lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD), total hip, femoral neck BMD between the two groups. Similarly, change in C-telopeptide, procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide levels at 1, 6 and 12 months from baseline and vertebral fractures were similar between the two groups. There was no difference between the two groups in terms of safety outcomes including treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE), grade ≥ 3 TEAEs. Denosumab biosimilars were comparable in efficacy and short-term safety compared to denosumab in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
