cards.title: A High-Energy Military Femoral Fracture With Multidrug-Resistant Infection: A Case Report.
cards.abstract: BACKGROUND The Masquelet induced membrane technique is a 2-stage surgical procedure used to reconstruct large bone defects and uses a temporary cement spacer to generate a biologically active, vascularized membrane that promotes bone healing when filled with an autograft. This report describes the case of a 37-year-old military man with a high-energy femoral fracture, multiple debridement procedures, and a bone defect managed with the Masquelet induced membrane technique. CASE REPORT In the patient's home country, life-saving surgery was performed, followed by repeated excision of damaged tissue and long-term treatment, including the use of an external fixation device. After 6 months, the patient was transferred to Latvia for rehabilitation. In March 2023, he was admitted from a rehabilitation center to Riga East Clinical University Hospital in an acute setting, presenting with severe pain and purulent discharge from the left thigh. During treatment, he underwent multiple debridement procedures, insertion of a cement-coated nail, and defect reconstruction using the Masquelet induced membrane technique. Due to shortening of the affected limb, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, and poor bone quality, further osteosynthesis and stable implant fixation in the proximal femur were not feasible. Consequently, cementless left hip arthroplasty using a revision femoral stem was performed. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates that staged orthopedic management combining the Masquelet induced membrane technique, cementless revision hip arthroplasty, and individualized antimicrobial therapy guided by infectious disease consultation can achieve a favorable functional outcome at 2-year follow-up in a patient with high-energy femoral trauma complicated by multidrug-resistant infection.

cards.title: [Nonunion: cause before treatment : From time-based definition to cause-directed treatment].
cards.abstract: Fracture nonunion is a multifactorial complication of fracture healing. A solely time-based definition does not adequately reflect the underlying disturbances in healing and provides an insufficient basis for treatment decisions. Instead, management should be guided by a systematic assessment of the factors preventing osseous union. These include fracture-related infection, mechanical deficits, impaired biological healing potential, and patient-related risk factors. Occult infection should also be considered in clinically presumed aseptic nonunion. Mechanical instability requires restoration of adequate stability, whereas biological deficits may necessitate targeted augmentation. Modifiable patient-related risk factors should be optimized in parallel. As several contributing factors may coexist, treatment should not be based solely on temporal or morphological criteria but should address the individual causes of impaired fracture healing. A systematic, cause-directed approach therefore enables targeted treatment and, in multifactorial cases, the appropriate combination of therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Differential Adaptation of Osteocyte Lacunar Morphology at Bone (Re)modeling Sites under Mechanical Loading and Pharmacological Therapies in a Mouse Model of Osteoporosis
cards.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a highly prevalent disease characterized by low bone mass and structural deterioration of bone tissue leading to increased bone fragility and fracture risk. Osteocytes orchestrate local bone (re)modeling and therefore, characterizing their 3D morphological and spatial distribution across distinct (re)modeling microenvironments is essential for understanding the cellular mechanisms underlying divergent tissue-level responses. To address this, we used a 3D-3D multiscale registration framework mapping endpoint osteocyte lacunae onto dynamic, time-lapsed in vivo (re)modeling sites. Ovariectomized 15-week-old mice were subjected to 4 weeks of anabolic parathyroid hormone (PTH) or anti-catabolic bisphosphonate (BIS) treatment as monotreatment or combined with cyclic mechanical loading (ML). Biweekly in vivo micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) to identify (re)modeling sites and endpoint ultra-high resolution (ultra-HR) micro-CT to characterize osteocyte lacunae was performed. Osteocyte lacunae were characterized by lacunar density, volume and sphericity. Our findings showed that physical and pharmacological therapies differentially regulate the osteocyte lacunar network through distinct perilacunar adaptations across functional microenvironments. While BIS stabilizes local lacunar architecture, PTH drives asymmetrical lacunar expansion (increased volume with reduced sphericity) through perilacunar remodeling that supersedes any added ML effects. Crucially, estrogen loss disrupts the natural spatial maturation gradient by inducing rounding of lacunae in newly formed bone. Therapies counteract this disruption, restoring the healthy gradients in lacunar morphometry between spatially distinct microenvironments. Additionally, despite restoring tissue-level bone volume, physical and pharmacological osteoporosis therapies do not fully recover persistent lacunar density deficits. The overall lacunar morphological spatial signatures confirm active osteocytic tuning to endocrine, physical and matrix cues.

cards.title: Orthopaedic Care in Norway: Organization, Research, and Quality Improvement.
cards.abstract: ➢ Norway has a universal, publicly funded orthopaedic health-care system through a network of public hospitals serving a geographically dispersed population of 5.6 million inhabitants.➢ Orthopaedic care is characterized by salaried surgeons, close collaboration between hospitals, standardized treatment pathways, and equitable access to specialist services.➢ National orthopaedic quality registries and high-quality clinical research are integrated into clinical practice, enabling continuous outcome monitoring, benchmarking, and rapid implementation of evidence-based improvements.➢ Orthopaedic leadership has been central to several national quality improvement initiatives, including the development of secondary fracture prevention programs and national clinical guidelines, demonstrating how clinician-led collaboration can translate research into improvements in patient care.➢ The Norwegian model demonstrates how universal health care, national collaboration, orthopaedic quality registries, and clinician-led innovation can be integrated to support high-quality orthopaedic care and continuous improvement.

cards.title: Long-term outcomes of modified-intensity lenalidomide, bortezomib and dexamethasone (RVD-lite) in transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma: final report of a phase II trial.
cards.abstract: We report the long-term survival outcomes of modified-intensity lenalidomide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (RVD-lite) as frontline treatment for transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma (MM). RVD-lite was evaluated in an investigator-initiated, multicenter phase II trial in transplant-ineligible MM patients. RVD-lite was administered over a 35-day cycle with lenalidomide 15 mg orally on days 1-21; bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 subcutaneously on days 1, 8, 15, 22; and dexamethasone 20 mg orally on days 1, 2, 8, 9, 15, 16, 22, and 23 in patients aged £75 years and days 1, 8, 15, and 22 in patients aged >75 years for 9 cycles of induction followed by 6 cycles of consolidation (lenalidomide + bortezomib). Lenalidomide maintenance was not mandated. Fifty patients were enrolled. Median age was 73 years (range 65-91), and 14% of patients had an ECOG performance status of 2. At best response, the ORR and ³VGPR were 90% and 66%, respectively. After median follow-up of 72 months, the median PFS was 42 months (5-year PFS: 40%), and the median OS was 76 months (5-year OS: 63%). ECOG performance status of 2 was associated with inferior PFS and OS. Thirty-three patients (66%) received lenalidomide maintenance. Two patients (4%) discontinued treatment due to toxicity, and there was no treatment-related mortality. RVD-lite is a well-tolerated and highly effective regimen in transplant-ineligible MM with prolonged PFS and OS. This study provides the framework for frailty-adapted triplet and quadruplet regimens in MM patients. This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01782963).

cards.title: Engineering the geriatric heart to model HFpEF.
cards.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) clinical trials suffer from high rates of attrition due to a biological mismatch between preclinical models and patients. While clinical HFpEF is fundamentally driven by advanced age, female sex, systemic inflammation, and progressive myocardial stiffness, preclinical screening still relies predominantly on young male rodents or foetal-like pluripotent stem cell derivatives. In this perspective, we propose a modular and testable geriatric engineering framework for reconstructing the myocardial features of this disease in vitro. The framework integrates four pathogenic drivers: inducible nuclear senescence to mimic ageing-like phenotypes, post-menopausal estrogen withdrawal, programmable biomaterial-driven stiffness, and macrophage-mediated immune activation. De-risking HFpEF drug development requires deliberately engineering this target pathophysiology, ensuring candidate compounds are evaluated against the biology of the ageing myocardium. Because such platforms isolate myocardial phenotypes from the broader multisystem clinical syndrome, we outline the strict model inputs, functional outputs, and clinical benchmarking criteria required to establish their translational validity.

cards.title: Reevaluating predictive factors for treatment success in therapy with OnabotulinumtoxinA for iOAB in a real-world study.
cards.abstract: OnabotulinumtoxinA is an established third-line therapy for idiopathic overactive bladder (iOAB), with efficacy demonstrated in randomized trials and real-world studies. Despite the growing body of literature, predictors of treatment response remain insufficiently defined, with heterogeneous endpoints and definitions across studies. We performed a retrospective analysis to reevaluate prior identified predictors of treatment success using both patient-reported and objective outcomes. We included consecutive patients receiving a first intradetrusor injection of 100AE onabotulinumtoxinA for iOAB between January 2018 and April 2026. All patients had prior treatment with at least two anticholinergics and completed a 3-day bladder diary. Urodynamic studies were performed in all men and selectively in women. Injections were administered at 20 detrusor sites sparing the trigone. Outcome was treatment success defined by the Treatment Benefit Scale (TBS; success= 1-2), the definition by Abrar (≥ 50% improvement in urgency and urgency urinary incontinence), or a reduction by 11 points in the Urogenital Distress Inventory (UDI-6). Duration of effect was defined as time to patient-requested reinjection. Univariate logistic regression identified predictors of treatment success and duration (> 12 months, <6 months). A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Of 180 treated patients, 175 were included (74.9% female; median age 73 years [IQR 61-78]). Overall, 71.4% achieved success by TBS, 74.3% by Abrar criteria, and 70.3% by UDI-6. No significance differences between the methods were noted (p=0.21). Complete continence was newly achieved in 37.2%. Symptom relief lasted <6 months in 28%, 6-12 months in 45.1%, and >12 months in 26.9%. No major complications occurred but 44.8% developed a urinary tract infection within 3 months after injection. Active smoking (p=0.016) post-OP UTI (p=0.003) and a diabetes mellitus (p=0.005) were negative predictors of treatment success. Female sex (p=0.09) showed a non-significant trend toward treatment success. In multivariate analysis, no variable achieved statistical significance. Age, urodynamic findings, and baseline symptom severity were not predictive. Longer duration (> 12 months) was associated with TBS success (p<0.001), absence of frailty (p=0.01), and newly achieved complete continence (p=0.029). Short duration (< 6 months) was associated with failure to achieve continence (p<0.001) and UTI post-OP (p=0.001). Active smoking (p=0.059) and absence of detrusor overactivity in urodynamic studies (p=0.096) showed trends for short duration. OnabotulinumtoxinA is a safe and highly effective treatment option for patients with iOAB and therefore can be offered to all patients. Treatment success is associated with smoking status and metabolism, whereas age and underlying diagnosis do not appear predictive. Postoperative urinary tract infections may adversely affect outcomes and should be minimized. These findings may improve patient counseling and expectation management.

cards.title: Iterative Optimization of Photoactivatable BRD4 Degraders for Aging-Amplified Immunotherapy in Patient-Derived Lung Cancer Organoids.
cards.abstract: Cancer remains a major global health threat. Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has revolutionized the modulation of protein function in therapeutic development. Nevertheless, the design of current TPD agents continues to face challenges, including hook effects and, more critically, the frequent lack of spatial and temporal precision required for in vivo applications. Herein, we report a photoactivatable targeted degradation (PATD) strategy and describe the iterative optimization of compound 9, the first two-photon-excited BRD4 photodegrader, achieved through molecular engineering of the photosensitizer core, auxiliary ligands, and linkers. Notably, BRD4 degradation downregulates GPX4 transcription, promoting lipid peroxidation and thereby inducing ferro-aging, while simultaneously triggering chemo-aging via histone H3 cleavage, which leads to DNA damage and cell cycle arrest. This dual-aging mechanism accelerates tumor cell senescence, enabling synergistic seno-immunotherapy. Beyond conventional photosensitizers that primarily elicit immunogenic cell death (ICD) alone, complex 9 integrates senescence-driven immunity with ICD-mediated antitumor immunity. This combined immunostimulatory strategy elicits robust systemic antitumor responses and achieves amplified therapeutic efficacy in patient-derived organoids (PDOs), presenting a new paradigm for precision targeted protein degradation in therapy-resistant tumors.

cards.title: Circular RNAs in Skeletal Muscle Aging and Sarcopenia: Mechanistic Evidence, Biomarker Potential, and Therapeutic Readiness
cards.abstract: Skeletal muscle aging arises from interacting defects in proteostasis, mitochondrial quality control, inflammatory signaling, neuromuscular integrity, regenerative capacity, and mechanical–metabolic plasticity, and may culminate in sarcopenia. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are plausible regulators and biomarker candidates, but most evidence derives from developmental myogenesis, expression profiling, or non-aging atrophy models. This critical review organizes the literature around skeletal muscle aging and applies a four-level framework encompassing discovery, mechanistic support, in vivo causality, and functional intervention. We assess human linkage, species, treatment timing, locus of action, and endogenous or engineered modality separately. circSnd1 and circDdb1 currently provide the strongest combination of functional preclinical evidence and association with aged human skeletal muscle. circFUT10, circBBS9, circNEB, and circGLIS3 define less mature regenerative, discovery, histological, or muscle-quality domains. Non-aging atrophy studies, including circTmeff1 and engineered circmiR-29b, test whether proposed mechanisms remain active under defined catabolic stress. Human blood and serum-vesicle studies provide discovery-level associations with strength or mobility, but clinical validation of a circulating circRNA biomarker for sarcopenia remains insufficient. Therapeutic development is constrained by quantitative target credibility, systemic skeletal-muscle exposure, post-onset functional efficacy in aged organisms, safety, reversibility, and independent replication. The field should now prioritize rigorous validation over additional descriptive cataloging.

cards.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
cards.abstract: Long stays in the emergency department compromise patient safety and health system performance. Physiotherapist-led models of care may improve care and emergency department performance, but their effects have not been rigorously evaluated in randomised trials. We compared the effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness of physiotherapist-led care with usual care for patients presenting to the emergency department with musculoskeletal conditions. RESHAP-ED was an open-label, pragmatic, randomised trial that recruited adults aged 18 years and older at five emergency departments in New South Wales, Australia, with uncomplicated musculoskeletal conditions (eg, soft tissue conditions, neck and back pain, and fractures or dislocations not requiring orthopaedic review or surgery). Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using statistician-generated randomly permuted blocks, to either physiotherapist-led care (intervention) or usual physician-led or nurse practitioner-led care (control). The primary outcome was length of stay in the emergency department, calculated as time from arrival to discharge, analysed in the intention-to-treat population using a linear mixed-effects model. The trial was prospectively registered on the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12623000782639) and is completed. Between Nov 22, 2023 and March 29, 2025, 4219 patients were screened, 2728 were deemed ineligible for inclusion, and 1491 participants were randomly assigned (746 assigned to the physiotherapy-led intervention group and 745 assigned to the physician-led or nurse-led practitioner control group). Following the exclusion of 16 participants after randomisation, 1475 were included in the analysis (737 in the intervention group and 738 in the control group). The mean age of participants was 40·1 years (SD 16·5). 719 (48·7%) participants were male, 755 (51·2%) were female, and one (0·1%) participant had unreported sex data. Follow-up for the primary outcome was 100% complete. The mean length of stay in the emergency department was 2·4 h in the intervention group and 3·4 h in the control group (-1·0 h [95% CI -1·2 to -0·8]). Adverse events were reported by 39 (6·6%) of 591 participants in the intervention group versus 33 (5·9%) of 555 in the control group (p=0·72). The intervention group had lower costs (-$35·1 [95% CI -69·0 to -1·7]) and a high probability (98·1%) of being cost-effective. A physiotherapist-led model of care in the emergency department reduced length of stay among patients presenting with uncomplicated musculoskeletal conditions, without compromising health outcomes or safety, and was cost-effective. Medical Research Future Fund.

cards.title: Immunosenescence in tumor progression: from synergistic mechanisms to therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Tumor-associated immunosenescence is not a decline in immune function, but rather a state of immune ecological imbalance. It drives tumor progression through multi-dimensional mechanisms, including decreased immune surveillance, chronic inflammation, accumulation of suppressive cells, remodeling of TME, metabolic disorders, and epigenetic regulation. The challenges in immunosenescence research include conceptual confusion, an imbalance in research perspectives, the limitations of preclinical models, and the translational hurdles. This review summarizes the latest research findings on the role of immunosenescence in tumor progression and its multiple regulatory mechanisms and highlights the promise of targeted therapeutic strategies against immunosenescence. The synergy among multiple mechanisms of immunosenescence creates a self-reinforcing cycle of chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction, thereby driving immune ecological imbalance. The core strategies of targeted therapy for immunosenescence include eliminating or regulating senescent immune cells to rejuvenate the immune system, as well as enhancing the immune system's ability to clear senescent cells, thereby achieving immune ecosystem remodeling. Future research should focus on deciphering the deep heterogeneity of immunosenescence, elucidating the mechanisms of key overlapping processes such as T-cell exhaustion, developing clinical tools for precise assessment of immune age, optimizing preclinical models, and conducting innovative "immune age-oriented" clinical trials.

cards.title: Effect of a project achievement-oriented Quality Control Circle on traditional Chinese medicine nursing outcomes in elderly patients with distal radius fractures: A retrospective comparative study.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a project achievement-oriented Quality Control Circle (QCC) model in improving traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) nursing outcomes for elderly patients with conservatively treated distal radius fractures (DRFs). This retrospective comparative study included 112 elderly DRF patients admitted between June 2022 and December 2023. Based on the admission period, 56 patients (June 2022-March 2023) received routine care (control group), and 56 patients (March-December 2023) received a comprehensive TCM nursing model driven by a project-oriented QCC. Outcomes included complication rate, TCM intervention delivery rate, pain (Visual Analog Scale), swelling score, wrist function (Cooney score), and patient/staff satisfaction. Both groups received identical Menghe School bone-setting and small splint fixation. The intervention group additionally received a QCC-driven comprehensive TCM nursing model. The intervention group showed significantly lower total complication rates (3.6% vs 19.6%, relative risk = 0.18, P = .008), a higher TCM delivery rate (100% vs 64%, P < .05), greater reductions in pain and swelling, and higher Cooney scores (95 vs 75, P < .05) compared with the control group. All 9 quality indicators met or exceeded targets. Staff competency and team cohesion also improved. This retrospective study suggests that a project-oriented QCC model may enhance TCM nursing quality and short-term clinical outcomes in elderly DRF patients. However, given the study's observational design and single-center setting, these preliminary findings require validation through multicenter prospective trials with validated instruments and long-term follow-up. Robustness analysis using a propensity score-matched concurrent control group yielded consistent findings, supporting the validity of the primary results.

cards.title: Myokines and mitochondrial function in cardiometabolic diseases.
cards.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMD) encompass a group of disorders sharing a common pathophysiology that increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality. Key events underlying CMD pathophysiology include insulin resistance, low-grade inflammation, altered hormonal and myokine profiles, and mitochondrial dysfunction. The latter manifests as reduced mitochondrial mass and oxidative function, increased oxidative stress, altered Ca2+ handling and decreased mitochondrial membrane potential. Skeletal muscle plays a pivotal role in CMD pathophysiology through two main mechanisms: i) the storage and oxidation of energy substrates and ii) the release of myokines, which in turn modulate metabolism and mitochondrial function. Here, we propose that the unfavorable myokine profile associated with CMD pathophysiology leads to mitochondrial alterations, and that restoring a healthy myokine profile helps improve mitochondrial structure, function, and overall metabolic health. To test this idea, in this narrative review, we critically present evidence of an altered myokine profile in CMD and highlight the most important mitochondrial alterations in CMD before examining the direct effect of specific myokines on mitochondria and CMD-associated mitochondrial dysfunction. Finally, we summarize the effects of therapeutic interventions on both the myokine profile and mitochondrial function, also appraising human trials that use myokine-based interventions to improve CMD. We focus on molecular mechanisms and causal relationships, while also indicating novel perspectives in the field. Understanding the role of mitochondria in the effect of myokines on metabolic health may open new preventive and therapeutic strategies for addressing CMD more efficiently.

cards.title: Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE): a non-invasive, in vivo measure of cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence is a central hallmark of aging, yet its measurement in humans remains invasive, low-throughput and tissue-specific, precluding population-scale study. We developed Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE) predictors: whole-blood DNA methylation proxies of p14ARF, p16INK4A and p21CIP1 expression, plus a composite score, providing the first scalable measure of senescence-marker expression. Deployed across Generation Scotland (n=18,859), MaGE yielded 45 Bonferroni-significant associations spanning 18 incident diseases and all-cause mortality. The two strongest associations recapitulated the established tissue specificity of p21CIP1 and p16INK4A activation, with MaGE-p21 associating with incident alcoholic liver disease and MaGE-p16 with pulmonary fibrosis. In a separate study, MaGE tracked disease severity and treatment response in Crohn's disease. MaGE is a scalable, interpretable biomarker of senescence that enables its study at population scale and offers a route to patient stratification in senolytic trials.

cards.title: Antibiotic Prescribing Patterns and Stewardship Opportunities in Pediatric Facial Trauma: A Five-Year Retrospective Analysis.
cards.abstract: To assess antibiotic prescribing practices in pediatric facial trauma at a tertiary academic center, examine their association with infection outcomes, and identify stewardship opportunities to inform future larger-scale evaluation of antibiotic use in pediatric facial fractures. This retrospective chart review included pediatric patients (< 18 years) presenting via trauma activation with facial trauma to a tertiary academic medical system over 5 years. Patients were identified through the institutional data warehouse. Data collected included demographics, injury patterns, antibiotic prescribing details (route, duration, timing), surgical interventions, and clinical outcomes. The primary outcome was infection development; secondary outcomes included antibiotic-related complications. Descriptive statistics characterized prescribing patterns, and univariate tests evaluated associations between antibiotic use and outcomes. Multivariable modeling was not performed due to only two infection events. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Among 223 pediatric patients with facial fractures, the infection rate was low (< 1%). Despite this, 46.2% received antibiotics, though only 32.3% received systemic therapy. Among treated patients, 68.9% received courses exceeding 5 days (median 8 days), and over 70% received intravenous antibiotics. Surgical intervention was most strongly associated with antibiotic use, with surgical patients receiving antibiotics significantly more often than non-surgical patients. Open fractures were associated with higher utilization and longer durations compared with closed fractures. Both documented infections occurred in antibiotic recipients, though this association was not statistically significant. Notably, 51% of antibiotic recipients were candidates for shorter courses or oral conversion. These findings suggest potential antibiotic overutilization and highlight substantial opportunities to optimize stewardship in pediatric facial trauma, including limiting prophylactic duration, favoring oral therapy when appropriate, and better targeting antibiotics to high-risk patients. Prospective, multicenter studies are needed to guide evidence-based guideline development. Level IV.

cards.title: Preserving the Bone Envelope: A Prospective Observational Study of Closed Reduction and Ilizarov Circular Fixation for Open and Closed Distal Tibial Fractures.
cards.abstract: Distal tibial fractures are challenging injuries because of limited soft-tissue coverage, frequent high-energy mechanisms and the potential for soft-tissue compromise. Extensive surgical exposure may further disturb the local soft-tissue and biological environment. Ilizarov circular external fixation permits stable fixation with limited exposure of the fracture site. This prospective observational study evaluated fracture union, bone and functional outcomes and complications following closed or indirect reduction and Ilizarov circular external fixation in patients with open and closed distal tibial fractures and was conducted in the Department of Orthopaedics, Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, Bangladesh from 15 March 2018 to 15 March 2024. Forty skeletally mature patients with distal tibial fractures were treated with an Ilizarov circular external fixator. Fracture reduction was performed by closed or indirect manipulation under C-arm fluoroscopic guidance. Twenty patients had closed fractures and 20 had open fractures. Among the open fractures, 6 were Gustilo-Anderson Grade I, 9 Grade II and 5 Grade IIIA. Clinical and radiological outcomes were assessed during follow-up. Bone and functional outcomes were classified using the Association for the Study and Application of the Method of Ilizarov (ASAMI) criteria. There were 30 male patients (75.0%) and 10 female patients (25.0%), with a mean age of 28 years. The right tibia was involved in 28 patients (70.0%) and the left tibia in 12(30.0%). Road traffic accidents accounted for 28 injuries (70.0%), falls from height for 8(20.0%) and physical assault for 4(10.0%). The mean interval from injury to Ilizarov fixation was 5 days. All 40 fractures united during follow-up. The mean time to radiological union was 17.12 weeks (range, 14-20 weeks). The mean duration of external fixation was 195 days (range, 180-210 days). The mean follow-up was 12 months (range, 6-15 months), with a minimum follow-up of 6 months after frame removal. According to ASAMI bone criteria, 24 patients (60.0%) had excellent results, 12(30.0%) good results and 4(10.0%) fair results. No poor bone result was recorded. Functional results were excellent in 18 patients (45.0%), good in 16(40.0%), fair in 4(10.0%) and poor in 2(5.0%). Pin-tract infection occurred in 16 patients (40.0%), involving 20 wires. Most infections were managed with local wound care and oral antibiotics. Eight patients (20.0%) required exchange of loose wires. No limb-length discrepancy was recorded during follow-up. In this prospective single-center series, closed or indirect reduction followed by Ilizarov circular external fixation was associated with a high observed rate of fracture union and predominantly favorable bone and functional outcomes in open and closed distal tibial fractures. The technique provided stable fixation while limiting direct surgical exposure of the fracture site. The findings support Ilizarov circular fixation as a useful treatment option in appropriately selected distal tibial fractures, particularly when preservation of the soft-tissue envelope is an important consideration. Comparative studies with larger samples and standardized functional outcome measures are required to determine its relative effectiveness against other fixation methods.

cards.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Formulas in Delaying Aging: From Theoretical Foundations to Molecular Mechanisms and Translational Perspectives.
cards.abstract: Aging is a systemic decline in physiological integrity, driving chronic diseases such as neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disorders, and metabolic syndromes. Rapid global population aging urgently demands effective interventions. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas, characterized by multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway synergy, offer a promising paradigm for delaying aging. This review systematically integrates recent advances in TCM formula-based anti-aging research, bridging classical TCM gerontology with the 14 modern hallmarks of aging. We categorize representative formulas into four mechanistic groups targeting mitochondrial homeostasis and autophagy, cellular senescence and inflammatory microenvironment, stem cell maintenance and epigenetic reprogramming, and gut microbiota and systemic metabolism, and explore their holistic efficacy, key bioactive constituents, and multi-component synergy. In terms of methodological innovations, we introduced network pharmacology combined with AI-driven target screening and proteomic aging clocks to assess biological age. We discussed challenges in chemical complexity, mechanistic completeness, and clinical translation, and proposed a roadmap for development. This review establishes an integrative model that integrates TCM principles with modern aging biology, offering insights for translational research toward healthy longevity.

cards.title: Five-Year CT-Based Skeletal Muscle Decline Curves in Cirrhosis According to Liver Functional Reserve and Routinely Available Clinical Factors.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is common in cirrhosis and is associated with poor outcomes. We aimed to identify factors associated with longitudinal skeletal muscle loss and to explore estimation of future L3 skeletal muscle index (L3-SMI) using routinely available clinical variables. This retrospective longitudinal study included 175 patients with cirrhosis who underwent serial abdominal CT over five annual time points between 2010 and 2022. The primary analysis used a linear mixed-effects model including annual time point, baseline Child-Pugh class, and their interaction. An exploratory linear regression model estimated Year 5 L3-SMI. In the primary model, L3-SMI declined by -1.144 cm2/m2/year in baseline Child-Pugh class A. The time-by-class B interaction was not significant (β = 0.024; 95% CI, -0.250 to 0.298; p = 0.865), whereas class C was associated with an additional annual decline of -1.812 cm2/m2/year compared with class A (95% CI, -2.735 to -0.890; p = 0.0001). This association remained after adjustment for age, sex, baseline HCC status, and the time-by-HCC interaction. In the exploratory Year 5 model, baseline L3-SMI was the dominant predictor; estimates for class C were interpreted cautiously because only five patients were baseline class C. Baseline hepatic functional reserve, particularly Child-Pugh class C, was associated with faster annual CT-based L3-SMI decline. The Year 5 prediction model is exploratory and requires external validation. Early sarcopenia assessment may facilitate risk stratification in patients with impaired hepatic reserve. Trial Registration: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry: UMIN000051577.

cards.title: The Growth and Trends in Cancer-Induced Cachexia Research: A Bibliometric and AI-Guided Visualization Analysis.
cards.abstract: Over the past several decades, advances in basic and clinical research have increasingly established cancer-induced cachexia as a distinct pathophysiological syndrome that warrants targeted therapeutic approaches alongside conventional anticancer treatments. Despite its high prevalence and substantial impact on morbidity, mortality, and quality of life, the condition remains underrecognized and inadequately managed in clinical practice. Correspondingly, scientific activity in the field has expanded rapidly, spanning molecular mechanisms, clinical characterization, and emerging interventional strategies. This bibliometric analysis aims to provide a comprehensive, quantitative overview of evolving research in cancer-induced cachexia over the past 25 years. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of cancer cachexia research published between 2001 and 2025 using the Web of Science Core Collection. A total of 5775 English-language primary research articles were retrieved using the search terms "cancer AND cachexia," and including papers in English of the types articles, letters, and proceedings papers. Data were analyzed using the Bibliometrix R package and its web interface, BiblioShiny, to assess publication trends, author productivity, collaboration networks, and keyword co-occurrence. Additional visualizations were generated using the R programming language and AI-guided analyses to explore trends and bursts in the evolution of cachexia research. Cancer cachexia publications increased at an annual rate of 6.7%, exceeding the overall growth rate of scientific literature. In terms of number of papers and citation indices, the Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle is the dominant journal in the field. Research is characterized by high levels of international collaboration, though research networks remain geographically clustered. Keywords were analyzed using co-occurrence networks to reveal specific connections and clusters of research topics. Trend analyses of keywords showed the progression of research in the areas of metabolism and the role of inflammatory mediators. Burst analysis revealed research "hotspots" over the last 25 years including studies of specific interventions such as immunotherapy, gastrointestinal cancers, and metabolic dysregulation. Cancer cachexia research has expanded significantly over the past two decades but remains limited in scale and fragmented across geographic and disciplinary boundaries. A shift toward investigating biological mechanisms and therapeutics indicates a maturing field with growing translational potential. Growing trends and recent research bursts in immune function and inflammation suggest an important role of these areas in further therapeutic development. Continued integration of clinical, nutritional, and molecular research will be essential to advance effective interventions. This bibliometric analysis offers a data-driven foundation to inform future research priorities and collaboration strategies in cancer-induced cachexia.

cards.title: ADP Inhibits Macrophage Senescence via the AMPK/KLF10 Pathway in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
cards.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a critical complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and a leading cause of mortality in those affected. Abnormal energy metabolism of macrophages is closely associated with LN pathogenesis. Adenosine diphosphate (ADP) is known to regulate macrophage proinflammatory function; however, its specific role in SLE progression remains unexplored. We employed a spontaneous SLE mouse model and an integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic approach to investigate the effect of ADP on SLE disease progression and macrophage function. Our study revealed that ADP stimulates the AMPK signaling pathway, curtails macrophage senescence, and diminishes the release of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors, ultimately alleviating SLE progression. Mechanistically, ADP promotes KLF10 expression, which binds to Sirtuin1 to facilitate deacetylation at the promoter region of Cdkn1a in macrophages. This process leads to reduced p21 expression and macrophage senescence. Collectively, the findings uncover a novel regulatory role of ADP in the pathogenesis of SLE and macrophage senescence, indicating its potential as a target for treatment.

cards.title: Disulfiram Attenuates Adenine-Induced Renal Fibrosis by Modulating Inflammatory and Immunometabolic Responses.
cards.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is partly driven by excessive innate immune activation, which contributes to progressive renal injury and fibrosis. Disulfiram (DSF), an approved treatment for alcohol dependence, has recently emerged as an inhibitor of innate immune responses such as pyroptosis. In this study, we investigated whether DSF attenuates kidney injury in adenine-induced nephropathy and explored the underlying mechanisms. DSF treatment markedly ameliorated kidney injury in adenine-induced nephropathy, accompanied by suppression of inflammatory cell infiltration and inflammasome- and pyroptosis-related markers. RNA sequencing revealed restoration of disrupted fatty acid metabolism in the kidneys following DSF treatment. Furthermore, DSF alleviated DNA damage, cellular senescence, and fibrosis. Importantly, activation of gasdermin D, a central executor of pyroptosis, was closely associated with disease severity in human CKD biopsy samples, supporting the clinical relevance of this pathway. Collectively, these findings suggest a potential role for DSF in modulating inflammatory and immunometabolic pathways in CKD.

cards.title: Local acetyl-CoA metabolism and acetate recycling as epigenetic regulators of chromatin dynamics.
cards.abstract: Histone acetylation depends on acetyl-CoA, a central metabolic intermediate linking nutrient availability to chromatin regulation. Beyond bulk acetyl-CoA abundance, accumulating evidence indicates that chromatin-proximal acetyl-CoA production and acetate recycling provide spatial control over histone acetylation. In budding yeast, acetyl-CoA synthetase Acs2 supports nucleocytosolic acetyl-CoA production and associates with chromatin during transcriptional transitions, enabling local acetyl-CoA generation for histone acetyltransferases. Its mammalian ortholog, ACSS2, can accumulate in the nucleus in response to metabolic or signaling cues, where it recaptures acetate released by histone deacetylation to sustain promoter-localized histone acetylation. Acs2/ACSS2 also function within multi-enzyme or chromatin-associated assemblies, such as the yeast SESAME complex, coupling acetate metabolism with other metabolic and epigenetic pathways. These mechanisms influence gene expression, heterochromatin maintenance, senescence, and tumor-associated transcriptional programs. Together, these findings support a spatial model in which local metabolite production shapes epigenetic output independently of bulk metabolite abundance. Defining how such nuclear metabolic microenvironments are established and regulated may refine our understanding of metabolic control of chromatin and inform more selective therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Proximal Scaphoid Pole Reconstruction Utilizing Ipsilateral Proximal Hamate Autograft.
cards.abstract: Proximal pole scaphoid fractures complicated by nonunion and osteonecrosis present a challenging scenario with few good reconstructive options, especially when the proximal fragment is small or fragmented1-4. The use of an ipsilateral proximal hamate osteochondral autograft has emerged as a promising technique for reconstructing the proximal scaphoid pole, with the potential to restore carpal mechanics while avoiding the morbidity associated with free vascularized bone grafts or distant autograft sites. The procedure involves replacing the diseased proximal scaphoid with a structurally matched osteochondral graft from the ipsilateral proximal hamate. After excising the necrotic or fragmented scaphoid pole, a size-matched graft-harvested with its attached volar capitohamate ligament-is rotated 180° on its longitudinal axis to replicate normal scaphoid anatomy. The defect is measured in 3 planes using the scapholunate joint (proximal) and viable distal scaphoid surface as boundaries. On the hamate, an osteotomy is marked 8 to 10 mm distal to its proximal tip, parallel to the articular surface. The volar capitohamate ligament is preserved to guide graft orientation and maintain stability. These measurements align with recent anatomic and biomechanical studies that have confirmed 6 to 10-mm grafts accurately reproduce scaphoid morphology without compromising carpal kinematics. The graft is then inserted into the defect and secured with rigid internal fixation (headless compression screws or Kirschner wires). Residual gaps may be filled with cancellous bone graft. Scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) reconstruction is typically performed by suturing the hamate's volar capitohamate ligament to the dorsal SLIL remnant on the lunate with a 2-0 nonabsorbable suture. In patients with a partially intact SLIL, such as after failed fixation, the hamate graft alone may provide adequate stability, making formal reconstruction unnecessary. If intraoperative findings reveal dorsal scapholunate instability or an attenuated SLIL, reconstruction is indicated. Healthy, tensionable ligament remnants are repaired directly or reinforced with suture anchors. When dorsal fibers are deficient but volar remnants remain, the attached volar capitohamate ligament is used for reinforcement. For small defects, a micro-interference screw may be employed for fixation. Postoperatively, the wrist is immobilized in a cast. When radiographic evidence of union is observed, the cast is removed and the patient begins a structured hand therapy program. Alternatives include vascularized and nonvascularized bone grafts (e.g., iliac crest), a vascularized medial femoral trochlear osteochondral flap, costochondral rib graft, proximal row carpectomy, and wrist arthrodesis1,2. These may be limited by donor-site morbidity, complexity, or suboptimal restoration of wrist biomechanics. The articular surface of the proximal hamate closely matches the curvature and size of the proximal pole of the scaphoid, making it an ideal structural substitute. The use of an articular autograft from the same wrist avoids the need for distant donor sites and microsurgical anastomoses, reducing overall morbidity. Additionally, because the graft is harvested with its volar ligament attached, it enables a simultaneous SLIL reconstruction, addressing carpal instability in a way that standard bone grafts cannot. This technique is relatively straightforward and reproducible, and it is especially beneficial in young, active patients with an irreparable proximal scaphoid, offering a chance to heal the nonunion and preserve near-normal wrist function without resorting to salvage procedures. Radiographic union is expected in the majority of cases within 8 to 12 weeks. Published series have demonstrated union rates of >90%, improved pain, restoration of near-normal wrist kinematics, and substantial improvements in range of motion and grip strength, although not always to the level of the contralateral wrist. Complications are rare but include nonunion, donor-site pain, and persistent stiffness. cards.title: Suture-Button Fixation Provides a Statistically But Not Clinically Important Improvement in Function for Syndesmotic Injuries in Unstable Ankle Fractures: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
cards.abstract: No consensus exists on the optimal syndesmotic fixation for unstable ankle fractures. We compared strategies using a network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Seven databases and trial registers were searched through November 1, 2025 for RCTs of adults undergoing fixation of an ankle fracture with syndesmotic injury; quasirandomized and duplicate/follow-up reports were excluded. Interventions were grouped a priori as suture-button/dynamic fixation, metallic 3-cortex screw (reference), metallic 4-cortex screw, bioabsorbable screw, and no fixation. A frequentist random-effects NMA estimated mean differences (MD) for function (Olerud-Molander Ankle Score [OMAS] at 1 year, the outcome reported by the most trials; AOFAS) and odds ratios (OR) for malreduction and reoperation (primary definition excluding planned implant removal), with treatments ranked by P-score and effects interpreted against the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). Certainty was rated with a CINeMA-equivalent assessment. Twelve RCTs (883 patients) formed a connected network. For 1-year OMAS, suture-button fixation ranked highest (P-score 0.86; MD +5.2 points versus the 3-cortex screw; 95% CI, +1.1 to +9.2)-statistically significant but below the 10-point MCID-while the 4-cortex screw ranked lowest; heterogeneity was low (I2 = 10%) without inconsistency. The AOFAS did not differ between suture-button and the 3-cortex screw (MD 0.0; 95% CI, -4.5 to +4.5). Malreduction was lower with suture-button fixation (OR 0.26; 95% CI, 0.06-1.11; 0.27 [0.11-0.64] fixed-effect). Unplanned reoperation did not differ between constructs (suture-button OR 0.45; 95% CI, 0.17-1.16), whereas all-cause reoperation favored the suture-button and bioabsorbable constructs. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. Suture-button/dynamic fixation provides 1-year function at least equivalent to screws, with lower malreduction and fewer all-cause reoperations from avoiding routine implant removal. Functional differences are small and below the MCID, and certainty is low. Therapeutic, Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence. PROSPERO CRD420251166994.

cards.title: Leptin Neutralization Attenuates Inflammaging in Endothelial and Immune Cell Models.
cards.abstract: Leptin, a proinflammatory adipokine, contributes to the chronic low-grade inflammation seen in obesity, but its role in age-related inflammation, that is inflammaging, has been poorly studied. We thus tested the effect of blocking leptin receptor (LEP-R) binding in five models of inflammaging, that is replicative senescent endothelial cells, hyperglycemia-treated macrophages or endothelial cells, lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-exposed macrophages, and TCR-stimulated CD4+ T cells. In endothelial cells, leptin enhanced senescence, while leptin neutralization suppressed the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, two effects mediated in part by the mTOR pathway. In both macrophages and endothelial cells, leptin blockade blunted hyperglycemia-induced inflammation, while in macrophages, it also suppressed the LPS-induced senescent and proinflammatory phenotype. In T cells, leptin neutralization produced divergent effects, attenuating the expression of inflammatory and senescence markers in conventional T cells but not in regulatory T cells. To assess translational relevance, we measured leptin and inflammaging markers in plasma samples from two independent cohorts, one of healthy individuals (n = 121) and another of people with Type 2 diabetes (n = 93). In healthy subjects, leptin levels were higher in people with hs-CRP ≥ 3 mg/dL compared with those below such threshold, also after adjustment for BMI. Leptin levels showed BMI-adjusted positive correlations with IL-6 and hs-CRP in healthy individuals and with hs-CRP and IL-8 in people with diabetes. These findings suggest that leptin might fuel inflammaging and that its neutralization exerts anti-inflammatory effects across multiple, related models.

cards.title: Pre-transplant vulnerability and clinically consequential osteonecrosis after liver transplantation.
cards.abstract: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) after liver transplantation (LT) frequently progresses to joint collapse and surgical intervention. Although corticosteroids have traditionally been implicated in its pathogenesis, their independent contribution under contemporary immunosuppressive protocols remains uncertain. We aimed to identify factors associated with clinically consequential ONFH, with particular attention to pre-transplant disease burden and systemic vulnerability. This retrospective cohort study included 1,836 adults who underwent first-time LT between 2000 and 2023. To minimize time-dependent bias, corticosteroid exposure was assessed as cumulative dose over a fixed 3-month post-transplant period and examined using risk-set percentile analysis and an adjusted Cox model. Additional candidate factors were screened using covariate-balancing approaches and evaluated in a full-cohort multivariable Cox model. ONFH developed in 64 patients (3.5%) at a mean of 5.86±4.58 years after LT, and 71.9% of affected patients subsequently underwent surgical intervention. Corticosteroid exposure was not significantly associated with ONFH after adjustment for baseline covariates (p=0.47), and findings were consistent across analyses accounting for time-dependent bias. In contrast, other diagnoses including primary biliary cholangitis or Wilson disease (HR 4.21; 95% CI, 1.19-14.91; p=0.03) and preoperative enteral nutrition requirement (HR 2.98; 95% CI 1.03-8.64; p=0.04) were associated with increased risk. Cumulative smoking exposure (p=0.08) and time-weighted average MELD score (p=0.07) demonstrated suggestive associations with ONFH risk. Clinically consequential ONFH after LT may be influenced more by pre-transplant vulnerability and nutritional frailty than by corticosteroid exposure alone. These findings support a vulnerability-based framework for post-transplant ONFH and may help identify recipients who could benefit from heightened clinical awareness and timely diagnostic evaluation when compatible symptoms develop.

cards.title: Preoperative risk stratification for anastomotic leakage after gastrectomy: a model based on dual‑energy CT extracellular volume fraction and sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: To develop a purely preoperative risk stratification model for anastomotic leakage (AL) after radical gastrectomy using clinical, dual-energy CT (DECT), and body composition variables available before surgery. This retrospective study included 439 patients with gastric cancer who underwent radical gastrectomy. Preoperative clinical, DECT, and body composition data were collected. A domain-based predictor selection strategy was used, followed by Firth penalized logistic regression to account for the low event rate. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with an additional full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and risk stratification. AL occurred in 27 patients (6.15%). The final model included cardia tumor location (OR = 4.44), higher ECV (OR = 1.09 per 1%), and sarcopenia (OR = 3.66). The model showed good discrimination, with an apparent AUC of 0.853 and a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.843. Full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity analysis yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.833. Calibration was acceptable, with a Brier score of 0.050, and DCA suggested potential net benefit. Observed AL rates increased stepwise across low-risk (< 3%), intermediate-risk (3%-10%), and high-risk (≥ 10%) groups: 1.23%, 5.13%, and 22.78%, respectively. The high-risk group comprised 18.0% of the cohort but accounted for 66.7% of all AL events. A concise model integrating tumor location, DECT-derived ECV, and sarcopenia showed favorable performance for preoperative AL risk stratification after gastrectomy. This internally validated model may help preoperative AL risk stratification, but multicenter external validation and impact analysis are required before implementation.

cards.title: Automatic measurement of vertebral compression ratio on lumbar MR images fracture assessment based on MS-Res-AttU-Net model framework.
cards.abstract: To develop an MS-Res-AttU-Net-based deep learning framework for automatic measurement of vertebral compression ratio (VCR) on lumbar magnetic resonance images and to evaluate its value for image-based assessment of lumbar vertebral fractures. This retrospective study included 92 patients with lumbar vertebral fractures who underwent sagittal T2-weighted MRI. An MS-Res-AttU-Net framework was constructed for vertebral segmentation and automatic VCR calculation. The dataset was divided into a training cohort (n=64) and an independent test cohort (n=28). Segmentation performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient. Agreement between automated and manual VCR measurements was evaluated using correlation, intraclass correlation coefficient, and Bland-Altman analysis. An ablation study was further performed to assess the contribution of residual, attention, and multi-scale refinement modules. The final MS-Res-AttU-Net achieved stable segmentation performance and showed close agreement between automated and manual VCR measurements. The ablation study demonstrated progressive improvement in both segmentation quality and downstream VCR estimation, while A qualitative comparison of four lumbar MR cases showed MS-Res-AttU-Net produced the smoothest and most accurate vertebral contours. Automatic VCR measurement on lumbar MR images is feasible and clinically interpretable. The MS-Res-AttU-Net-based framework may provide a rapid and objective quantitative tool for lumbar fracture evaluation.

cards.title: Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty in the Setting of an Intact Rotator Cuff: A Contemporary Review of Current Indications, Outcomes, and Surgical Considerations.
cards.abstract: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) was designed for rotator cuff tear arthropathy but is now used in patients with an intact rotator cuff, most often for primary glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA). This review examines the current evidence for rTSA in cuff-intact patients, focusing on the indications, functional outcomes, complications, implant design considerations and surgical technique. In matched cohorts and meta-analyses restricted to cuff-intact GHOA, rTSA and aTSA produce comparable pain relief, patient-reported outcomes, satisfaction, and overhead elevation. ATSA restores greater external and internal rotation, but this difference often falls below clinically important thresholds and narrows over time. RTSA generally has a lower overall complication and revision rate, with baseplate loosening as the leading though still rare reason for revision surgery. Instability, acromial and scapular spine stress fracture, and revision surgery rates are all lower when the rotator cuff is intact. Current studies on the cuff-intact population are limited to 10-year outcomes, with registry survivorship of rTSA for GHOA approximately 96.1% at 10 years. RTSA is an efficacious and durable option for patients with glenohumeral arthritis and an intact rotator cuff, providing consistent pain relief and function. Patient outcomes are influenced by surgical technique, implant design and positioning, and avoidance of complications. Long-term follow-up and further comparative studies are needed to define the role of rTSA versus aTSA in this population.

cards.title: Reshaping the tumor immune microenvironment via therapy-induced senescence: senescence-associated secretory phenotype networks and senolytic strategies.
cards.abstract: Anticancer therapy can suppress tumor growth by inducing cell death, but many treatments also impose durable stress programs in malignant and stromal cells. Therapy-induced senescence (TIS) has emerged as a central non-lethal outcome of chemotherapy, radiotherapy and targeted therapy. Senescent cells remain metabolically active and communicate with their surroundings through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), a heterogeneous mixture of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, proteases, extracellular vesicles and immune-modulatory signals. In cancer, this secretory program can support immune surveillance when it is transient and efficiently cleared, yet it can also promote chronic inflammation, immune suppression, stromal remodeling, recurrence and resistance when senescent cells persist. This review summarizes the TIS-SASP-tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) axis, with emphasis on the molecular regulation of SASP, immune-cell-specific remodeling, the biphasic nature of SASP-mediated immunity and the rationale for sequential senogenic-senolytic therapy. Here, "senogenic" refers to interventions that induce cellular senescence, "senolytic" to approaches that selectively eliminate senescent cells, and "senomorphic" to strategies that suppress or remodel harmful senescence-associated phenotypes without necessarily killing senescent cells. We discuss how senolytics, senomorphics and immune checkpoint combinations may convert therapy-induced senescence from a liability into a therapeutically exploitable state. We also highlight the translational barriers that currently limit this strategy, including biomarker specificity, cell-type heterogeneity, treatment timing, safety and the need for spatially resolved monitoring of senescent niches.

cards.title: Polyol Pathway Inhibition by Epalrestat Attenuates Pathological Bone Loss through Redox Homeostasis and Sorbitol-Linked Calcium Signaling.
cards.abstract: The contribution of polyol metabolism to pathological bone remodeling remains incompletely understood. Here, we examined its role in osteoclastogenesis and evaluated the skeletal effects of epalrestat, a clinically approved aldose reductase inhibitor. Exploratory single-cell analysis of two human femoral-head specimens suggested greater macrophage-associated polyol-pathway activity in the osteoporosis specimen. In primary bone marrow-derived macrophages, silencing of Akr1b3 and Sord produced opposing effects on osteoclast differentiation. Epalrestat suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis and attenuated bone loss in diabetic, ovariectomy-induced, and inflammatory mouse models under early-intervention regimens. Mechanistic analyses showed improved NADPH/NADP⁺ and GSH/GSSG balance, reduced oxidative stress, and attenuated cytosolic and mitochondrial Ca²⁺ signals and Ca²⁺ oscillations. Genetic and osmotic-compensation experiments further supported a model in which intracellular sorbitol contributes to the osmotic regulation of Ca²⁺ oscillations. Additional findings included reduced inflammation in osteolysis and arthritis models, altered macrophage polarization, and partial preservation of bone marrow vascular features. Together, these findings connect glucose metabolism with redox and Ca²⁺ regulation during osteoclast differentiation and provide a rationale for further evaluation of epalrestat in skeletal disease.

cards.title: Development and internal validation of the Laboratory-based Liver Frailty Index (Lab-LFI)-a prediction model for frailty in patients with cirrhosis.
cards.abstract: Frailty, as measured by the Liver Frailty Index (LFI), is a well-established predictor of outcomes in cirrhosis, but testing requires in-person encounters. We sought to develop a blood-based biomarker index that correlates with frailty. Seven serum/plasma analytes (myostatin, IL-6, growth differentiation factor-15 [GDF-15], testosterone, leucine-rich alpha-2 glycoprotein [LRG1], fetuin-A, and IGF-1) were measured by ELISA in 527 ambulatory cirrhosis patients. "Frail" was defined as LFI≥4.4. The cohort was split in half; the "Lab-LFI" was developed using LASSO regression in the training set and validated in the test set. Other machine learning methods (generalized additive model [GAM], Random Forest, and XGBOOST) were considered to compare discrimination. Of 527 patients (median age 59, MELD 14), 114 (21.6%) were frail. All seven biomarkers were associated with frailty. In the test set, Lab-LFI's c-statistic was 0.80 (95% CI 0.74-0.87) for frailty. The GAM, random forest, and XGBOOST approaches produced similar discrimination (c-statistics 0.79-0.82); as such, the LASSO model was chosen for maximum interpretability. Addition of clinical variables to the LASSO model, including MELD labs and sex, did not improve discrimination (c-statistic 0.79, 95% CI 0.72-0.85). Patients were stratified by Lab-LFI using a cutpoint maximizing Youden's index; after adjusting for MELD and liver disease etiology, the high-risk group had higher pre-transplant death/waitlist dropout (HR 1.77, 95% CI 1.17-2.68, p=0.007). We developed and internally validated the Lab-LFI, a frailty prediction model consisting of 7 laboratory-based biomarkers. Lab-LFI enables blood-based assessment of physical function, as MELD does with liver function.

cards.title: Sustained increases in lumbar spine and hip BMD with denosumab therapy beyond 10 years.
cards.abstract: Denosumab therapy results in a sustained increase in BMD at the lumbar spine and hip and lower fracture rates during 10 years of treatment. However, data on efficacy and safety beyond 10 years are limited. We present the case of a female who demonstrated a large and continued rise in BMD after 10 years of denosumab therapy. An 80-year-old woman was referred to our Bone Health Clinic for advice regarding osteoporosis diagnosed 1 year earlier on routine DXA: lumbar spine T-score of -4.2 (0.585 g/cm2) and total hip T-score of -4.0 (0.503 g/cm2). Her GP had commenced her on alendronate 70 mg once weekly. Given her low T-scores, treatment was switched to denosumab, which was continued over the next decade. In her 10th year of treatment, she fell and sustained a left hip fracture. Repeat DXA revealed a T-score of -2.7 (0.754g/cm2) in the lumbar spine and -3.0 (0.572g/cm2) in the total hip. Our orthogeriatric service advised her to continue denosumab until reassessment in 3 years. Follow-up DXA 3 years later revealed an 8.0% improvement in BMD at lumbar spine (0.814 g/cm2, T-score -2.1), 6.6% at the total hip (0.610 g/cm2, T-score -2.7) (see Table 1). Denosumab was continued with advice that lifelong therapy may be needed. This case illustrates that denosumab therapy beyond 10 years can be associated with significant further increases over a subsequent 3 years in BMD at both the lumbar spine and total hip. This may allow some patients to achieve a desirable treatment target, though future studies on safety and efficacy are needed.

cards.title: Association between serum vitamin D levels and pediatric distal radius fractures: a case-control study.
cards.abstract: This study evaluated whether serum vitamin D levels are associated with distal radius fractures in children. In this case-control study, pediatric patients with confirmed distal radius fractures (cases) were compared to children visiting an orthopedic clinic for routine checks or minor muscular pain (controls). Serum vitamin D, phosphorus, and calcium levels were analyzed. We enrolled 98 children (mean age: 8.2 ± 2.6 years). Overall, 87.8% had serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations below 30 ng/ml, with a cohort mean of 22.04 ± 7.35 ng/ml. No statistically significant differences were found between the case and control groups regarding serum vitamin D (P = 0.806), calcium, or phosphorus levels. Logistic regression confirmed none of these metabolic markers were significantly associated with fracture incidence. Serum vitamin D levels were not associated with pediatric distal radius fractures in this population. The generally low 25(OH)D concentrations observed in both groups suggest that other factors may have a greater role in fracture risk. The level of evidence is III.

cards.title: Long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation with intracanal bone fragment compaction for indirect anterior column support: a single-arm feasibility study in high load-sharing classification score thoracolumbar burst fractures.
cards.abstract: Thoracolumbar burst fractures with high Load Sharing Classification (LSC) scores are mechanically unstable and associated with severe vertebral comminution and failure risk after short-segment fixation. This study evaluated outcomes of long-segment posterior fixation combined with intracanal bone fragment compaction as an indirect means of supporting the anterior column. This retrospective study analyzed prospectively collected data from 121 consecutive patients with unstable thoracolumbar burst fractures (T10-L2) and LSC scores >6. All patients underwent open long-segment posterior instrumentation, decompression, and compaction of retropulsed intracanal bone fragments. Radiological outcomes included Cobb angle, percentage of anterior height compression (PAHC), vertebral body compression ratio (VBCR), and spinal canal compromise. Neurological recovery was assessed using the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) scale, and functional outcomes using the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). The cohort included 70 men and 51 women, with a mean age of 37.2 years and follow-up of 23.2 months. At final follow-up, 58.7% (95% CI 49.8-67.1%) achieved ASIA grade E. Significant improvements were observed in VBCR, PAHC, Cobb angle (15.6° to 7.9°; p = 0.008), and spinal canal compromise (65.2% to 8.7%; p < 0.001). Mean ODI improved from 59.4 to 8.4 (p < 0.001). Long-segment posterior fixation with intracanal bone fragment compaction was associated with favorable short- to mid-term neurological, functional, and radiological outcomes. Prospective comparative studies with CT-based fusion assessment, standardized safety reporting, and longer follow-up are required to confirm effectiveness and durability.

cards.title: Abdominal ultrasound mitigates neurodegenerative pathology and alters specific gut microbial taxa in senescence-accelerated mice.
cards.abstract: Age-related changes in gut microbiota composition have been implicated in brain aging and cognitive decline, acting through the gut-brain axis on amyloid accumulation, tau pathology, synapse damage, and glial activation. Live microbial approaches such as probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation address this mechanism, but they still suffer from low efficacy and unknown safety issues. We tested whether abdominal ultrasound, an approach that does not involve microbes, can alleviate age-related neurodegeneration in the senescence-accelerated mouse strain SAMP8. We treated 6-month-old male SAMP8 mice for 1 month. We then assessed behavior, neuropathology, and synaptic proteins, and quantified four pre-specified fecal bacterial taxa. Ultrasound preserved neuronal survival in the hippocampal CA3, decreased amyloid-β load in the cortex and CA3, decreased tau hyperphosphorylation in all three regions, reduced Iba-1 and GFAP immunoreactive areas, and increased synaptophysin and cortical PSD-95. Neuronal survival in the cortex and CA1 did not differ significantly from sham-treated SAMP8 mice. In the gut microbiota, ultrasound significantly reduced the enriched taxon Tyzzerella, whereas the changes in Lactobacillus, Akkermansia and Atopobiaceae were large in magnitude but not statistically significant. In an exploratory analysis, four of 64 microbiota-neuropathology associations survived correction for multiple testing. Neither object recognition memory nor spatial memory differed significantly between treated and sham-treated SAMP8 mice. Abdominal ultrasound applied to the periphery therefore reduced age-associated neuropathology in the brain, accompanied by changes in specific gut microbial taxa whose causal contribution remains untested.

cards.title: Mitochondrial modulator M1 attenuates ovarian aging by remodeling granulosa cell metabolism and improving oocyte maturation.
cards.abstract: Ovarian aging is characterized by granulosa cell (GC) dysfunction and compromised oocyte maturation, yet effective mitochondria-targeted interventions remain limited. We investigated the association of the mitochondrial fusion promoter M1 with age-related transcriptional, mitochondrial, and metabolic phenotypes. Reanalysis of public single-cell transcriptomic data identified age-associated differences in a granulosa-enriched cluster across mitochondrial dynamics-related, glycolysis/lactate metabolic, bioenergetic/TCA-cycle, and granulosa-cell phenotype programs. RT-qPCR in early-passage, late-passage, and M1-treated late-passage HGL5 cells showed partial concordance with this transcriptomic framework. In late-passage HGL5 cells, M1 treatment induced a less fragmented, elongation-associated mitochondrial morphology accompanied by altered DRP1 phosphorylation, increased per-well respiratory readouts, and increased ATP fluorescence. In ex vivo aged oocytes, M1 increased polar body extrusion and was associated with reduced DCFDA fluorescence and increased CMXRos fluorescence. These findings indicate that M1 is associated with mitochondrial and metabolic remodeling in a late-passage HGL5 model displaying senescence-associated features and favorable maturation-associated readouts in aged oocytes. These data do not establish physiological granulosa-cell rejuvenation, improved developmental competence, or a DRP1-dependent mechanism. Further studies are required to establish the molecular target of M1 and its effects on fertilization, embryo development, and reproductive outcomes.

cards.title: The role of low muscle strength in predicting mortality in patients with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is a prevalent complication in chronic liver disease (CLD), traditionally assessed by muscle mass. Recent paradigm shifts focus to dynapenia as the primary determinant of adverse outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the role of dynapenia, as measured by handgrip strength (HGS) and ultrasound-derived diaphragmatic excursion, in predicting mortality in this population. This prospective study included consecutive outpatients with cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma history attending a tertiary hepatology unit. Muscle mass was assessed in subgroups using bioimpedance analysis (BIA) and computed tomography (CT). Associations between sarcopenia proxies and 24-month all-cause mortality were analyzed with adjusted Cox regression models, and survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves. Ninety-one patients were included (age 73.4 ± 8.1 years; 71 [78%] male); 20 (22%) had dynapenia. Twenty-two deaths occurred at two years (24.2%). Over 24 months, dynapenia (by HGS) and diaphragmatic excursion were associated with mortality in adjusted models (aHR 1.68, 95% CI 1.12-2.53, p = 0.012; aHR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97, p = 0.042). In subgroups, they remained the only muscle parameters associated with mortality, while muscle mass indices were not significant. Finally, Kaplan-Meier estimates showed lower 24-month survival in dynapenic patients across groups (in overall population 65% vs. 79%, p = 0.05). Low muscle strength is a key prognostic parameter in patients with cirrhosis and HCC. In our small cohort, it was the only muscle-related measure significantly associated with mortality. These findings support further evaluation of muscle strength assessment as a potential tool for risk stratification in this population.

cards.title: Physical Frailty Accelerates Multimorbidity Accumulation Across Distinct Disease Patterns
cards.abstract: Background Emerging evidence has linked frailty to individual chronic diseases, but whether it predicts a broad disease spectrum and accelerates multimorbidity accumulation over time remains unknown. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the associations of physical frailty with the burden of incident disease across a wide range of chronic conditions, and with the long-term rates of multimorbidity accumulation. Methods In this prospective cohort study of 466,864 UK Biobank participants , frailty status was assessed using the Fried frailty phenotype and categorized as robust, pre-frailty, or frailty. Chronic diseases were defined based on International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes, and disease patterns were identified using network analysis. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations of frailty status with incident chronic diseases, and linear mixed models were used to assess the annual rate of chronic disease accumulation. Results During a median follow-up of 13.8 years (IQR: 13.1-14.5), 536 incident chronic diseases across multiple systems were recorded. Physical frailty was associated with a significantly increased risk of 458 incident diseases (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.05/536). In the overall cohort, compared with robust participants, those with pre-frailty ({beta} = 0.266, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.264-0.267) and frailty ({beta} = 0.941, 95% CI: 0.936-0.946) exhibited significantly faster rates of multimorbidity accumulation. This accelerated multimorbidity accumulation was consistently observed across strata of baseline disease burden, including participant with 0 ({beta} = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.635-0.653), 1 ({beta} =0.748, 95% CI: 0.727-0.768), [≥] 2 ({beta} =0.940, 95% CI: 0.933-0.947) chronic conditions at baseline. Similar associations were also found across distinct disease patterns, including neurodegenerative, metabolic, and psychiatric patterns. Conclusions Physical frailty predicts a broad range of incident diseases and is associated with accelerated multimorbidity accumulation. Incorporating frailty assessment into prevention strategies may help mitigate the growing burden of multimorbidity.

cards.title: Restoring Physical Resilience: Consistent Functional and Sarcopenia Gains Across Two Vivifrail Cohorts
cards.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate change in physical function and probable sarcopenia following a 36-week community multicomponent exercise programme (Vivifrail model) across two consecutive cycles, and to assess the consistency of this change between cohorts. Study design: Quasi-experimental, single-arm, repeated-measures service evaluation. Ninety-two older adults (2025-2026 cohort; mean age 75.9 years, 88.0% women) completed baseline and post-intervention assessments; an independent 2024-2025 cohort (n = 86) was analysed jointly for replication (n = 178). Main outcome measures: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score (primary); Timed Up and Go (TUG), handgrip strength, 6-metre walk time and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) (secondary); probable sarcopenia (EWGSOP2), SPPB-based frailty category, and a fall-risk indicator computed identically in both cohorts. Results: SPPB improved by a mean of 1.33 points (Cohen's d = 0.96; p < .001), with concordant improvement in all four secondary outcomes (all q < .005). 72.8% reached the substantial minimal clinically important difference. Probable sarcopenia fell from 17.4% to 5.4% (p = .006), and frailty category shifted toward higher functional levels (p < .001). Effect sizes were consistent between cohorts for SPPB, handgrip and 6-metre walk; the Time x Cohort interaction was significant for TUG only. In the pooled sample, elevated fall risk fell from 19.7% to 11.2% (p = .002). Conclusions: A 36-week multicomponent exercise programme was associated with clinically meaningful, reproducible improvement in physical function and a reduction in probable sarcopenia across two independent cohorts. The single-arm design precludes causal inference.
