cards.title: Cellular senescence is an early feature and therapeutic target in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis TDP-43Q331K mice.
cards.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron degeneration in the motor cortex and spinal cord. Aging is a key risk factor for ALS, and cellular senescence - a hallmark of aging marked by irreversible cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype - has been implicated in neurodegeneration, yet its role in ALS progression remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that molecular markers of cellular senescence emerge in the motor cortex and spinal cord alongside declines in neural and neuromuscular function in TDP-43Q331K ALS mice, supporting senescence as an early feature of ALS pathology. To test whether reduced senescence ameliorates ALS pathology, we evaluated longitudinal senolytic treatment with dasatinib and quercetin (D&Q) in TDP-43Q331K mice. D&Q treatment improved motor behavior, neuromuscular function, and reduced axonal damage as measured by plasma neurofilament light chain, accompanied by robust improvements in motor cortex excitability and preservation of layer V neuron counts. At the cellular level, cortical microglia were implicated as a potential mediator of senolytic benefits based on reduced microglial TDP-43 burden and senescence markers. Together, these findings identify cellular senescence as an early, disease-relevant, and modifiable feature of ALS pathology.

cards.title: The double-edged sentinel: cGAS-STING as a context-dependent regulator of microglial senescence and neuronal genotoxic stress in neurodegeneration.
cards.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases may continue to progress even when a pathogenic protein aggregate is reduced, suggesting that downstream inflammatory and genotoxic circuits can become partly autonomous. This narrative review examines cGAS-STING as a context-dependent regulator of DNA-stress responses in the ageing and proteinopathic brain. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for mechanistic, translational, and human-tissue studies of cGAS-STING, DNA damage, mitochondrial quality control, neuroinflammation, and major neurodegenerative diseases. Evidence was separated into biochemical or cellular, animal, and human observations, and contradictory findings were retained. Mitochondrial DNA leakage is a recurrent candidate trigger, while activity-induced nuclear DNA breaks, defective repair, retrotransposon-derived cDNA, and micronuclear rupture provide conditional inputs. Microglial evidence is currently more extensive and causally developed than neuron-specific evidence; neuronal STING is most firmly supported in selected contexts such as excitotoxic or ischemic stress. Across Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, ALS/FTD, multiple sclerosis, and Huntington disease, cGAS-STING-associated inflammation is plausible but not uniform, and human validation remains limited. Therapeutic strategies therefore require cell-, source-, and stage-aware modulation rather than indiscriminate pathway ablation. cGAS-STING is best regarded as a testable kinetic-bottleneck model, not a universal driver of neurodegeneration. Longitudinal human studies and cell-resolved biomarkers are needed to determine when recalibration can suppress pathological inflammation while preserving antiviral and homeostatic functions.

cards.title: THE BILE ACID RECEPTOR TGR5 MODULATES HIPPOCAMPAL NEURAL STEM CELL STATE AND AGEING
cards.abstract: Ageing locks hippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) into deeper quiescence and inflammation-driven senescence, which are also associated with impaired cognition. The bile-acid receptor TGR5, a member class I G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs), is expressed in cultured hippocampal NSCs and in SOX2-positive cells of the adult sub granular zone, yet its role in NSC homeostasis is unknown. In this study we show that TGR5 selective agonist, TC-G 1005, expanded the NSC pool without forcing neuronal differentiation. Primary NSCs treatment with TC-G 1005 increased BrdU incorporation and PCNA in a concentration-dependent manner, and both responses were lost after TGR5 knockdown. TGR5 agonism in differentiating cultures increased nestin, left doublecortin (DCX) unchanged and suppressed MAP2 expression, preserving stemness rather than neuronal commitment. The agonist also released BMP4-imposed quiescence, lowering FOXO3a and restoring phospho-EGFR and ASCL1, and reopened autophagic flux, with less p62 and LC3-II, fewer LAMP2 puncta and more Beclin-1. Furthermore, activation of TGR5 suppressed IL-6 induced p53 and p16 expression, restored proliferation and contracted the inflammatory transcriptome by more than 90%, including Cdkn2a, Cdkn2b and Cdk6. In 18-month-old mice, brain-penetrant TC-G 1005 (5 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily for 28 days) expanded SOX2-positive and proliferating NSCs, reduced p16, recovered ASCL1 and improved spatial memory, without changing locomotion or generating DCX-positive neurons. Dentate gyrus-restricted TGR5 knockdown abolished these cellular effects and the rescue of spatial and social discrimination. Hippocampal proteomic analysis revealed that TC-G 1005 treated aged mice occupied an intermediate, partially rejuvenated position between young and aged proteomes, with 86 proteins shared between ageing- and treatment-responsive sets, and mitochondrial and complement C1q modules shifted toward youthful levels. TGR5 activation therefore relieves both quiescence and senescence in the aged neurogenic niche without driving neuronal differentiation. Collectively, these results suggest that TGR5 could be targeted to preserve cognition in ageing by rejuvenating the hippocampal stem-cell niche.

cards.title: Baseline history of primary fragility fracture is associated with medical complications and revision through 1 year in adult spinal deformity patients undergoing thoracolumbar spinal fusion.
cards.abstract: Fragility fractures (FFx) can indicate osteoporosis following posterior spinal fusion (PSF) in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients. We sought to evaluate the impact of a history of FFx on adverse postoperative outcomes following ≥ 3-level PSFs. This retrospective cohort study queried the Mariner10 PearlDiver database to identify patients aged ≥ 50 years undergoing ≥ 3-level PSF for ASD from 2010 to 2022. All trauma, infection, and tumor indications were excluded. Patients with and without a history of FFx (hip, proximal humerus, distal radius, vertebral body, or pelvis fracture) were stratified. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with adverse outcomes (covariates: age, sex, CCI, obesity, FFx history). 439 ASD patients were identified, of which 33 (7.5%) had FFx. These patients had higher overall medical complications (38.3% vs. 5.2%), respiratory failure (8.3% vs. 2%), DVT (8.3% vs. 0.6%), and infection (6.7% v 0.9%) at 90-day postoperatively, all p < 0.05. FFx patients had higher surgical complications (20% vs. 2.5%), revision/extension (15% vs. 0.4%), and decompression/laminectomy (6.7% vs. 0.8%) at 1-year, all p < 0.005. FFx history was associated with higher risk of wound disruption (OR = 3.9), respiratory failure (OR = 3.1), pneumonia (OR = 2.4), and PE (OR = 1.1). FFx history was associated with higher odds of revision/extension (OR = 3.5), all p < 0.05. FFx history was associated with both medical and surgical complications through 1-year postoperatively, demonstrating how important risk stratification/optimization data can be identified from simple preoperative assessment of FFx history. III.

cards.title: Diet-wide association study (DWAS) of hip fracture risk in UK postmenopausal women: a prospective cohort study of 541,887 women with 27,318 incident cases over ~ 20 years.
cards.abstract: Previous research on diet and hip fracture risk focused on selected foods and nutrients. We aim to conduct a systematic diet-wide association study of 99 dietary factors. The study population comprised 541,887 postmenopausal women in the Million Women Study. Dietary information was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire in 2000-2004, and calibrated using a 24-hour dietary recall. Incident hip fracture was ascertained through linked hospital admission records. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). After an average of 19.7 years of follow-up, 27,318 incident hip fractures occurred. In multivariable-adjusted models, 60 dietary factors were associated with hip fracture risk after multiple testing correction. The top five foods (based on p-value) were: chicken (HR and 95% CI = 0.84, 0.80-0.87 per 20 g/day), vegetables (0.88, 0.85-0.91 per 100 g/day), pasta (0.87, 0.83-0.91 per 20 g/day), chips (1.14, 1.10-1.18 per 25 g/day), and fizzy drinks (1.18, 1.12-1.24 per 50 g/day). The top five nutrients were: protein (0.79, 0.75-0.84 per 15 g/day), zinc (0.81, 0.77-0.86 per 2 mg/day), carotene (0.91, 0.88-0.94 per 1000 µg/day), fibre (0.89, 0.85-0.92 per 5 g/day), and niacin (0.82, 0.77-0.87 per 10 mg/day). The results were consistent across subgroup analyses and in analyses excluding the first five years of follow-up. Many "healthy" foods were associated with lower risk of hip fracture, and "unhealthy" foods with higher risk. Further research is needed to assess whether these associations were causal or reflect overall diet quality or other lifestyle confounding.

cards.title: Correlation Between Paravertebral Muscles Degeneration and Spinopelvic Parameters in Patients With Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures.
cards.abstract: BACKGROUND Osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) are correlated with thoracolumbar sagittal imbalance associated with paravertebral muscles (PVM) atrophy and fatty infiltration (FI). This study investigated PVM degeneration and its correlation with spinopelvic parameters in patients with OVCFs. MATERIAL AND METHODS This retrospective case-control study enrolled 50 patients with OVCFs and 50 controls with lumbar degeneration, frequency-matched for age (±5 years). Complete sex matching was not achieved. Primary comparisons were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and lumbar bone mineral density (BMD); subgroup analyses were exploratory and unadjusted. MRI measured the PVM from T11 to L2 and the cross-sectional area (CSA) and FI of the multifidus (MF) and erector spinae (ES) at L3. RESULTS Patients with OVCFs showed reduced CSA and increased FI (P<0.05). After adjustment, sagittal vertical axis, thoracic kyphosis, and pelvic tilt increased and lumbar lordosis (LL) decreased (all P≤0.003), whereas sacral slope (P=0.538) and pelvic incidence (P=0.602) did not differ. MF and ES CSA correlated negatively with SVA and positively with LL, while FI showed the opposite (all P<0.01). In exploratory analyses, patients aged ≥65 years had a larger SVA (P=0.040), and women a smaller LL and lower BMD (both P<0.05); no PVM differences were seen across subgroups. CONCLUSIONS In this cross-sectional cohort, PVM degeneration correlated with sagittal malalignment after adjustment for measured confounders (adjusted cross-sectional associations). Advanced age correlated with greater SVA, and female sex with smaller LL and lower BMD. No PVM differences were detected across subgroups. Further trials are required to validate targeted paravertebral rehabilitation strategies.

cards.title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
cards.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

cards.title: Driver or Passenger? A Bradford Hill Framework for Aging-Associated lncRNAs.
cards.abstract: Transcriptomic surveys of aging tissues routinely report hundreds to thousands of differentially expressed long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and the field has no agreed way of separating causal drivers from passengers that merely track the aging phenotype. I translate Sir Austin Bradford Hill's nine criteria for causal inference, formulated in 1965, into operational tests for aging-associated lncRNAs. Each criterion is recorded as 0, 1 or 2, and the per-criterion profile is the result: no sum or band decides a category. Hill offered viewpoints, not independent quantities to be added; here half of the cited studies support two or more criteria, so a total counts some evidence twice. Two axes are reported separately - molecular causal evidence, and organism-level validation (criterion 8), recorded as supportive, not evaluated, or in vivo at a non-aging endpoint - so that an animal experiment on development, reproduction, cancer or injury is not read as a negative test of aging. Applied to ten worked examples chosen to illustrate rather than to sample the field - NEAT1, MEG3, lincRNA-p21, MALAT1, MIR31HG, SALNR, TERRA, PANDAR, HOTAIR, TUG1 - the profiles separate candidates awaiting an animal experiment from those whose animal experiments addressed something else. MALAT1 is instructive: of six in-vivo perturbation studies, one assays a senescence endpoint. No candidate has an aging experiment that returned a negative result, and none reaches the top of criterion 8, which requires conditional deletion or a titrated antisense regimen with rescue. Organism-level evidence, not literature volume, is the structural bottleneck.

cards.title: Loss of KMT2D accelerates hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation and senescence by increasing mitochondrial ROS production
cards.abstract: Longitudinal bone growth occurs through endochondral ossification, which is accompanied by the differentiation of chondrocytes in the growth plate. Disruption in chondrocyte maturation can lead to skeletal growth abnormalities, such as those observed in Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1), a genetic disorder caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in the KMT2D gene. KS1 patients exhibit postnatal growth deficiency, craniofacial hypoplasia, and skeletal deformities, yet the mechanisms underlying these phenotypic manifestations remain poorly understood. Our study investigated the effects of KMT2D deficiency on chondrocyte maturation and identified premature chondrocyte hypertrophy as a key driver of skeletal abnormalities in KS1. We previously observed reduced femur and tibia length in a KS1 mouse model, along with altered growth plate architecture, particularly affecting the heights of the proliferative and hypertrophic zones. Here, we show that KMT2D-deficient chondrocytes exhibit accelerated differentiation and early senescence upon exposure to supraphysiological oxygen levels (20% O2). These pathological changes were linked to increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production likely caused by deficiencies in electron transport chain function, leading to oxidative stress and premature hypertrophy. Pharmacological ROS neutralization or hypoxic conditions mitigated these effects, restoring normal chondrocyte differentiation and preventing premature ossification. These findings demonstrate that KMT2D loss induces oxidative stress-driven chondrocyte hypertrophy, disrupting the balance of cartilage growth and ossification. Our study provides crucial mechanistic insights into KS1-associated skeletal abnormalities and suggests mitochondrial ROS regulation as a potential therapeutic avenue.

cards.title: Handgrip Strength for Mortality Prediction in Hemodialysis Patients Using the Chronological-to-Metabolic Age Ratio: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Hemodialysis patients face disproportionately high mortality, with sarcopenia and reduced muscle strength as major contributors. In this study, we aimed to investigate whether the prognostic value of handgrip strength for all-cause mortality is modified by the chronological-to-metabolic age ratio, a marker of biological aging and cumulative physiological stress. This multicenter prospective cohort study enrolled 307 adult hemodialysis patients. handgrip strength was measured with a standardized dynamometer prior to dialysis, and metabolic age was estimated via multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis to calculate the chronological-to-metabolic age ratio. Demographic, clinical, anthropometric, and dialysis-related parameters were also collected. Participants were followed every three months through three years for all-cause mortality, and the prognostic value of handgrip strength was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models, and discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Higher handgrip strength was associated with reduced all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients, particularly among those whose metabolic age exceeded chronological age (HR = 0.879; 95% CI: 0.812-0.953; P = 0.002). While handgrip strength showed poor discrimination across chronological (AUC = 0.550-0.578) and metabolic age categories (AUC = 0.571-0.648), it demonstrated relatively higher discriminative performance in patients with accelerated metabolic aging (AUC = 0.810; cut-off = 22.16; sensitivity 65%; specificity 94%). Handgrip strength was associated with all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients, and this association may be modified by the chronological-to-metabolic age ratio. However, the chronological-to-metabolic age ratio did not provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical variables and handgrip strength. The observed subgroup-specific discriminative performance and HGS cut-off values are exploratory and require external validation before clinical application.

cards.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of GFAP and UCH-L1 for Acute Intracranial Trauma in a Predominantly Blast-Exposed Cohort of Combat Casualties
cards.abstract: Importance There is an urgent need for objective blood tests to guide triage of suspected traumatic brain injury (TBI) in far-forward combat environments, where blast exposure is common and neuroimaging is frequently unavailable. Blood-based glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) are transforming triage of suspected TBI due to their 99% negative predictive value for ruling out acute intracranial trauma in civilian impact TBI. However, accuracy in military blast-dominant TBI is unclear. Objective To determine accuracy of day-of-injury serum or plasma GFAP and UCH-L1 levels for ruling-out acute intracranial trauma in a sequential real-world cohort of combat casualties. Design Retrospective cohort study leveraging existing data from a clinical laboratory validation protocol that processed and stored leftover day-of-injury clinical samples from evacuated combat casualties between January 1, 2024, and February 6, 2025 for subsequent analysis for GFAP and UCH-L1 using FDA-cleared assay thresholds. Setting Single-center, tertiary referral trauma center. Participants Day-of-injury plasma or serum GFAP and UCH-L1 levels were available for 137 combat casualties. The cohort was 99.3% male with a median age of 21.8 years; 75.2% sustained blast-related injuries. Most (92.7%) had blood collected within 6 hours of injury. Exposure Serum or plasma GFAP and UCH-L1 measured with Abbott Alinity-i or i-STAT TBI assays. Elevation was defined as GFAP [≥]35 pg/mL or UCH-L1 [≥]400 pg/mL on Alinity-i, and GFAP [≥]30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 [≥]360 pg/mL on i-STAT. Main Outcomes and Measures Accuracy of biomarker elevation for ruling-out intracranial trauma on head CT, including sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value (NPV). Results Among 137 casualties, 83 (60.6%) were biomarker-elevated. Sixteen participants (11.7%) had CT-confirmed intracranial trauma, of whom 15 were biomarker-elevated, yielding 93.8% sensitivity and 98.2% NPV, and 43.8% specificity. Twenty-three participants (16.8%) had intracranial trauma and/or head/face/c-spine fracture; 21 were biomarker-elevated, corresponding to 91.3% sensitivity, 96.3% NPV, and 45.6% specificity. Conclusions and Relevance In this real-world cohort of blast-dominant combat casualties, day-of-injury GFAP and UCH-L1 demonstrated high NPV and sensitivity for intracranial trauma, with modest specificity. These findings support the utility of GFAP and UCH-L1 to aid early triage and decision-making in blast-dominant military TBI.

cards.title: Association of systemic bone mineral density and tibial cortical thickness with postoperative subsidence after surgical treatment of tibial plateau fractures.
cards.abstract: Tibial plateau fractures are common fractures above the age of 50 years old and are frequently considered osteoporosis-associated fractures. However, the association between bone mineral density (BMD) and postoperative articular subsidence remains unclear. The primary objective was to assess whether there was an association between systemic BMD or tibial cortical thickness and articular subsidence after surgical treatment of tibial plateau fractures. Secondary objectives were to evaluate preoperative fracture displacement and the prevalence of reduced BMD in this cohort according to WHO criteria. In this retrospective cohort study, patients treated surgically for low-energy tibial plateau fractures between 2017 and 2024 who underwent Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DEXA) within 12 months before or after injury were included. DEXA-derived T-scores were used to assess systemic bone density and Tibial Cortical Thickness (TCT) was used as a measure of tibial cortical bone status. Fracture subsidence and preoperative displacement were measured in the coronal plane using articular depression. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed adjusting for age, BMI and fracture comminution. The primary outcome was also adjusted for preoperative articular depression. Fifty-nine patients were included in the analysis. There were 57 women and 2 men. Mean age was 63.9 years (SD ± 8.1) and mean BMI was 26.2 (SD ± 4.8). Schatzker type II was the most common fracture pattern (30/59, 50.8%), followed by Schatzker type VI (20/59, 33.9%). According to WHO criteria, 1.7% had normal bone mineral density, 49.2% had osteopenia and 49.2% had osteoporosis. There was no statistically significant association between postoperative subsidence and systemic BMD (p = 0.259) or TCT (p = 0.340). Nor was there a statistically significant association between preoperative articular depression and systemic BMD (p = 0.132) or TCT (p = 0.397). In this study, no statistically significant association was identified between systemic BMD or tibial cortical thickness and postoperative articular subsidence or preoperative depression, although the limited sample size warrants cautious interpretation. Osteoporosis and osteopenia were common in this selected cohort of DEXA-assessed patients above the age of 50 years with surgically treated low-energy tibial plateau fractures.

cards.title: Early fixation of traumatic mandible fractures is associated with decreased morbidity and resource utilization.
cards.abstract: There is no clear guidance on when isolated mandibular fractures should undergo surgical fixation. Multiple studies have assessed the timing of mandibular fracture repair, with a consensus that earlier repair does not change outcomes. We aimed to challenge this consensus and identify a data-driven time for surgical fixation. We hypothesized that delayed fixation would be associated with worse outcomes. Data on adult patients with closed mandible fractures who underwent surgical fixation were abstracted from the Trauma Quality Improvement Program database from 2017 to 2023. Patients with prehospital cardiac arrest, Abbreviated Injury Scale >2 in other body regions, interfacility transfers, deaths, and those discharged from the emergency room were excluded from analysis. The primary outcome was a composite variable of in-hospital complications. The secondary outcome was prolonged mechanical ventilation. A receiver operating characteristic curve was generated to determine a data-driven timing of surgical fixation based on observed differences in the primary outcome. Patients who underwent fixation before and after this defined time were grouped as "early" or "delayed," respectively. Statistical analyses used to compare outcomes between the groups included multivariable logistic regression and negative binomial regression. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 40 hours as the proposed data-driven time to fixation. Delayed fixation was associated with a higher composite complication rate (4.1% vs. 1.5%, p < 0.001) and independently associated with a two-fold increase in overall complications (adjusted odds ratio, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.90-2.79, p < 0.001). The negative binomial generalized linear model also identified delayed fixation as a risk factor for prolonged mechanical ventilation (incidence rate ratio, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.26-1.61, p < 0.001). The proposed data-driven timing for fixation in traumatic mandibular fractures is within the first 40 hours from admission. Repair within this time frame is associated with fewer complications and shorter duration of mechanical ventilation. cards.title: Regenerative Strategies for Traumatic Dental Injuries in Craniofacial Trauma: A Narrative Review.
cards.abstract: Traumatic dental injuries are an important component of craniofacial and dentoalveolar trauma and may compromise oral function, facial aesthetics, alveolar support, and long-term tooth preservation, particularly in young patients. They can lead to disruption of pulpal blood supply, pulp necrosis, and periapical tissue damage; in immature permanent teeth with open apices and thin root walls, infection control must be balanced against preservation of further root development. Within the broader context of craniofacial trauma, this narrative review summarizes the indications, operative procedures, scaffold materials, clinical efficacy, influencing factors, imaging assessment, and multidisciplinary role of REPs as a tooth-preservation strategy for crown/root fractures, luxation injuries, and replanted avulsed teeth. In traumatized immature permanent teeth, REPs achieved an overall success rate of approximately 80%, with symptom resolution, periapical healing, and continued root development in most cases, whereas outcomes were less favorable for avulsed and replanted teeth. In summary, REP may provide a biological-based dental preservation option for selected traumatized teeth, although standardized case selection, treatment plans, and long-term follow-up remain crucial.

cards.title: Beyond reduced intake: tumor metabolism and immune dysregulation drive cancer-related malnutrition in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).
cards.abstract: Cancer-related malnutrition is highly prevalent in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and represents a major determinant of treatment tolerance, quality of life, and survival. Although traditionally attributed to reduced oral intake caused by dysphagia, mucositis, and treatment-related toxicity, increasing evidence indicates that malnutrition in HNSCC is largely driven by tumor-induced metabolic and inflammatory alterations. Enhanced aerobic glycolysis, systemic inflammation, and tumor-derived factors promote hypermetabolism, substrate redistribution, and progressive skeletal muscle depletion. Within this immune-metabolic framework, the tumor behaves as a metabolic sink, redirecting glucose, lipids, and amino acids from host tissues to sustain its growth, thereby contributing to energy wasting and sarcopenia independently of caloric intake. Recent clinical data support the translational relevance of this model. Imaging-based assessment of body composition at the third cervical vertebra (C3) and metabolic imaging parameters such as total lesion glycolysis (TLG) provide measurable indicators of tumor metabolic burden and its association with skeletal muscle loss and nutritional risk. Integrating metabolic imaging, inflammatory biomarkers, and body composition analysis may enable earlier identification of patients at high risk of malnutrition and treatment-related toxicity. This review integrates these complementary biological and imaging domains into a unified immune-metabolic framework for nutritional risk stratification in HNSCC. Recognizing cancer-related malnutrition in HNSCC as a tumor-driven immune-metabolic syndrome has important therapeutic implications. Early immune-metabolic nutritional strategies, rather than reactive caloric supplementation alone, may represent a key component of integrated oncologic care aimed at preserving lean body mass and improving clinical outcomes.

cards.title: Rheumatology capacity building for health care providers in Uganda: an ILAR project report.
cards.abstract: The burden of rheumatological diseases in Uganda is unknown. Availability of rheumatologic services is limited with patients presenting late. The program set out to improve rheumatology disease knowledge in diagnosis, patient care, and clinical examination among health care providers. Using an educational curriculum adopted for medical residents and community-based/generalist physicians, we trained over 395 doctors. Through online webinars, ten lectures focusing on topics such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), osteoarthritis (OA), infectious arthritis, gout/crystalline arthritis, osteoporosis, and an overview of joint disease and autoimmunity to increase awareness and improve diagnosis and management of RMDs among healthcare providers in Uganda and east Africa were delivered. We assessed the training to ascertain learning with pre- and post-test assessments conducted with real-time analyses. Analysis of changes in knowledge performance was conducted and p < 0.05 was considered significant. Across the sessions with data available, post-session correct response rates were higher than pre-session rates for nearly all questions. The most pronounced improvements were observed in Session 2 (Osteoarthritis), where the absolute increases in correct responses ranged from 40 to 72% (all P < 0.001). Our project utilized a successful model of providing professional rheumatologic training and health education to healthcare providers in resource limited settings. It also lays foundations for short- and long-term medical education in rheumatology and raising public awareness of rheumatic diseases. Key Points • Successful professional rheumatologic training and health education models can be used to improve rheumatology knowledge to healthcare providers in resource limited settings. • Developing a rheumatology registry is critical in bridging a critical information gap in Uganda for research, surveillance and clinical care. • Improving health care providers' rheumatology knowledge improves early referrals and disease diagnosis.

cards.title: Single-Nucleus Atlas of Spinal Sarcopenia Patients Reveals Disruption of Quiescent and Regenerative Satellite Cell Niches in Fatty-Infiltrated Muscle.
cards.abstract: Severe muscle fat infiltration is a contributing factor to muscle loss, particularly in the spinal sarcopenia population. However, the underlying mechanism largely remains elusive. Here, we identified the intramuscular fat fraction (IMFF), rather than perimuscular fat fraction, as an independent determinant of trunk muscle strength. Individuals with higher IMFF (10-15% and >15%) exhibited significantly lower paraspinal muscle mass and strength compared to those with lower IMFF (<5%). Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing, we established the first cellular atlas of fat-infiltrated paraspinal muscle, revealing profound remodeling of muscle architecture, extracellular matrix organization, and satellite cell niches. Among the adipose-derived factors, ANGPTL4 emerged as a key paracrine suppressor of myogenesis, acting through upregulation of syndecan-2 (SDC2) in satellite cells. Inhibition of SDC2 partially rescued ANGPTL4-induced myogenic impairment in C2C12 cells. Furthermore, we identified a GPC3+ fibro/adipogenic progenitor (FAP) subpopulation with enhanced lipogenic potential, characterized by high expression of GPC3, PPARG, ADIPOQ, and FABP4, representing a transition from MMEhigh GPC3low FAPs into MMElowGPC3high adipogenic FAPs. Collectively, our findings delineate the cellular landscape and signaling interactions that underlie pathological fat infiltration in spinal muscles, providing mechanistic insight and potential therapeutic targets for spinal sarcopenia.

cards.title: From Restrictions to Reopening: Changing Epidemiology of Midfacial Fractures After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
cards.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected trauma epidemiology, but data on post-pandemic maxillofacial trauma remain limited. This study compared midfacial fracture epidemiology between intra-pandemic and post-pandemic periods at a tertiary maxillofacial trauma center. This retrospective cohort study included 156 adults with non-nasal midfacial fractures treated intra-pandemic (February 2020 - January 2021; n = 57) or post-pandemic (February 2023 - January 2024; n = 99). Demographics, trauma etiology and context, fracture patterns, associated injuries, temporal distribution, and treatment parameters were compared. Falls (66.7 % vs. 20.2 %; q < 0.001), accidents at home (56.1 % vs. 15.2 %; q < 0.001), and syncope-related trauma (17.5 % vs. 5.1 %; q = 0.034) decreased post-pandemic, whereas alcohol-associated trauma increased (10.5 % vs. 27.3 %; q = 0.034). Differences in falls, accidents at home, and alcohol-associated trauma remained significant after adjustment for age and sex. Road-traffic, interpersonal-violence, sports, and e-scooter injuries increased numerically but none of these differences were statistically significant after FDR adjustment. The overall time-of-day distribution differed between cohorts (p < 0.001), with proportionally fewer morning and more evening/night injuries post-pandemic. Time to presentation and surgery decreased post-pandemic (respectively p = 0.008, p = 0.001), while no statistically significant differences were detected in fracture distribution or length of stay. Post-pandemic midfacial trauma was characterized by fewer fall- and home-associated injuries and more alcohol-associated and night-time trauma, whereas no statistically significant differences were detected in fracture distribution or treatment modality. These findings suggest that the principal differences between the study periods concerned exposure circumstances and injury timing rather than anatomical fracture patterns. Given the observational design and absence of a directly analyzed pre-pandemic comparator, these findings describe differences between the two study periods without establishing a causal effect of reopening or a return to pre-pandemic patterns.

cards.title: Outcomes of Surgical Interventions in Children With Fibrous Dysplasia/McCune-Albright Syndrome.
cards.abstract: Fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright (FD/MAS) is a rare bone disorder with an increased risk of skeletal deformities and fractures. Data on surgical indications, techniques, outcomes, and complications remain limited. An observational retrospective cohort study was conducted on children with FD/MAS who underwent FD-related orthopaedic surgery before the age of 18 years. Time-to-event analyses were performed, with the event defined as (re)fracture or second surgery after the first surgery. A total of 45 children with FD/MAS were included (57.8% boys), with a median age of 10 years at diagnosis and 13 years at first surgery. In total, 64 surgical sites were included, and the median follow-up was 10 years (range 0.8 to 25.3). Surgery was performed for (impending) fractures in most cases (n=45, 70.3%), involving the proximal femur in 50.0%. Most frequently performed were osteosynthesis with hardware/implants (56.3%), followed by cortical strut grafting (21.9%). (Re)Fractures were the most common complication, often adjacent to the surgical site of the previous surgery. The probability of remaining free from an event was 70.3% at 1 year and 41.9% at 5 years. Increased risk of an event was associated with female sex (HR 2.2, 95% CI: 1.1-4.5, P=0.02) and lower age at index surgery (HR 0.93 per year increase, 95% CI: 0.86-0.99, P=0.04). In this largest series of children with orthopaedic surgery for FD/MAS, the proximal femur was the most common surgical site, typically for (impending) fractures. Risk of an event ((re)fracture or second surgery) was higher in females and those operated at a younger age. Level III.

cards.title: Reduced serum Irisin levels in systemic sclerosis: a cross-sectional case-control study.
cards.abstract: Irisin is a muscle-derived myokine implicated in metabolic regulation, endothelial function, inflammation, and fibrotic remodeling. Its relevance in systemic sclerosis (SSc), a disease characterized by autoimmunity, vasculopathy, and fibrosis, remains unknown. To compare serum Irisin levels between patients with SSc and healthy controls and to evaluate their associations with clinical-serological phenotype and organ-domain involvement in SSc. This single-center cross-sectional case-control study included 52 patients with SSc and 47 healthy controls. Serum Irisin was measured by ELISA. Clinical-serological subsets, nailfold videocapillaroscopy findings, modified Rodnan skin score, pulmonary function, HRCT-derived ILD and Warrick scores, echocardiographic variables, gastrointestinal involvement, comorbidities, treatment exposure, and laboratory parameters were assessed. Adjusted analyses used log-linear models with robust standard errors. Serum Irisin levels were significantly lower in SSc patients than in controls [696.70 pg/mL, IQR 611.16-1288.50 vs. 755.84 pg/mL, IQR 689.34-1899.75; p = 0.004]. This association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and smoking status, corresponding to 23.8% lower Irisin levels in SSc. Exploratory within-SSc analyses suggested lower Irisin levels in diffuse SSc and Scl-70-positive disease, particularly in adjusted models; however, unadjusted subgroup comparisons were weaker and should be interpreted cautiously. Irisin was not associated with NVC damage burden, mRSS, ILD severity, pulmonary function, or echocardiographic variables. Serum Irisin levels are reduced in patients with SSc compared with healthy controls. Exploratory phenotype analyses suggest a possible association with diffuse/Scl-70-related disease, but this signal requires confirmation in independent cohorts. Irisin did not reflect established organ-domain damage, suggesting that it may represent a broader myokine-metabolic alteration in SSc rather than a direct organ severity biomarker. Key Points • Serum Irisin levels were lower in patients with systemic sclerosis than in healthy controls. • Exploratory phenotype analyses suggested lower Irisin levels in diffuse and Scl-70-positive SSc, but these subgroup findings require cautious interpretation. • Serum Irisin was not associated with NVC damage, skin score, ILD severity, pulmonary function, or echocardiographic variables.

cards.title: Cellular senescence: six decades of discovery and reinvention.
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence has undergone a remarkable conceptual evolution since its discovery in 1961. Initially described by Hayflick and Moorhead as the finite proliferative lifespan of cultured human cells, senescence was first viewed as a consequence of cellular aging. The identification of telomere shortening, senescence biomarkers, and oncogene- and damage-induced senescence subsequently established its molecular basis and role as a tumor-suppressive stress response. The discovery of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) further transformed the field by revealing that senescent cells actively communicate with and remodel their tissue environment. Genetic mouse models later demonstrated causal roles for senescent cells in tissue repair, aging, and age-related disease, while senotherapeutics established senescence as a therapeutic target. Here, we trace the major conceptual transitions that shaped the field, from replicative endpoint to stress-response program, regulator of tissue homeostasis, driver of chronic pathology, and clinically actionable process. We discuss the discoveries, controversies, and technological advances underlying these transitions and how emerging single-cell technologies, precision biomarkers, and targeted interventions are shaping the next era of senescence research.

cards.title: Dogs and cats undergoing surgery for penetrating thoracic trauma have high survival despite frequent complications, and imaging may underestimate injury severity.
cards.abstract: To describe clinical and radiographic findings in dogs and cats with surgically confirmed penetrating thoracic trauma and evaluate associations with outcomes. This retrospective, multicenter observational study reviewed records from 5 referral hospitals to identify dogs and cats with surgically confirmed penetrating thoracic trauma between July 1, 2010, and July 31, 2025. Inclusion required thoracic radiographs, surgical reports, and perioperative records. A total of 86 dogs and 5 cats were identified. Mean animal trauma triage score was higher in nonsurvivors (7.6 ± 2.4; n = 20) than survivors (5.2 ± 2.5; 71). Radiographic findings included pneumothorax (73.6%), pulmonary contusions (65.9%), and rib fractures (62.6%). Computed tomography findings often identified more injuries. Time from presentation to surgery did not differ in survivors versus nonsurvivors. Lung lobectomy was performed in 24.2% of patients and was more common in nonsurvivors (45.0% vs 18.3%). Intra- and postoperative complications occurred in 56% and 51.7% of patients, respectively. Survival to discharge was 78.0% (71 of 91 patients), with a median hospitalization of 3.3 days (range, 1 to 12 days). Among 55 patients with follow up, 11 (20%) had complications related to thoracic trauma. Surgical management of penetrating thoracic trauma was associated with a high survival rate despite frequent complications. Animal trauma triage is a useful prognostic indicator. Computed tomography may alter treatment plans. Clinicians should anticipate higher injury severity than anticipated based on routine imaging and examination. Higher animal trauma triage scores were associated with nonsurvival and may provide useful prognostic information. Close monitoring is needed following surgery for penetrating thoracic trauma.

cards.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis Accelerates Frailty and Functional Decline
cards.abstract: Frailty reflects declining physiological reserve across multiple organ systems with aging, yet the underlying biological mechanisms contributing to frailty remain poorly understood. We tested whether somatic mutations in the blood were associated with incident frailty and faster progression in 730,088 participants from UK Biobank, All of Us, BioVU and the Womens Health Initiative. We found that clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and autosomal mosaic chromosomal alterations showed strong associations with frailty, whereas mosaic loss of chromosome X or Y did not. Findings were consistent across survey-based, directly measured and clinically assessed frailty, as well as healthspan phenotypes. A Tet2 mouse model demonstrated multisystem frailty-like functional decline and T-cell remodeling. In humans, T-cell activation-related proteins directly mediated the association between clonal hematopoiesis and frailty. Collectively, these findings support a model in which clonal hematopoiesis accelerates biological aging through immunosenescence.

cards.title: Association of Sarcopenia With Global, Motor, Cognitive, and Swallowing Function Prognosis in Stroke Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia has been demonstrated to correlate with the prognosis of stroke. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the impact of sarcopenia on global, motor, cognitive, and swallowing function outcomes in stroke patients. Relevant studies investigating the association between sarcopenia and multidimensional prognostic outcomes in stroke were retrieved from the PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Scopus databases. The primary outcome was the risk of poor global functional prognosis assessed by the modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Secondary outcomes included motor function scores (Functional Independence Measure-motor, FIM-motor), cognitive function scores, and the risk of swallowing dysfunction. A total of 36 cohort studies were finally included. Pooled results indicated that stroke patients with comorbid sarcopenia faced a notably elevated risk of poor global functional prognosis (mRS, OR = 2.43, 95% CI: 1.95 to 3.03, p < 0.001). The motor function scores (FIM-motor, SMD = -0.94, 95% CI: -1.11 to -0.77, p < 0.001) and cognitive function scores (FIM-cognition or Montreal Cognitive Assessment, SMD = -0.95, 95% CI: -1.22 to -0.69, p < 0.001) in the sarcopenia group were significantly lower than those in the non-sarcopenia group, while the risk of swallowing dysfunction showed a notable but non-significant elevation (endotracheal intubation or Functional Oral Intake Scale, OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 0.94 to 2.25, p = 0.09). Subgroup analyses indicated that the patient populations, cut-off value of mRS, follow-up duration, stroke type, and diagnostic criteria for sarcopenia were the main sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results. Egger's test suggested the presence of publication bias, but the conclusions remained valid after correction using the trim-and-fill method. Sarcopenia is an important risk factor for poor global, motor, cognitive, and swallowing function prognosis in stroke patients. In clinical practice, sarcopenia screening should be incorporated into the routine assessment of stroke patients, and individualized interventions should be promptly implemented for high-risk populations to improve long-term prognosis.

cards.title: Occipital plate-assisted posterior reduction for tumor-related severe atlantoaxial dislocation: a single-case surgical technique.
cards.abstract: Tumor-related severe atlantoaxial dislocation is rare but may rapidly endanger the cervicomedullary junction when axis destruction, pathological fracture, and craniovertebral instability coexist. This single-case technical note describes a posterior-only occipital plate-assisted reduction technique for a selected patient with severe but reducible tumor-related atlantoaxial dislocation in whom the atlas and axis could not be used as reliable reduction anchors. Conventional reduction strategies for congenital, inflammatory, traumatic, or degenerative atlantoaxial dislocation commonly depend on traction, atlantoaxial joint release, direct C1-C2 manipulation, or C1/C2 screw-based reduction. These maneuvers may be unsafe when the atlas has translated anteriorly beyond the axis body or when osteolysis structurally compromises the axis. The operative principle is to use the occipital plate as an active proximal reduction handle and the subaxial cervical spine as a reliable distal fixation base. After neutral Mayfield positioning, posterior exposure, decompression when indicated, and distal cervical screw placement, a precontoured rod is locked to the distal anchors. The occipital plate is connected to the proximal rod while maintaining a deliberate plate-to-skull step-off. The plate is then compressed to the occipital surface and fixed with occipital screws; release of compression allows the skull-occiput complex to settle into the rod-defined alignment, indirectly reducing the atlantoaxial dislocation without lifting the tumor-involved C1-C2 segment. The illustrative case demonstrates immediate radiographic correction and decompression through a single posterior approach, with quantitative radiographic and clinical outcomes reported in tabular form. As the evidence is limited to one patient, the technique should be considered hypothesis-generating and requires larger clinical series and biomechanical validation before broader adoption.

cards.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Reveal Senescent Fibroblast-Associated ADAMTS2 as a Critical Indicator of Intestinal Inflammation in IBD.
cards.abstract: Although cellular senescence contributes to tissue dysfunction in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), the heterogeneity of senescence at the single-cell resolution remains poorly defined. In this study, we systematically characterized the senescence landscape within the IBD microenvironment, with particular emphasis on fibroblast subpopulations and their systemic consequences. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset was applied to profile senescence-associated feature heterogeneity. Fibroblasts were classified into high-senescence (HS-Fibro) and low-senescence (LS-Fibro) groups according to senescence scores. HS-Fibro-specific gene signatures were identified and functionally annotated. Intercellular communication networks were constructed using CellChat to delineate the HS-Fibro interactome atlas, with emphasis on identifying cellular targets responsive to senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) signals. Integrated microarray datasets were employed to elucidate the systemic impact of HS-Fibro in IBD. Through the integration of differential expression analysis, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), and an ensemble of 113 machine learning algorithms, seven hub genes implicated in IBD progression were systematically identified and prioritized. In the IBD microenvironment, fibroblasts exhibited enhanced senescence activity. HS-Fibro displayed potent pro-inflammatory properties and enhanced communicative capacity. IBD patients with high HS-Fibro infiltration showed sustained immune-inflammatory activity. Systematic bioinformatic analysis and immunohistochemistry validation identified ADAMTS2 as a robust diagnostic indicator for IBD, with substantially elevated expression in patients relative to controls. The human colon fibroblast cell line CCD-18Co was treated with H2O2 to establish a cellular senescence model, demonstrating marked upregulation of ADAMTS2, SASP markers, and fibrosis-related genes. Moreover, siRNA-mediated knockdown of ADAMTS2 resulted in obvious attenuation of these SASP and fibrosis-associated genes.

cards.title: Quantitative lipidomics reveals Lipid perturbation of plasma apoptotic extracellular vesicles during physiological aging
cards.abstract: Introduction Aging is closely implicated in the pathogenesis of chronic diseases, degenerative conditions, and mortality, making it a core research focus in geroscience. As direct secretory products of apoptotic cells, apoptotic bodies can directly reflect the intensity of apoptotic activity and the degree of systemic and cellular aging. Given their close correlation with senescence progression, apoptotic bodies hold great potential as reliable and sensitive biomarkers for evaluating aging status. However, apoptotic bodies as effective indicators of aging remain to be explored. Methods We characterized the lipid profile of apoptotic bodies (ApoEVs) and explored the changes in lipid species related to aging. Total lipids, multiple lipid subclasses, and fatty acid saturation within plasma apoptotic bodies were analyzed to identify aging-associated lipid alterations. Results and Discussion A comprehensive reduction in total lipids, multiple lipid subclasses, and fatty acid saturation within plasma apoptotic bodies highlights systemic lipid reprogramming in aging. Decreased total levels of Hex2Cer, LPC, LPE, TG, ChE, SM, and SPH are the features of aging. This study not only deepens the understanding of aging-related lipid dysfunction, but also offers circulating lipid biomarkers for assessing biological aging and age-related pathologies.

cards.title: Five-Year Clinical Outcomes of Surgically Treated Different Types of Tibial Pilon Fractures.
cards.abstract: Intra-articular distal tibial pilon fractures are most commonly caused by high-energy trauma and are often associated with severe soft-tissue injuries. The literature on medium-to-long-term clinical outcomes is limited. The purpose of this follow-up study was to evaluate the 5-year clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction among patients with different types of tibial pilon fractures. One hundred twenty-six consecutive patients with operatively treated tibial pilon fractures were identified between 2012 and 2016 from a level 1 trauma center. A total of 105 patients (mean age 43 years, 30 females, 100% White, 100% European) were eligible for follow-up and were contacted 5 years after the initial trauma. Outcomes were assessed using a questionnaire, Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS), American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, functional tests, and posttraumatic osteoarthritis (OA) Kellgren-Lawrence (K-L) grade. For outcome analysis, patients were categorized into the following 3 groups according to AO-OTA fracture classification: type 43B2-B3 (Group 1), type 43C1-C2 (Group 2), and type 43C3 (Group 3) tibial pilon fractures. No statistically significant differences between study groups were observed in FAOS (mean 74, standard deviation [SD] 16.9) and AOFAS (mean 82, SD 12.7) scores. Posttraumatic OA (K-L grade 3-4) was diagnosed in 35% in Group 1, 8% in Group 2, and 48% in Group 3. Ten patients (8%) underwent ankle arthrodesis. The incidence of deep surgical-site infections increased with severity of fracture type (no patients in Group 1, 21% in Group 2, and 23% in Group 3). Two patients (1.6%) required below-the-knee amputation. Approximately 90% of the healthcare resources were needed within the first 2 years after injury; patients in Group 3 required the most surgeries and had the longest hospitalization. Surgically treated pilon fractures seem to result in good mid-term clinical outcomes, even for severe C3 fractures. However, type C3 fractures had more complications and required more surgical interventions, including ankle arthrodeses, longer hospitalization, and additional other healthcare resources than the less severe fractures. Therapeutic Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

cards.title: Depressive symptoms are associated with the incidence of frailty in older adults with cardiometabolic diseases: Interaction between depression and diabetes.
cards.abstract: Older adults with diabetes are prone to frailty and increased mortality. In this longitudinal study, we examined the association between depressive symptoms and the incidence of frailty in older people with cardiometabolic diseases. We also investigated whether comorbidities modified the association between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in this patient population. We analyzed longitudinal data from 431 outpatients aged 65 years or older with cardiometabolic diseases who visited a frailty clinic from 2015 to 2023. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS)-15. The outcome during follow-up (median, 2.9 years) was incident frailty, as defined by the modified Cardiovascular Health Study (mCHS) criteria or the Kihon Checklist (KCL). Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident frailty were estimated using multivariable Cox regression models. Depressive symptoms (GDS-15 ≥ 5) were independently associated with incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty across all models. The fully adjusted HRs for incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty were 1.92 and 2.05, respectively. Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent associations between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in participants with diabetes and hyperglycemia. Significant interactions between depressive symptoms and diabetes were observed for both mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty, whereas no significant interactions were observed for cognitive impairment or physical inactivity. Depressive symptoms were independently associated with incident frailty, as defined by both the mCHS and KCL criteria, in older outpatients attending a frailty clinic for cardiometabolic diseases. A significant interaction between depressive symptoms and diabetes was observed, suggesting that patients with coexisting depressive symptoms and diabetes may represent a high-risk group for incident frailty. Further studies are needed to determine whether interventions targeting depressive symptoms and diabetes management can reduce the risk of incident frailty.

cards.title: OsteoNet-X: A deep residual learning framework for automated osteoporosis detection from knee X-ray images.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mineral density and increased susceptibility to fractures, making early diagnosis essential for effective clinical intervention and long-term patient management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated significant potential for automated bone disease assessment using medical imaging modalities. In this study, a unified deep learning framework, termed OsteoNet-X, is proposed for automated osteoporosis detection and multi-class bone health classification using knee X-ray images. Unlike conventional image classification approaches, OsteoNet-X integrates YOLO-based Region of Interest (ROI) localization, DenseNet-based feature extraction, Feature-Aware Learning (FAL) optimization, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance both classification performance and model interpretability. The ROI extraction stage automatically identifies anatomically relevant knee joint regions, reducing background interference and enabling more discriminative feature learning. Subsequently, DenseNet facilitates efficient feature propagation and hierarchical representation learning for distinguishing normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis conditions. The incorporation of XAI further provides visual explanations of model decisions by highlighting clinically relevant regions within the knee joint. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that OsteoNet-X achieves a classification accuracy of 97.08%, a macro F1-score of 96.61%, and a weighted F1-score of 97.11%.

cards.title: Beyond reproduction: the emerging role of FSH in postmenopausal aging.
cards.abstract: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is traditionally regarded as a biochemical marker of menopause and declining ovarian function. However, emerging evidence suggests that its role may extend beyond reproductive physiology. During the menopause transition, FSH concentrations rise progressively, initially due to declining inhibin B and later to loss of ovarian estradiol and inhibin production. Evidence of FSH effects in bone, adipose tissue, the cardiovascular system and brain has raised the possibility of broader physiological actions. Higher FSH levels have been associated with bone loss and hip fracture risk, adverse cardiometabolic and vascular changes, and cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease. Although these associations do not establish causality, they suggest that FSH may contribute to some consequences of reproductive aging rather than simply reflect ovarian failure. Experimental studies indicate that reducing FSH may benefit bone and adiposity, while preliminary clinical evidence regarding cognition remains inconclusive. Thus, FSH may represent not only a marker of menopause, but also a potential marker of risk and, ultimately, a therapeutic target.

cards.title: Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide attenuates BMSC senescence by inhibiting NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy.
cards.abstract: BMSC senescence is associated with osteoporosis progression. Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) shows potential anti-senescence activity, but its effects on bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) remain unclear. To investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of PSP against tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBH)-induced senescence in BMSCs. Senescence was induced in primary rat BMSCs with TBH, followed by PSP intervention. Viability was assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, while senescence-associated β-galactosidase, alkaline phosphatase, and Oil Red O staining assessed senescence and osteogenic/adipogenic differentiation. Ferritinophagy-associated proteins (NCOA4, FTH1, and LC3) and intracellular Fe2+ were quantified using western blot, immunofluorescence, and FerroOrange staining. Mitochondrial function was evaluated using MitoSOX and JC-1 assays and ATP quantification. Cytosolic mtDNA accumulation and the cGAS-STING pathway were assessed using immunofluorescence colocalization, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting. NCOA4 involvement was examined using an NCOA4-overexpressing lentiviral vector. PSP concentration-dependently attenuated TBH-induced senescence phenotypes in BMSCs, partially restored osteogenic differentiation, and reduced adipogenic differentiation. PSP downregulated NCOA4 expression, attenuating ferritinophagy-associated changes and intracellular Fe2+ accumulation. Reduced Fe2+ accumulation preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation, and reduced cytosolic mtDNA accumulation, alongside attenuated cGAS-STING signaling. Lentiviral overexpression of NCOA4 attenuated the protective effects of PSP on mitochondrial homeostasis and cGAS-STING pathway suppression. PSP may attenuate BMSC senescence by suppressing NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, thereby preserving mitochondrial homeostasis and inhibiting cGAS-STING signaling. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of PSP as a potential therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis-associated BMSC dysfunction.

cards.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
cards.abstract: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength. Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Cross-sectional. Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728). CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3). Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis. Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated. Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women. In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

cards.title: Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula alleviates hepatic fibrosis in acute-on-chronic liver failure by regulating ferritinophagy-mediated hepatic stellate cell senescence.
cards.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) represents a severe clinical syndrome characterized by rapid exacerbation of chronic hepatic disease. Liver fibrosis (LF) significantly contributes to the advancement of ACLF pathology. The traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) preparation Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula (YQJPF) exhibits promising therapeutic effects on ACLF and LF; however, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms and active components remain incompletely understood. This study seeks to elucidate the pharmacodynamic properties, active constituents, and underlying mechanisms of YQJPF in treating liver fibrosis within an ACLF rat model, focusing specifically on ferritinophagy activation and the induction of hepatic stellate cell (HSC) senescence. A rat model of ACLF was induced via combined administration of CCl4 and LPS/D-GalN, and an in vitro model was established using human hepatic stellate cells (LX2). Liver-targeted active components were characterized using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis, with network pharmacology utilized to predict critical molecular targets. NCOA4 siRNA and ferrostatin-1 were used to validate mechanism specificity. The therapeutic effects and associated mechanisms were systematically evaluated through biochemical assays, histopathological examinations, and molecular and cellular analyses. YQJPF improved liver histopathology and attenuated fibrosis and ACLF in rats. It inhibited viability and proliferation of LX2 cells, decreased TGF-β1 secretion, and downregulated α-SMA and Collagen I expression. UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 82 liver-tropic components (including 50 prototypes and 32 metabolites) in rat liver tissues. Network pharmacology revealed 257 potential targets, with 135 overlapping with hepatic fibrosis-related targets (core targets included TP53, NCOA4, and CDKN2A). YQJPF induced HSC senescence (upregulated p16, p21, and HMGA1; downregulated TERT; triggered cell cycle arrest) and activated ferritinophagy (upregulated NCOA4, Beclin1, LC3BII/I; downregulated FTH1 and p62; increased ROS/iron accumulation). NCOA4 knockdown or Fer-1 treatment reduced YQJPF-induced HSC senescence and antifibrotic effects. YQJPF reduces ACLF-related LF by NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, which promotes HSC senescence. The 82 liver-tropic components and 135 overlapping targets highlight its multi-component, multi-target effects, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application.

cards.title: 4'-Hydroxywogonin Attenuates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Suppressing Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT Signaling.
cards.abstract: 4'-Hydroxywogonin, a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanism in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-tumor effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin and its regulatory role in Gas6/Axl-associated signaling. Human HCC cells were used to evaluate proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, senescence, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, molecular docking, and thermal shift analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanism, and antitumor efficacy and safety were further examined in a mouse xenograft model. 4'-Hydroxywogonin significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing G1-phase arrest, apoptosis, and senescence. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses identified Axl as a key affected target. 4'-Hydroxywogonin reduced Gas6 and Axl expression, suppressed PI3K/AKT activation, and downregulated cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between 4'-hydroxywogonin and Axl, which was supported by thermal shift analysis. Axl overexpression partially rescued the inhibitory effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin, suggesting involvement of Axl-dependent and additional pathways. In vivo, 4'-hydroxywogonin markedly reduced tumor growth with efficacy comparable to sorafenib and without evident hepatotoxicity. These findings indicate that 4'-hydroxywogonin suppresses HCC progression, at least in part, through inhibition of the Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, supporting its further development as a natural therapeutic candidate.

cards.title: Editorial Commentary: Arthroscopic Bony Bankart Fixation Stands the Test of Time-Preserve Native Glenoid Anatomy When You Can!
cards.abstract: Bony Bankart lesions provide an opportunity to restore native glenoid anatomy through direct fragment fixation. Arthroscopic bony Bankart repair can provide long-term shoulder stability, high patient satisfaction, and sustained participation in sport. Although we prefer double-row bridge fixation for its broad compression across the fracture bed, rotational control, and biomechanically stronger fixation, a properly indicated and well-executed single-row repair can achieve excellent results. Latarjet and other glenoid bone-augmentation procedures remain important options for patients with attritional or irreparable bone loss and high-risk bipolar lesions. However, increasing enthusiasm for these procedures should not displace anatomic repair when a viable bony Bankart fragment can be mobilized, anatomically reduced, and securely fixed. When native glenoid anatomy can be reliably restored, arthroscopic bony Bankart fixation is an effective and durable treatment.

cards.title: HCT-FS-Defined Frailty Is Associated With Lower Survival Across Diverse Hematologic Diagnoses After Allogeneic Transplantation.
cards.abstract: To evaluate whether Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Frailty Scale (HCT-FS)-defined frailty predicts overall survival (OS), nonrelapse mortality (NRM), and relapse across diverse hematologic diagnoses undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (alloHCT), including nonmalignant disorders. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of 992 adults undergoing alloHCT at 16 centers in Canada and Spain (2018-2023). Frailty was assessed at consultation using the HCT-FS (fit, prefrail, frail). OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier, competing-risks methods by cumulative incidence. Multivariable models assessed associations with OS and NRM. Frailty was assessed across six diagnostic categories, including nonmalignant disorders (4.8%). At consultation, 32.1% were fit, 54.7% prefrail, and 13.2% frail. Increasing frailty was associated with progressively lower 2-year OS (78.9%, 66.0%, 51.7%; p < 0.001) and higher 2-year NRM (10.5%, 18.9%, 33.2%; p < 0.001; HR 1.77 [95% CI 1.21-2.60] prefrail and 3.65 [2.36-5.65] frail vs. fit), while 2-year relapse incidence did not differ (19.0%, 23.5%, 22.3%; p = 0.229). Disease-specific estimates were exploratory and limited by small subgroup sizes. HCT-FS-defined frailty is associated with OS and NRM but not relapse in this multicenter alloHCT cohort. Larger disease-specific studies are needed to establish its prognostic value in less represented indications.

cards.title: [Emphasizing the damage and repair of bone collagen in osteoporosis].
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized not only by reduced bone mass but also by impaired structure and function of the bone matrix and bone collagen. Although conventional bone mineral density assessment can reflect the level of bone mineralization, it cannot fully capture bone quality and the biomechanical performance of bone tissue. Bone collagen plays a critical role in maintaining bone tissue toughness, energy-absorbing capacity and the stability of bone microarchitecture. Its abnormal cross-linking, degradation and defective repair are closely associated with increased bone fragility. This article focuses on the roles and values of bone collagen in osteoporosis, elaborates on bone collagen-related pathological changes, influencing factors, and its mechanisms in osteoporotic fractures, and introduces the latest diagnostic and therapeutic technologies as well as future development directions. It highlights the great value of establishing a "mineralized-collagen two-dimensional" bone-quality evaluation system that takes both bone mineralization and bone collagen status into account, providing new insights for the precise diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fractures.

cards.title: Sonic hedgehog-matrix metalloproteinase crosstalk in neurovascular ageing and stroke: a potential mechanistic link.
cards.abstract: Neurovascular ageing is a major contributor to cerebrovascular vulnerability and poor stroke outcomes in older adults. Progressive deterioration of the neurovascular unit (NVU), driven by oxidative stress, neurovascular coupling dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, inflammageing, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy compromises neurovascular resilience and increases susceptibility to ischemic injury. Among the molecular pathways implicated in these processes, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are important regulators of neurovascular remodeling, BBB integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Although these pathways have largely been investigated independently, emerging evidence suggests potential bidirectional interactions between Shh signaling and MMP activity. In particular, Shh/Gli1 signaling has been associated with regulation of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in experimental models, whereas MMP-2 can disrupt SCUBE2, an extracellular regulator of Shh ligand presentation, providing a potential mechanism for reciprocal pathway modulation. This review examines the Shh-MMP axis as a potential mechanistic link between neurovascular ageing and ischemic vulnerability, integrating current evidence to evaluate how dysregulation of these pathways may contribute to BBB dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, neuroinflammation, and impaired neurovascular repair. We further discuss the potential therapeutic implications of modulating the Shh-MMP axis to preserve neurovascular resilience and improve cerebrovascular outcomes in the ageing brain, while highlighting the importance of temporal and cell-specific targeting.

cards.title: Association between remaining teeth and femoral neck bone mineral density in patients undergoing dialysis.
cards.abstract: Assessing bone mineral density and implementing fracture prevention measures are useful in managing dialysis patients. This study aimed to assess oral health, including the number of remaining teeth, and to investigate factors associated with the young adult mean (%YAM) of the femur and lumbar spine in this population. This cross-sectional study included 110 patients who initiated dialysis treatment at our hospital and underwent panoramic radiography, oral assessments and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans of the femur and lumbar spine within one month. Associations between oral health and YAM were examined using univariate and multivariable analyses, with the latter focusing on femoral YAM because of potential artefacts affecting lumbar measurements. In the univariate analysis, femoral YAM was significantly associated with sex (B = -21.62, p < 0.001), body mass index (BMI; B = 1.926, p < 0.001), and the number of remaining teeth (B = 0.388, p = 0.026). However, in the multivariable analysis, the final model did not include the number of remaining teeth. BMI (B = 1.12, p = 0.005) and sex (B = -18.49, p < 0.001) remained significant factors, with sex showing the strongest association. In incident dialysis patients, fewer remaining teeth were associated with lower femoral YAM in univariate analysis, but this association was not independent of age, sex and BMI in multivariable analysis. Tooth loss may therefore reflect the cumulative effects of these factors rather than representing an independent predictor of bone mineral density.

cards.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Osteoporosis Treatments on Bone Strength and the Impact of Sequential Anabolic Therapy
cards.abstract: Purpose Evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of osteoporosis treatments in improving bone strength in clinical practice remains limited. This real-world study compared the effectiveness of different osteoporosis treatments in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO), including treatment-naive patients initiating Romo, TPTD, or DMAb (Study 1) and patients switching from one anabolic therapy to another (Study 2). Methods Japanese women with PMO aged >55 years were included. In Study 1, 57, 34, and 50 women received Romo, TPTD, or DMAb, respectively, for 12 months. In Study 2, 16 received Romo for 12 months after TPTD (TPTD-Romo) and 29 received twice-weekly TPTD for 12 months after Romo (Romo-TPTD). The primary and secondary endpoints were average percent change from baseline at 12 months in vertebral bone strength and volumetric BMD (vBMD), respectively, assessed using biomechanical CT analysis (BCT). Results At baseline, overall bone strength and vBMD were comparable across groups in both studies. In Study 1, average percent change (95% CI) in vertebral strength was highest with Romo (39.5% [34.2, 44.7]), followed by TPTD (24.4% [18.8, 30.0]), and DMAb (10.9% [7.6, 14.2]). In Study 2, vertebral strength increased by 16.1% (10.6, 21.6) with TPTD-Romo, and decreased by 7.7% (-10.7, -4.6) with Romo-TPTD despite subsequent TPTD treatment. Similar trends were observed for vertebral vBMD. Conclusion In this real-world BCT study, Romo showed greater increases in both vertebral bone strength and density versus TPTD and DMAb in treatment-naive women with PMO. Among prior TPTD, Romo further increased bone strength and density; however, twice-weekly TPTD failed to maintain the gains following prior Romo.
