cards.title: Evaluation of the Functional Outcome of Thoraco-Lumbar Burst Fractures Stabilization By Pedical Screw and Rod.
cards.abstract: Thoraco-lumbar burst fractures are a type of spinal injury that typically result from high-energy trauma. These fractures involve compression of the vertebral body with posterior displacement of bone fragments into the spinal canal. Treatment typically involves surgical stabilization with pedicle screw and rod instrumentation. The aim of the study was to evaluate the results of thoracolumbar burst fractures with incomplete neurological lesion stabilized by pedicle screw and rod. This was a prospective experimental study carried out at Bangladesh Medical University, Dhaka, Bangladesh from January 2019 to December 2019. A total of 15 patients with Thoraco-Lumbar Burst fracture aged over 15 years were included in the study. A detailed history of the selected patient was taken with mode of injury, time of injury, other history, then thorough general, local, neurological examination for proper assessment. Among the 15 cases, 12 cases (80.0%) were male and 3 cases (20.0%) were female. The age range of patient was from 17 55 years. Most commonly affected people were laborers 5(33.33%). Fall from height was the commonest cause of injury 11(73.30%). Most commonly level of injury was L1 07 (46.70%). Pedicle screw and rod used in all cases for long segment reconstruction above and below the involved level. According to Frankel grade preoperatively most common grade was C 10 and next common was B 5. Post operatively most was D 9 and next was E 4 and C-2. According to Denis et al pain scale most commonly 8 (53.34%) cases complain no pain and work scale most commonly 2(13.33%) cases were completely well and can perform normal work up to latest follow-up. Mean hospital stay was (13.27±3.54) days (10 20) days. Satisfactory results (excellent and good) were in 13(86.66%), fair 1(6.67%) and 1(6.67%) unsatisfactory (poor) results. The results of the study demonstrates that functional outcome of Thoraco-Lumbar burst fractures stabilization by pedicle screw and rod is an effective procedure.

cards.title: Mechanobiology of Osteoarthritis: Interactions Between Mechanical Stress, Inflammation, and Joint Remodeling.
cards.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a multifactorial whole joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and progressive functional impairment. Increasing evidence suggests that OA is not simply a wear and tear disorder, but a mechanobiological disease in which abnormal mechanical stress interacts with inflammatory and metabolic pathways to drive joint degeneration. This review summarizes recent advances in the mechanobiology of OA, focusing on the interplay between mechanical stress, inflammation, and joint remodeling. We discuss the major mechanosensing and mechanotransduction mechanisms in chondrocytes, including primary cilia, integrins, the cytoskeleton, the LINC complex, and mechanosensitive ion channels such as TRPV4, TRPM7, and PIEZO channels. We further examine how these pathways regulate extracellular matrix homeostasis, chondrocyte fate, and the transition from anabolic maintenance to catabolic degeneration, as well as how altered joint loading affects subchondral bone remodeling through osteocyte responses, the RANK/RANKL/OPG axis, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Particular attention is given to the crosstalk between mechanotransduction and inflammatory signaling, including NF-κB, MAPK, and macrophage polarization pathways, which together amplify structural damage under pathological loading. Finally, we highlight emerging therapeutic strategies based on biomechanical modulation and mechano-inflammatory targeting. A better understanding of these integrated mechanisms may provide new insight into OA pathogenesis and support the development of disease-modifying therapies.

cards.title: Prodh2‐Mediated Mitochondrial Stress Drives <scp>TNF</scp> ‐α‐Induced Myoblast Dysfunction and Sarcopenia in <scp>COPD</scp>
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Sarcopenia in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is driven by elevated tumor necrosis factor‐alpha (TNF‐α), yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here, we identify the mitochondrial metabolic enzyme Prodh2 as a pivotal mediator. Prodh2 was significantly upregulated in sarcopenic COPD patients and a corresponding mouse model. Mechanistically, TNF‐α induced Prodh2 transcription in myoblasts via a p53‐dependent pathway. This upregulation triggered excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, leading to the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Cytosolic mtDNA subsequently activated the cGAS/STING innate immune pathway, causing myoblast apoptosis, proliferation arrest, and atrophy. While Prodh2 knockdown reversed these effects in vitro, muscle‐specific knockdown of Prodh2 in vivo critically ameliorated muscle atrophy and restored strength. Our study unveils a novel TNF‐α‐p53‐Prodh2‐cGAS/STING axis that links chronic inflammation to sarcopenia through metabolic‐immune crosstalk, validating Prodh2 as a promising therapeutic target.

cards.title: Multi-omics integration of flavor metabolome and lipidome elucidates 1-methylcyclopropene effects on postharvest quality in yellow-fleshed peach at 30 °C.
cards.abstract: 1-Methylcyclopropene (1-MCP) is widely used to extend peach shelf life, yet its efficacy under elevated-temperature (≥30 °C) storage remains unquantified. Flavor metabolism and membrane lipid remodeling share fatty acid precursors, but their quantitative cross-omics coupling during postharvest senescence is poorly understood. This study integrated flavor metabolomics (138 compounds), lipidomics (253 species), physiological indices, and electronic sensory analyses in yellow-fleshed peach 'Jinhua' stored at 30 °C. Despite no between-group difference in ethylene production, softening, DA index decline, and the volatile compositional shift from C6 aldehydes to lactones were all significantly delayed in the 1-MCP group (e.g., γ-decalactone odor activity value at day 8: control 316.5 vs. 1-MCP 44.3). Between-treatment divergence in the lipidome preceded that in the flavor metabolome (day 4 vs. 6), and variance decomposition revealed a larger treatment effect for the lipidome (21.3%) than for the flavor metabolome (16.5%). The 1-MCP group preferentially retained polyunsaturated glycerophospholipids (77% of enriched lipids), whereas the control accumulated more sterol lipids and galactolipids. Only 26 sterol lipid species predicted 91.3% of flavor variation (R2 = 0.913), highlighting a novel predictive association between microdomain components and flavor. Data-driven consensus clustering indicated that 1-MCP extended the acceptable quality window from approximately 5.8 to 8.9 days, although both groups deteriorated by day 10 via distinct metabolic trajectories. Network analysis showed that 1-MCP attenuated global lipid-flavor coupling (Mantel r from 0.765 to 0.609) and shifted network hubs from sterol lipids to glycerophospholipids. These findings provide a quantitative framework associating membrane lipid remodeling with flavor fate under elevated-temperature logistics.

cards.title: Assessing frailty in lung transplantation candidates
cards.abstract: Frailty assessment is important while awaiting lung transplantation (LTx), as frailty is associated with disability and death before and after LTx. We assessed known risk factors and/or frailty indicators in frail, pre-frail, and non-frail patients according to the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) and the Frailty Instrument for primary care of the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE-FI), and evaluated the value of SHARE-FI as a proxy to detect frail patients. Frailty was assessed using SPPB and SHARE-FI in 82 patients on a waiting list for LTx. Demographic, anthropomorphic, and clinical variables were collected, and patients underwent respiratory/cardiorespiratory, biochemical, and quadriceps muscle performance assessments. The mean age was 57.3 {+/-} 9.4 years. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (41.5%) and interstitial lung disease (ILD) (30.6%) were the most common indications for LTx. Four (4.9%), 13 (15.9%), and 65 (79.3%) patients were classified as frail, pre-frail, and non-frail by SPPB, respectively. These figures were 26 (31.7%), 41 (50%), and 15 (18.3%) with SHARE-FI. SPPB found differences between frail/pre-frail and non-frail patients in physical performance (6-minute walking distance) and muscular assessment, while SHARE-FI found differences in age, 6-minute walking distance, and oxygen saturation, and a trend in muscular strength. For COPD and ILD, frailty discrimination was better with SPPB. Concordance between the two measurements was weak, although all SPPB-frail ILD patients were detected by SHARE-FI. In patients awaiting LTx, SPPB showed better discrimination than SHARE-FI for COPD and ILD. SHARE-FI seems appropriate as a preliminary screening instrument for patients with ILD.

cards.title: Fracture propagation and permeability enhancement mechanisms induced by near-roof hydraulic fracturing in soft coal seams.
cards.abstract: Soft and low-permeability coal seams are prone to borehole collapse, unstable gas-extraction pathways, and a restricted stimulation range when conventional in-seam fracturing is applied. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a near-roof hydraulic-fracturing strategy. Coal-immediate-roof assemblages from Heyuan Coal Mine were tested using a large-scale true-triaxial hydraulic-fracturing system under different triaxial in-situ stress states and injection rates. Fracture initiation, propagation, and failure modes were identified by jointly analyzing injection pressure, acoustic-emission (AE) hit counts, cumulative AE energy, and RA-AF parameters. A hydro-mechanically coupled model containing pore-pressure cohesive elements was then established, and the inferred mechanism was evaluated against field observations from the HYL1 surface L-shaped well. Increasing the in-situ stress state from 3/4/6 MPa to 9/12/18 MPa raised the breakdown pressure from 5.15 to 12.23 MPa and increased the contribution of mixed tensile-shear failure. Increasing the laboratory injection rate from 0.1 to 0.4 mL/s raised the breakdown pressure from 4.30 to 6.79 MPa, whereas the stable propagation pressure remained within 3.91-4.94 MPa. The minimum principal stress controlled the dominant fracture plane, whereas the intermediate principal stress and stress difference regulated the width and intensity of the damaged zone. After field fracturing, the mixed-gas drainage rate remained at 630-690 m3/d and the methane concentration exceeded 82%. These drainage responses indicate sustained fracture connectivity and improved gas-migration conditions, although permeability was not measured directly. The results support a coupled mechanism involving pore-pressure accumulation, effective-stress reduction, roof damage and pressure relief, coal-roof fracture connectivity, and improved gas migration.

cards.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation: A cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: To determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and identify clinical and functional factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation. This cross-sectional study enrolled 209 adults with stroke admitted for neurological rehabilitation. Sarcopenia was defined according to the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) algorithm, using SARC-CalF, handgrip strength, five-times sit-to-stand test, physical performance measures and appendicular skeletal muscle mass by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia. Confirmed sarcopenia was identified in 55 of 209 participants (26.3%; 95% CI: 20.6% to 32.8%). Participants with sarcopenia were older and had lower body mass index (BMI), poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment than those without sarcopenia. In the multivariable model, lower BMI (OR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.59 to 0.83), positive SARC-CalF screening (OR = 6.37; 95% CI: 2.03 to 20.05), and lower Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores (OR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.69 to 0.99) remained independently associated with sarcopenia. Motor impairment severity, assessed using Fugl-Meyer motor categories, was also independently associated with sarcopenia. DXA-confirmed post-stroke sarcopenia affected approximately one in four individuals undergoing rehabilitation and was independently associated with lower BMI, poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment. These findings indicate that sarcopenia is closely linked to functional impairment after stroke and reinforce the importance of integrating muscle health and functional assessment during rehabilitation. Early identification of individuals at risk may support more individualized rehabilitation strategies and improve clinical decision-making.

cards.title: Unraveling the shared genetic architecture of metabolic bone diseases via genomic structural equation modeling and multi-omics integration.
cards.abstract: The shared genetic etiology underlying the comorbidity of skeletal degeneration and metabolic dysregulation remains poorly understood. This study aims to decipher the pleiotropic genetic architecture of multivariate metabolic bone diseases (mvMBDs) through an integrative summary-statistics framework. We applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling (Genomic SEM) to integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for six complex traits: osteoporosis (OP), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Subsequent analyses incorporated robust fine-mapping (SuSiE/FINEMAP), transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), and partitioned heritability assessments to identify putative functional loci and regulatory mechanisms. Genomic SEM revealed significant genetic covariance among the six traits, successfully deriving a latent mvMBD construct. We identified 197 genomic risk loci, including 193 lead SNPs that did not achieve genome-wide significance in the six constituent univariate GWAS, predominantly localized in non-coding cis-regulatory elements (e.g., super-enhancers and intronic regions). Fine-mapping and TWAS prioritized critical pleiotropic genes (e.g., MACF1, CETP, SPP1, and HNF1A). Gene-set enrichment analyses identified enrichment for terms related to bone biology, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Our findings robustly demonstrate that mvMBDs are not isolated clinical entities but rather interconnected systemic syndromes underpinned by glycolipid metabolic dysregulation and shared pleiotropic regulatory networks. This study establishes a novel theoretical paradigm for the genetic basis of metabolic bone diseases, offering promising functional targets for future precision medicine interventions.

cards.title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning.
cards.abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a "dirty" mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting "dirty" irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical "gene of scrap compatibility," this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

cards.title: Association between circadian syndrome and frailty progression among middle-aged and older adults in China: A longitudinal study based on CHARLS.
cards.abstract: Frailty is a significant predictor of adverse outcomes. Circadian syndrome (CircS), a cluster of cardiometabolic risk factors linked to circadian disruption, may interact with frailty; however, evidence for this relationship remains limited. A total of 7330 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included. CircS was defined by seven components. Frailty was measured by the frailty index (FI). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) was employed to identify different frailty trajectories. Multinomial logistic regression models were conducted to assess the association between baseline CircS status and frailty trajectories. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the association between the number of baseline CircS components and the subsequent rate of change in FI over time. Three frailty trajectories were identified: low-stable frailty (n = 4670, 63.71%), moderate-rising frailty (n = 2109, 28.77%), and high-stable frailty (n = 551, 7.52%). Compared to participants without CircS, those with CircS at baseline had a significantly higher risk of belonging to the moderate-rising trajectory (RRR = 2.48, 95% CI: 2.17, 2.84, p <0.001) and the high-stable trajectory (RRR = 4.37, 95% CI: 3.51, 5.45, p <0.001). Furthermore, participants with 4, 5, and ≥6 CircS components had greater annual increases in FI, with additional increases of 0.0022 (95% CI: 0.0011, 0.0033, p <0.001), 0.0020 (95% CI: 0.0007, 0.0033, p <0.01), and 0.0033 (95% CI: 0.0016, 0.0049, p <0.001) per year, respectively, compared with those with <4 components. This study showed that baseline CircS status was significantly associated with unfavorable frailty trajectories, while a greater CircS component burden was associated with both higher baseline FI levels and a faster subsequent increase in FI. These findings highlight the potential relevance of CircS for identifying individuals at increased risk of adverse frailty outcomes.

cards.title: When Neutrophils Do Not Die: Senescence as a New Axis of Tumor Immunosuppression.
cards.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Discovery, Chen and colleagues leverage single-cell RNA sequencing of neutrophils in the tumor microenvironment of colorectal cancer liver metastases to characterize neutrophil heterogeneity within the metastatic immune landscape. They show that the glucose-deprived metastatic microenvironment drives BHLHE40 upregulation in neutrophils, inducing a senescent tumor-associated neutrophil (TAN) population, TAN1, that actively promotes angiogenesis and excludes CD8+ T cells from the tumor, thereby supporting tumor growth and survival. See related article by Chen et al., p. 2130.

cards.title: Morphometric Study of the Distal Articular Surface of Fully Ossified Dry Human Humeri in the Bangladeshi Population.
cards.abstract: The distal humerus is a complex anatomical region essential for the stability and range of motion of the elbow joint; therefore, precise morphometric data of the trochlea and capitulum are critical for successful orthopaedic interventions and prosthetic design. This cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted at the Department of Anatomy, Mymensingh Medical College, Bangladesh from July 2021 and June 2022 to establish a standardized anatomical baseline for the distal humeral articular surface in a Bangladeshi adult population. Utilizing a purposive sampling technique, researchers examined 100 specimens (43 right and 57 left humeri), excluding any bones with damage, fractures, or incomplete ossification to ensure data integrity. Morphometric measurements taken with digital caliper revealed that the mean maximum transverse diameter of the distal articular surfaces was 41.095±4.379 mm for the right humeri and 40.998±3.810 mm for the left. Additionally, the maximum transverse diameter of the capitulum measured 17.940±0.569 mm on the right and 17.270±0.630 mm on the left, while the diameter of the trochlea remained nearly identical bilaterally, recording 23.399±2.778 mm on the right and 23.445±2.458 mm on the left. These findings underscore a significant degree of morphological diversity and fill a vital gap in the anatomical record, serving as a key resource for developing population-specific elbow prostheses and refining reconstructive surgical techniques.

cards.title: The Spatiotemporal Coupling Imbalance of Senescent Grey Hair: Remodelling of the HFSC-MeSC-Niche Network and a New Paradigm of Stem Cell Senescence.
cards.abstract: This review examines age-related hair greying as a potential imbalance in the HFSC-MeSC-niche network in terms of time, space and signal quality. We define signal quality as the effective strength, temporal precision and noise-to-threshold relationship of niche-derived cues that regulate MeSC activation. We propose that ageing may progressively weaken the temporal coordination between HFSC activation and MeSC responsiveness. ECM remodelling and altered guidance-related cues may further impair MeSC niche engagement. Meanwhile, chronic oxidative stress, low-grade inflammation and stress-related sympathetic norepinephrine signalling may increase background noise, distort signal timing and push the MeSC activation threshold upward, so residual MeSC-lineage cells may fail to engage effectively with the niche. Such functional uncoupling may represent an early or intermediate stage, whereas sustained genotoxic stress or niche failure can eventually drive irreversible MeSC depletion. Based on this, the article constructs an integrative model, emphasizing that future intervention strategies may need to shift from simply protecting MeSCs to preserving the temporal and spatial coupling of the HFSC-MeSC-niche network. Potential approaches may include reducing chronic niche stress, maintaining HFSC-MeSC communication, preserving ECM organization and improving the timing and strength of pro-pigmentation cues. We further propose that hair greying may provide an accessible visual readout of stem-cell niche ageing.

cards.title: Gamified spatial‑participatory model for urban social cohesion in a post‑conflict city: Bridging accessibility, inclusion, and intergroup trust through co‑design in Kabul.
cards.abstract: Post‑conflict cities exhibit profound socio‑spatial fractures, institutional weakness, and eroded public trust. Conventional planning repeatedly fails to address ethnic segregation, accessibility disparities, and social fragmentation. The aim of this study is to propose and empirically validate an integrated model, the Gamified Spatial-Participatory Model (GSPM), that combines spatial justice theory, participatory co-design, and conflict-sensitive gamification to foster social cohesion. Using Kabul, Afghanistan, as a paradigmatic case, a sequential mixed‑methods design was employed. Quantitative spatial diagnostics mapped severe accessibility deficits, while qualitative inquiry identified deep trust deficits and cultural barriers; these jointly informed gamified co‑design workshops as the intervention. Pilot results provide strong preliminary evidence of GSPM efficacy: 90% of participants reported substantially increased engagement; gamification correlated strongly with intergroup trust (r = 0.76, p < 0.01); perceived accessibility improved by 38% in intervention areas. Critically, 70% of women and 55% of ethnic minorities reported meaningfully stronger belonging. The study demonstrates that this approach shifts planning epistemology from technocratic to deeply human, operationalising spatial justice in fragile settings, and offers transferable principles for fostering inclusion in divided urban contexts.

cards.title: Vitamin D deficiency is associated with higher frailty risk among middle-aged and older adults: a national population-based analysis of NHANES 2007-2018.
cards.abstract: Although frailty is common in older adults, the relationship between vitamin D and frailty remains unclear. Using NHANES data, this study examined the association between frailty and serum vitamin D in middle-aged and older adults. Eight thousand and sixty-four participants aged 40 and older from NHANES (2007-2018) underwent cross-sectional analysis. Serum vitamin D was categorized as deficiency (<25 nmol/L), insufficiency (25-50 nmol/L), or adequate (≥50 nmol/L). Frailty was quantified using a 49-item Frailty Index (FI) based on the cumulative deficit model; frailty was defined as FI ≥ 0.21. Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were used. The deficiency group had the highest frailty prevalence (55.9%), followed by insufficiency (42.9%) and adequate (37.2%). Frailty was significantly associated with deficiency (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.42-3.25) after full adjustment, whereas insufficiency was not significantly associated with frailty (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.95-1.38). Serum vitamin D and FI showed a U-shaped dose-response relationship, robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In middle-aged and older adults, vitamin D deficiency, but not insufficiency, is associated with higher frailty risk. Serum vitamin D may have a U-shaped association with FI. Monitoring vitamin D levels may help inform frailty management in aging populations.

cards.title: Biomechanical, Structural, and Composition Characterization of the Vertebra-Disc Interface.
cards.abstract: The spinal endplate region consists of the cartilage endplate (CEP), bony endplate (BEP), and subchondral trabecular bone (STB). Although this region is often involved in vertebral fractures and disrupted with disc degeneration, the biomechanics of these tissues are incompletely understood. The goal of this study was to characterize the mechanical, structural, and compositional properties of the spinal endplate region across aging and disc degeneration. Cadaveric human lumbar spine segments (n = 45) were imaged with magnetic resonance imaging to assess disc degeneration. BEP and STB microstructure were analyzed with micro-computed tomography. BEP specimens were subjected to four-point-bend testing, and CEP specimens to confined compression testing. BEP and STB composition was measured with ash analysis. Several BEP mechanical properties, including flexural modulus, were associated with structural measures such as bone volume fraction, but showed few correlations to composition. Measures of structure and composition were generally different but correlated between the BEP and STB. Superior and inferior endplates differed from each other in structure but not composition. Apart from the STB microstructure, which became sparser with age in superior endplates, none of the endplate region properties correlated with age or disc degeneration, despite large ranges in values observed for many of these properties, particularly, BEP fracture strain (1%-52% strain). Structural measures are more reliable indicators of endplate region properties than are compositional measures, age, or disc degeneration. The BEP may play an important, independent role in spine function, due to its range in ductility and limited correspondence in properties to those of neighboring tissues.

cards.title: Construction and validation of an identification model for frailty in maintenance hemodialysis patients using multiple machine learning algorithms: a cross-sectional study of retrospectively collected data.
cards.abstract: Frailty adversely affects survival and quality of life in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). This study aimed to develop a clinical multimodal model to identify prevalent frailty in MHD patients. Clinical data from 626 MHD patients across four tertiary hospitals were retrospectively collected, including demographics, clinical characteristics, laboratory indicators, and physical function assessments. Frailty was assessed using the FRAIL scale. Patients from Wuxi (n = 502) were divided into training (n = 352) and internal validation (n = 150) sets, while patients from Yancheng (n = 124) formed the external validation set. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Boruta were used for feature selection. Ten machine learning models were developed and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. SHAP was applied for model interpretation. Frailty prevalence was 48.6%. Six predictors were identified: age, grip strength, comorbidities, Charlson comorbidity index (CCI), albumin, and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (pro-BNP). The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best external validation performance (AUC=0.917, 95% CI: 0.867-0.967; accuracy=0.847; sensitivity=0.850; specificity=0.844), with good calibration and clinical net benefit. The shapley additive explanations (SHAP) identified pro-BNP as the most influential predictor and revealed nonlinear associations and clinically relevant thresholds. The interpretable XGBoost model effectively identified prevalent frailty in MHD patients, demonstrating strong discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability, and may support systematic frailty screening and individualized assessment.

cards.title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring.
cards.abstract: Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm2. By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

cards.title: Bone Organoids Across the Development-to-Remodeling Continuum: From Tissue Formation to Functional Competence and Translation.
cards.abstract: Bone organoids are emerging as three-dimensional skeletal models that reproduce selected aspects of bone development, organization, and function under controlled conditions. Physiologically relevant models require more than cellular aggregation and mineral deposition; they must progressively acquire organized matrices, multicellular interactions, vascular and metabolic support, and mechanical responsiveness. In this review, we examine developmental principles guiding bone-organoid construction, including skeletal hierarchy, cellular niches, ossification pathways, and spatiotemporal signaling. We then discuss current strategies based on skeletal, mesenchymal stromal, and pluripotent stem cells, together with advances in biomaterials, three-dimensional bioprinting, perfusion, and microfluidic culture. To organize these developments, we introduce the development-to-remodeling continuum (DRC), which distinguishes tissue formation from multicellular integration, adaptive responsiveness, and remodeling competence. We assess collagen-mineral organization, osteocyte-network formation, vascular and metabolic maturation, osteoblast-osteoclast coupling, marrow and immune integration, and mechanical adaptation. We further evaluate applications in developmental and disease modeling, drug assessment, personalized modeling, and bone regeneration. Current limitations include variability, incomplete maturation, transport constraints, and insufficient functional benchmarking. By linking construction strategies to specific bone-related functions and the evidence supporting them, the DRC provides a framework for evaluating functional claims in relation to intended application and translational readiness.

cards.title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs.
cards.abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro-angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual-specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain- and loss-of-function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300-regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)-mediated PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1-dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro-angiogenic activity of BMSC-conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying a runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter-driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic-lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation-associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26-directed approaches for osteoporosis.

cards.title: PHGDH-Mediated Serine Metabolism in Nucleus Pulposus Cells Is a Potential Therapeutic Target for Intervertebral Disc Degeneration.
cards.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine-serine-threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. In vivo, AAV mediated PHGDH overexpression alleviates puncture induced IVDD, while a serine deficient diet exacerbates degeneration. Collectively, we uncover a PHGDH/Rap1b/mTORC1/autophagy cascade linking serine deprivation to NPC senescence, and propose that restoring PHGDH or serine availability may be a viable strategy to combat age related disc degeneration.

cards.title: The impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty in old age: A systematic literature review and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM).
cards.abstract: BackgroundFrailty is common in older adults and associated with inadequate nutrition, reduced physical function, and increased vulnerability. While physical exercise benefits frailty outcomes, evidence on combined nutrition and exercise interventions remains unclear.AimTo systematically review evidence on the impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty status among community-dwelling frail older adults (≥65 years).MethodsThe review followed the Cochrane Handbook, Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidelines. Searches were conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus. Randomised controlled trials explicitly defining frailty were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and assessed methodology using RoB 2.0. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis without meta-analysis was performed.SummaryOf 2447 records identified, 10 publications met the inclusion criteria. Two trials directly assessed frailty reversal and reported improvements favouring structured exercise, with one showing additional benefit when combined with a nutritional supplement. Odds of frailty reversal ranged from two- to fivefold. Additional studies reported modest improvements in mobility disability risk, lean body mass, and functional performance. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high, limited by small samples and heterogeneity.Although some studies reported favourable effects of combined nutrition and exercise interventions, the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether nutrition adds benefits beyond exercise alone. Structured exercise consistently benefited frailty-related outcomes. However, due to few studies and substantial heterogeneity, firm conclusions cannot be drawn. Further standardised trials are needed to clarify the role of nutritional components within combined nutrition-exercise interventions in frailty management.

cards.title: PPARγ/P21 Signaling Mediates Butyrate-Driven Protection against Aging-Related Endothelial Dysfunction: A Novel Effect of Soybean Polysaccharide via the Gut-Vascular Axis.
cards.abstract: Aging-induced endothelial dysfunction is a core driver of age-related cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In 20-month-old naturally aged mice, 12-week soybean polysaccharide (SP) supplementation restored endothelium-dependent relaxation, reduced aortic reactive oxygen species and VCAM-1 in the aortic endothelium, and attenuated colon senescence, improved gut barrier integrity, and reduced systemic inflammation, as shown by decreased serum LPS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and fecal and serum TMA/TMAO levels. SP enriched butyrate-producing gut bacteria, including Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group, and increased gut and serum butyrate, consistent with enhanced microbial short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis capacity predicted by PICRUSt2. Direct butyrate supplementation reproduced these vascular and colonic benefits. It activated PPARγ signaling and downregulated p21, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, and p16, whereas PPARα and PPARδ remained unchanged. These findings support a gut microbiota-butyrate-PPARγ/p21 axis through which SP protects against aging-related endothelial dysfunction, providing a nutritional basis for targeting the gut-vascular axis in cardiovascular aging.

cards.title: Rethinking the functional relevance of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures in anterior cruciate ligament injury.
cards.abstract: Posterolateral tibial plateau fractures (PLTFs) are increasingly recognised in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-injured knees, yet their functional relevance remains unsettled. In our view, the recent study by Willinger et al. adds valuable prospective data on the association between PLTFs and lateral-sided soft-tissue pathology, but its findings should be interpreted with caution. The main concern is that PLTFs were analysed as a relatively uniform lesion despite substantial morphologic heterogeneity. Small cortical impressions are unlikely to have the same biomechanical significance as deeper depression defects associated with loss of submeniscal bony support or altered local slope geometry. In addition, preoperative pivot shift is an incomplete surrogate for the functional effect of PLTFs within a multifactorial instability pattern influenced by meniscal, anterolateral, and osseous restraints. The imaging framework also does not quantify structural variables likely to determine mechanical relevance. We therefore believe the study supports only a narrow conclusion: PLTF presence alone is not a reliable surrogate for greater preoperative pivot-shift laxity, whereas the significance of high-grade PLTF phenotypes remains unresolved.

cards.title: Performance of ChatGPT-5 under a minimal binary prompt for detection of distal radius fractures on plain radiographs.
cards.abstract: General-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) are being applied to radiology, but their performance under the simplest realistic clinical query (a single binary fracture-or-not prompt) has not been rigorously quantified. We evaluated ChatGPT-5 on this task using a public distal radius dataset. In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 396 anteroposterior distal radius radiographs from the Stanford MURA dataset were submitted to ChatGPT-5, each in a fresh temporary chat session. The prompt was: "Is there a fracture in this X-ray? Answer with yes or no." The reference standard was an image-level label assigned by consensus between a senior orthopedic resident and a board-certified orthopedic surgeon; MURA study-level labels were used only to select candidate images. Twenty-six radiographs (6.6%) returned a hedged response and were excluded from the primary analysis, leaving 370; all 26 were added back in three sensitivity analyses. Outcomes were sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, F1, balanced accuracy, and Cohen's kappa, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals and McNemar's test for error asymmetry. Fracture prevalence in the analyzed sample was 45.9% (170/370). Sensitivity was 51.2% (95% CI 43.7-58.6), specificity 70.5% (63.8-76.4), accuracy 61.6% (56.6-66.4), PPV 59.6% (51.5-67.2), NPV 62.9% (56.5-69.0), F1 0.551, Cohen's kappa 0.219 (0.112-0.318). False negatives exceeded false positives (McNemar χ2 = 4.06, p = 0.044). Non-binary responses occurred in 7.6% of fracture-positive and 5.7% of fracture-negative radiographs (p = 0.54); counting all as errors lowered sensitivity to 47.3% (40.2-54.5), and no assumption raised it above 54.9%. Projected to 20% prevalence, PPV was 30.3% and NPV 85.2%. Under a minimal binary prompt and without task-specific fine-tuning, ChatGPT-5 missed approximately half of distal radius fractures and fell well below published performance for dedicated CNN-based fracture detectors. Results are specific to this model version, this prompt, this anatomical region, and this dataset; they constrain claims about autonomous, minimal-prompt use rather than the broader potential of engineered LLM-based radiological workflows.

cards.title: Sensitivity of stochastic growth rate and lifetime reproductive output to kin effects: A nonlinear feedback model
cards.abstract: Humans exhibit a coevolutionary relationship between the trajectory of social evolution and senescence. A focal individual's kinship network is a function of his/her life history, while that network in turn shapes the focal individual's life history through kin effects on reproduction, generating a dynamic, nonlinear feedback loop across the population. Assessing directional selection on kin effects, therefore, requires explicitly modelling the feedback between the kinship network and life history. Here, we develop such a framework and apply it to examine selection pressures on the cooperative behaviour of closely related kin, including mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters. We hypothesise that the negative association of grandmothers, mothers, and older sisters (>10 years) with child mortality are under positive selection because increasing the absolute values of these kin effects would increase the stochastic growth rate. Furthermore, we hypothesise that the positive association of older sisters with child mortality is subject to negative selection, as increasing this effect would reduce the stochastic growth rate. We estimate kin-specific slope coefficients for child mortality using a Bayesian hierarchical model and solve a system of nonlinear equations linking kinship structure and survival to account for the nonlinear feedback between kinship and child survival. Thereafter, we compute stochastic sensitivities of both the stochastic growth rate and the mean lifetime reproductive output to these slope coefficients. Consistent with our hypotheses, all slope coefficients for kin presence on child mortality are negatively sensitive to both fitness metrics. We discuss the applications of our framework to examine the coevolution of social behaviours and senescence in age-structured populations.

cards.title: Intestinal Phosphate Absorption and Phosphate Metabolism in Chronic Kidney Disease: Direct and Indirect Toxicity of Phosphate Additives in Ultra-processed Diets.
cards.abstract: In chronic kidney disease (CKD), intestinal phosphate absorption stays largely constant even as the kidneys lose the ability to excrete phosphate, creating a tendency toward positive phosphate balance. Rising fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) and parathyroid hormone (PTH) keep serum phosphate near normal until advanced CKD, but these same adaptations can cause systemic harm long before overt hyperphosphatemia develops. Ultra-processed foods worsen this burden through phosphate additives (Pi-additives) used as preservatives, emulsifiers, stabilizers, leavening agents, and moisture retainers. These additives are absorbed more readily than natural food phosphate and are poorly captured by nutrient databases. Therefore, true phosphorus exposure is easily underestimated. This perspective outlines 2 pathways of harm. The direct pathway involves PTH and FGF23 activation, vascular and soft-tissue calcification, endothelial dysfunction, disordered bone remodeling, faster CKD progression, and cellular senescence-effects documented in CKD and possibly relevant even with preserved kidney function. The indirect pathway reflects that Pi-additives rarely occur alone: they accompany added sugars, non-nutritive sweeteners, nitrites, emulsifiers, and preservatives in ultra-processed foods, combinations that may drive gut dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammation, and the formation of advanced glycation endproducts and other gut-derived toxins. We synthesize current understanding of phosphate homeostasis with mechanistic and epidemiologic evidence linking Pi-additives-alone and combined with other additives-to cardiovascular, skeletal, renal, and metabolic disease. Future research should move beyond single-additive safety testing toward evaluating additive mixtures, cumulative exposure, and food-matrix interactions. Better exposure assessment and transparent phosphorus labeling are essential to clarify the long-term health effects of these ubiquitous additives.

cards.title: Acute sucrose availability before and during high-intensity interval exercise modifies recovery-phase myonectin responses in postmenopausal women with obesity: A randomized crossover trial.
cards.abstract: Myonectin is a nutrient-responsive myokine implicated in systemic lipid handling, yet whether acute carbohydrate availability modifies exercise-induced myonectin responses in postmenopausal obesity remains unclear. This randomized crossover study examined the effects of sucrose ingestion before and during high-intensity interval exercise (HIIT) on circulating myonectin and related metabolic-myokine responses in postmenopausal women with obesity. Fifteen postmenopausal women with obesity completed two experimental trials in randomized order: sucrose ingestion before and during HIIT and a non-caloric control trial. Trials were separated by a 7-day washout period. Venous blood samples were obtained before exercise, immediately after exercise, and 2 h after exercise. Circulating myonectin was the primary outcome; glucose, insulin, free fatty acids, glycerol, lactate, and interleukin-6 were secondary outcomes used to characterize the accompanying metabolic and myokine environment. Linear mixed-effects models included condition, time, condition × time, period, and treatment sequence. Significant condition × time interactions were observed for myonectin, glucose, insulin, free fatty acids, glycerol, lactate, and interleukin-6. Myonectin increased in both conditions, but the 2 h increase was greater following sucrose ingestion than control (between-condition difference: 0.543 ng/mL, 95% CI 0.346-0.741, p < 0.001). Sucrose produced higher glucose, insulin, and lactate responses, while attenuating free fatty acid and glycerol responses during early recovery. Although interleukin-6 increased in both trials, the 2 h interleukin-6 response was lower in the sucrose condition. No period or sequence effect was observed for myonectin. Under a common HIIT stimulus, the sucrose condition was associated with a greater recovery-phase increase in circulating myonectin and distinct metabolic responses compared with the non-caloric control condition. Without non-exercise conditions or another carbohydrate comparator, these findings cannot establish an effect independent of exercise, an exercise × sucrose interaction, or specificity to sucrose. Circulating measurements also do not establish altered myonectin production or secretion.

cards.title: A putative iron-related evolving framework in Alzheimer's disease: From iron dyshomeostasis and ferro-aging to ferroptosis.
cards.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) ranks as a prototypical age-related neurodegenerative disorder. Emerging evidence indicates that disrupted brain iron metabolism and ferroptosis act as critical upstream drivers of AD pathological progression. AD exhibits core hallmarks of ferroptosis, including iron overload, lipid peroxidation, elevated reactive oxygen species, and impaired antioxidant enzyme activity. These abnormalities interact synergistically with amyloid-β plaques and tau pathology. Iron accumulation during aging and damage-associated molecular patterns released concomitantly with ferroptosis drive susceptible microglia toward M1-like polarization, propagate chronic neuroinflammation, and fuel the vicious cycle of AD pathology. Targeting ferroptotic pathways represents a promising strategy to alleviate cognitive impairment in AD. Ferro-aging ranks as a recently identified form of programmed cellular senescence marked by iron dependency, ACSL4 regulation, and lipid peroxidation-driven damage. Although ferro-aging has only been preliminarily validated in aging models, its molecular signatures, regulatory axes, and phenotypic outcomes align remarkably well with the progression of brain aging and AD. It thus emerges as a potentially pivotal hub linking physiological aging to iron-associated pathology in AD. We systematically summarize the physiological regulation of brain iron homeostasis and core ferroptotic pathways disrupted in AD. We further integrate current evidence to explore how ferro-aging may contribute to AD pathogenesis, proposing a mechanistic framework in which: iron dyshomeostasis initiates damage, ferro-aging drives chronic progression, and ferroptosis mediates acute injury. Finally, we review intervention strategies targeting iron-related pathology, providing theoretical insights for understanding the aging-dependent nature of AD and developing novel therapeutic approaches.

cards.title: FibriLysins disrupt Staphylococcus aureus biofilms and abscess communities.
cards.abstract: The rise of antibiotic resistance, particularly among pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, necessitates innovative antibacterial strategies. Here we introduce FibriLysins, a class of engineered enzymes combining staphylokinase and endolysin, which dismantle fibrin-encapsulated multicellular staphylococcal communities, including biofilms and staphylococcal abscess communities (SACs). We characterized diverse staphylokinases, developing a library of 27 FibriLysins, with a 78% positive hit rate. The lead variant, FL-028, has significant antibacterial activity against prevalent clinical S. aureus isolates. In vitro, FL-028 reduced bacterial counts in SACs by 3.4 log and in biofilms by 2.3 log. In vivo, FL-028 exhibits superior efficacy in a mouse model of bone fracture-related infection, outperforming vancomycin by 1 log and eliminating SAC presence in tissues. FL-028 shows no adverse effects on bone healing, as confirmed by histological examination, mechanical testing and micro-computed tomography analyses. These preclinical findings highlight the potential of FibriLysins as a robust and safe therapeutic approach against difficult-to-treat staphylococcal infections.

cards.title: Exercise for Older People with Heart Failure and Frailty: Should We Even Try?
cards.abstract: The benefits of exercise in older patients with heart failure (HF) and frailty are twofold: (i) improvement in cardiopulmonary capacity, thus reducing HF-related sequelae; (ii) attenuation of decline in physical function, thus improving frailty status. Despite the clear benefits, exercise training (ET) remains underutilised as a treatment modality in this patient population. Guidelines on the specific type of exercise intervention best suited for this population are still lacking. In this review, we discuss (i) pathophysiology underlying exercise intolerance in patients with HF; (ii) impact of frailty on HF and exercise capacity; (iii) benefits and safety of ET; (iv) recommended ET programme for this population; (v) mode of delivery and (vi) potential barriers in the uptake of ET and strategies to overcome them. An effective ET intervention in this population warrants individualisation to patient's physical capacity, while addressing possible barriers to uptake so as to ensure sustained participation in the programme.

cards.title: Live and Heat-Killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 Attenuate D-Galactose-Induced Aging-Related Brain Changes and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption with Gut Microbiota Modulation in Mice.
cards.abstract: Aging is associated with changes in systemic homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and brain function. This study investigated the effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 on aging-related alterations in a D-galactose-induced accelerated aging mouse model. Male C57BL/6J mice were administered D-galactose for 8 weeks and orally treated with live or heat-killed HY7715. D-galactose increased circulating advanced glycation end products (AGEs), blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, hippocampal inflammation, and aging-related molecular changes, while impairing cortical and colonic tight junction-associated markers. Both live and heat-killed HY7715 reduced serum AGE levels, Evans blue leakage, and hippocampal inflammatory responses, while restoring CLDN5 immunoreactivity, tight junction-associated gene expression, and antioxidant-related gene expression. HY7715 also attenuated senescence- and apoptosis-related changes in the hippocampus and colonic tight junction- and inflammation-related gene expression changes. Gut microbiota analysis showed taxon-specific changes following HY7715 treatment, including significant increases in Bifidobacterium in both HY7715-treated groups, whereas live HY7715 was associated with significant changes in microbial community structure. Several microbial taxa were correlated with serum AGEs, BBB permeability, and neuroinflammation-related parameters. Together, these results show that both live and heat-killed HY7715 attenuated multiple aging-related changes in the D-galactose-induced accelerated aging model, accompanied by changes in gut microbiota composition.

cards.title: Osteocyte-Derived Extracellular Vesicles: Bridging the Gap in Skeletal Physiology and Pathophysiology.
cards.abstract: Osteocytes are the most abundant cells in bone and serve as central skeletal regulators. Recent findings from our and other groups demonstrate that beyond soluble mediators, osteocytes communicate by releasing extracellular vesicles (EVs). This review provides a systematic overview of osteocyte-derived EVs and highlights their importance in diagnostic and therapeutic innovation. Accumulating evidence has linked osteocyte mechanotransduction to EV biogenesis and secretion. Mechanically induced calcium oscillations and signaling pathways impact load-induced EV release. Under normal conditions, osteocyte-derived EVs contribute to local and systemic intercellular communication within experimental models, whereas their direct role in immune-microenvironment remodeling remains insufficiently defined. In pathological states, alterations in osteocyte EV release and cargo composition are associated with both benign diseases and malignancies. Engineered osteocyte-derived EVs and EV-inspired delivery systems are being investigated as cell-free therapeutic platforms for skeletal regeneration. Continued research in osteocyte-derived EVs will deepen understanding of bone communication networks and resolve the principal conceptual and technical challenges.

cards.title: Association between functional tooth units and frailty in older adults: a cross-sectional study using NHANES 2005-2018.
cards.abstract: Dental status, dietary intake, and frailty are closely interrelated among older adults. Nevertheless, the association between posterior occlusal support and frailty, and whether diet-related indicators can statistically account for part of this association, remain insufficiently elucidated. To primarily investigate the association between functional tooth units (FTUs) and frailty. This study used data from the NHANES 2005-2018. Weighted multivariate logistic regression models were applied to examine the associations of FTUs, overall dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM), and its specific components with frailty. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to test the nonlinear relationship between FTUs and frailty, and further subgroup analyses were conducted. Exploratory mediation analyses were used to assess whether DI-GM and its components statistically partially explained the association between FTUs and frailty. 6,758 individuals were included, with a frailty prevalence of 18.34%. Following comprehensive covariate adjustment, higher FTUs were associated with lower odds of frailty (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91-0.96, P < 0.001). RCS analysis revealed no significant nonlinear association between FTUs and frailty (P-for-non-linearity > 0.05). Subgroup analyses showed no significant interactions between FTUs and frailty (P-interaction > 0.05). Among older adults in the United States, higher FTUs are associated with lower odds of frailty. Nevertheless, these findings only suggest interrelationships among oral status and frailty in older adults and cannot establish causal relationships.

cards.title: Advanced Deformable Ceramics: The Origin, Evolution, and Prospectives of Electrospun Ceramic Nanofiber Materials.
cards.abstract: Ceramics are renowned for their exceptional high-temperature stability and resistance to corrosion and oxidation. However, their inherent brittleness and susceptibility to fracture significantly limit their practical use in harsh and mechanically demanding environments. Ceramic nanofibers (ceramic NFs) combine the intrinsic thermal and chemical robustness of ceramics with the structural advantages afforded by fibrous architectures. This combination unlocks substantial potential for a wide range of advanced applications. This review critically examines the origin and evolution of electrospun ceramic NF materials. Key aspects include the underlying principles and preparation methodologies, structural diversity and classification of ceramic NFs, mechanical characterization techniques, and the mechanisms governing strength enhancement at both individual fiber and network levels. Recent advances in leveraging these materials for energy regulation, material separation and conversion, and biomedical functions are critically analyzed. Furthermore, the challenges impeding the scalable manufacturing of electrospun ceramic NFs are discussed, along with proposed strategies to address these limitations. Finally, the review outlines future perspectives for enhancing performance and broadening the application scope of electrospun ceramic NFs.

cards.title: Skeletal Muscle Aging Is a Significant Contributor to Systemic Aging
cards.abstract: Skeletal muscle aging is a conserved biological process characterized by progressive declines in muscle mass, strength, regenerative capacity, and metabolic adaptability, contributing to impaired mobility, frailty and age-related diseases. Beyond its canonical role in locomotion, skeletal muscle functions as an endocrine and metabolic organ that actively regulates organismal aging through myokines, metabolites, extracellular vesicles, thermogenic activity, and dynamic communication with distant organs. In this review, we summarize the intrinsic mechanisms driving skeletal muscle aging, including protein turnover imbalance and anabolic resistance, myosteatosis, denervation and motor unit loss, and cellular composition remodeling. We also discuss how aging skeletal muscle influences systemic aging through bidirectional interactions with metabolic organs, brain, cardiovascular system, and bone via endocrine signaling and interorgan communication. Finally, we highlight emerging interventions targeting skeletal muscle aging, including exercise, nutritional strategies, pharmacological approaches, and other novel therapies. Understanding skeletal muscle as both a target and regulator of systemic aging provides a framework for developing strategies to promote healthy aging and reduce the burden of age-associated diseases.

cards.title: A One-Stone-Two-Birds Strategy to Develop P-Por COF/PDES Composite Gels for Photothermal/Photodynamic Antibacterial Activity and Wearable Strain Sensing.
cards.abstract: Flexible wearable electronics face growing bacterial infection risks from prolonged skin contact, creating an urgent demand for flexible materials integrating efficient sensing and antibacterial functions. Herein, a novel phosphorus-containing porphyrin covalent organic framework (P-Por COF) was synthesized via a solvothermal Schiff-base reaction, and incorporated into a polymerizable deep eutectic solvent to fabricate P-Por COF/PDES composite gels through in-situ UV polymerization. The resulting gel exhibited enhanced photothermal performance, improved mechanical properties, and excellent near-infrared (NIR) triggered antibacterial activity. Under 730 nm NIR light irradiation, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel could reach 76 °C with 4 min, while showing excellent stability of photothermal cycle. Based on the synergistic effect of photodynamic production of singlet oxygen and photothermal effect, the P-Por COF/PDES composite gel resulted in a high bactericidal rate of nearly 100% against both Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Escherichia coli (E. coli). The P-Por COF/PDES composite gel delivered a fracture strain up to 2435.82% and 2.6-fold higher toughness than pure PDES, along with stable, sensitive and self-healable strain sensing for human motion monitoring. Overall, this work provides a simple and effective strategy for developing antibacterial materials and multifunctional gels with integrated therapeutic and sensing capabilities.

cards.title: [Translated article] Versatile Extended Anterolateral (EAL) Approach with a progressive four-window strategy for posterolateral column management in tibial plateau fractures: A detailed cadaveric study.
cards.abstract: Background The posterolateral (PL) column is often the most difficult one to access and manage in tibial plateau fractures. Although multiple approaches have been described, many provide limited flexibility to address diverse fracture patterns. The Versatile Extended Anterolateral (EAL) Approach with four progressive windows has been previously introduced within the Main Deformity Direction (MDD) framework. In this cadaveric study, we provide a detailed anatomical and technical description of this modified approach, characterized by an optimized skin incision and four stepwise deep windows for PL column management. The primary aim was to assess the technical feasibility of this approach. Potential reduction and fixation options associated with each window were also explored descriptively. Materials and methods Four fresh-frozen cadaveric specimens were used to evaluate surgical exposure and relationships with relevant anatomical structures. Based on the anatomical exposure achieved with each window, potential reduction and fixation strategies were explored descriptively. Representative clinical cases were included to illustrate fixation techniques. Results The skin incision allowed access to all windows, achieving safe progressive PL column exposure. The four windows (pre-fibular, supra-fibular, retro-fibular, trans-fibular) expanded reduction and fixation possibilities stepwise. The trans-fibular window enabled complete articular and metaphyseal exposure. The anterior tibial artery crossing, located at a mean of 3.5 cm from the tip of the fibular head, represented the distal anatomical limit of posterior exposure. Conclusion The versatile EAL Approach is a feasible option for managing lateral and PL columns in tibial plateau fractures. Its progressive four-window strategy may allow tailored exposure and fixation according to fracture-specific requirements.

cards.title: Identification of Senescence-Associated β-Galactosidase With Single-Molecule Resolution.
cards.abstract: The majority of human senescent cells exhibit overexpression of senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal), rendering this enzyme the most extensively utilized biomarker of senescence and a key prodrug target for intervening in aging. However, strategies for the authentic in situ identification of SA-β-gal with single-molecule resolution have not been established, limiting the accuracy of senescence targeting. Here we present an unprecedented molecular approach to identify SA-β-gal in a manner that avoids dissociation from the target enzyme, which integrates the atomic hybridization of SA-β-gal substrates with protein-environment-sensitive fluorescence technology. Using this design principle, we created nine fluorescent probes with distinct working modes for the single-molecule (target enzyme)-resolved identification of SA-β-gal. Five of them formed crystal complexes with the wild-type β-galactosidase by binding at the active site, clearly evidencing their single-molecule resolution capability. Our strategy, capable of both identifying and locating SA-β-gal, facilitated its application in dynamic single-molecule localization microscopic imaging, achieving the in situ tracking of SA-β-gal in living cells at the nanoscale. Significantly, the probing of SA-β-gal with high fidelity enabled the precise evaluation of the aging degree in mice. As such, our research provides a promising method for the authentic in situ identification of this senescence-associated protein with single-molecule resolution.

cards.title: Histological evaluation of three-dimensional rectangular grid plates in treatment of mandibular fractures: an experimental study.
cards.abstract: Evaluate the efficacy of 3D rectangular grid plates in treatment of mandibular fractures in comparison to the more commonly used locking plates. This experimental study was conducted on sixteen mature male Mongrel dogs (ranged from 1-2 years old), weighting about 15-20 kg each. A linear fracture was done using surgical sagittal saw with aid of mallet and chisel in the right side of the mandible in the premolar molar area for each animal of the study under general anesthesia. The animals were divided into two groups: Group A was fixated with 3D rectangular grid plate and six 7 mm monocortical screws and Group B was fixated with two locking plates; the inferior plates fixated with 11 mm bicortical screws and the superior one fixated with 7 mm monocortical screws. The bone formation and remodeling is assessed using histomorphometric analysis of bone biopsy. Group A subjects showed significantly less bone formation than group B (26.78±4.3 vs 48.4±10.3 respectively in postoperative week 4 P<0.005 and 28.119±10.507 vs 51.109±11.348 respectively in postoperative week 12 P<0.005). The surface area of the fracture was also significantly lower in group A than in group B (0.317 ± 0.065 vs 0.485 ± 0.105 respectively in postoperative week 4 P<0.005 and 0.287 ± 0.105 vs 0.511 ± 0.115 respectively in postoperative week 12 P<0.005). Fixation with 3D rectangular grid plates demonstrated a bone healing pattern characterized by closer fracture segment approximation and reduced callus formation, consistent with primary bone healing, as evidenced by histological and histomorphometric analysis, compared with locking plates.

cards.title: The prevalence of nutritional disorders in inflammatory bowel disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: The epidemiology of nutritional disorders in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains poorly characterized. Existing evidence is fragmented across specific conditions or confined to single regions, and no study has simultaneously assessed the principal nutritional disorders-malnutrition, overweight or obesity, and sarcopenia-in a unified framework. To address this gap, we systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and China Biology Medicine from inception to July 31, 2024 and updated on July 30, 2026. Observational studies reporting prevalence based on standard diagnostic criteria were included. Pooled estimates with 95% confidence interval (CI) and prediction interval (PI) were derived using a random-effects model. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, disease subtype and activity, diagnostic criteria, study setting and gepgraphic variation. Study quality and publication bias were also assessed. After literature screening, 201 studies across 32 countries were included. Underweight affected 11.5% (95% CI: 9.0-14.6%, 95% PI : 1.0-61.7), whereas consensus-based malnutrition [GLIM (Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition), ESPEN (European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism), MNA (Mini Nutritional Assessment), SGA/PG-SGA (Subjective Global Assessment or its variant Patient-Generated SGA) affected 27.6% (95% CI: 20.5-36.1%, 95% PI : 3.6-79.7). Notably, this malnutrition estimate was derived almost exclusively from hospital-based settings (over 80%) and predominantly from a single region. Overweight and obesity affected 23.1% (95% CI : 20.6-25.9, 95%PI : 8.1-50.8) and 13.5% (95%CI : 11.7-15.6, 95%PI : 2.9-44.6), respectively. For muscle depletion, low muscle mass defined by skeletal muscle index was identified in 48.3% (95% CI: 41.8-55.0%, 95% PI : 19.7-78.1), whereas consensus-based sarcopenia [EWGSOP (European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People) or AWGS (Asian Working Group on Sarcopenia)] affected 12.6% (95% CI: 6.1-24.2%, 95% PI : 0.9-70.6). Of note, the majority of included studies for malnutrition and sarcopenia were hospital-based. Active disease was associated with significantly higher prevalence of malnutrition. No significant differences were observed between disease subtypes. In conclusion, our findings provide a broad overview of the prevalence of major nutritional disorders in patients with IBD, highlighting that nutritional care in IBD should extend beyond simple weight monitoring. However, given the wide prediction intervals, these pooled estimates should be viewed as averages across highly heterogeneous settings rather than a precise global figure. Future research, particularly population-based studies with standardized diagnostic criteria across diverse regions, is needed to validate our observation.

cards.title: Fatigue reliability and failure modes of metal-ceramic, monolithic zirconia, and lithium disilicate implant-supported crowns cemented to titanium bases: A step-stress accelerated life testing study.
cards.abstract: The fatigue behavior under clinically relevant loading conditions of implant-supported screw-retained crowns cemented to titanium bases fabricated from different restorative materials remains insufficiently understood. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the failure modes, fatigue reliability, and survival probabilities of metal-ceramic (MC), monolithic zirconia (3Y-TZP), and lithium disilicate (LD) single premolar implant-supported screw-retained crowns cemented to titanium bases using step-stress accelerated life testing (SSALT). Sixty crowns were bonded to titanium bases (UNP RH 4 mm, GH 2 mm; Adin Dental Implant Systems Ltd), connected to internal hexagon implants (4.2-mm platform diameter, 10-mm length; Touareg S, Adin Dental Implant Systems Ltd), embedded in acrylic resin blocks, and subjected to single-load-to-failure testing (n=6) to determine stress profiles for SSALT (n=54). Use-level probability Weibull curves were calculated to estimate reliability for a mission of 100 000 cycles at 200 and 300 N. Failed specimens underwent polarized light stereomicroscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) for fractographic analysis. All specimens failed during SSALT loading profiles. Beta (β) values derived from use-level probability Weibull curves were greater than 1 for all groups, indicating fatigue-driven failure behavior. 3Y-TZP crowns demonstrated the highest fatigue reliability, with survival probabilities up to 98% at tested load levels (200 and 300 N). LD showed intermediate performance (93% at 200 N and 88% at 300 N), whereas MC crowns showed the lowest survival probabilities (86% at 200 N and 82% at 300 N). At 200 N, no statistically significant differences were observed among groups. At 300 N, 3Y-TZP crowns showed significantly higher survival probability than MC crowns (P=.038), while LD showed intermediate values and was not significantly different from either group. Fractographic analysis revealed material-specific fracture origins and crack propagation patterns. All crown types demonstrated high survival probabilities. 3Y-TZP crowns showed higher fatigue reliability than MC crowns, while LD crowns demonstrated intermediate performance.

cards.title: Integrative network toxicology, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments identify SLC6A2 as a novel candidate target in nicotine-induced osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: In recent years, the health problems attributable to cigarette smoke (CS) have attracted widespread attention. However, the pathogenic mechanisms underlying osteoporosis development induced by nicotine, a neuroactive component of CS, remain unclear. In this study, we examined a potential molecular mechanism underlying nicotine-induced osteoporosis by network toxicology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and in vitro experiments. On screening multiple databases, we identified 47 overlapping targets for nicotine- and osteoporosis-related genes, and subsequently performed protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis on the identified targets. KEGG analysis suggested that the potential targets were mainly involved in the calcium, PI3K-Akt, and MAPK pathways. We identified seven core targets using five algorithms, among which SLC6A2 exhibited the strongest predicted binding affinity. Molecular docking confirmed good binding affinities between nicotine and these core targets, and molecular dynamics simulation verified the stability of the nicotine-SLC6A2 complex. Moreover, in vitro experiments further confirmed that nicotine significantly inhibits osteogenic differentiation of MC3T3-E1 cells, and differentially regulates the transcriptional expression of all seven core targets, with SLC6A2 being one of the downregulated ones. This identifies a previously unrecognized neural-related target (SLC6A2) in nicotine-induced bone toxicity. Our study provides a theoretical basis for developing multi-target regulation strategy that could contribute to mitigating the bone toxicity of complex environmental toxins.

cards.title: Design and adhesion mechanism of multi-component natural polysaccharide-based adhesives for paper fracture repair.
cards.abstract: Cracks and losses in paper-based cultural relics critically threaten structural integrity and aesthetic coherence. Repairing paper fractures under stringent conservation criteria remains challenging, particularly when avoiding synthetic materials. Here, we designed film-forming adhesives composed of four polysaccharides, with curdlan as the primary component and chitosan, xanthan, and locust bean gum as synergistic texturizers that suppressed nanocrystal formation. The optimized formulation C9C1XL1 (1.215 wt% curdlan, 0.135% chitosan, 0.05% xanthan, 0.05% locust bean gum) achieved a tensile strength of 0.74 ± 0.05 kN/m in torn-edge raw Xuan paper fractures after accelerated aging, exceeding the cross-direction strength of intact paper with minimal chromatic shift. It also proved effective on bamboo paper and naturally aged wood pulp paper. SEM and confocal microscopy revealed a dual-role adhesion mechanism: curdlan formed a transparent film matrix filling interfiber voids for bulk mechanical support, while water-soluble polymers coated fiber surfaces, anchoring the fiber network through mechanical interlocking. Additionally, protruding cellulose fibers at repair sites functioned as load-bearing elements, substantially reinforcing tensile strength. The adhesive exhibited antifungal activity against the paper-degrading fungus Aspergillus niger, and showed promising reversibility (>90%) as evaluated by morphological analysis and fluorescence reduction. This study provides new insights into polysaccharide-based adhesives for paper conservation.
