cards.title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles Enable Oral Alendronate Therapy for Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

cards.title: Convergent Early Dysregulation of Sarcopenia-Associated Genes in Skeletal Muscle During Aging and SOD1G93A ALS Models
cards.abstract: Skeletal muscle undergoes structural and functional decline due to aging and neuromuscular disorders such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), both of which impact protein expression and contribute to muscle atrophy. This study investigates how aging and the SOD1G93A ALS-related mutation affect the expression of eight genes previously linked to sarcopenia (PF4, OIT3, MMRN1, MASP1, C1R, SVEP1, VCAN and SPTB) but not yet characterized in muscle tissue. To this end, we analyzed their expression (1) during muscle aging in WT mice (5 and 24 months), (2) in SOD1G93A-transfected myotube cells in vitro, (3) in a muscle-specific SOD1G93A mouse model (5 and 24 months), and (4) in a systemic SOD1G93A transgenic mouse at different disease stages (60 and 120 days) by quantitative PCR. All eight target genes were expressed in skeletal muscle and most of them showed increased transcription with aging. In ALS models, gene expression was significantly overexpressed at early stages, particularly in muscle-specific (MLC/SOD1G93A) and systemic (SOD1G93A) models, mimicking aging-related profiles. These alterations attenuated with disease progression, suggesting an early transient muscle response to ALS-linked SOD1 mutations. Hence, this study demonstrates that sarcopenia-associated proteins are actively expressed and modulated in skeletal muscle during aging and ALS and suggests convergent response mechanisms.

cards.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta bone matrix alterations affect the resorptive function of human osteoclasts in-vitro.
cards.abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) results most commonly from altered collagen type I that impairs both bone formation and resorption, producing a fragile bone matrix prone to fracture. While most studies emphasize deficient osteoblast function, there is a paucity of data related to the contribution of osteoclast-mediated resorption. We investigated whether intrinsic alterations in OI bone matrix directly modulate human osteoclast activity. Identical human osteoclast populations were seeded onto bone samples from donors with OI types 1, 3, and 4 and compared with non-OI controls. In addition, cleaned calvarial bones from the Col1a1Aga2/+ and Col1a1Jrt/+ mouse OI models served as substrates for human osteoclasts. On OI type 1 bone, osteoclasts generated a greater eroded surface covered by pits, whereas trench formation remained unchanged. OI type 4 bone yielded significantly reduced eroded surface but produced deeper pits and trenches. Osteoclast behaviour on OI type 3 bone did not differ from that of healthy bone. Using Col1a1Jrt/+ substrates, human osteoclasts displayed a general increase in resorptive activity, particularly in pit formation. Col1a1Aga2/+ substrates similarly enhanced pit formation but reduced trench formation. Multiple linear regression confirmed that OI bone matrix preferentially stimulates pit-making osteoclasts while leaving trench-making osteoclasts largely unaffected. Independent of OI status, increasing donor age promoted trench formation. These findings demonstrate that OI-specific matrix characteristics directly influence osteoclast resorption patterns. More broadly, they highlight the importance of extracellular matrix properties in shaping osteoclast behaviour and underscore the need to consider matrix-driven effects when interpreting bone pathologies.

cards.title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions.
cards.abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system's multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

cards.title: Changes in gray matter volume associated with gait speed and muscle mass in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
cards.abstract: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early stage of cognitive decline between normal aging and dementia. Gait speed, a key marker of physical function, has been associated with both cognitive decline and brain atrophy. Sarcopenia, characterized by age-related loss of muscle mass and function, has also been linked to structural brain changes.ObjectiveTo investigate the associations between sarcopenia, its individual components and regional gray matter volume (GMV) in older adults with MCI.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 234 older adults with MCI. Sarcopenia, gait speed, handgrip strength, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) were assessed according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Brain T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging was analyzed using voxel-based morphometry. Voxel-wise group comparisons were performed to identify GMV differences after adjustment age, sex, comorbidity, depressive symptoms, nutritional status, and total intracranial volume.ResultsSlower gait speed was significantly associated with lower GMV in the bilateral putamen and left superior frontal cortex. Lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV in the left inferior temporal cortex. No significant GMV differences were found by sarcopenia status or handgrip strength.ConclusionsSlower gait speed is associated with reduced GMV in motor-related brain regions, indicating early brain structural changes in older adults with MCI. Although lower ASMI was associated with higher GMV, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. These findings highlight the complex interactions between physical function and brain structure, emphasizing gait speed as a potential indicator of brain health in older adults with MCI.

cards.title: Practical consideration for the application of continuous glucose monitoring in older adults with insulin treated diabetes.
cards.abstract: The increased prevalence of diabetes among older individuals presents challenges for delivery of effective care for each older person with diabetes, for their families, and for healthcare providers. Along with established risks for microvascular and macrovascular disease, diabetes in older adults is also associated with risk factors for cognitive impairment and dementia, depression and physical frailty. Many of these risk factors are linked to hypoglycaemia, which in turn can be related to polypharmacy and overprescribing in older individuals. Use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) technology is proven to prevent hypoglycaemia and can mitigate many averse outcomes of frailty, both in type 1 diabetes (T1D and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Similarly, use of CGM improves glucose stability, reducing risks for vascular complications of diabetes. Intrinsic capacity (IC) is a concept used in geriatric medicine to provide an objective composite of physical and mental capacities that an older individual can draw on. Reduced IC is associated with a number of CGM metrics, including time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), rather than hypoglycaemia. Use of CGM can also facilitate telemedicine for adults with diabetes and frailty, reducing the burden of clinic attendance and increasing the frequency of healthcare contacts, further increasing the quality of care and quality of life for older individuals with diabetes. Given the significant benefits, the application of CGM alongside geriatric principles can be proposed to improve overall care and outcomes for people with diabetes.

cards.title: Live Fast, Die Old: Lowering Insulin Signalling During Development Can Speed Growth, Increase Reproduction and Lifespan, but Impair Environmental Sensing and Harm Offspring in Caenorhabditis elegans
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Genetic trade‐offs can constrain life‐history evolution resulting in the evolution of ageing. Reduced insulin/insulin‐like signalling (rIIS) improves somatic maintenance and dramatically increases lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans , but the effects on fitness are unclear. Here we used a novel experimental approach to show that, contrary to the prevailing paradigm, rIIS via daf‐2 RNAi during development can improve development, reproduction, survival, individual fitness, and population growth rate in the laboratory and semi‐natural conditions. However, developmental rIIS extends lifespan and improves fitness only in some temperatures, which explains why our results differ from previous findings. Furthermore, while developmental rIIS can improve a suite of life‐history traits in parents, it slows down offspring development. Finally, because rIIS interferes with environmental sensing and compromises adaptive developmental plasticity in response to stress, a central part of C. elegans life history in nature, the ability to sense the environment correctly during development comes at the cost of accelerated senescence. These results suggest the complexity of gene‐by‐environment interactions during development imposes constraints on molecular signalling networks leading to genetic trade‐offs across the life course that natural selection in late‐life is unable to resolve. However, these constraints can be resolved by artificially fine‐tuning gene expression at different ages.

cards.title: Cracking and Self-Healing in a Molecular Crystal Driven by Topochemical Polymerization.
cards.abstract: Topochemical reactions in molecular crystals are often accompanied by severe lattice strain, frequently leading to crystal fracture and loss of crystallinity. Here we report an unusual case in which heat-driven topochemical azide-alkyne cycloaddition (TAAC) polymerization in a non-centrosymmetric molecular crystal induces macroscopic cracking that is followed by autonomous self-healing. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals a regiospecific single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation to a helical polymer, despite large-amplitude molecular motion and anisotropic lattice deformation (a +19.9%, b -2.9%, c -13.3%). Face-indexing and morphology analysis correlate the crystallographic axes with macroscopic crystal dimensions, rationalizing the observed breadth expansion, length contraction, and cleavage along a weakly bound crystallographic plane. Mechanistically, crack formation originates from reaction-induced bimorphic lattice strain, while self-healing is driven by electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged fracture surfaces in the polar crystal, followed by continued intradomain polymerization that eliminates the bimorphic interface. Autonomous healing occurs upon completion of the topochemical polymerization in the crystalline material.

cards.title: Influence of Screw Access Hole Diameter and Preparation Method on the Fit and Fracture Resistance of Implant-Supported Monolithic Zirconia Crowns.
cards.abstract: To evaluate how screw access hole (SAH) presence, diameter, and preparation method affect marginal and internal fit and fracture resistance of implant-supported monolithic zirconia crowns. Seventy-two crowns were assigned to six groups (n=12): no SAH; 1-, 2-, or 3-mm presintered SAHs; a 1-mm SAH enlarged to 3 mm after cementation; or a 3-mm SAH prepared after cementation in crowns without an initial SAH. Marginal and internal fit was assessed in the first four groups by the silicone replica technique. After thermocycling and cyclic loading, fracture load, Weibull parameters, fracture patterns, and scanning electron microscopy findings were evaluated. Overall discrepancy and internal gap were greater without an SAH (184.7 and 182.1 μm) than with an SAH (54.7-65.9 and 60.1-71.1 μm) (P<.05), with no differences among SAH diameters (P>.05). Fracture loads were higher for no SAH and a 1-mm SAH than for all groups with 2- or 3-mm openings (P<.001). Among final 3-mm openings, preparation method did not affect mean fracture load (P>.05), although handpiece-prepared groups had lower Weibull moduli. The 1-mm SAH improved crown fit without reducing fracture resistance, whereas openings of 2 mm or larger reduced fracture resistance. For 3-mm SAHs, preparation method did not affect mean fracture load.

cards.title: Jellyfish-inspired multilayered responsive hydrogels via micelle-confined photopolymerization for underwater communication and emergency rescue.
cards.abstract: Hydrogels offer considerable promise as flexible sensors. However, maintaining their stable performance in complex underwater environments characterized by high pressure, high salinity, and temperature fluctuations remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the dynamic adaptive capabilities of jellyfish, this study reports a biomimetic composite conductive hydrogel with multi-level environmental responsiveness, synthesized via the copolymerization of N-isopropylacrylamide, 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid, and octadecyl methacrylate (OMA), incorporating color-changing microcapsules through a cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) micelle-confined polymerization strategy. The long alkyl chains of OMA promote hydrophobic association networks inside CTAB micelles, endowing the hydrogel with both high strength and exceptional stretchability (fracture strength of 690 kPa; elongation at break 1370%). This hydrogel achieves multi-parameter, synchronized responses to complex marine conditions: strong temperature sensitivity (-15.344%/°C), an electrical response to water-depth pressure (7.13 kPa-1, corresponding to 0-500 m water depth), stable tensile responsiveness, and reversible color changes visible to the naked eye. Building on these capabilities, the hydrogel can monitor human motion in conventional settings and also enable underwater sensing and Morse-code-based information transmission, demonstrating substantial potential for applications for underwater communication and emergency rescue applications.

cards.title: Stretching Training of Microgel-Reinforced Composite Hydrogel for Tunable Strain-Stiffening Property.
cards.abstract: Achieving tunable strain-stiffening in tough hydrogels via muscle-mimicking training remains a key challenge for nonlinear biomimetic mechanics. Microgel-reinforced composite hydrogels (MR-gels), combine rigid polyelectrolyte microspheres with a soft polyacrylamide matrix, offering an ideal platform for programming strain-stiffening behavior via hierarchical microsphere fracture. Here, we report that physical training controlling stretching amplitude and number of repetitions enables stable and tunable strain-stiffening in MR-gels. Unlike conventional expectations, a single stretch is insufficient, training equilibrium requires approximately 300 cycles. The resulting MR-gel exhibit stable and broadly tunable soft-to-stiff transition (0.4-3.1), strain-stiffening capacity (3.1-17.8), and modulus of the soft (240 to 40 kPa) and stiff (814 to 713 kPa) regimes, matching the nonlinear mechanics of diverse biological mechanicals. Mechanistically, the training mode achieves tunable strain-stiffening by controlling the degree of microgel fracture and entangled polymer chain sliding. At equilibrium, fragmented microgels form an interconnected string-like network via topological entanglements and covalent crosslinks, raising the fatigue threshold from 689.6 to 1269.8 J/m2. Furthermore, the trained MR-gel enables full envelopment of a high-speed falling iron ball for effective deceleration and superior impact cushioning. This work establishes a versatile strategy for programming mechanical behavior in soft materials, with broad implications for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and biomedicine.

cards.title: Oral Astilbin Nanogels Modulate Senescence-Associated CD4+ T Cells and Promote Treg Induction in Aged Mice with Colitis.
cards.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in older individuals is characterized by immune senescence and deteriorating intestinal homeostasis, both of which limit the efficacy of current therapies. Here, we develop fluorinated β-glucan/pectin nanogels (F2-Ast@NGs) for oral delivery of astilbin, a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. This multifunctional platform integrates gastrointestinal protection, colon-targeted release, and local immune modulation. The β-glucan shell preserves nanogel stability during upper gastrointestinal transit while enabling β-glucanase-responsive disassembly in the colon. Fluorocarbon segments enhance mucus penetration, and the pectin matrix prolongs colonic retention, promoting drug accumulation at inflamed sites. In aged mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, F2-Ast@NGs alleviate disease severity, attenuate senescence-associated features of colonic CD4+ T cells, and enhance Foxp3+ regulatory T cell (Treg) responses. Concurrently, the β-glucan/pectin nanogel matrix contributes to increased short-chain fatty acid production and favorable alterations in gut microbial composition. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of F2-Ast@NGs is markedly attenuated in Foxp3+ Treg-depleted mice, supporting an important role for Treg-mediated immunoregulation. Collectively, F2-Ast@NGs enable precise colonic delivery while coordinately remodeling the intestinal immune and microbial microenvironment, providing a promising oral nanotherapeutic strategy for colitis in aged hosts.

cards.title: Robust polyvinyl alcohol based multifunctional films with pH-responsive via electrostatic self-assembly of TOCNF and quaternary ammonium chitosan by loading apple polyphenol.
cards.abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based materials with pH-responsive colorimetric properties have attracted increasing attention for sustainable and intelligent packaging applications. Although numerous studies have reported PVA-based pH-responsive packaging films with antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, further optimization is still required in achieving a balanced integration of multiple functionalities, including antioxidant performance, antimicrobial efficiency, and long-term structural stability. Thus, a new kind of multifunctional PVA based composite film was fabricated via direct solvent casting combined with ultrasonication by mixing PVA with TEMPO-oxidized nanocellulose (TOCNF), quaternary ammonium chitosan (QCS), and apple polyphenol (APP). The effects of APP and QCS incorporation on the structural, mechanical, barrier, biological, and intelligent-responsive properties of the films were systematically investigated. The optimized PT-1.5(QA) film exhibited a balanced mechanical performance, with a tensile strength of approximately 8.1 MPa and an elongation at break of approximately 243%, attributed to the formation of intermolecularly associated polymer networks. Meanwhile, APP incorporation significantly enhanced the antioxidant and UV-shielding properties, achieving approximately 92.8% DPPH and 96.5% ABTS radical scavenging activities. Furthermore, the composite film exhibited enhanced barrier properties, strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, and distinct pH-responsive color changes over a broad pH range (1-12). Cytotoxicity evaluation confirmed good in vitro biocompatibility. Importantly, the composite film effectively delayed postharvest senescence and quality deterioration of litchi fruit, while maintaining favorable biodegradability. These findings highlight the potential of TOCNF/QCS/APP/PVA films as sustainable active and intelligent packaging materials for food preservation.

cards.title: Association of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and physical frailty with cardiovascular health in US adults: A cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Evidence on the association between cardiovascular health (CVH) and frailty remains limited, and the role of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) in this relationship is not fully understood. This study aimed to examine the association between frailty and CVH and to investigate the independent association of serum 25(OH)D and its potential interaction with frailty. This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2007 to 2018, including 8015 adults aged ≥20 years. Frailty was assessed using a frailty index, and CVH was evaluated based on the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 metrics. Multinomial logistic regression models accounting for the complex survey design were applied to assess associations. Frailty was highly prevalent in the study population. After multivariable adjustment, higher frailty levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of poor CVH in a graded manner. Serum 25(OH)D levels were independently and inversely associated with poor CVH. Stratified analyses showed that the association between frailty and CVH varied by sex and 25(OH)D status. However, no statistically significant multiplicative interaction between frailty and serum 25(OH)D levels was observed. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer CVH in US adults, demonstrating a clear dose-response relationship. Serum 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with CVH, whereas no statistically significant multiplicative interaction between frailty and serum 25(OH)D was observed. These findings highlight the importance of addressing multiple modifiable risk factors to improve CVH.

cards.title: Sarcopenia in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: A cross-sectional radiological and functional assessment.
cards.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is a significant complication that impairs lung function and increases morbidity. Sarcopenia, characterized by the loss of muscle mass and function, is commonly found in chronic diseases such as systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with SSc-ILD and investigate its cross-sectional associations with pulmonary function test parameters, estimated pulmonary artery pressure and quantitative radiological lung involvement. In this cross-sectional study conducted between 2024 and 2025, 40 patients with systemic sclerosis (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) and high-resolution computed tomography-confirmed interstitial lung disease were evaluated. Patients with overlap myositis, acute infections, severe orthopedic/neurological limitations, and end-stage organ failure were excluded. Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 criteria using muscle mass (bioelectrical impedance analysis) and handgrip strength measurements. Pulmonary function tests (FVC, single-breath transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide), echocardiographic sPAP estimations, and quantitative high-resolution computed tomography lung density analysis were performed. These findings highlight the potential impact of sarcopenia on lung function and the association of sarcopenia with radiological findings in SSc-ILD SSc-ILD. Among the 40 analyzed patients (mean age: 55.8 ± 10.8 years, 85.0% female, mean BMI: 28.7 ± 5.0 kg/m2), sarcopenia was identified in 10 patients (25.0%). Patients with and without sarcopenia were compared to analyze its effects on pulmonary function and radiological findings. Patients with sarcopenia had significantly lower lung diffusion capacity (transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide) and forced vital capacity % values and significantly higher radiological lung involvement compared to those without sarcopenia (P = .004, P = .023, and P = .035, respectively). Systolic pulmonary artery pressure was also significantly higher in sarcopenic patients (P = .031). Additionally, fat-free mass index, fat-free mass, muscle mass, and handgrip strength were significantly lower in sarcopenic patients (P < .001).

cards.title: Socioeconomic position and preoperative characteristics in Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants: a UK national observational study.
cards.abstract: Patients from more deprived backgrounds experience poorer postoperative outcomes. We analysed preoperative characteristics in UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants according to socioeconomic position to explore opportunities for targeted interventions. Participants were adults aged ≥18 yr undergoing major elective surgery at UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme sites. Socioeconomic position was determined using postcode data and the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) standardised aggregate scale of area-level deprivation. Associations between IMD position and patient characteristics, health behaviours, and comorbidities were analysed using descriptive statistics with appropriate parametric and nonparametric testing. Of 55 938 participants included, quintile 1 (most deprived) represented the smallest subgroup (14.2%), with recruitment varying by region and site. Median age was 66 yr with IMD 1 participants 5 yr younger (62 yr) than IMD 5 (67 yr). Deprivation gradients (IMD 5 to 1) were seen for home ownership, occupation, and educational attainment. Prevalences of smoking, inactivity, and obesity increased from IMD 5 to 1. Higher prevalences of major long-term conditions including diabetes mellitus, heart failure, stroke, and ASA physical status 3-4 were observed in more deprived quintiles. Prevalence rates of dementia and renal impairment were similar across quintiles despite the age gradient. Notably, the proportions of patients living with frailty and disability increased with deprivation. Patients presenting for major surgery from more deprived backgrounds do so in poorer overall health. They can encounter barriers to both research participation and available preoperative support. Addressing this unmet need to prevent widening perioperative health inequalities requires interventions tailored to the patient's socioeconomic context.

cards.title: Exact solutions produce a full picture of crack behavior in dynamic fracture.
cards.abstract: The theory of fracture normally describes cracks as propagating discontinuities in a continuous medium where stresses vanish on free crack faces. We describe cracks instead at the particle level and obtain more general analytical results than were available previously. Using dynamical crack solutions for widely varying dissipation and general isotropic elastic moduli, we construct a catalog of 100,000 crack solutions and from it a general picture of when cracks are stable. For our exactly solvable model of dynamic fracture, the surface wave speed sometimes sets an upper limit on crack velocity, as expected. However tensile cracks traveling faster than the shear wave speed are possible and their stability is enhanced when they travel along weak interfaces, when dissipation increases, and when system sizes are small. Our results reinforce a standard view that supersonic cracks require supersonic energy transport near the tip, but we show it can come from dissipation as well as hyperelasticity.

cards.title: "It's quite a dark, long journey to the light at the end of the tunnel": a qualitative study of children's experiences of living with Long COVID.
cards.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic had a significant impact on global health, with some individuals experiencing long-term health effects known as Long COVID. This study explored the lived experiences of children with Long COVID, providing further insight into the impacts and needs within this group. Semi-structured interviews, facilitated by children's drawings, were conducted with 15 children. Thematic analysis was used to analyse the data. Four themes were identified: (1) 'I feel completely different': the physical and emotional burden of Long COVID (2) 'Like the buzz of people speaking and I can't concentrate': education challenges created by Long COVID, (3) 'I'm on my third friend group since I've had COVID': disrupted relationships and fractured connections and (4) 'What can I do now to get myself better?': managing life with Long COVID. These findings reveal a narrative of loss and change during key developmental periods. This research illustrates the life-altering impact of Long COVID on children across many domains. Despite these challenges children were hopeful for the future. A multi-faceted approach to management is needed, including utilising technology to aid self-management strategies such as pacing and to support social connection, as well as psychological support and school adjustments.

cards.title: Nanoscale Analysis of Large Deformation of Tough Microparticle-Based Polymer Films Revealed by Atomic Force Microscopy and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering.
cards.abstract: For understanding the mechanical properties of polymer materials and establishing design guidelines, elucidation of nanoscale structural changes under deformation is crucial. This study focused on microparticle-based polymer films exhibiting high fracture energies of several tens of MJ/m3 without additives, and the influence of intraparticle crosslinking on nanoscale deformation was investigated using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The improvement of an AFM equipped with a stretching device enabled nanoscale observation of films under strain conditions of up to 700%. As intraparticle crosslinking increased, a trade-off was observed in which the Young's modulus increased while the fracture strain decreased. AFM observations showed that, although the increase in intraparticle crosslinking density did not significantly affect the deformation of each microparticle or particle clusters constituting the assembly, their surface roughness increased with increasing crosslinking density. SAXS measurements under tensile deformation revealed that the strain-induced structural anisotropy decreased with increasing intraparticle crosslinking density, suggesting suppressed nanoscale deformation within highly crosslinked microparticles. These results suggest that the trade-off in macroscopic mechanical properties is associated with a change in nanoscale deformation, from smooth elongation to surface roughening, highlighting that particle design is an important factor contributing to tough microparticle-based film properties.

cards.title: Rhenium-Based β-Galactosidase Probe Allows Senescence Profiling by Mass Cytometry.
cards.abstract: Mass cytometry is an attractive analytical technique for the study of cellular senescence due to its ability to simultaneously interrogate the multiple biomarkers necessary to define senescent phenotypes. However, measuring senescence-associated β-Galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) activity, the gold standard biomarker for detection of senescent cells, requires a functional mass cytometry detectable probe compatible with an antibody-based panel. Herein, we report a small-molecule mass cytometry probe for SA-β-Gal, ReGal, that uses a piano-stool rhenium complex as a mass tag. We demonstrate that the probe measures β-Gal activity in vitro and in cellulo with minimal background signal. We further show that the probe improves the discrimination of senescence-induced mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) against untreated cells compared to using only antibody-based mass cytometry reagents. Finally, we demonstrate that the probe reveals a putatively senescent sub-population of mouse peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), which is enriched in old vs. young mice, that could not be segmented by antibody-based reagents alone.

cards.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is associated with higher bone mineral density: results from NHANES.
cards.abstract: We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to investigate the association between metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and bone mineral density (BMD) among U.S. adults. Our findings indicated that participants with MASLD had higher BMD than those without MASLD. Given the stigma associated with the term "NAFLD," experts participating in a Delphi consensus proposed renaming the condition "MASLD". Nevertheless, the association between MASLD and BMD remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between MASLD and BMD. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6470 participants aged 18 years or older using data from the 2005 to 2010, 2013 to 2014, and 2017 to 2018 cycles of the NHANES. MASLD was defined according to diagnostic criteria established through a Delphi consensus. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of MASLD with femoral neck and total femur BMD, while logistic regression analysis was used to investigate the association between MASLD and osteoporosis. Among the 6470 participants, the mean age was 53.16 ± 17.27 years, 49.54% were male, and 23.52% met the criteria for MASLD. After multivariable adjustment, participants with MASLD had higher femoral neck BMD (β = 0.0238; 95% CI, 0.0154-0.0321) and total femur BMD (β = 0.0332; 95% CI, 0.0244-0.0419) than those without MASLD. In subgroup analyses, participants with individual cardiometabolic components of MASLD, including BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, also exhibited higher femoral BMD after multivariable adjustment. Moreover, multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that MASLD was significantly associated with lower odds of osteoporosis. Our findings suggest that participants with MASLD have higher BMD compared to those without MASLD.

cards.title: Endogenous retrovirus control of calbindin is essential for human early embryogenesis.
cards.abstract: The cis-regulatory potential of human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) that have accumulated in our genome affects diverse host processes, including embryonic development and malignancy, where HERV epigenetic control is reduced. Non-small cell lung cancer optimal growth requires cancer cell-intrinsic expression of the calcium-binding protein calbindin under the control of a HERVH integrant on chromosome 8q21.3. Chimeric transcription of HERVH and CALB1, encoding calbindin, is also observed in human embryonic stem cells (ESCs), but its significance remained uncertain. Here, we show that HERVH integration on 8q21.3 during Homininae evolution coincides with acquisition of expression of CALB1 in preimplantation embryos. We further show that CALB1 expression is critical for human ESC growth and the prevention of cellular senescence and for the formation of ESC-derived preimplantation blastoids and postgastrulation amnioids. Thus, the co-option of HERVH 8q21.3 cis-regulatory activity in lung cancer may echo its essential requirement for human embryo development.

cards.title: Effect of connector dimensions and span length on fracture resistance of high-translucency 4Y-TZP: An in vitro and finite element study.
cards.abstract: High-translucency 4-mol% yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia polycrystal (4Y-TZP) has been increasingly used for implant-supported prostheses because of its superior esthetics, yet connector size recommendations have been derived from studies of stronger conventional 3-mol% Y-TZP. Whether these guidelines remain valid for materials with 30 to 40% lower flexural strength is unknown. The purpose of this in vitro and finite element study was to evaluate the effect of connector cross-sectional dimensions and span length on the fracture resistance of high-translucency monolithic 4Y-TZP and to characterize stress distribution and concentration at the connector. Bar-shaped specimens incorporating 4 connector regions were milled from presintered high-translucency 4Y-TZP (KATANA Zirconia HTML PLUS A2). Four connector configurations were tested: 3×3 mm, 4×3 mm, 4×4 mm (elliptical cross-sections), and 5×4 mm (full cross-section control), with cross-sectional areas of 7.1, 9.4, 12.6, and 20.0 mm². The specimens were tested at 2 span lengths (22 and 42 mm) by 3-point bend testing (n=6 per group). Fracture load (N) was recorded, and flexural stress at the connector (MPa) was calculated from the local bending moment and the section modulus appropriate to each cross-sectional geometry. Three-dimensional finite element models determined maximum principal stress (σ₁) and stress concentration factors. Data were analyzed with 2-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), the Tukey honestly significant difference (HSD) test, and the Pearson correlation (α=.05). Connector configuration (P<.001), span length (P<.001), and their interaction (P<.001) significantly affected fracture load. Mean ±standard deviation fracture load ranged from 208 ±14 N (3×3 mm, 42-mm span) to 1806 ±142 N (5×4 mm, 22-mm span) and correlated strongly with connector area (r≥.979, P<.001). Load gain per mm² of connector area was approximately twice as large for the 22-mm span (98.3 N per mm²) as for the 42-mm span (52.3 N per mm²). When load was converted to flexural stress at the connector, only connector configuration remained significant (P<.001); span length (P=.816) and the interaction (P=.162) were not significant. Connector stress converged into a narrow range (533 to 745 MPa) within published 4Y-TZP flexural strength values. Finite element analysis confirmed stress concentration at the connector base, with σ₁ spanning a factor of only 1.5 (613 to 939 MPa) despite an 8.7-fold range in fracture loads. Under equal applied load, stress concentration factors ranged from 1.67 to 3.92 at the 22-mm span and from 2.62 to 6.42 at the 42-mm span. Reducing connector area disproportionately decreased fracture load, with greater reduction at longer spans. Connector stress values fell within a narrower range than fracture loads, suggesting that load differences are driven predominantly by geometry.

cards.title: Sacrificial Coating-Assisted Deformation Regulation in GO-Coated Kevlar Structures under Dynamic Bending.
cards.abstract: Kevlar-based flexible protective materials exhibit excellent tensile deformability and energy-dissipation capability under impact loading. However, under dynamic bending, the deformation response of Kevlar gradually evolves from distributed deformation toward highly localized structural failure with increasing loading velocity, which severely limits its resistance against catastrophic perforation. In this work, graphene oxide (GO) multilayer coatings were introduced onto Kevlar structures to regulate deformation localization and improve their dynamic bending tolerance. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to investigate the quasi-static and dynamic bending behaviors of uncoated, single-layer-GO-coated, and bilayer-GO-coated Kevlar structures. The results reveal that the deformation behavior of Kevlar is governed by a velocity-dependent transition between distributed deformation and localized rupture. The introduction of GO coatings fundamentally modifies the stress redistribution and failure evolution of the Kevlar network. Under quasi-static bending, the GO layers enhance the load-bearing capability of the structure through coating-assisted stress transfer. Under dynamic bending, sacrificial fracture of the GO coatings delays severe Kevlar degradation and promotes broader deformation redistribution within the fibrous network. Compared with the uncoated structure, the critical perforation velocity increases by approximately 28.6 and 48.6% for the single-layer-coated and bilayer-coated systems, respectively. These findings provide mechanistic insight into coating-mediated deformation regulation in flexible fibrous networks and demonstrate the potential of GO-based interfacial engineering for improving dynamic bending resistance under extreme loading conditions.

cards.title: TGA6 directly activates ABF2 and ABF3 to promote leaf senescence in Arabidopsis thaliana.
cards.abstract: Leaf senescence is a tightly regulated developmental process governed by a complex transcriptional network. Although the TGACG motif-binding (TGA) family of basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factors are well-characterized regulators of plant defense responses, their roles in leaf senescence remain poorly understood. Here, we report that overexpression of TGA6 in Arabidopsis thaliana promotes early leaf senescence. Independent TGA6-overexpressing lines displayed premature leaf yellowing and significantly lower chlorophyll levels than wild-type (WT) plants under both normal growth and dark-induced senescence conditions. At the molecular level, RT-qPCR analysis revealed significant upregulation of canonical senescence marker genes, including NYC1, PAO, SAG12, SAG13, SGR1, and SGR2, in the TGA6-OE lines relative to WT plants. Furthermore, we found that the transcript levels of ABA-responsive element binding factor 2 (ABF2) and ABF3, which act upstream of these senescence markers, were significantly elevated in the TGA6-OE lines. Dual-luciferase reporter assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assay demonstrated that TGA6 directly binds to the TGACG motifs within the promoters of ABF2 and ABF3 to activate their transcription. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TGA6 functions as a positive regulator of leaf senescence.

cards.title: Recurrent Sleep Restriction During Aging Induces Early Recognition Memory Impairment, Neuroinflammation, and Blood-Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Female Wistar Rats.
cards.abstract: Sleep restriction is associated with neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, and cognitive impairment. Although reduced sleep duration in women is well recognized and the impact of sleep disorders is correlated with a higher incidence of neurodegenerative diseases, its consequences during female aging remain poorly understood. Hence, the aim of this study was to evaluate whether recurrent sleep restriction in female rats accelerates aging-related processes, compared with aged females with normal sleep patterns. Female Wistar rats were subjected to sleep restriction for 10 consecutive days, every three months from 6 to 18 months of age. An additional group of 3-month-old rats underwent a single sleep restriction episode as control. BBB permeability, neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and recognition memory were assessed. Recurrent sleep restriction increased BBB permeability in the cerebral cortex to tracers of different molecular weights and induced hippocampal increase in TNF-α and IL-1β. In contrast, senescence markers showed age- and region-dependent changes, with no clear effect of recurrent sleep restriction in aged animals. A single sleep restriction episode was sufficient to impair recognition memory, whereas recurrent sleep restriction accelerated age-related cognitive decline. These findings indicate that the BBB dysfunction and neuroinflammatory alterations during sleep restriction depend on age and brain region, as well as the recurrence of these episodes.

cards.title: How do 3M Command™ strips work? A fracture mechanics approach.
cards.abstract: Removable adhesive systems such as 3M Command™ strips are designed to support substantial loads while allowing clean, damage-free removal from the substrate. These systems rely on a highly extensible adhesive strip that bonds strongly during use but releases when stretched, causing the adhesive layer to elongate and progressively debond from the surfaces. A central challenge in the design of stretch-release adhesives is therefore to maximize load-bearing capacity while minimizing the force required for removal. This study investigates the finite-deformation mechanics governing both load support and tape release in a hyperelastic stretch-release adhesive system, with particular focus on the 3M Command™ tape geometry. Explicit analytical expressions are derived for the energy release rate of interfacial cracks under both load-bearing and release conditions and are validated against J-integral evaluations from finite element simulations. The results show that the ratio of maximum supported load to release force scales linearly with the ratio of bonded length to adhesive thickness, which is typically very large. We also investigate geometry-driven alternating crack propagation between the backing and substrate interfaces, governing tape removal, by analytical solutions and simulations. Parametric studies of competing interfacial fracture toughnesses produce failure envelopes that provide a predictive framework for estimating release forces and unstable crack propagation in multilayer stretch-release adhesive systems.

cards.title: Mitochondrial YME1L Restrains GRP75-Dependent ISR Activation to Prevent Podocyte Senescence in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
cards.abstract: Loss of YME1L promotes podocyte senescence in diabetic kidney disease. YME1L deficiency induces sustained maladaptive integrated stress response activation. YME1L interacts with and regulates mitochondrial GRP75 homeostasis. GRP75 accumulation drives persistent integrated stress response activation and mitochondrial dysfunction.

cards.title: Phantom Fairness: A Reproducible Audit of How Automatically Extracted Labels Can Conceal Demographic Disparities in Chest Radiograph Classifiers
cards.abstract: Fairness audits of chest radiograph artificial intelligence usually score subgroup performance against labels extracted from radiology reports by natural language processing (NLP). We tested whether these labels can make a model look fairer than it is, a failure we call phantom fairness. On 4,376 NIH ChestX-ray14 images with both NLP and radiologist-adjudicated labels, we audited classifiers from three backbones by sex, age, projection and older women. NLP labels missed 54% to 59% of radiologist-confirmed airspace opacity, pneumothorax and nodule or mass, and every fracture. These misses were not random: models scored them lower than NLP-caught positives for every finding and backbone (median rank-biserial correlation 0.20 for the primary backbone and 0.16 for the others; all adjusted p [≤] 0.038), so the labelling errors hid the models' own mistakes. Subgroup gaps were larger on adjudicated labels in 16 of 24 comparisons, none individually significant. For pneumothorax in women older than 60 years, the NLP audit showed a sensitivity gap of 0.064 against a true gap of 0.184; removing the hardest positives reproduced this concealment (0.124 against 0.120 observed), whereas random label errors produced less (0.077). Fairness audits based on NLP-extracted labels should be treated as provisional until checked against radiologist-adjudicated labels.

cards.title: The discovery of potent and selective N6-modified adenosine derivatives as effective chemotherapeutic agents to overcome p53-dependent drug resistance in cancer and HPIV-3/AdV5 respiratory tract infections.
cards.abstract: A library of N6-modified adenosine derivatives (compounds 7-36) was synthesized via a one-step reaction of 6-chloro- or 2-amino-6-chloro-(β-D-ribofuranosyl)-9H-purine with primary or secondary amines. The structures of selected compounds (14, 31, 34) were confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, revealing diverse crystal packing motifs and hydrogen-bonding networks. Biological evaluation demonstrated a broad range of cytotoxic activities across a panel of cancer and non-cancer cell lines, ranging from highly potent to non-toxic derivatives. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the biological properties of the synthesized compounds were strongly influenced by the nature of the N6 substituent, with distinct structural features governing anticancer and antiviral activities. Several compounds (21, 22, 28, 30, and 32) markedly reduced cancer cell viability, with compound 28 exhibiting the highest potency across multiple solid tumor models. Importantly, compound 28 induced apoptosis, suppressed proliferation, and rapidly decreased cell viability in both HCT116 and HCT116 p53-/- colorectal carcinoma cells, indicating p53-independent activity. In contrast, cladribine displayed pronounced p53 dependence, promoting apoptosis primarily in p53-proficient cells and inducing a senescence-like phenotype rather than rapid cell death. Antiviral screening identified compounds 22, 25, and 35 as promising inhibitors of human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV-3), whereas compound 12 exhibited the highest activity and selectivity against human adenovirus type 5 (AdV5). Collectively, these findings identify N6-modified adenosines as a promising class of compounds for developing anticancer agents with p53-independent activity and reveal several derivatives as attractive scaffolds for further optimization toward antiviral agents targeting respiratory viruses.

cards.title: Fusaspironols A-E: Steroidal spirostanols from the deep-sea-derived Fusarium inflexum ZEN8 with inhibitory activities against osteoclastogenesis and adipogenic differentiation.
cards.abstract: Five previously undescribed polyhydroxylated spirostanols, fusaspironols A-E (1-5), along with eight known compounds (6-13), were isolated from the deep-sea-derived fungus Fusarium inflexum ZEN8. Their structures were elucidated using spectroscopic analysis, GIAO-based NMR calculations, and DP4+ probability analysis. Notably, this represents only the second report of spirostanols of fungal origin. A plausible biosynthetic pathway linking compounds 1-5 to the putative precursor cholesterol in this fungus was proposed. In biological assays, compound 8 significantly inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis in bone marrow macrophages, whereas compounds 2, 3, and 7 suppressed adipogenesis in mature bone marrow stromal cells. None of the compounds exhibited detectable cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations, suggesting their potential as lead compounds for anti-osteoporosis drug development.

cards.title: Plant photosynthetic responses to drought, rewatering, and flooding.
cards.abstract: The review discusses how plants modulate photosynthesis under contrasting water regimes, highlighting stress-specific limitations, recovery dynamics, and physiological indicators to inform breeding and management under climate change. Climate change is intensifying rainfall extremes, including prolonged droughts, sudden rewatering, and extended flooding, threatening crop productivity worldwide. Here, we present an integrative review synthesizing how major crops modulate photosynthesis under these contrasting water regimes. Drought restricts stomatal and mesophyll conductance, downregulates RuBisCo, and heightens photo-oxidative stress, whereas flooding impairs root structure, water transport, and ATP production. Both stresses can trigger oxidative processes and reduce root-to-shoot hydraulic conductance, imposing similar limitations on photosynthesis. Responses to drought and flooding, and recovery after rewatering and flooding depends on stress intensity and duration, plant species/genotype, and developmental stage. Chlorophyll stability, gas exchange, and PSII fluorescence emerge as robust indicators of photosynthetic resistance and resilience. Trade-offs between stress tolerance and recovery reflect coordinated adjustments in energy use, carbon allocation, and senescence process. Despite recent advances, critical gaps remain in long-term acclimation, compound heat-drought impacts, and canopy-scale carbon dynamics. Finally, we propose an innovative research framework linking photosynthetic plasticity to precipitation variability and highlight breeding and management practices to enhance plant resilience under future climate extremes.

cards.title: Baicalein-loaded nanocochleates for improving oral bioavailability: design, statistical optimization, and in vivo pharmacokinetic evaluation.
cards.abstract: Baicalein, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits potent lipoxygenase-inhibitory, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities that are beneficial for treating osteoporosis. However, its poor aqueous solubility, low oral bioavailability, and extensive presystemic metabolism restrict its clinical applicability. Thus, the present work aimed to develop baicalein-loaded nanocochleates to improve its oral bioavailability. Baicalein-loaded nanocochleates were prepared from preformed liposomes using the trapping method and further statistically optimized using a 3-factor, 3-level Box-Behnken Design (BBD). The optimized batch showed a particle size of 230.53 ± 7.86 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.39 ± 0.01, a zeta potential of -19.07 ± 1.21 mV, and an entrapment efficiency of 93.50 ± 1.32%. Further, DSC and ATR-FTIR results confirmed the successful encapsulation of baicalein within the lipid matrix of nanocochleates, while TEM images revealed elongated, rod-like nanocochleate structures. Importantly, the optimized formulation showed 88.59 ± 1.53% drug release over 24 h compared with baicalein-loaded liposomes (96.10 ± 7.03%), indicating sustained drug release. In vivo oral pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated a 1.49-fold and 11.50-fold increase in Cmax and a 2.47-fold and 14.71-fold increase in AUC0-24 h compared with baicalein-loaded liposomes and plain baicalein, respectively. Collectively, the results suggest that nanocochleates represent a promising carrier system to improve the oral bioavailability of baicalein.

cards.title: Nonplanar Bouligand Architectures for Enhanced Mechanical Performance in Cementitious Composites.
cards.abstract: Brittle and quasi-brittle materials such as hydraulic cement-based materials, glass, and ceramics exhibit limited toughness and poor energy absorption, often leading to catastrophic failure under extreme loading. Inspired by the dactyl club of the Mantis shrimp, we introduce a sinusoidal Bouligand architecture into concrete enabled by nonplanar additive manufacturing. Under quasi-static compression, the elements with sinusoidal Bouligand architecture exhibit a 53.6% higher compressive strength and a 216.1% greater work of failure than regular 3D-printed elements, while also outperforming cast counterparts by 13.5% in strength and 35% in work of failure. Under impact loading, the sinusoidal Bouligand samples exhibit up to a 68.6% increase in peak load and a 49.2% increase in absorbed energy compared to cast counterparts. These improvements enable the architected samples to maintain structural integrity without catastrophic failure, whereas the cast samples fail by highly localized fracture. Fiber alignment during 3D printing induces strong and tunable local anisotropy which, coupled with the sinusoidal Bouligand architecture, enables interfacial crack deflection, crack twisting, and damage delocalization. These results demonstrate the effective translation of biological toughening principles into engineered materials and establish a design paradigm for cementitious composites with enhanced damage tolerance and energy-absorbing capability.

cards.title: Cleanroom-Free Microfluidic Chips with Capacitively Coupled 3D Liquid-Metal Electrodes as a Platform Technology for Controlled Electrical Field Stimulation of 2D and 3D Cell Cultures.
cards.abstract: Existing in vitro electrical stimulation platforms are limited by cleanroom-dependent fabrication, direct electrode-electrolyte contact that generates cytotoxic byproducts, and poor compatibility with 3D culture systems. This study reports a modular, cleanroom-free workflow for fabricating polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) microfluidic chips with capacitively coupled 3D liquid metal (EGaIn) electrodes using digital light processing (DLP)-printed molds. The process achieves sub-day turnaround at electrode resolutions of ∼200 µm, which extends to ∼25 µm via a hybrid DLP/two-photon polymerization approach. A ∼150 µm PDMS dielectric barrier isolates the electrodes from the culture medium to eliminate faradaic reactions. COMSOL and ANSYS HFSS simulations show uniform electric fields of 27-108 V/m (three-channel chip) and (1.72-2.63) × 103 V/m (five-channel chip) across the culture chamber. Platform performance was validated across multiple cell types and culture formats. Stimulus-evoked calcium signaling was demonstrated in 50B11 dorsal root ganglion neurons (2D and 3D collagen) and in primary cortical neurons. Daily stimulation (∼4.68 × 103 V/m, 60 kHz) of OCY454 osteocytes in 3D collagen resulted in an 8-fold increase in cell proliferation (compared to 2-fold in controls) and a significant reduction in sclerostin expression. An automated pipeline combining Cellpose segmentation with hierarchical clustering identified three distinct cell subpopulations based on their calcium signaling dynamics. These results establish a customizable, cleanroom-free platform for delivering quantified 3D electrical fields to diverse cell cultures.

cards.title: A DNA G-Quadruplex-Targeting Ligand Suppresses c-MYC Expression: Implications for Gemcitabine‑Resistant Pancreatic Cancer.
cards.abstract: The MYC oncogene is dysregulated in nearly 70% of human cancers and plays a central role in tumor initiation and progression. However, direct targeting of c-MYC remains challenging because of its "undruggable" nature. Stabilization of DNA G-quadruplex (G4) structures within the c-MYC promoter offers an alternative strategy to suppress c-MYC transcription. Here, we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of a series of styryl quinolinium ligands, identifying PQB-4 as a selective c-MYC DNA G4-binder (KD <1.0 µM). PQB-4 exhibited marked antiproliferative activity against pancreatic cancer cell lines, including MIA PaCa-2 (IC50 = 2.9 µM), PANC-1 (IC50 = 4.5 µM), and gemcitabine-resistant PANC-1 cells (IC50 = 5.0 µM), while showing substantially lower toxicity toward noncancerous HK-2 cells (IC50 = 40.1 µM). Mechanistically, PQB-4 stabilized c-MYC DNA G4-structures, suppressed c-MYC mRNA and protein expression, induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest, and activated a p53-dependent DNA damage response. PQB-4 also promoted telomere damage, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, ferroptosis, and mitophagy, while inhibiting cancer cell migration, proliferation, and survival. Notably, PQB-4 synergized strongly with gemcitabine in resistant PANC-1 cells (CI = 0.027). In a PANC-1 xenograft model, PQB-4 reduced tumor weight by 44%. These findings highlight c-MYC DNA G4 targeting by PQB-4 as a feasible therapeutic strategy for pancreatic cancer, particularly in gemcitabine-resistant disease.

cards.title: Astrocytic cathepsin D promotes α-synuclein processing and Lewy neurite-like aggregate maturation.
cards.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) and related synucleinopathies are marked by the accumulation and propagation of α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregates, a process primarily studied in neurons. Whether astrocytes actively contribute to α-syn processing and intercellular transfer remains unclear. Here, using a physiologically relevant neuron-astrocyte co-culture system that recapitulates tripartite synapse architecture, we show that astrocytes process α-syn and influence the morphological maturation of neuronal aggregates. Astrocytes internalize α-syn pre-formed fibrils (PFFs) and generate C-terminally truncated α-syn species via a Cathepsin D (CtsD)-dependent process. PFF-loaded astrocytes transfer α-syn-containing material to neurons and promote the formation and maturation of pS129-α-syn-positive Lewy neurite (LN)-like aggregates. Notably, α-syn PFF exposure induces lysosomal membrane damage, a senescence-like reactive state, and CtsD upregulation in astrocytes. Although PFF-containing lysosomes undergo autophagic engulfment, they persist within astrocytes, and a subset is detected beyond the astrocytic membrane boundary. Together, our findings support a model in which astrocytic lysosomal remodeling of internalized α-syn contributes to the morphological maturation and intercellular propagation of neuronal α-syn pathology in this co-culture system.

cards.title: Ultrahigh Ductility in the BCC Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 Refractory Multiprincipal Element Alloy: Energetic and Electronic Origins.
cards.abstract: Recent experimental discovery of the ultrahigh ductility of the body-centered cubic (BCC) Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 refractory multiprincipal element alloy (RMPEA) exhibits a clear distinction from the MoNbTaW RMPEA with low ductility. To unravel the physical origins of this remarkable ductility, this study employs first-principles calculations to investigate the factors governing intrinsic ductility of the RMPEAs. The energy calculation results indicate a stronger tendency for double cross-slip, dislocation multiplication, and twinning deformation of the Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 RMPEA. Integrated with fracture criteria, it is further confirmed that multiple dislocations and twins can emit from the crack tip in this alloy. Analysis of the electron structure reveals that the compositional substitution induces the charge delocalization, bonding metallization and a higher and smoother density of states curve near the Fermi level of the Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 RMPEA. Furthermore, increasing Nb content generally raises the calculated fault and surface energies, while favorable plasticity tendencies persist across the investigated BCC configurations. Nb addition can increase the energetic barrier to fault formation and dislocation nucleation without suppressing the intrinsic propensity for crack-tip plasticity over a broad composition range. These findings can provide energetic and electronic insights into the intrinsic ductility of the BCC RMPEAs containing group IV elements.

cards.title: Adaptation to heat stress by diversification of the vertebrate heat shock transcription factor family.
cards.abstract: Cells survive and reproduce by coping with acute or chronic exposure to a fixed elevated temperature or fluctuating temperatures. These properties are one of the main evolutionary forces and involve the heat shock response. This response is characterized by the induction of heat-shock proteins (HSPs) and is mainly regulated by heat-shock transcription factors (HSFs) in vertebrates. A single HSF is present in yeast and invertebrates, such as Caenorhabditis elegans and Drosophila, whereas vertebrates have evolved multiple HSFs. The potential of HSFs to induce HSP expression is linked to the amino acid conservation of their domains and regions that are responsible for transcriptional activation and appears to be associated with the homeothermic capacity of vertebrate animals in a thermally fluctuating environment. HSFs protect cells and organisms from heat stress by regulating not only their expression of HSPs that assist in protein folding and suppress protein misfolding and aggregation, but also the expression of genes related to protein clearance, metabolism, the cell cycle, DNA damage response, apoptosis, senescence, the cytoskeleton, extracellular matrix and inflammation. The diversification of HSF genes may expand the cellular capacity to adapt to thermal changes in vertebrate animals. This article is part of the Theo Murphy meeting issue 'ProteostaSys: a systems view of proteostasis'.

cards.title: Osteosarcopenia: More Than the Sum of Its Parts? A Community-Based Study Across Sarcopenia Definitions.
cards.abstract: Osteosarcopenia, the co-existence of osteoporosis and sarcopenia, is described as a geriatric syndrome arising from shared determinants of muscle and bone. We asked how far the prevalence of sarcopenia and osteosarcopenia depends on the definition of low muscle mass, whether osteoporosis and sarcopenia co-occur more often than expected under statistical independence, and whether the muscle-bone relationship is expressed in areal bone mineral density (BMD) or in femoral geometry. Cross-sectional study of 649 community-dwelling adults aged 65 years and over (72% women; mean age 71.5 years; mean body mass index (BMI) 29.6 kg/m2) assessed with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (GE Lunar iDXA), grip dynamometry (Jamar Hydraulic Hand Dynamometer) and the Short Physical Performance Battery. Osteoporosis followed World Health Organization criteria. Sarcopenia was classified according to EWGSOP2, and low muscle mass was defined three ways (appendicular lean mass (ALM)/height2; absolute ALM; and the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) ALM/BMI index). Observed co-occurrence was compared with the value expected under independence (Fisher exact test, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI)); for the best-powered analysis the two one-sided tests (TOST) equivalence procedure using pragmatic equivalence bounds of OR 0.5 to 2.0. Hip structural analysis provided section modulus and cross-sectional area. Low muscle mass ranged from 3.7 to 15.7%, and confirmed sarcopenia from 1.4 to 4.2%, according to the metric. Osteoporosis prevalence was 17.6% (95% CI 14.9 to 20.8). Under none of the sarcopenia definitions was there statistically significant evidence of excess co-occurrence (Fisher p = 0.50 to 1.00), although observed overlap under the absolute-ALM definition was slightly above the independence expectation. For probable sarcopenia (low grip strength), the best-powered comparison, the OR was 0.89 (95% CI 0.47 to 1.67) and equivalence within broad OR bounds of 0.5 to 2.0 was supported (90% CI 0.52 to 1.51; TOST p = 0.037); equivalence was not supported under narrower bounds. Appendicular lean mass was not associated with areal BMD after adjustment for body size (femoral neck standardised β = 0.03, 95% CI - 0.18 to 0.24) but was associated with femoral section modulus substantially more strongly in men than women (globally standardised interaction Δβ = 0.30, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.44, p < 0.001). In this community sample, there was no statistically significant evidence that osteoporosis and sarcopenia co-occurred more often than expected under statistical independence, across several sarcopenia definitions, although estimates for confirmed sarcopenia were imprecise. The muscle-bone association was more apparent for femoral geometry than areal BMD and was seen predominantly in men. These findings do not support assuming that low bone mass and low muscle mass identify the same individuals, but they concern statistical co-occurrence and do not establish biological independence.

cards.title: Reliability, Readability, and Safety of Generative AI Chatbots for Osteoporosis Health Counseling: A Multidimensional Cross-Sectional Comparative Study.
cards.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots are increasingly used for health information, but their reliability, readability, and safety in osteoporosis counseling remain uncertain. This study compared four widely available chatbots under standardized conditions. Twenty-five standardized osteoporosis questions were submitted once to ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Copilot, and Perplexity Pro, generating 100 responses. Two model-blinded specialists evaluated the final responses using DISCERN, EQIP, the Global Quality Scale, JAMA benchmarks, and the NOHARM framework. Six automated indices assessed readability. Because each question was answered by all four models, outcomes were compared using Friedman tests, followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment. DISCERN scores differed across models (p < 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.82, 95% CI 0.76-0.89). Median scores were 55.0 for Perplexity Pro, 54.0 for Copilot, 44.0 for Gemini 2.5 Pro, and 42.0 for ChatGPT-5. JAMA benchmark scores did not differ significantly (p = 0.63). All six readability indices differed across models (all p < 0.001). Perplexity Pro had the highest median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score at 16.18, whereas Copilot had the lowest at 9.49; all models exceeded the sixth-grade benchmark. The qualitative safety assessment also identified clinically relevant omissions and an unsupported claim. In this set of osteoporosis questions, retrieval-enabled systems achieved higher scores on selected information-quality measures but produced more difficult text. These findings are limited to the tested models, prompts, and evaluation period and do not establish a universal effect of retrieval augmentation.

cards.title: What Embedding-Based Guideline-Literature Drift Measures (and What It Doesn't): A Proof-of-Concept and Mechanistic Dissection of TIDE in Orthopedic Surgery
cards.abstract: Purpose: We introduce the Temporal Index of Divergent Evidence (TIDE), a metric that evaluates how the topic center of gravity of a corresponding corpus of literature aligns with, or shifts relative to, a recommendation's semantics over time. Methods: TIDE computes annual mean cosine similarity using MedCPT embedding vectors between a recommendation and corresponding PubMed records binned by year (2000-2024), testing for monotonic temporal trend (Kendall {tau}). Three recommendations with expected divergent, stable, and convergent trajectories were examined: two-stage exchange for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), emergent fasciotomy for acute compartment syndrome (ACS), and non-operative management of distal radius fractures (DRF) in adults [≥] 65 years. The signal was characterized by an additive per-token attribution, an isolated vs. in-context analysis, and an adversarial minimal-pair test. Results: PJI diverged ({tau} = -0.84, year-shuffle p = 0.001), DRF converged ({tau} = +0.42, p = 0.005), and ACS showed no detectable trend ({tau} = -0.07, p = 0.66). The two significant directions (PJI, DRF) held under matched input [CLS] pooling, while ACS remained near zero. Publication volume baselines did not distinguish the three trajectories (publication count was universally positive, {tau} = +0.77 to +0.97). A reversed-meaning minimal-pair control showed little cosine sensitivity to reversal. Paper-level TF-IDF recovered the qualitative three-case pattern. Conclusion: Embedding-based drift analysis is a proof-of-concept candidate pre-triage signal that tracks topical alignment, not evidentiary direction; superiority over TF-IDF remains unproven. The present study is hypothesis-generating, showing potential use of embedding representations as an analytical unit rather than simply for retrieval.

cards.title: Investigation of age- and sex-related changes in cancellous bone density in the human spine using CT.
cards.abstract: Studies of cancellous bone density across all spinal segments in relation to age and sex remain limited. This investigation aimed to quantify vertebral cancellous bone density in Hounsfield units (HU), to explore age‑ and sex‑related bone loss, and to compare HU measurements with bone mineral density (BMD) and bone volume fraction (BV/TV). Cancellous bone density was assessed in 71 spines (CT) covering vertebrae C3-L5 and the age range from 4 to 102 years. HU values were derived from mid‑vertebral regions, and in addition, BMD (L1-L3) and BV/TV measurements (Th12-L2, micro‑CT, 50 spines) in broad subsets of samples. The association between bone density and age was investigated by HU profiles along the spine in age groups and by regression approaches. HU values decreased with age (p < 0.001) and from cranial to caudal levels (p < 0.001), for both sexes (p < 0.001), with a marked reduction at the thoracolumbar junction beyond 60 years. Regression and cluster analyses revealed two phases of HU density loss with ongoing age, the second occurring in women (older than 64 years), later than in men (after 56 years) (p < 0.001). HU values were correlated with BMD (r = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.72-0.94) and with BV/TV (r = 0.51; 95% CI: 0.17-0.75). Density loss of bone with age is significant for BMD (for both sexes, p < 0.001) and for BV/TV (p ≤ 0.021), too, with an earlier reduction detected in the microarchitecture. These findings highlight the need for sex‑specific assessment and prevention strategies in osteoporosis research and clinical care.

cards.title: Mechanical properties and failure characteristics of geocells: A comparative experimental study.
cards.abstract: The tensile performance of geocells depends on the mechanical responses of both cell walls and junctions. Three commercial geocells, liquation-welded polypropylene (LW), injection-molded polyester (IM), and ultrasonic-welded high-density polyethylene (UW), were examined through tensile testing, macroscopic observation, and scanning electron microscopy of cell-wall fracture surfaces. Five configurations were used: cell-wall tension, junction-inclusive tension, and junction seam, shear, and split tests. The cell-wall peak strengths of LW, IM, and UW were 143.03 ± 4.43, 185.61 ± 7.96, and 39.42 ± 2.41 kN/m, respectively. Including a junction changed the strengths by +28.99%, -59.79%, and -23.76%. The LW and IM cell walls lost load rapidly after the peak. UW exhibited necking and extended post-yield deformation. SEM revealed microfibrillar bundles in LW, a smooth layered surface in IM, and dense drawn microfibrils in UW. Under junction-inclusive tension, LW tore near the raised-tab edge, IM cracked through the ligaments between the holes, and UW fractured at a weld-wall boundary. LW provided the highest seam and shear strengths of 66.16 ± 4.20 and 146.02 ± 8.46 kN/m. IM provided the highest split strength of 158.55 ± 10.34 kN/m. UW showed lower junction strengths but reached 343.09 ± 13.72% rupture strain under shear. Under seam and shear loading, LW failed near the tab-wall transition, while IM fractured from hole edges. UW failed within the weld region under seam loading and at a weld-wall boundary under shear loading. Under split loading, failure occurred at the heat-fused interface in LW, the molded body in IM, and the central weld in UW.

cards.title: Research on the design and mechanical properties of extended constant resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolts.
cards.abstract: To address the premature fracture of anchor bolts caused by the mismatched yielding distance between anchor bolts and hydraulic supports in the advanced support section of rock burst-prone roadways, an elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt was designed-with its yielding distance specifically coordinated to match that of hydraulic supports. ABAQUS numerical simulation was utilized to investigate the mechanical characteristics of this novel anchor bolt under static loading, as well as under varying impact energies and impact velocities. A comparative analysis was further performed against the mechanical performance of conventional anchor bolts. The results reveal the following: Under static loading, the elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt exhibits a fracture load of 160.6 kN, a fracture displacement of 523.2 mm, an elongation rate of 20.93%, and an energy absorption capacity of 69.7 kJ. Under impact velocities within 9 m/s, the impact velocity has little effect on the fracture load, elongation, and energy absorption of constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolts, while the impact resistance time exhibits a nonlinear decreasing trend with increasing impact velocity. Under both static and dynamic loading conditions, the extended constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolt exhibits superior impact resistance and can effectively address the problem of premature bolt fracture caused by the mismatch between the bolt yielding distance and that of the hydraulic support in the three-level energy-absorbing support system. The findings provide a new perspective for bolt design.

cards.title: Numerical study on infill fracturing of mature wells under free-drainage boundary conditions.
cards.abstract: Infill fracturing of mature wells involves re-fracturing within previously stimulated clusters, targeting unstimulated regions of the parent well's fracture network. This strategy sustainably enhances hydrocarbon recovery from depleted reservoirs without the environmental footprint of new drilling. Establishing a numerical simulation model for this process is essential for optimization. In this study, a numerical model for mature well infill fracturing was developed based on the extended finite element method and a free-drainage boundary module. The results indicate that prior production from mature wells primarily affects the fracture length and curvature in the infill wells. As infill fracturing-induced fractures propagate toward the far-field region, they are significantly influenced by the heterogeneous pore pressure distribution in the reservoir. This leads to a pronounced increase in fracture curvature. Compared with conventional fracturing, the curvature of fractures under infill fracturing is approximately 30% higher within the same simulation time, while the fracture length is notably shorter. With the increase in production time, fractures in infill wells tend to exhibit greater tortuosity. This enhanced complexity allows for more effective contact between the fractures and the reservoir, thereby improving the production potential of the infill wells to some extent.
